elements on a decor layer are placed by.rule: Elements on a decor layer are placed by the decor stage, not the build stage; the build stage correctly leaves them for the decor stage.

drawn elements that are 60% or more insi.rule: Drawn elements that are 60% or more inside a larger fixture are parts of that fixture, not separate pieces; they are not built separately.

exterior site areas (parking, terrace, p.rule: Exterior site areas (parking, terrace, pool) are built as site surfaces (paving, grass, water), not as individual furniture pieces; the build stage correctly handles them at the site level.

drawn details inside a kitchen counter (.rule: Drawn details inside a kitchen counter (appliance fronts, drawers) are parts of the counter module, not separate pieces; they are not built separately.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces; the build stage leaves it for the furniture agent to split or place as a built-in.

a drawn symbol that both recognition pas.rule: A drawn symbol that both recognition passes classify as not_furniture is kept as an obstacle and not built as a piece.

a drawn outline around a table and its c.rule: A drawn outline around a table and its chairs that is 78% or more of its box is a rug mark, not a furniture piece; the decor stage places the rug.

cushions and pillows that are part of a.rule: Cushions and pillows that are part of a sofa or chair model are not separate decor pieces; they are included in the model.

two floor lamps that overlap by 30% or m.rule: Two floor lamps that overlap by 30% or more are one lamp drawn twice; the larger footprint is kept and the smaller is not built.

two floor lamps that overlap by 15% or m.rule: Two floor lamps that overlap by 15% or more are one lamp drawn twice; the larger footprint is kept and the smaller is not built.

when two pieces of the same type overlap.rule: When two pieces of the same type overlap by more than 10% and are of similar size, the recognition stage must treat them as a single drawn element and keep only the larger or more complete one.

a small outline (under 0.5 m) drawn 80%.rule: A small outline (under 0.5 m) drawn 80% or more inside a larger seat piece is its cushion or part, not a separate ottoman; the recognition stage must not type it as independent furniture.

a large outline (over 2 m on a side) tha.rule: A large outline (over 2 m on a side) that encloses other furniture pieces is a rug or zone boundary, not a piece; the build stage must not attempt to build it as furniture.

a stair's upper landing on the top floor.rule: A stair's upper landing on the top floor is not a separate piece to be built; it is the arrival point of the stair from the floor below.

a zone label like 'açik mutfak' (open ki.rule: A zone label like 'AÇIK MUTFAK' (open kitchen) in a living room indicates an open-plan kitchen zone; the recognition stage must map it to the kitchen pieces already present in the room and not flag it as an unknown warning.

an l-shaped outline with 0.5-1.3 m deep.rule: An L-shaped outline with 0.5-1.3 m deep arms in a living room is a corner sofa; the recognition stage may type it as sofa_corner by context.

a small seat (0.6-0.7 m) on one side of.rule: A small seat (0.6-0.7 m) on one side of a coffee table, facing it, in a living room is an armchair; the recognition stage may type it as armchair by context.

a drawn seat symbol of armchair size (0..rule: A drawn seat symbol of armchair size (0.55-0.75 m) placed facing a coffee table in a living room is typed as an armchair by context; the inference is recorded as a warning, not an error.

a desk symbol whose drawn footprint incl.rule: A desk symbol whose drawn footprint includes the chair in front of it is read as the desk alone (minus the chair depth); the chair is a separate piece placed in front.

when the plan draws kitchen fixtures ins.rule: When the plan draws kitchen fixtures inside a living room with no separating wall, the layout is an open kitchen; the fixtures are placed in the living room and the zone is recorded as an open kitchen.

when the plan labels a room as a terrace.rule: When the plan labels a room as a terrace (or balcony) with a door to it, and the section draws the roof closed over that area, the roof must be cut to create the terrace opening; the roof_terraces brief must be applied automatically.

when a door on a top-floor wall has its.rule: When a door on a top-floor wall has its head above the roof underside, the roof must be modified (dormer, raised eave, or flat section) to provide at least 2.0 m of clear headroom over the door; a clipped door is not acceptable.

an opening with no room on either side (.rule: An opening with no room on either side (a threshold or transition point) is assigned the floor material; this is recorded as a warning, not an error.

when a room has a sloped ceiling with li.rule: When a room has a sloped ceiling with limited headroom, the camera is placed at the nearest point with at least 0.3 m of headroom; this is recorded as a warning, not an error.

a labelled site pool (a 'havuz' area wit.rule: A labelled site pool (a 'havuz' area with a drawn outline) must be built as a pool volume with water and a coping edge, not dropped as 'no outline'; when several pool areas share one label, build each distinct drawn outline.

a labelled sunbathing/terrace site area.rule: A labelled sunbathing/terrace site area must be built as a paved deck with its outline, not dropped as 'no outline'.

a labelled parking site area must be bui.rule: A labelled parking site area must be built as a paved lot with its outline, not dropped as 'no outline'.

a site area drawn in the plan (pool, ter.rule: A site area drawn in the plan (pool, terrace, parking) must be built as a site element; 'NOT built (no outline)' for a drawn pool or terrace is a loss, not a good reason.

every bedroom must have at least one doo.rule: Every bedroom must have at least one door connecting it to a hall or corridor; a bedroom with no door is a loss.

every bathroom must have at least one do.rule: Every bathroom must have at least one door connecting it to a hall or corridor; a bathroom with no door is a loss.

every stair hall must have at least one.rule: Every stair hall must have at least one door connecting it to a hall or corridor; a stair hall with no door is a loss.

every corridor must have at least one do.rule: Every corridor must have at least one door connecting it to a hall or corridor; a corridor with no door is a loss.

a room whose name indicates a leisure, p.rule: A room whose name indicates a leisure, play or activity function and whose area exceeds 20 m2 with a full seating program should be typed 'living', not 'other', so the furniture agent places a coherent living set.

when a site area is labelled as a pool i.rule: When a site area is labelled as a pool in the documents and a pool model is present in the 3D scene, the site area must be marked as built with its outline; a pool that is rendered but whose site area record says 'NOT built' is a data inconsistency that must be resolved by either building the outline or removing the pool model.

when a site area is labelled as a terrac.rule: When a site area is labelled as a terrace or sunbathing area in the documents and a paved surface is present in the 3D scene at that location, the site area must be marked as built with its outline; a terrace that is rendered but whose site area record says 'NOT built' is a data inconsistency.

when a site area is labelled as a parkin.rule: When a site area is labelled as a parking area in the documents, it must be built with its outline and appropriate paving; a parking area that is not built and not visible in the 3D scene is a missing element that must be added or explicitly waived by the architect.

every level present in the plan with roo.rule: Every level present in the plan with rooms and openings must have its walls and openings built; a level whose walls are all missing after the build stage is a build failure, not a reading choice.

every room the documents name with a lab.rule: Every room the documents name with a label and area must be matched to a model room; a named room with no model room using it is a reading-stage loss.

a room label in the documents that match.rule: A room label in the documents that matches an already-built room by position and function is not a lost room; the ledger must not flag it as missing.

decor pieces must stay below the roof un.rule: Decor pieces must stay below the roof underside; any piece whose top exceeds the roof line must be lowered, resized, or removed by the decor stage.

every open-side stair must include a saf.rule: Every open-side stair must include a safety railing or guard as part of its parametric model; a stair without a guard on its open side is not acceptable.

every stair opening in a corridor or hal.rule: Every stair opening in a corridor or hall must have a safety railing or guard on its open edge; an unguarded opening is not acceptable.

decor pieces on furniture must rest on t.rule: Decor pieces on furniture must rest on the surface without penetration; any penetration > 0.03 m must be corrected by the decor stage.

a wardrobe model must show functional st.rule: A wardrobe model must show functional storage features (doors, handles); a flat panel or wall-like model is not acceptable for a wardrobe.

an armchair must face the main seating g.rule: An armchair must face the main seating group, not the back of another piece; the agent must orient it correctly.

a piece reaching through a room outline.rule: A piece reaching through a room outline by less than 0.03 m is within tolerance and not a finding.

furniture pieces must not overlap; the a.rule: Furniture pieces must not overlap; the agent must resolve collisions by repositioning pieces.

furniture must not block the walkway to.rule: Furniture must not block the walkway to a door; the agent must ensure a 0.60 m clear path to the front use zone of each piece.

a floor lamp must not stand in front of.rule: A floor lamp must not stand in front of a window opening; the furniture agent must place it clear of the window's sightline and egress.

an armchair must face its seating group,.rule: An armchair must face its seating group, not the back of another piece; the furniture agent must orient it toward the group's centre.

a wardrobe must sit fully inside the roo.rule: A wardrobe must sit fully inside the room outline; the furniture agent must keep it within the walls.

a coffee table must not overlap an armch.rule: A coffee table must not overlap an armchair; the furniture agent must keep seating and tables clear of each other.

an armchair's front use zone must be rea.rule: An armchair's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the door; the furniture agent must keep the approach clear.

a sofa's front use zone must be reachabl.rule: A sofa's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the door; the furniture agent must keep the approach clear.

a stove must have its back on a wall; th.rule: A stove must have its back on a wall; the furniture agent must snap it to the wall.

a kitchen aisle in front of a counter mu.rule: A kitchen aisle in front of a counter must be at least 0.90 m; the furniture agent must keep the aisle clear.

an armchair must face its seating group;.rule: An armchair must face its seating group; the furniture agent must orient it toward the group's centre.

a chair must have at least 0.81 m behind.rule: A chair must have at least 0.81 m behind it to the wall or piece; the furniture agent must keep the clearance.

a sofa must have its back on a wall; the.rule: A sofa must have its back on a wall; the furniture agent must snap it to the wall.

a seating group's chairs must face the g.rule: A seating group's chairs must face the group's anchor (sofa or table) within 30 degrees; the solver must orient every chair toward the anchor, not leave it at its drawn or default heading.

a dining chair must leave at least 0.81.rule: A dining chair must leave at least 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; the solver must seat the chair with that pull-back clearance, not tuck it against the back wall.

a double bed must leave at least 0.60 m.rule: A double bed must leave at least 0.60 m of free walkway along each side; the solver must place the bed with that side clearance, not squeeze it against the wall or a nightstand.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window opening (sill plus 0.05 m); the solver must place the nightstand clear of the window, not between the bed head and the glazing.

a wardrobe must leave at least 0.80 m of.rule: A wardrobe must leave at least 0.80 m of free space in front for the doors to open; the solver must place the wardrobe with that front clearance, not against the walkway.

a shower must be a real product size wit.rule: A shower must be a real product size within the type's catalogue range; the solver must pick a shower model that fits the bay, not a parametric box outside the product sizes.

a sofa's free zone in front must be clea.rule: A sofa's free zone in front must be clear of other pieces; the solver must keep the seating zone open, not place a table or chair in the sofa's front clearance.

a coffee table must sit in the free zone.rule: A coffee table must sit in the free zone in front of the sofa it serves; if the solver leaves it off-axis or behind the sofa, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit.

an armchair in a seating group must face.rule: An armchair in a seating group must face the coffee table within 30 degrees and sit within 2.50 m of it; the group solver must enforce both.

a dining chair must have at least 0.81 m.rule: A dining chair must have at least 0.81 m of clearance behind it to the nearest wall or piece; the dining group solver must enforce this.

the free zone in front of a sofa must re.rule: The free zone in front of a sofa must remain unobstructed; the seating group solver must not place any piece in that zone.

no furniture may block the sightline or.rule: No furniture may block the sightline or egress through a window opening; the balcony group solver must keep the window zone clear.

a dining table and chairs must not be pl.rule: A dining table and chairs must not be placed in a narrow window recess that blocks the window; the dining group solver must place the group in a proper dining zone.

site areas labeled in the documents (poo.rule: Site areas labeled in the documents (pools, terraces, parking) must be built by the site stage; if the outline is not built, the site stage must generate the outline and the model.

every bedroom must have a door connectin.rule: Every bedroom must have a door connecting it to the corridor; if the door is missing from the door list, the build stage must add it.

every room that is not a stair shaft or.rule: Every room that is not a stair shaft or a shared hall must have at least one door opening in the door list that connects it to a circulation space; if the build stage leaves a furnished room without a door, the run is incomplete and the door must be added from the drawing.

the build stage must preserve every piec.rule: The build stage must preserve every piece the final stage lists; a piece that is in the final list but absent from the built model is a build-stage loss and the stage must be re-run to restore it.

The build stage must preserve every piece the final stage lists in a room; a piece that is in the final list but absent from the built model is a build-stage loss and the stage must be re-run to place it.

The build stage must preserve every piece the final stage lists in a room; a piece that is in the final room's piece list but absent from the built scene is a build-stage loss and the build must be re-run to place it.

a room's listed functional pieces (stove.rule: A room's listed functional pieces (stove, fridge, sink, cabinets) must be built and visible; if the scene has no object for a planned piece, the build stage failed to place it and must be re-run.

a kitchen run's sink must be built as a.rule: A kitchen run's sink must be built as a distinct fixture on the counter; if the counter is built but the sink is missing from the scene, the build stage failed to place it.

a stair core room whose only camera poin.rule: A stair core room whose only camera point is inside the stair must not have its own interior view; the stair is shown from the adjacent hall or landing instead.

a drawn sofa that is dropped by the buil.rule: A drawn sofa that is dropped by the build stage due to a wall-snap conflict must be re-placed by the build stage at its drawn position or the nearest valid spot; it must not be silently removed.
A drawn sofa that is dropped by the build stage due to a conflict must be re-placed by the build stage at its drawn position or the nearest valid spot; it must not be silently removed.

a drawn floor lamp that is dropped by th.rule: A drawn floor lamp that is dropped by the build stage due to a conflict must be re-placed by the build stage at its drawn position or the nearest valid spot; it must not be silently removed.

a kitchen sink that is dropped by the bu.rule: A kitchen sink that is dropped by the build stage due to a conflict must be re-placed by the build stage at its drawn position or the nearest valid spot; it must not be silently removed.

a drawn piece that is dropped by the bui.rule: A drawn piece that is dropped by the build stage due to a conflict must be re-placed by the build stage at its drawn position or the nearest valid spot; it must not be silently removed.

a piece that the reading stage typed fro.rule: A piece that the reading stage typed from the drawing must survive the build stage; if the build drops it, the build stage must re-place it rather than let it vanish.

a drawn block in a kitchen that is not t.rule: A drawn block in a kitchen that is not typed must be classified from its size and neighbours before the build stage; an untyped kitchen block is a reading failure, not a valid skip.

every drawn fixture block on a level mus.rule: Every drawn fixture block on a level must be matched to a model element; a drawn stove with no model counterpart is a reading loss.
Every drawn fixture block on a level must be matched to a model element; a drawn toilet with no model counterpart is a reading loss.
Every drawn fixture block on a level must be matched to a model element; a drawn washbasin with no model counterpart is a reading loss.
Every drawn fixture block on a level must be matched to a model element; a drawn wall cabinet with no model counterpart is a reading loss.
Every drawn fixture block on a level must be matched to a model element; a drawn kitchen sink with no model counterpart is a reading loss.

a drawing layer dedicated to a structura.rule: A drawing layer dedicated to a structural element (stair) that the model already represents must be reconciled: the reading stage must either map its entities to the model element or record why they are redundant, never leave them unaccounted.

a layer whose name names a specific elem.rule: A layer whose name names a specific element (stair, door, window) must be read and its entities mapped to that element; if the element is already built from another source, the layer is reconciled against it, not silently dropped.

a kitchen's required appliance set (frid.rule: A kitchen's required appliance set (fridge, stove, sink) must be placed even when the counter run is tight; the solver must allow the fridge to stand at the end of the run or in a corner, and must not drop a required appliance just because the run is crowded.

a bathtub must be placed so that at leas.rule: A bathtub must be placed so that at least 0.53 m of clear floor remains in front of it; if the drawn bay is too shallow, the fitter must select a shorter tub model or shift the tub to the far end of the bay before the run is accepted.

a toilet's centre must be at least 0.38.rule: A toilet's centre must be at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; if the drawn position is too tight, the fitter must select a narrower toilet model or shift it to the nearest valid spot.

an opening must be cut through its wall;.rule: An opening must be cut through its wall; if the door ray hits the wall, the opening is not cut and the build stage must re-cut it.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.97 m); if the model's top is higher, the build stage must select a model with the correct height.

a frontal view of the entrance facade mu.rule: A frontal view of the entrance facade must be present; if missing, the camera stage must add it.

when the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3.rule: When the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3, a retaining edge must be built along the slope; the site stage must detect the slope and add the edge.

a railing must have a clear function (gu.rule: A railing must have a clear function (guarding an open edge, stair, or balcony); if it stands next to an unexplained hole, the build stage must either remove it or build the feature it guards.

a drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side in a.rule: A drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side in a living room must be resolved into its component furniture (sofa, table, sideboard) or marked as a single built-in before the build stage; it must not be left untyped and unbuilt.

a room whose name and drawn program indi.rule: A room whose name and drawn program indicate a children's play/leisure room must be typed 'other' (or a dedicated play type) and furnished with play/leisure pieces, not a full living-room set; a living-room furniture set in a play room is a misread.

when the plan labels a roof terrace with.rule: When the plan labels a roof terrace with a door to it, the roof build stage must cut an opening over the terrace footprint so the terrace is open to the sky; a closed roof over a labelled terrace is a build error.

a door under a sloped roof whose head wo.rule: A door under a sloped roof whose head would reach over the roof underside must be paired with a dormer or a raised roof line at that wall; a door clipped under the roof is unusable and must be flagged for a dormer.

a site area that is drawn in the plan an.rule: A site area that is drawn in the plan and rendered in the 3D scene must have its site-area record marked as built with an outline; a 'NOT built (no outline)' record for a rendered pool is a contradiction.

the sheets stage must answer all pending.rule: The sheets stage must answer all pending sheet questions before the run is accepted; unanswered questions block the milestone.

a sofa's front must face the long side w.rule: A sofa's front must face the long side with the most free space, not the short side; an AI front on the short side is a reading error.

a bench's front must face away from the.rule: A bench's front must face away from the wall it stands on; an AI front on the short side against a wall is a reading error.

a scene check failure on a built decor i.rule: A scene check failure on a built decor item must trigger a re-run of the scene stage for that level before the run is accepted.

the big loop must run enough cycles to r.rule: The big loop must run enough cycles to raise the house score above the baseline; stopping at the deadline with 0 improvement cycles is a failure.

a tall floor lamp (over 1.4 m) must not.rule: A tall floor lamp (over 1.4 m) must not be placed in front of a window whose sill is below 0.90 m; the furniture stage must keep the window's sightline and light clear, and the agent must not spend its move budget re-trying a position the code has already refused.

a dining chair must have at least 0.80 m.rule: A dining chair must have at least 0.80 m of clear pull-out space behind it; when the room cannot provide it, the furniture stage must drop or re-seat that chair rather than leave a sub-tolerance gap.

a coffee table must not overlap a seatin.rule: A coffee table must not overlap a seating piece; when the drawn coffee table's locked position collides with a drawn armchair, the furniture stage must shrink or re-seat the seating group, not push the locked table.

a wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of.rule: A wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of clear opening space in front of it; if the bedroom layout cannot provide it, the wardrobe must be repositioned to a wall with clearance or removed, not left with a 0.15 m gap.

a double bed must have at least 0.60 m o.rule: A double bed must have at least 0.60 m of clear walkway on at least one side; when the drawn bed's locked position cannot provide it, the furniture stage must re-seat the bed on a wall span that allows the clearance.

a shoe cabinet must be a finished, detai.rule: A shoe cabinet must be a finished, detailed model that fits the room's material palette; if the current model is a placeholder, the furniture stage must swap to a library model that passes the fit rules (caps, height) rather than leaving a crude block.

a wardrobe (or any tall storage) must no.rule: A wardrobe (or any tall storage) must not protrude through the room outline; if the drawn piece extends beyond the wall by more than 0.01 m, the architect rule must flag it as a geometry error, not accept it.

every seating piece's front use zone mus.rule: Every seating piece's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; if the walkway is blocked, the architect rule must flag it as an egress/access problem.

a tall floor lamp (over 1.4 m) must not.rule: A tall floor lamp (over 1.4 m) must not be placed in front of a window whose sill is below 0.90 m; the architect rule must flag any furniture that blocks the window's sightline or light.

a kitchen must include a fridge as part.rule: A kitchen must include a fridge as part of its functional set; if the kitchen has no fridge, the architect rule must flag it as a missing fixture.

a toilet must have at least 0.38 m of cl.rule: A toilet must have at least 0.38 m of clear space from the side wall or adjacent fixture; if the clearance is less, the architect rule must flag it as a fit problem.

a sofa's front use zone must be free of.rule: A sofa's front use zone must be free of blocking furniture; if a piece blocks the sofa's viewing or access zone, the architect rule must flag it as a layout problem.

a bedroom window must be dressed with cu.rule: A bedroom window must be dressed with curtains or blinds as part of the room's decor set; if the window is bare, the decor stage must add the missing window treatment.

a dining table and its chairs must not o.rule: A dining table and its chairs must not overlap by more than 0.010 m; if the chair cuts into the table by more than tolerance, the furniture stage must re-seat the chair or resize the table.

a living room's seating group (sofa, arm.rule: A living room's seating group (sofa, armchairs) must be dressed with soft layers (cushions, throws) and a rug to match the reference's layered look; bare furniture is not acceptable in a furnished render.

a dining table model must have a finishe.rule: A dining table model must have a finished, textured surface (wood grain, detail) that matches the room's style; a plain, untextured slab is not acceptable.

dining chairs must be a coherent, curate.rule: Dining chairs must be a coherent, curated set that matches the room's style; generic, repetitive, mass-produced models are not acceptable.

a room's render must present a cohesive,.rule: A room's render must present a cohesive, warm, layered look (rugs, throws, cohesive lighting) that matches the reference; a chaotic mishmash of styles is not acceptable.

a coffee table must be sized and positio.rule: A coffee table must be sized and positioned to function as the anchor of the seating group; a small table floating in open space that blocks the view is not acceptable.

a large, textured rug must anchor the li.rule: A large, textured rug must anchor the living area; bare wood flooring throughout is not acceptable in a furnished render.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main functional group (tub, toilet, washbasin) with a wide enough lens to show the ceiling and floor; a tight, low-angle crop of a corner is not acceptable.

a bathroom washbasin must be a modern, c.rule: A bathroom washbasin must be a modern, clean-lined model that matches the room's style; an ornate, bronze-colored grille is not acceptable.

a bathroom render must present a sophist.rule: A bathroom render must present a sophisticated, modern aesthetic that matches the reference; a stark, unfinished utility space with a decorative grille that looks like a prison bar is not acceptable.

a window in a modern bathroom must have.rule: A window in a modern bathroom must have a clean, modern frame or glazing; a heavy, ornate metal grille that looks like a security gate is not acceptable.

a bathroom render must present a sophist.rule: A bathroom render must present a sophisticated, modern aesthetic that matches the reference; a kitchen-style utility sink and a bizarre, oversized mirror are not acceptable.

a bathroom must be lit with layered, war.rule: A bathroom must be lit with layered, warm lighting (spotlights, cove lighting) to create the mood in the reference; flat, shadowless light is not acceptable.

a nightstand must be a modern, clean-lin.rule: A nightstand must be a modern, clean-lined model that matches the bed's style; a mid-century modern model with ornate inlay is not acceptable in a minimalist room.

a bedroom render must present a warm, la.rule: A bedroom render must present a warm, layered style (curtains, art, lamps, styled surfaces) that matches the reference; a bare grey-box with a blank white slab bed and dark block wardrobe is not acceptable.

a nightstand must be a modern, clean-lin.rule: A nightstand must be a modern, clean-lined model that matches the bed's style; a rustic, distressed model is not acceptable in a minimalist room.

a hall/entry must have warm layered ligh.rule: A hall/entry must have warm layered lighting (sconce or pendant); flat grey light is not acceptable in a finished render.

a desk in a bedroom or study must be sty.rule: A desk in a bedroom or study must be styled with a lamp and small decor; a bare desk surface is not acceptable in a furnished render.

a bed must be styled with a textured thr.rule: A bed must be styled with a textured throw and layered bedding; a bare sheet and two pillows is not acceptable in a furnished render.

a bedroom with large windows must have c.rule: A bedroom with large windows must have curtains or soft window treatments; bare windows are not acceptable in a furnished render.

bathroom wet surfaces must be finished w.rule: Bathroom wet surfaces must be finished with the project's tile/stone palette (e.g. large porcelain or zellige on walls, matching stone or tile on the floor); flat untextured grey is not acceptable in a furnished render.

interior rooms must have warm, layered l.rule: Interior rooms must have warm, layered lighting (e.g. floor lamps, wall sconces, or warm ambient) in the render; flat, dim, or cold single-source lighting is not acceptable.

living and leisure rooms must have warm,.rule: Living and leisure rooms must have warm, layered lighting (e.g. floor lamps, table lamps, or warm ambient) in the render; a single flat ceiling light is not acceptable.

outdoor furniture on a balcony or terrac.rule: Outdoor furniture on a balcony or terrace must be a coherent set (matching table and chairs) in a style and material that coordinates with the house's exterior palette; a single dated or mismatched piece is not acceptable.

paired outdoor furniture (chairs, tables.rule: Paired outdoor furniture (chairs, tables) must use the same model and finish; mismatched chairs or a plain box table are not acceptable on a finished terrace.

exterior renders must use photorealistic.rule: Exterior renders must use photorealistic materials, warm directional lighting, and textured landscaping; a flat grey-box massing study with an overcast void is not client-ready.

exterior facade views must include warm.rule: Exterior facade views must include warm interior light glowing from windows and directional sun or landscape lighting to create depth and a welcoming atmosphere; a flat grey overcast sky with no interior glow is not acceptable.

an exterior camera must frame the house.rule: An exterior camera must frame the house as a whole, showing the main facade, entrance, and roofline; a tight low-angle crop of a corner is not acceptable.
An exterior camera must frame the house as a whole, showing the main facade, entrance, and roofline; a low tight crop of a corner and blank wall is not acceptable.

exterior renders must show material rich.rule: Exterior renders must show material richness (cladding, lighting, furniture), proper landscaping, and a non-void environment; a grey-box massing study is not client-ready.

exterior renders must use textured groun.rule: Exterior renders must use textured ground, proper paving, and warm directional lighting with material richness; a raw grey-box massing study with flat green ground and bare grid paving is not client-ready.

drawn furniture in a living room that is.rule: Drawn furniture in a living room that is untyped must be typed to a plausible type (e.g., sideboard, console_table) based on its size and position; leaving it untyped means nothing builds it.

decor items must rest on a valid top sur.rule: Decor items must rest on a valid top surface of their host; if no top is found, the agent must re-place the decor or adjust the host geometry.

decor throws and cushions must not penet.rule: Decor throws and cushions must not penetrate their host beyond a small tolerance; if the host shows through the cloth, the agent must adjust the placement or model.

decor cushions must not penetrate their.rule: Decor cushions must not penetrate their host beyond a small tolerance; if the penetration exceeds the limit, the agent must adjust the placement or model.

decor throws must have at least 80% of t.rule: Decor throws must have at least 80% of their footprint over the support; if less, the agent must re-place the throw.

decor cushions must have at least 80% of.rule: Decor cushions must have at least 80% of their footprint over the support; if less, the agent must re-place the cushion.

decor plants must rest on a valid top su.rule: Decor plants must rest on a valid top surface of their host; if no top is found, the agent must re-place the plant or adjust the host geometry.

decor throws must not penetrate their ho.rule: Decor throws must not penetrate their host beyond a small tolerance; if the host shows through the cloth, the agent must adjust the placement or model.

decor items that rest on a host (plant o.rule: Decor items that rest on a host (plant on a table, throw on a sofa) must be placed only on hosts whose built geometry exposes a flat, load-bearing top surface; if the host's top is not found or is recessed, the decor item must be dropped rather than forced into a non-existent surface.

soft decor items (throws, cushions) must.rule: Soft decor items (throws, cushions) must be modeled with a minimum thickness that prevents the host geometry from showing through; if the host's surface is not flat or the item's thickness is less than the host's surface irregularity, the item must be repositioned or removed.

entities on layers that are off, frozen,.rule: Entities on layers that are off, frozen, or invisible in the source DWG are intentionally excluded from the reading process and do not represent a loss of architectural information.
entities on layers that are off, frozen,.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

ole2frame and wipeout entities are non-g.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are non-geometric or masking entities that do not represent architectural elements and are correctly excluded from the reading process.

when a camera view is dropped during the.rule: When a camera view is dropped during the camera stage, the reason for its removal must be recorded in the ledger; if no reason is given, the view must be retained or the drop must be justified by a specific architectural or technical constraint.

all named blocks in the source dwg that.rule: All named blocks in the source DWG that represent architectural elements (e.g., 'bulmak' for a fixture, 'merdiven' for a stair) must be mapped to a corresponding element in the 3D model; if a block is not mapped, the reading stage must flag it for manual review or the building stage must generate a parametric element from its geometry.

blocks with names starting with 'a$c' ar.rule: Blocks with names starting with 'A$C' are typically auto-generated by CAD software for hatches, dimensions, or other non-architectural entities and do not represent physical elements that need to be mapped to the 3D model.

drawing blocks that are small symbols, t.rule: Drawing blocks that are small symbols, text frames or placeholder inserts with no architectural function must be ignored by the reading stage, not flagged as lost elements.

auto-generated blocks with the a$c prefi.rule: Auto-generated blocks with the A$C prefix are CAD annotation artifacts and must be excluded from the element ledger.

site decor elements that are recorded as.rule: Site decor elements that are recorded as site decor and not built by design must not be flagged as lost elements.

drawing blocks that represent elements a.rule: Drawing blocks that represent elements already built in the model must not be flagged as lost elements.

a drawn block whose name is not in the f.rule: A drawn block whose name is not in the furniture or fixture dictionary and whose footprint (here ~1.57 x 2.87 m) matches a built-in or storage unit must be typed as a built-in (wardrobe, tall_cabinet or sideboard) in the room it sits in, not dropped as an unrecognised insert.

a drawn block of ~0.6 m square on a floo.rule: A drawn block of ~0.6 m square on a floor plan is a small table or stool; the reading stage must type it (side_table or chair) rather than drop it as an unrecognised insert.

a drawn block of ~0.79 m square on a flo.rule: A drawn block of ~0.79 m square on a floor plan is a dining or side table; the reading stage must type it (table_dining or side_table) rather than drop it as an unrecognised insert.

entities on layers that are off or froze.rule: Entities on layers that are off or frozen in the source DWG are intentionally hidden by the architect and are not part of the active drawing set; the reading stage is correct to skip them, and this is not a loss.

ole2frame and wipeout entities are non-g.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are non-geometric annotation/occlusion objects (embedded OLE content and whiteout masks) that carry no architectural geometry; the reading stage is correct to skip them, and this is not a loss.

a reading-stage note confirming that a w.rule: A reading-stage note confirming that a wall layer was selected by strong evidence (rooms closed, strokes paired) is informational, not a loss; columns that stand out of the wall bands are structural elements handled by the structure pass, not furniture to be built.

a drawn symbol that both reading passes.rule: A drawn symbol that both reading passes classify as not_furniture and that is kept as an obstacle is a deliberate, recorded decision; it is not a lost element and needs no build.

a drawn element on a structural layer (e.rule: A drawn element on a structural layer (e.g. 'A-BA') that is a column is structure, not furniture; it is correctly excluded from the furniture build and handled by the structure pass, so this is not a loss.

a drawn element that is 60% or more insi.rule: A drawn element that is 60% or more inside an already-built fixture of the same kind is a duplicate drawing (or a part) of that fixture; it is correctly not built a second time, so this is not a loss.

when a drawn symbol is 60% or more insid.rule: When a drawn symbol is 60% or more inside another symbol of the same type, it is a duplicate or detail of that symbol and must not be built as a separate piece.

when a smaller drawn symbol is inside a.rule: When a smaller drawn symbol is inside a larger symbol of the same type, it is a duplicate or detail, not a second piece; only the larger symbol is built.

layers named '2d', 'ref', 'dim', or simi.rule: Layers named '2D', 'Ref', 'Dim', or similar containing only basic entities (lines, circles) are reference layers and are not used for 3D model generation.

layers containing decorative 2d patterns.rule: Layers containing decorative 2D patterns (tiles, textures) are not used for 3D geometry generation.

layers containing thin 2d annotations or.rule: Layers containing thin 2D annotations or details (like glass lines) that do not form 3D volumes are not used for 3D geometry generation.

a bench in a room typed as 'other' (like.rule: A bench in a room typed as 'other' (like a game/activity room) is likely a misread armchair or chair; retype to a seating type allowed in the room.

when a room outline contains labels for.rule: When a room outline contains labels for multiple room types (e.g., 'Salon' and 'AÇIK MUTFAK'), the reading stage must identify it as an open-plan space and either split it into sub-zones or assign the primary type while allowing fixtures from the secondary type.

a washbasin model must be fully visible.rule: A washbasin model must be fully visible and presented as a functional element in the render; if it is cut off or tiny, swap to a model with better proportions or adjust the camera.

a piece that looks like a tall cabinet i.rule: A piece that looks like a tall cabinet in the render but is typed as a fridge should be verified; if it is indeed a fridge, ensure the model is distinct from a tall cabinet.

a dining table model must match the draw.rule: A dining table model must match the drawn size within tolerance; if it differs, swap to a model with closer dimensions.

an armchair model must match the drawn s.rule: An armchair model must match the drawn size within tolerance; if it differs, swap to a model with closer dimensions.

the fitting stage must prefer a library.rule: The fitting stage must prefer a library model over a parametric mesh whenever a library model exists for the piece's type and its dimensions fall within the library's size range; a parametric mesh is only acceptable when no library model fits the piece's size and room.

the render stage must use warm ambient l.rule: The render stage must use warm ambient lighting (2700-3000K) for interior scenes to create a cozy atmosphere, matching the reference's warm glow; flat, even lighting is not acceptable for a lived-in home.

door leaves must be built as finished pr.rule: Door leaves must be built as finished products with visible hardware (handle, hinges) and a surface finish that matches the project's door material slot; a flat, untextured slab is not acceptable in a furnished render.

a conservation check must compare the fi.rule: A conservation check must compare the final stage's piece list against the final model, not against an intermediate build-stage snapshot; a piece present in the final room's piece list is not lost.

a drawn piece in a kitchen or dining zon.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen or dining zone that is small (under 0.5 m on a side) and sits at counter height in front of a kitchen island or counter must be read as a bar stool, not as a structural column, even if it is drawn on a structure layer; the build stage must not drop it as 'not furniture'.

when a room is a twin of another, the bu.rule: When a room is a twin of another, the build stage may merge the pair's identical furniture into a single built piece; the twin's duplicate record is then dropped and is not a conservation loss.
When a room is a twin of another, the build stage may merge the pair's identical fixtures into a single built piece; the twin's duplicate record is then dropped and is not a conservation loss.

when the same piece is drawn twice (one.rule: When the same piece is drawn twice (one outline nested inside the other), the build stage keeps one and drops the duplicate; the dropped record is not a conservation loss.

a piece that the final stage lists must.rule: A piece that the final stage lists must survive the build stage; if a build conflict drops a drawn fixture, the build must re-place it in a valid spot rather than delete it.

a kitchen zone label (e.g. 'açik mutfak'.rule: A kitchen zone label (e.g. 'AÇIK MUTFAK') inside a living room is an open-plan kitchen, not a misread: keep the room type as living and treat the kitchen pieces as part of the living room's program; do not raise an unhandled zone-label warning.

when a plan labels a room as a terrace o.rule: When a plan labels a room as a terrace or balcony on the top floor and a door leads to it, the roof build stage must cut an opening in the roof over that room to create the outdoor space; a closed roof over a labeled terrace is a build error.

when a door on the top floor under a slo.rule: When a door on the top floor under a sloped roof has its head above the roof underside, the reading stage must flag it as requiring a dormer or a roof modification; a door clipped under the roof is not a usable door and must not be built as-is.

a site area the documents label and draw.rule: A site area the documents label and draw (pool, terrace, parking) must be built as a site element; 'no outline' is a loss, not a valid reason.

a labelled outdoor area (terrace/sunbath.rule: A labelled outdoor area (terrace/sunbathing) in the documents must be built; dropping it as 'no outline' loses drawn content.

a labelled parking area in the documents.rule: A labelled parking area in the documents must be built as a site element; 'no outline' is a loss.

every open-sided stair must be built wit.rule: Every open-sided stair must be built with a guard/railing on the open side; a bare open stair is a safety defect.

a kitchen must keep at least 0.90 m of a.rule: A kitchen must keep at least 0.90 m of aisle in front of the counter and a counter top at working height; a tighter or higher run is a fit failure.

a stove must be a real appliance model f.rule: A stove must be a real appliance model flush to its wall; a crude box floating off the wall is a model failure.

a grille or screen in a window slot is a.rule: A grille or screen in a window slot is a window treatment, not a door; the read stage must not type it as a door.

a door whose height is not drawn must be.rule: A door whose height is not drawn must be flagged for review, not silently built at an assumed height.

site pools and platforms drawn in the pl.rule: Site pools and platforms drawn in the plan must be built as 3D elements (water volume, coping, deck) when the site area is labelled.

labelled outdoor terraces and sunbathing.rule: Labelled outdoor terraces and sunbathing areas must be built as raised decks or paved platforms.

labelled parking areas must be built as.rule: Labelled parking areas must be built as paved surfaces with parking lines.

when the site plan draws a pool or a sun.rule: When the site plan draws a pool or a sunning terrace, the site stage must build them as site areas with their paving and furniture, not leave them as 'NOT built'.

a large room on the top floor of a house.rule: A large room on the top floor of a house that is labelled as a relaxation or activity room and has no other function should be typed as a bedroom, not 'other'.

a shoe cabinet should only be placed at.rule: A shoe cabinet should only be placed at the entrance hall (ground floor), not in a top floor hall.

built-in kitchen appliances (stove, frid.rule: Built-in kitchen appliances (stove, fridge, oven) that are part of a kitchen counter run must be rendered as visible objects in the scene, even if they are integrated into the counter module. The build stage should not skip them as 'built_in' without providing a visible representation.

furniture strokes on the 'tefriş' layer.rule: Furniture strokes on the 'tefriş' layer that form recognizable shapes (sofa, chairs, table) must be read as furniture pieces even if they are not explicitly labeled. The reading stage should use shape recognition to identify common furniture items from stroke patterns.

a bathroom set is incomplete without a m.rule: A bathroom set is incomplete without a mirror over its washbasin; the set's completeness check must list a mirror as a required partner of the basin, not only the basin, toilet and tub.

a room under 3 m2 with no door of its ow.rule: A room under 3 m2 with no door of its own and no fixtures is a passage or shaft, not a room; the reading must type it hall or shaft, not 'other', and the model must not build it as an enclosed room.

a kitchen run is not assembled until its.rule: A kitchen run is not assembled until its sink, hob and worktop are visible as a working set; the group's completeness check must verify the sink and stove are fitted to the counter, not only present in the piece list.

a salon with a dining zone in its progra.rule: A salon with a dining zone in its program must have its dining set (table and chairs) placed as a coherent group; the reading must not merge the dining zone label into the living room without placing the dining furniture.

a children's room with one child must ha.rule: A children's room with one child must have one bed, not two; a second double bed in a single-child room is a misread and must be retyped to a single bed or removed.

a small interior room (under 4 m2) with.rule: A small interior room (under 4 m2) with a shoe cabinet and no entrance door is a storage or utility space, not a hall; the reading must type it storage, not hall.

a veranda or balcony drawn in the plans.rule: A veranda or balcony drawn in the plans must be built as a distinct site area with a floor, posts and railing; the site stage must not skip it because it has no outline in the model data.

a balcony drawn in the plans must be bui.rule: A balcony drawn in the plans must be built as a distinct site area with a floor and railing; the site stage must not skip it because it has no outline in the model data.

the building's coordinate frame must be.rule: The building's coordinate frame must be anchored to the sheets' outline corner, not to the outer wall faces of a reference region; the reading stage must re-anchor the frame so that all regions and coordinates are consistent with the sheets.

the ground floor's level mark in the sec.rule: The ground floor's level mark in the section must be read as the building's z=0, not as +0.50; the reading stage must re-baseline the level frame so that all relative marks are correct.

a zone label (e.g. 'yemek bölümü') insid.rule: A zone label (e.g. 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ') inside a room is a sub-zone of that room, not a second room; the reading must not treat it as a separate label that causes a 'more labels' warning.

a door whose approach is blocked by furn.rule: A door whose approach is blocked by furniture (no free passage) is a misread; the reading must check the approach and re-read it as a window if it is not a passage.

a gap in the outer wall whose approach i.rule: A gap in the outer wall whose approach is blocked by furniture (no free passage) is a misread; the reading must check the approach and re-read it as a window if it is not a passage.

a warning that an opening is 'no passage.rule: A warning that an opening is 'no passage' because furniture blocks its approach is a fit finding, not a reading error; do not apply door_to_window to an opening already read as a window.

a wide outer-wall opening (>= 1.5 m) in.rule: A wide outer-wall opening (>= 1.5 m) in a bedroom or living room that is blocked by furniture and has no clear passage function should be read as a window, not a door.

a narrow outer-wall opening (< 0.80 m) t.rule: A narrow outer-wall opening (< 0.80 m) that is completely blocked by furniture and has no passage function should be read as a window, not a door.

a wide outer-wall opening (>= 1.5 m) in.rule: A wide outer-wall opening (>= 1.5 m) in a bedroom that is blocked by furniture and has no clear passage function should be read as a window, not a door.

furniture must not cover or block window.rule: Furniture must not cover or block windows; if a piece is placed in front of a window, it should be moved to a free spot in the room.

if the big loop stops with 0 cycles and.rule: If the big loop stops with 0 cycles and a low score, the agent should be given another round to attempt improvements.

if multiple views are marked for review,.rule: If multiple views are marked for review, the agent should be given another round to address them.

when a dining group cannot be placed in.rule: When a dining group cannot be placed in a living room due to walkway constraints from a door, the solver should allow placement in a corner or along a wall that does not block the walkway, or the door position should be adjusted if it is a reading error.

when a kitchen run is missing essential.rule: When a kitchen run is missing essential appliances (fridge, hob), the solver should add them to the run if there is space, or the room layout should be adjusted to accommodate them.

when a bed blocks a door and cannot be m.rule: When a bed blocks a door and cannot be moved due to overlap or room constraints, the door position should be adjusted if it is a reading error, or the bed should be resized to a smaller model that fits.

dressing rooms should have a styled floo.rule: Dressing rooms should have a styled floor (rug) and baseboards to match the project's style.

outdoor views should have a believable e.rule: Outdoor views should have a believable environment, not low-poly placeholders.

child's bedrooms should have playful dec.rule: Child's bedrooms should have playful decor (bunk bed, climbing equipment, colorful mural) to match the reference.

bathroom renders should have warm wood,.rule: Bathroom renders should have warm wood, textured stone, and functional styling (mirror, towel rail) to match the project's style.

a bathroom set (bathroom_set group) must.rule: A bathroom set (bathroom_set group) must always include a mirror over the washbasin; the set is incomplete without it.

a kitchen or dining room with a referenc.rule: A kitchen or dining room with a reference style that includes wall art must have at least one wall art piece placed on a visible wall.

a kitchen island or counter that is a st.rule: A kitchen island or counter that is a standalone piece (not part of a kitchen_run with sink/stove) must have a sink or cooktop fixture on its worktop to look functional.

a living room with a reference style tha.rule: A living room with a reference style that includes plants must have at least one potted_plant placed in a visible corner or beside the seating group.

a room's furniture must be one coherent.rule: A room's furniture must be one coherent set: the agent picks models from a single style family and adds the soft styling layers (textiles, decor) the reference shows, so a room never reads as a catalog of clashing pieces.

a dining table's base must be a finished.rule: A dining table's base must be a finished, coherent model that matches the room's style, never a low-poly placeholder that reads as a rendering error.

a bathroom's main camera must frame the.rule: A bathroom's main camera must frame the room's main pieces (basin, toilet, bath/shower), not a bare corner.

a bathroom's styling set includes a mirr.rule: A bathroom's styling set includes a mirror over the basin plus the soft layers (towels, decor, warm light); the agent adds them when the reference shows them.

a room's furniture and styling must matc.rule: A room's furniture and styling must match its named brief (a children's room is playful and layered, not a generic adult bedroom); the agent restyles when the render misses the brief.

every furnished room gets its styled sur.rule: Every furnished room gets its styled surfaces (rug, art, cushions, small objects on surfaces); the agent adds them so no room reads as a bare shell.

a room's furniture must be one coherent.rule: A room's furniture must be one coherent set: a desk's model must coordinate with the bed, dresser and wardrobe, not an off-style industrial piece.

furniture surfaces in a client-ready ren.rule: Furniture surfaces in a client-ready render are styled with small objects (books, decor, a lamp); the agent adds them so no surface reads as bare.

a room's furniture must match its named.rule: A room's furniture must match its named brief; a children's room is furnished as a children's room (playful, multi-level), not as a generic adult bedroom.

a bedroom holds one coherent bed set; th.rule: A bedroom holds one coherent bed set; the agent resolves duplicate or mismatched beds and styles the room to its brief.

a bedroom holds one coherent bed set; a.rule: A bedroom holds one coherent bed set; a second, differently-styled bed in the same room is a mismatched set the agent must resolve.

a room's palette and styling must match.rule: A room's palette and styling must match its named brief; a children's room is colorful and playful, not sterile adult neutrals.

a bathroom's main camera must frame the.rule: A bathroom's main camera must frame the room's main pieces (shower, toilet, basin), not a blank wall or corner.

a camera's focus must be the room's main.rule: A camera's focus must be the room's main group, not a blank wall with the main piece cut off.

a wet room's lighting is warm and ambien.rule: A wet room's lighting is warm and ambient, not flat clinical white; the agent sets the lighting to match the reference.

a room's lighting fixtures must fit its.rule: A room's lighting fixtures must fit its palette and provide warm ambient light; a loud artificial object that clashes with the scheme is restyled by the agent.

the furniture library must include organ.rule: The furniture library must include organic/boho armchair models (rattan, boucle, curved wood) so that a room styled organic/boho is not forced to take a mid-century modern piece; a style tag that is not present in the library must not be assigned to a room.

exterior presentation views must be rend.rule: Exterior presentation views must be rendered with the project's facade materials, roof detailing, and site landscaping applied, not as a grey-box massing study.

exterior renders must include exterior l.rule: Exterior renders must include exterior lighting (bollards, architectural lights) to match the reference standard; a completely dark exterior is not client-ready.

exterior renders must include designed l.rule: Exterior renders must include designed landscaping (planters, paths, hardscape) rather than a flat, untextured green ground plane.

exterior facade renders must show rich m.rule: Exterior facade renders must show rich material contrast (timber, stone, dark metal) and a designed entrance, not a flat white box.

exterior cameras must be at eye level (1.rule: Exterior cameras must be at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or above the ridge, never a top-down aerial that crops the house to a fragment of roof.

exterior renders must convey the project.rule: Exterior renders must convey the project's style (modern, warm, layered) with proper materiality and landscape, not as a grey-box massing study with crude lollipop trees.

the house's entrance door must be a libr.rule: The house's entrance door must be a library entrance door (statement door), not a generic door; the build stage must assign the correct door family by role.

decor items that cannot rest on their ho.rule: Decor items that cannot rest on their host due to minor penetration (host pokes through cloth) are acceptable to leave unbuilt if the penetration is small and the decor is not critical to the room's function.

decor items (cushions) that cannot rest.rule: Decor items (cushions) that cannot rest on their host due to angle-dependent penetration are acceptable to leave unbuilt if the penetration is small and the decor is not critical to the room's function.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece (e.g., a bed) but is named by an AI pass as a distinct type (e.g., floor_lamp) that fits its size should be built as that type, not left out as a detail.

the reading stage must read all entity t.rule: The reading stage must read all entity types in the source DWG file, including ATTDEF (attribute definitions), to ensure no data is lost.

site decor items read outside the walls.rule: Site decor items read outside the walls of a level (e.g., L1) that repeat the ground plan's symbols at the same place should be used for the ground floor (L0) site, not left unused.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms (e.g., 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ'), the reading stage must split the room into two distinct rooms, not treat the second label as a duplicate.

printed area labels (e.g., '9,00 m²' of.rule: Printed area labels (e.g., '9,00 m²' of 'HOL' on L1) must be used for area checks of the corresponding space, not left unused.

when walls are drawn as face lines, the.rule: When walls are drawn as face lines, the reading stage must use all wall primitives, not just those on the chosen layer (e.g., 'SIVA'), to ensure no walls are left out.

site decor read on an upper level that d.rule: Site decor read on an upper level that duplicates the ground-floor plan at the same coordinates is a reading artifact, not a missing site element; the site stage takes the ground-floor set.

a drawing layer of pure line entities th.rule: A drawing layer of pure line entities that no stage uses and no warning names is a reading artifact, not a missing model element.

a drawn bookshelf that is not built beca.rule: A drawn bookshelf that is not built because its assigned model is unusable is rebuilt by swapping to a library model of the same type and size.

a drawn potted plant that is not built b.rule: A drawn potted plant that is not built because its assigned model was removed by audit is rebuilt by swapping to a real library model of the same type (never a generated model when a real product fits).

a drawn dining table that is not built b.rule: A drawn dining table that is not built because its assigned model fails the fit rules is rebuilt by swapping to a library model of the same type that passes the fit rules.

a drawn chair that is not built because.rule: A drawn chair that is not built because its assigned model is unusable is rebuilt by swapping to a library model of the same type and size.

a drawn shoe cabinet in a hall that is n.rule: A drawn shoe cabinet in a hall that is not built is rebuilt by the furniture agent fitting a library shoe cabinet of the drawn size.

a drawn desk that is not built because i.rule: A drawn desk that is not built because its assigned model is unusable is rebuilt by swapping to a library model of the same type and size.

a drawn office chair that is not built b.rule: A drawn office chair that is not built because its assigned model is unusable is rebuilt by swapping to a library model of the same type and size.

a drawn desk in a room that is not built.rule: A drawn desk in a room that is not built is rebuilt by the furniture agent fitting a library desk of the drawn size.

a drawn console table that is not built.rule: A drawn console table that is not built because its assigned model is unusable is rebuilt by swapping to a library model of the same type and size.

a drawn piece in a bedroom that is 4.64.rule: A drawn piece in a bedroom that is 4.64 m long and 0.68 m deep and typed 'unknown' is a misread of a built-in wall unit or long low cabinet; the reading stage should type it from its size and room context, or the building stage should treat it as a wall element, not a furniture item.

a drawn piece in a hall that is 0.50 m l.rule: A drawn piece in a hall that is 0.50 m long and 0.12 m deep and typed 'unknown' is a misread of a small wall element (e.g. a coat hook, a small shelf, or a door stop); the reading stage should type it from its size and room context, or the building stage should treat it as a wall element, not a furniture item.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading stage should detect the internal wall that separates the two labelled spaces and split the room outline accordingly, rather than keeping the larger label and losing the smaller room.

when no library model of a building's wi.rule: When no library model of a building's window or door family fits an opening's dimensions, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct fallback and is not a defect.

when no library model of a building's do.rule: When no library model of a building's door family fits an opening's configuration (e.g., double leaf), the parametric door in the style's finish is the correct fallback and is not a defect.

when a fixture is built with a parametri.rule: When a fixture is built with a parametric mesh due to a library gap, and a suitable library model exists that fits the drawn size and room, the fitting stage should select the library model to ensure higher quality and consistency.

when a piece is built with a parametric.rule: When a piece is built with a parametric mesh due to a library gap, and a suitable library model exists that fits the drawn size and room, the fitting stage should select the library model to ensure higher quality and consistency.

the furniture agent should ensure that l.rule: The furniture agent should ensure that large blank walls in living areas are styled with art or other decor to create a layered, inhabited look, as expected in photorealistic renders.

the furniture agent should ensure that k.rule: The furniture agent should ensure that key surfaces like coffee tables are styled with small decor objects to make the space feel inhabited and complete.

the furniture agent should ensure that w.rule: The furniture agent should ensure that windows are treated with curtains or other softening elements to match the project's style and create a cohesive look.

when a piece's style clashes with the ro.rule: When a piece's style clashes with the room's atmosphere, the fitting stage should select a library model that better matches the project's style and reference.

the furniture agent should ensure that b.rule: The furniture agent should ensure that beds are dressed with layered, textured bedding to match the project's style and create a cohesive, inhabited look.

a nightstand (or any small side table) i.rule: A nightstand (or any small side table) is complete on its own; do not flag a missing decorative object on it as a defect.

interior doors must carry a finished, te.rule: Interior doors must carry a finished, textured wood look that matches the project's reference style, never a plain untextured panel.

the main entrance must be defined with a.rule: The main entrance must be defined with an approach (steps or a ramp) and a focal point, not left as a bare door in a wall.

every exterior door that is an entry mus.rule: Every exterior door that is an entry must be framed with an approach (steps or a ramp), not left as a bare door.

a room's camera must frame the room's ma.rule: A room's camera must frame the room's main piece; a view that shows an empty corner while the room's anchor piece is out of frame is a defect.

a drawn desk that the decor stage placed.rule: A drawn desk that the decor stage placed must survive the agent stage; dropping it is a loss, not a choice.

an opening read from the drawing (with e.rule: An opening read from the drawing (with evidence) must be built; dropping it in the build stage is a loss.

structural grid bubbles (axis labels) on.rule: Structural grid bubbles (axis labels) on the 'AKS YAZI' layer are drawing annotations and are correctly not built.

decor items drawn on a host piece that i.rule: Decor items drawn on a host piece that is itself not built are correctly not built.

a cushion, pillow or detail drawn on a p.rule: A cushion, pillow or detail drawn on a piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own, and is correctly not built separately.

decor that would stand in front of a win.rule: Decor that would stand in front of a window and reach over its sill, or that has no free spot on the worktop, is correctly not built.

structural grid bubbles (axis labels) on.rule: Structural grid bubbles (axis labels) on the 'AKS' layer are drawing annotations and are correctly not built.

columns drawn on the 'kolon' layer are s.rule: Columns drawn on the 'KOLON' layer are structural annotations and are correctly not built as furniture.

level mark symbols on the 'kot' layer ar.rule: Level mark symbols on the 'kot' layer are drawing annotations and are correctly not built.

an exterior label whose surface is alrea.rule: An exterior label whose surface is already built from site.paving / parking / grass is correctly not built as a separate element.

every outdoor space named in the documen.rule: Every outdoor space named in the documents (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be given a built outline (floor slab and edge) at the site stage, even when it is not a labelled room, so that its drawn edges, steps and guard can be built and attached.

when a drawn furniture label (e.g., 'sif.rule: When a drawn furniture label (e.g., 'SIFONIYER') is present in the documents but no corresponding piece is built, and the nearest valid placement is more than 1 m from the label, the system should either (a) place the piece at the nearest valid location and flag the discrepancy for architect review, or (b) omit the piece and flag the label as unfulfilled. The current behavior of silently omitting the piece without a clear flag is not acceptable.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) must be.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) must be furnished with its defining set (bench, full-length mirror, open storage or hanger rail); a lone wardrobe is not a dressing room and the room's program must be completed, not just re-modelled.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's layout and its main pieces, not be pressed against a door leaf or furniture edge at a low angle.

an exterior view must frame the main fac.rule: An exterior view must frame the main facade, entrance and the house's scale at eye level (1.5-1.7 m), not a corner of the roof and a hedge from too high and too far.

a scene check failure (s2) on a level me.rule: A scene check failure (S2) on a level means the build stage left a geometry inconsistency; the build stage must be re-run for that level.

a scene check failure (s3) on a level me.rule: A scene check failure (S3) on a level means the build stage left a geometry inconsistency; the build stage must be re-run for that level.

a furniture piece present in the decor s.rule: A furniture piece present in the decor stage must not be silently dropped by the agent stage; if the agent removes or moves it, the record must name it.

a stove that is built into a kitchen cou.rule: A stove that is built into a kitchen counter run (a hob in the worktop) is part of the counter module and does not need a separate scene object; the conservation check must not flag it as missing.

a fridge that is built into a kitchen co.rule: A fridge that is built into a kitchen counter run (an integrated fridge in the run's fronts) is part of the counter module and does not need a separate scene object; the conservation check must not flag it as missing.

an exterior view that must show a window.rule: An exterior view that must show a window must frame the facade section containing that window; the camera position and target must be chosen so the window is in frame.

drawings on the furniture layer ('tefriş.rule: Drawings on the furniture layer ('tefriş') that depict a sofa or chairs around a table must be read as furniture pieces (sofa, chairs, table) and placed in the model; strokes on the furniture layer that no piece uses are lost furniture.

when the documents name a space (e.g. 'a.rule: When the documents name a space (e.g. 'ANTRE') that is a second label of an existing room outline, the reading stage must split the room outline into two rooms if the documents show a wall or clear boundary between them; otherwise the space is lost.

a piece named in the documents (e.g. '*s.rule: A piece named in the documents (e.g. '*SIFONIYER' for a dresser) must be placed in the model at or near its named location; the furniture agent must add it if the reading did not.

a kitchen counter shown in the plan must.rule: A kitchen counter shown in the plan must be built in the model; if the kitchen run is incomplete, the furniture agent must complete it with the missing counter segments.

a drawn kitchen counter that the fit sta.rule: A drawn kitchen counter that the fit stage left unbuilt because it cut a neighbour is a loss of a drawn element: the kitchen run is re-solved as one unit around its drawn anchor so the counter is built, not dropped.

a standard bedroom-set piece (nightstand.rule: A standard bedroom-set piece (nightstand) that is left unbuilt because it cuts a neighbour is a loss of a drawn element: the sleeping group is re-solved as one unit around its drawn anchor so the nightstand is built, not dropped for a spatial conflict.

a decoration whose host piece is not bui.rule: A decoration whose host piece is not built is a cascading loss: the build stage must either build the host (re-solving its group) or explicitly remove the decoration, never leave it dangling as 'not built'.

a labelled outdoor space (veranda, balco.rule: A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a bounded site area with its own floor and guard, not left as ad-hoc geometry with no outline.

a room's main group (dining table and it.rule: A room's main group (dining table and its chairs) must be visible in at least one of the room's cameras; a camera that frames the room but misses its main group is a camera failure, not a model failure.

a room's main piece (a hall's console ta.rule: A room's main piece (a hall's console table) must be visible in at least one of the room's cameras; a camera that frames the room but misses its main piece is a camera failure, not a model failure.

a ray through a window opening must not.rule: A ray through a window opening must not hit furniture: the build stage must clear any piece that blocks the way through an opening.

a bathroom washbasin must be part of a c.rule: A bathroom washbasin must be part of a complete bathroom set (basin, mirror, vanity or at least a mirror above it); a bare bowl with no mirror is a fundamental design failure.

a bathroom's washbasin must be visible i.rule: A bathroom's washbasin must be visible in at least one of the room's cameras; a camera that frames the bathroom but misses the basin is a camera failure, not a model failure.

a bathroom washbasin must be part of a c.rule: A bathroom washbasin must be part of a complete bathroom set (basin, mirror, vanity or at least a mirror above it); a basin with no mirror over it is a fundamental design failure.

a small enclosed room (under 3 m2) with.rule: A small enclosed room (under 3 m2) with no function, no pieces and no door of its own is most likely a misread: it is a hall or passage, not a room of its own, and must be typed accordingly.

a sliding door read from lines in an out.rule: A sliding door read from lines in an outer wall that is blocked by furniture across its approach and has no outside destination is a misread window: convert it to a window at the floor's sill.

a gap in an outer wall that is blocked b.rule: A gap in an outer wall that is blocked by furniture across its approach and has no outside destination is a misread window: convert it to a window at the floor's sill.

furniture that covers a window opening m.rule: Furniture that covers a window opening must be moved to a free place in its room, clear of the opening.

views marked for review must be re-evalu.rule: Views marked for review must be re-evaluated in the next agent round after fixes are applied.

when a room's dining set is drawn but th.rule: When a room's dining set is drawn but the solver cannot place it due to walkway constraints from doors, the drawn pieces should be kept as drawn and the walkway constraint should be relaxed for the dining zone, or the dining table should be moved to a position that satisfies both the walkway and the room's program.

when a kitchen's run is drawn but the so.rule: When a kitchen's run is drawn but the solver cannot complete it due to missing appliances (fridge, hob), the drawn kitchen run should be kept as drawn and the missing appliances should be added as separate pieces, or the kitchen run should be re-solved with the missing appliances included.

when a bed_double blocks a door and cann.rule: When a bed_double blocks a door and cannot be moved due to overlap or plausibility constraints, the bed should be swapped for a smaller model (bed_single or a smaller bed_double) that fits the room and does not block the door, or the door should be moved to a different wall.

every room must have a visible floor fin.rule: Every room must have a visible floor finish that matches the project's style.

the outdoor view through windows must sh.rule: The outdoor view through windows must show a believable environment with trees, ground cover, and site elements, not a low-poly placeholder.

a child's room must have wall art (mural.rule: A child's room must have wall art (murals, posters, or art) to match the reference style.

bathroom renders must show warm wood, te.rule: Bathroom renders must show warm wood, textured stone, and functional styling (mirror, towel rail) to match the project's style.

a bathroom must have a mirror over the b.rule: A bathroom must have a mirror over the basin to match the reference style.

a bathtub's model must match the project.rule: A bathtub's model must match the project's light, minimalist aesthetic.

bathroom renders must show warm wood tex.rule: Bathroom renders must show warm wood textures, a vanity unit, a mirror, and a towel rail to match the project's style.

kitchen renders must show styling and 'l.rule: Kitchen renders must show styling and 'lived-in' layers to match the reference, not a raw architectural model.

a room typed as a child's room must be f.rule: A room typed as a child's room must be furnished with a cohesive, age-appropriate set (playful, warm, child-sized); a generic adult office or minimalist set is a mismatch that the furniture agent must resolve by swapping the models to a matching style.

a render of a child's room must show a p.rule: A render of a child's room must show a playful, warm, child-appropriate interior; a generic adult bedroom is a failure of the furniture set, not the camera.

a modern white office chair is not a val.rule: A modern white office chair is not a valid piece for a child's bedroom; the furniture agent must replace it with a child-appropriate chair that matches the room's style.

a minimalist white-framed office desk is.rule: A minimalist white-framed office desk is not a valid piece for a child's bedroom; the furniture agent must replace it with a child-appropriate desk that matches the room's style.
