a render of a child's room must show a p.rule: A render of a child's room must show a playful, warm, child-appropriate interior; a cluttered adult bedroom with clashing furniture is a failure of the furniture set.

an interior camera must be placed at a f.rule: An interior camera must be placed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main functional group; a camera pressed against a wall showing a bare corner is a bad camera.

a nightstand in a master bedroom must ma.rule: A nightstand in a master bedroom must match the room's warm, organic style; a loud, artificial object (e.g. a neon lamp) that clashes with the natural wood and neutral palette is a mismatch.

an armchair in a master bedroom must mat.rule: An armchair in a master bedroom must match the room's organic, boho style; a mid-century modern piece that clashes with the natural wood elements is a mismatch.

a render of a master bedroom must show a.rule: A render of a master bedroom must show a warm, organic, and layered interior; a sterile, unfinished shell with clashing surfaces is a failure of the furniture and material set.

a master bedroom must be lit with warm,.rule: A master bedroom must be lit with warm, cozy light; a flat, cool ambient light that feels like a hospital ward is a failure of the lighting and material set.

a render of a hall must show a warm, tex.rule: A render of a hall must show a warm, textured, and functionally styled interior; a bare, empty shell with no console table or decor is a failure of the furniture and material set.

a hall must have styled surfaces (consol.rule: A hall must have styled surfaces (console table, decor, and a rug); a bare, empty corner with no styling is a failure of the furniture and material set.

an interior camera must be placed at a f.rule: An interior camera must be placed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main functional group; a camera pressed against a door leaf is a bad camera.

a storage room must have styled surfaces.rule: A storage room must have styled surfaces (hanging clothes, a mirror, etc.); a bare, empty corner with no styling is a failure of the furniture and material set.

a bedroom under 12 m2 that the solver ca.rule: A bedroom under 12 m2 that the solver cannot relayout still gets one potted_plant in a corner the solver leaves free, so the room is never rendered bare.

when the current bed model is a blocky p.rule: When the current bed model is a blocky placeholder and a generated model of the same type and style is available, swap to the generated model rather than leaving the placeholder.

a bedroom render that shows only blocky.rule: A bedroom render that shows only blocky furniture and flat walls is a fit failure: the furniture agent must add at least one plant, one textile and one wall item before the view is scored.

an interior camera that frames only a do.rule: An interior camera that frames only a door and a fixture edge is a camera failure: the camera must be moved to a free point that shows the room's main pieces, not a fragment.

a dressing room with only a wardrobe is.rule: A dressing room with only a wardrobe is missing its program: the furniture agent must add a mirror, a bench and wall art so the room reads as a dressing room, not a storage closet.

a room whose walls are completely bare i.rule: A room whose walls are completely bare in the render is missing the wall-art layer: the furniture agent must add at least one framed piece on a free wall span.

an interior camera that frames only a wa.rule: An interior camera that frames only a wall corner and a fixture edge is a camera failure: the camera must be moved to a free point that shows the room's main pieces, not a fragment.

a facade that renders as a flat white bo.rule: A facade that renders as a flat white box is a material failure: the facade slot must carry a cladding look (wood, stone, or brick) that matches the project's reference style.

a ground-floor plinth with no planters,.rule: A ground-floor plinth with no planters, shrubs or ground cover is a site failure: the site must include planters and a hedge or fence to soften the transition to the lawn.

a facade that renders as a bare clay mod.rule: A facade that renders as a bare clay model is a material failure: the facade slot must carry a cladding look that matches the project's reference style.

a facade that renders as a flat untextur.rule: A facade that renders as a flat untextured white surface is a material failure: the facade slot must carry a cladding look that matches the project's reference style.

an exterior wall with no place to sit is.rule: An exterior wall with no place to sit is a site failure: the site must include a patio set or bench to make the exterior feel lived-in.

an exterior wall with no lanterns, wall.rule: An exterior wall with no lanterns, wall sconces or path lights is a site failure: the site must include exterior lighting to define the space at night.

a facade that renders as a grey-box mass.rule: A facade that renders as a grey-box massing study is a material failure: the facade slot must carry a cladding look that matches the project's reference style.

a house with outside doors but no librar.rule: A house with outside doors but no library entrance door is a build failure: the build stage must assign a statement entrance door model to the entrance opening.

a drawn piece the reading typed from the.rule: A drawn piece the reading typed from the plan (a chair in the salon) must be built in the model; the furniture stage must not drop a drawn piece that fits its room.
A drawn piece the reading typed from the plan (a shoe cabinet in the hall) must be built in the model; the furniture stage must not drop a drawn piece that fits its room.
A drawn piece the reading typed from the plan (a desk in the room) must be built in the model; the furniture stage must not drop a drawn piece that fits its room.
A drawn piece the reading typed from the plan (an office chair in the room) must be built in the model; the furniture stage must not drop a drawn piece that fits its room.
A drawn piece the reading typed from the plan (an unknown item in the hall) must be built in the model; the furniture stage must not drop a drawn piece that fits its room.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading must split the outline at the wall between them (a wall not read) so each label keeps its own room; the label with the largest printed area is kept only as a fallback.

a room's furniture must read as a design.rule: A room's furniture must read as a designed space, not a collection of pieces; the furniture stage must keep the room's function clear (a bedroom is not an office).

a piece must look like its type in every.rule: A piece must look like its type in every view; the fit stage must choose a model whose silhouette matches the type (a bed_double must not read as a bed_single).

a built piece must sit within 0.05 m of.rule: A built piece must sit within 0.05 m of its drawn place; the layout stage must place it at its drawn position.
A built piece must sit within 0.05 m of its drawn place and match its drawn size; the layout stage must place it at its drawn position and size.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) must con.rule: A dressing room (Soyunma Odası) must contain at least a mirror and a bench or seating in addition to a wardrobe to be functionally complete; a single wardrobe is insufficient for the room type.

when a drawn furniture label (e.g., 'sif.rule: When a drawn furniture label (e.g., 'SIFONIYER' for dresser) is present in the documents but no corresponding drawn piece is found within 1 m of the label, the system should attempt to place the furniture at the label's location if the space is free, or flag it for manual review if the space is obstructed.

elevation checks must be able to run eve.rule: Elevation checks must be able to run even if the north arrow is missing, by using the plan's orientation or a default bearing, or by flagging the missing north arrow as a critical error that blocks the check.

when a drawn section does not align one-.rule: When a drawn section does not align one-to-one with the plan (e.g., due to roof overhangs or section cuts), the check should either adjust the comparison to account for the offset or flag the misalignment for manual review.
when a drawn section does not align one-.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

elevations must have a view bearing or s.rule: Elevations must have a view bearing or side assigned to them to allow comparison with the model; if missing, the system should infer the bearing from the plan or flag the elevation as incomplete.

when an interior door is drawn as a doub.rule: When an interior door is drawn as a double and the library holds no double-leaf model, build it parametric in the style's finish and record a library_gap; do not force a single-leaf model onto a double opening.

a piece whose room is none (orphaned, no.rule: A piece whose room is None (orphaned, not assigned to a room) cannot be refitted or swapped; the fitting stage must assign every placed piece to a room before the library-quality check, or the check must skip orphaned pieces instead of flagging them.

when two interior doors in the same tigh.rule: When two interior doors in the same tight space (hall, corridor) are built from the same heavy traditional model, the fitting stage should vary at least one to a lighter or different-style model from the library to avoid a dated, repetitive look.

when an opening is read twice (duplicate.rule: When an opening is read twice (duplicate evidence) and is wide (>= 1.8 m), the build stage must build it as a single opening (or a double door) rather than dropping it; duplicate reads of the same opening should be merged, not discarded.

when a host piece is not built (e.g., re.rule: When a host piece is not built (e.g., removed or not placed), its attached decor elements should either be re-parented to a valid host or built independently if they are standalone items; the build stage should not silently drop decor just because its host is missing.

when a section prints a floor level offs.rule: When a section prints a floor level offset from the plan's 0.00 datum, treat the plan's 0.00 as the finished-floor reference and ignore the section's offset for level assignment.

small drawn pieces adjacent to level-mar.rule: Small drawn pieces adjacent to level-mark text are symbols, not furniture; move them to the symbol layer.

furniture name texts in the drawing conf.rule: Furniture name texts in the drawing confirm the presence of the named piece; no action needed if the piece is already built.

zone labels in the drawing confirm the p.rule: Zone labels in the drawing confirm the presence of the named zone; no action needed if the zone's furniture is already built.

small seat-sized pieces adjacent to a di.rule: Small seat-sized pieces adjacent to a dining table are chairs; type them by context.

when an armchair's inferred front is blo.rule: When an armchair's inferred front is blocked by a door or wall, and no alternative orientation is free, keep the inferred front.
When an armchair's inferred front is blocked and no alternative model fits, keep the inferred front.
When an armchair's inferred front is blocked and no alternative orientation is free, keep the inferred front.

when a furniture name text in the drawin.rule: When a furniture name text in the drawing names a piece that is not drawn at that location, and the nearest valid place is more than 1 m away, add the piece at the text's location if it fits the room's program, or flag it for review if it does not.

when a door in the outer wall is blocked.rule: When a door in the outer wall is blocked by a drawn piece, and the piece is not a door or a window, read the opening as a window at the floor's sill height.

an outer-wall opening whose approach is.rule: An outer-wall opening whose approach is fully blocked by a drawn counter or fixture is a window, not a door: the reading must classify it by what stands in front of it, not by its width.

a wall unit must not stand over a window.rule: A wall unit must not stand over a window; the fit must check the window's span and move the unit to a free wall span.

a piece must not cover a window; the fit.rule: A piece must not cover a window; the fit must check the window's span and move the piece to a free spot.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrac.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, terrace, balcony) in the plan must be built as a distinct site element with a floor slab and railing/outline, not left as an unrecognised open space.

a room typed as 'hall' with an area less.rule: A room typed as 'hall' with an area less than 3 m2 and no circulation function should be re-typed as 'storage' or 'other'.

stairs should not be assigned to a kitch.rule: Stairs should not be assigned to a kitchen room; they belong in a hall, stairwell, or circulation space.

a labelled veranda, terrace or balcony i.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace or balcony in the site plan must be built as a platform with its drawn outline, floor and railing, not dropped as 'no outline'.

a living room with a seating group must.rule: A living room with a seating group must include a rug under the coffee table and sofa.

a bathroom with a washbasin must include.rule: A bathroom with a washbasin must include a mirror above it.

site areas labeled as 'balkon' or 'veran.rule: Site areas labeled as 'BALKON' or 'VERANDA' in the plan must be built as functional outdoor rooms with floors, guards on open edges, and roofs where indicated, not left as unbuilt outlines.

every washbasin in a bathroom or wet roo.rule: Every washbasin in a bathroom or wet room must be paired with a mirror (over or beside it) as part of the bathroom set; a basin without a mirror is an incomplete set.

every kitchen worktop must carry a few r.rule: Every kitchen worktop must carry a few real small appliances and decor pieces (kettle, toaster/coffee machine, board, fruit bowl), placed off the hob, sink and window.

a drawn terrace/balcony site area must b.rule: A drawn terrace/balcony site area must be built as a slab with a guard before any door is allowed to open onto it; a door whose opening has no built deck is a defect.

a terrace must be built and reachable fr.rule: A terrace must be built and reachable from outside before a drawn window is promoted to a terrace door; an un-built deck with a door on it is a defect.

an upper-floor opening that reaches a te.rule: An upper-floor opening that reaches a terrace must have a built deck and a guard; an un-built deck behind a door is a fall hazard.

an outside door must open onto a built,.rule: An outside door must open onto a built, reachable deck or ground; a door whose target terrace is not built is an 'entrance to a window' defect.

every washbasin in a bathroom or kitchen.rule: Every washbasin in a bathroom or kitchen must carry a mirror mounted over or beside it; a basin left against a bare wall is incomplete.

when a site area (veranda, balcony, terr.rule: When a site area (veranda, balcony, terrace) is drawn with a roof or eaves in the plan, the building stage must construct that roof slab and its supports; a columned outdoor space without its drawn roof is a loss, not a valid omission.

outdoor-space columns must be sized to a.rule: Outdoor-space columns must be sized to a slender structural proportion (not thick piers), and any balcony/veranda drawn with an adjacent sloped roof must have that sloped roof built, not a flat slab on heavy columns.

every outside door that meets a level di.rule: Every outside door that meets a level difference must be served by a designed entrance: solid-tread steps with cheek walls and a landing (or a ramp where accessibility asks), never a bare concrete stair with a thin handrail.

every garden step must sit on its riser.rule: Every garden step must sit on its riser and the ground and be finished in the house's base stone or render with a coping; bare concrete treads in the grass are not acceptable.

each outdoor floor must carry the materi.rule: Each outdoor floor must carry the material of its use (terrace, steps, path, drive) in one language with the house's base, never one bare slab everywhere.

every outdoor room must be dressed for o.rule: Every outdoor room must be dressed for outside: no rug or carpet on its floor and only furniture made for outside (no upholstered indoor sofa or indoor table/chair).

a cushion or throw placed on a bed must.rule: A cushion or throw placed on a bed must rest on the mattress surface with no penetration; the rest stage must resolve any intersection before the run is accepted.

every wall of a level present in the fin.rule: Every wall of a level present in the final stage must be built; if a level's walls are missing, the build stage must be re-run to reconstruct them.

every door, window and opening read from.rule: Every door, window and opening read from the plan must be cut into the built walls; the build stage must not drop an opening that the reading stage placed.

every site area labelled in the document.rule: Every site area labelled in the documents (parking, terrace, pool) must be built as a modelled outdoor space; the site stage must not leave a labelled area without an outline.

every room label in the documents must b.rule: Every room label in the documents must be matched to a model room; if the model has no room at that anchor, the reading stage must add it.

when a document labels an 'open kitchen'.rule: When a document labels an 'open kitchen' or similar open-plan zone that is spatially contained within a larger labeled room (like a salon or living room), the reading stage must associate the label with the existing room rather than creating a new, overlapping room entity.

when a document labels a room that alrea.rule: When a document labels a room that already exists in the model with a very similar area and function, the reading stage must match the label to the existing room rather than flagging it as missing.

when a document labels a corridor or hal.rule: When a document labels a corridor or hall that is already represented by a larger room of the same type on the same level, the reading stage must verify if the label refers to a sub-part or a duplicate before flagging it as a missing room.

the reading stage must cross-reference t.rule: The reading stage must cross-reference the number of storeys indicated in sections and elevations with the levels extracted from plans. If a section shows a two-storey building, the model must not include more than two main storeys (excluding basements if clearly marked as such). Discrepancies must be resolved by re-evaluating the level definitions before proceeding to the build stage.

decor pieces must be checked for collisi.rule: Decor pieces must be checked for collision with the roof or ceiling. If a piece pokes through the roof, it must be removed or repositioned to fit within the clear height.

all open sides of stairs must have a saf.rule: All open sides of stairs must have a safety railing or guard. The build stage must automatically add a guard to any open side of a stair that is not enclosed by a wall.

all open sides of stair openings must ha.rule: All open sides of stair openings must have a safety railing or guard. The build stage must automatically add a guard to any open side of a stair opening that is not enclosed by a wall.

wardrobe models must be functional stora.rule: Wardrobe models must be functional storage units with doors or handles, not flat wall panels. If a model is rendered as a flat panel, it must be swapped for a functional wardrobe model.

scene checks must pass before the run is.rule: Scene checks must pass before the run is accepted. If a check fails, the build stage must be re-run to fix the geometry.

ceiling lights must be attached to the c.rule: Ceiling lights must be attached to the ceiling with a cord, rod, or canopy. If a light hangs in the air, it must be repositioned or replaced with a model that includes a hanging mechanism.

scene checks (s2) must pass on every lev.rule: Scene checks (S2) must pass on every level before the run is accepted; if a level fails, the build stage must be re-run to fix the geometry.

a seating piece must face its group; if.rule: A seating piece must face its group; if rotation cannot achieve a plausible orientation without breaking clearance, the fit stage must re-place the piece in a position where it can face the group.

a coffee table must not overlap an armch.rule: A coffee table must not overlap an armchair; if the drawn position causes a collision that cannot be resolved within the 0.3 m drawn-lock limit, the fit stage must re-place the table in a non-clashing position.

every seating piece must have a 0.60 m w.rule: Every seating piece must have a 0.60 m walkway from the nearest door to its front use zone; if the current position blocks the walkway, the fit stage must re-place the piece.

no furniture may block the sightline or.rule: No furniture may block the sightline or egress through a window opening; a floor lamp in front of a window must be moved to a position that does not obstruct the window.

a kitchen run must leave at least 0.90 m.rule: A kitchen run must leave at least 0.90 m of clear aisle in front of the counter; if the drawn run leaves less, the layout solver must shift the run or the opposing furniture to open the aisle.

a stove must sit flush against a wall or.rule: A stove must sit flush against a wall or the kitchen run; a gap of more than 5 cm behind it is a placement error the fitter must close.

an armchair in a living group must face.rule: An armchair in a living group must face the sofa within 30 degrees; if rotation alone cannot achieve this because the chair is on the wrong side of the group, the layout must reposition the chair.

a dining chair must have at least 0.81 m.rule: A dining chair must have at least 0.81 m of clearance from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; if the drawn position leaves less, the layout must shift the chair or the table.

a sofa must have its back against a wall.rule: A sofa must have its back against a wall or a solid piece; a sofa floating 2 m from any wall is a placement error the layout must correct.

A sofa must have its back against a wall or a solid piece; if the drawn position is more than 0.3 m from a wall and no wall span is free within 1.2 m, the layout must reposition the sofa to a valid wall.

a double bed must leave at least 0.60 m.rule: A double bed must leave at least 0.60 m of clearance on each side; if the current model is too wide for the room, swap to a narrower model that fits.

a nightstand must not block a window ope.rule: A nightstand must not block a window opening; if it stands in front of a window with a sill below 0.55 m, it must be moved to a position that does not obstruct the view or egress.

a wardrobe must leave at least 0.80 m of.rule: A wardrobe must leave at least 0.80 m of clearance in front of it; if the current model is too deep, swap to a shallower model that fits the room.

a wardrobe drawn against a wall in a bed.rule: A wardrobe drawn against a wall in a bedroom must be placed so its front clearance is at least 0.80 m; when the drawn position leaves less, the layout stage must shift the wardrobe along the wall or reduce its depth to a shallower model before the run is accepted.

a double bed in a bedroom must have at l.rule: A double bed in a bedroom must have at least 0.60 m free along each side; when the drawn position leaves less, the layout stage must shift the bed or choose a narrower model before the run is accepted.

kitchen wall cabinets must be built with.rule: Kitchen wall cabinets must be built with a finished, detailed model that matches the room's material palette; a low-poly grey block with a repetitive grid pattern is not acceptable.

site areas drawn in the documents (pools.rule: Site areas drawn in the documents (pools, terraces, parking) must be built in the model with their outlines and functional geometry; a 'not built (no outline)' status for a drawn site area is a site-stage failure.

pieces placed by the final stage must be.rule: Pieces placed by the final stage must be preserved by the build stage; if a piece is missing, the build stage must re-place it.

the build stage must place every piece t.rule: The build stage must place every piece the final stage lists in a room; a piece that exists in the final stage but is absent after build is a build-stage loss, not a furniture choice.

the build stage must preserve every piec.rule: The build stage must preserve every piece the final stage lists in a room; a piece that exists in the final stage but is absent after build is a build-stage loss, not a placement conflict.

the build stage must place every piece t.rule: The build stage must place every piece the final stage lists for a room; a piece that exists in the final record but has no object in the scene is a build failure, not a design choice.

a stove that is part of a kitchen run mu.rule: A stove that is part of a kitchen run must be built as a visible, separate appliance object (hob or range) on the counter; the build stage must not merge it into the counter run and leave no object for it.

a kitchen sink that is part of a counter.rule: A kitchen sink that is part of a counter run must be built as a visible, separate fixture object in the worktop; the build stage must not merge it into the counter and leave no object for it.

a planned kitchen appliance (fridge) tha.rule: A planned kitchen appliance (fridge) that is listed in the room's piece set must be placed by the build stage; if the scene has no object for it, the build stage failed to place it and must be re-run.

a stair-core room whose only camera poin.rule: A stair-core room whose only camera point falls inside the stair geometry must not be given its own interior view; the stair is shown from the adjacent hall/landing view instead, and the stair-core room is excluded from the interior camera set.

a drawn sofa whose back is not on a wall.rule: A drawn sofa whose back is not on a wall must be re-placed by the build stage onto a free wall span within its drawn tolerance; if the build stage drops it, the build stage must be re-run to place it.

a drawn floor lamp that is listed in the.rule: A drawn floor lamp that is listed in the room's piece set must be placed by the build stage; if the build stage drops it, the build stage must be re-run to place it.

a drawn kitchen sink that is listed in t.rule: A drawn kitchen sink that is listed in the room's piece set must be placed by the build stage; if the build stage drops it, the build stage must be re-run to place it.

a piece that the final stage lists must.rule: A piece that the final stage lists must survive the build stage; if the build drops it, the build stage must be re-run to place it.

a drawn piece in a kitchen that is 0.30.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen that is 0.30 x 0.20 m and does not match any kitchen fixture size table must be typed from its neighbours and the room's program, not left untyped; if no kitchen type fits, it must be marked as a non-furniture symbol with evidence.

a drawn block that matches a fixture typ.rule: A drawn block that matches a fixture type and size must be added to the model at its drawn anchor; if the reading stage misses it, the build stage must add it.

a stair layer (a-merdiven) with 94 entit.rule: A stair layer (A-MERDIVEN) with 94 entities on a level that has a stair room must be read into the stair piece; if the stair is already built from another source, the layer must be explicitly marked as redundant, not silently dropped.

a stair elevation layer (a-merdiven görü.rule: A stair elevation layer (A-merdiven görünüş) must be read to verify the stair's rise, run, and landing geometry; if the plan stair is already built, the elevation must be cross-checked and any discrepancy flagged.

a decoration/fixture layer (deko_vitrifi.rule: A decoration/fixture layer (Deko_Vitrifiye) with 216 entities must be read for bathroom fixtures, sanitary ware, or decorative elements; if the items are already placed by the furniture agent, the layer must be cross-checked and marked as redundant, not silently dropped.

a plumbing/fixture layer (piu_vitrifiye).rule: A plumbing/fixture layer (Piu_Vitrifiye) with 4964 entities must be read for sanitary fixtures, pipes, and connections; if the fixtures are already placed, the layer must be cross-checked and marked as redundant, not silently dropped.

when a room is dropped due to conflicts,.rule: When a room is dropped due to conflicts, the build stage must resolve the conflicts (e.g., missing fridge in kitchen zone) and rebuild the room; it must not silently drop the room and leave it out of the final model.
When a room is dropped due to conflicts, the build stage must resolve the conflicts and rebuild the room; it must not silently drop the room and leave it out of the final model.

when a piece is dropped after the build.rule: When a piece is dropped after the build stage, the build stage must re-run to resolve the conflicts and rebuild the piece; it must not silently drop the piece and leave it out of the final model.

when a kitchen fixture is dropped after.rule: When a kitchen fixture is dropped after the build stage, the build stage must re-run to resolve the conflicts and rebuild the fixture; it must not silently drop the fixture and leave it out of the final model.

a piece drawn on a structural layer (e.g.rule: A piece drawn on a structural layer (e.g., 'A-BA') must not be automatically classified as 'not furniture (column)' and dropped; the build stage must check the piece's type and context before applying layer-based exclusion rules. If the piece is a bar_stool or other furniture, it must be built regardless of the layer it is drawn on.

a drawn piece that the furniture stage t.rule: A drawn piece that the furniture stage typed as a functional item (bar_stool) must not be dropped by the build stage on the basis of its DWG layer name alone; the layer is a drawing convention, not a type, and a layer-based 'not furniture' override is only valid when the piece's own recognition crop shows a structural element (column, wall, axis), not a piece of furniture.

when a kitchen's drawn run is too short.rule: When a kitchen's drawn run is too short to host its full program (fridge, sink, stove, counter), the fit stage must not leave the missing appliance out; it must either extend the run along the available wall or place the missing appliance as a freestanding unit in the room, so every program member of a kitchen is built.

in a bathroom, the fit stage must place.rule: In a bathroom, the fit stage must place the toilet so its centre is at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; if the drawn position does not satisfy this, the fit stage must shift the toilet (or the neighbouring fixture) to a position that does, rather than leaving the clearance short.

in a bathroom, the fit stage must leave.rule: In a bathroom, the fit stage must leave at least 0.53 m of clear floor in front of a bathtub; if the drawn position does not satisfy this, the fit stage must reposition the bathtub or the room's other fixtures to create the clearance, rather than accepting a short approach.

In a bathroom, the fit stage must leave at least 0.53 m of clear floor in front of a shower; if the drawn position does not satisfy this, the fit stage must reposition the shower or the room's other fixtures to create the clearance, rather than accepting a short approach.

a bathtub's front clearance must be at l.rule: A bathtub's front clearance must be at least 0.53 m; the fitter must shift the tub along its wall to a spot that provides it before the run is accepted.

a toilet's centre must be at least 0.38.rule: A toilet's centre must be at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; the fitter must shift it to a compliant spot before the run is accepted.

a drawn opening whose leaf is a fixed me.rule: A drawn opening whose leaf is a fixed metal grille or security screen (no operable leaf, no latch) must be typed as a window or fixed grille, not a door; the read stage must check for an operable leaf before assigning a door type.

when a door's drawn height is missing bu.rule: When a door's drawn height is missing but its top is at a standard head (e.g. 2.10 m), the read stage must record the height as assumed and flag it for confirmation rather than leaving it unconfirmed; a door with an unconfirmed height is a reading gap, not a silent default.

every drawn opening must be cut through.rule: Every drawn opening must be cut through its wall; if a door ray hits a wall, the build stage must cut the opening before the run is accepted.

a stair's open sides must have a continu.rule: A stair's open sides must have a continuous handrail over at least 0.72 m of its run; the build stage must generate the balustrade and handrail as part of the stair model.

every project must include a frontal vie.rule: Every project must include a frontal view of the entrance facade; if missing, the camera stage must add one.

when the terrain slope exceeds 1:3, the.rule: When the terrain slope exceeds 1:3, the build stage must generate a retaining edge or retaining wall along the steep side; a steep slope without a retaining edge is a build omission.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.90-0.97 m); if the model's top is higher, the build stage must select a model with the correct height.

a bathroom's washbasin must be accompani.rule: A bathroom's washbasin must be accompanied by a mirror and basic styling (towels, soap) to read as a designed space; the decor stage must add these items.

an outdoor dining table must be styled w.rule: An outdoor dining table must be styled with at least a tablecloth, a bowl, or glasses to read as a designed, lived-in space; the decor stage must add these items.

a decor item that fails a scene check (s.rule: A decor item that fails a scene check (S5) on a level must be rebuilt or re-fitted before the level is accepted; a failed scene check is a build defect, not a review note.

the big loop must run enough cycles to r.rule: The big loop must run enough cycles to raise the house score; stopping at 0 cycles with no score gain is a failed run.

every camera view must be checked and ei.rule: Every camera view must be checked and either accepted or re-posed before the run is accepted; views left marked for review are a failed camera stage.

a drawn sofa whose back is off a wall by.rule: A drawn sofa whose back is off a wall by more than 0.3 m must be re-anchored to the nearest free wall span within 1.2 m; if no free span exists, the room layout must be re-solved, not the sofa moved beyond the drawn lock.

a wardrobe with less than 0.80 m clearan.rule: A wardrobe with less than 0.80 m clearance in front must be re-placed on a wall span that provides the clearance; if no such span exists in the room, the room layout must be re-solved.

a coffee table that overlaps an armchair.rule: A coffee table that overlaps an armchair must be re-placed in the seating group; if the group is too tight, the room layout must be re-solved.

a desk model that is a crude placeholder.rule: A desk model that is a crude placeholder or does not match the room's style must be swapped for a library model that fits the room's material palette and style; if no library model fits, the build stage must generate a parametric desk.

a bed with less than 0.60 m clearance on.rule: A bed with less than 0.60 m clearance on a side must be re-placed to provide the clearance; if no such position exists in the room, the room layout must be re-solved.

a coffee table that is not in front of t.rule: A coffee table that is not in front of the sofa must be re-placed in the seating group; if the group is too tight, the room layout must be re-solved.

a floor lamp that stands in front of a w.rule: A floor lamp that stands in front of a window must be moved to a position that does not block the window's sightline or egress; if no such position exists, the room layout must be re-solved.

an armchair that does not face its seati.rule: An armchair that does not face its seating group must be rotated to face the group; if the group is too tight, the room layout must be re-solved.

a room labeled as a game/activity and re.rule: A room labeled as a game/activity and rest room on the top floor must be typed as 'other' or 'living', not 'bedroom'; if the documents show it as a bedroom, the reading stage must correct the label.

a staircase with an open side must have.rule: A staircase with an open side must have a safety railing or guard built as part of the stair model; a stair without a guard is a safety defect.

a kitchen aisle must be at least 0.90 m.rule: A kitchen aisle must be at least 0.90 m wide; if the room layout does not provide this, the room must be re-solved.

a stove that is part of a built-in kitch.rule: A stove that is part of a built-in kitchen run (a hob in the worktop with the oven integrated in the run's fronts) must be modelled as the run's integrated appliance, not as a free-standing box; the fit stage must not leave a crude box standing off the counter, and the swap_model tool must not be offered for a built-in appliance that is already integrated in its run.

a piece whose footprint crosses a room o.rule: A piece whose footprint crosses a room outline by up to 0.05 m² (a depth of up to 0.02 m) is a tolerance case, not a violation: the architect's rule F5 must explicitly allow this small overlap so the critic does not flag it.

the architect's rule c1 must state wheth.rule: The architect's rule C1 must state whether a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door to each piece's front use zone is required; if it is not required for all pieces (e.g. pieces in a secondary zone), the rule must say so so the critic does not flag them.

the architect's rule f3 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F3 must explicitly allow a floor lamp (or similar tall, slim piece) to stand in front of a window when the lamp's footprint does not block the window's opening or egress; the critic must not flag this as a violation.

the architect's rule s4 must state wheth.rule: The architect's rule S4 must state whether a kitchen must have a fridge as a separate piece or whether the fridge can be integrated into the kitchen run; if integrated, the rule must say so so the critic does not flag the missing separate fridge.

the architect's rule s4 must state the m.rule: The architect's rule S4 must state the minimum clearance from a toilet's centre to the side wall or adjacent fixture (e.g. 0.38 m) and whether this is a hard requirement or a guideline; the critic must not flag it if the rule allows a smaller clearance.

the architect's rule f4 must state wheth.rule: The architect's rule F4 must state whether a sofa's free zone in front of it must be completely unobstructed or whether a small piece (e.g. a side table) can be placed in it; if a small piece is allowed, the rule must say so so the critic does not flag it.

a bedroom's reference-styled rug must be.rule: A bedroom's reference-styled rug must be placed by the agent; if the render shows only a small mat, the agent must add a large patterned rug that anchors the bed.

a kitchen's wall above the counter must.rule: A kitchen's wall above the counter must be fully designed (upper cabinets, backsplash, or styled open shelving); a large empty wall section is not acceptable.

a dining table and its chairs must not o.rule: A dining table and its chairs must not overlap by more than 0.010 m; the fit stage must ensure the chair's back does not cut into the table's edge, and the swap_model tool must not be used to fix a collision that is a fit error.

a toilet model must be realistic and det.rule: A toilet model must be realistic and detailed, not a crude low-poly box; the agent must select a model with a proper cistern shape.

a washbasin model must be realistic and.rule: A washbasin model must be realistic and detailed, not a crude low-poly box; the agent must select a model with a proper curved basin shape.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main functional group (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) in a coherent way, not a tight, low-angle crop of a corner.

a bathroom's washbasin and vanity must b.rule: A bathroom's washbasin and vanity must be styled with a finished counter, warm light, and texture; a bare, unstyled look is not acceptable.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main functional group (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) in a coherent way, not a cramped, unstyled corner.
A bathroom camera must frame the room's wet fixtures (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) as a group from a free corner with headroom, never a close-up of a wall or a single fixture rim.

when a piece's current model is the high.rule: When a piece's current model is the highest-rated option in the library for its type, a style-mismatch finding cannot be fixed by swap_model (which only takes higher-rated models); the fit stage must select the model by style coherence with the room's set, not by rating alone, and the library must carry a modern variant of the type.

a bed in a furnished render must be styl.rule: A bed in a furnished render must be styled with bedding (pillows, duvet, throw) as part of its model or a decor layer; a bare slab is not acceptable.

a bedroom render must show the full styl.rule: A bedroom render must show the full styled set (styled bed with bedding, rug, curtains, wall art, lamps, warm light); a bare grey-box is not acceptable for a client presentation.

a hall/entry render must show the room's.rule: A hall/entry render must show the room's defining pieces (shoe cabinet, stair) plus a place to sit and styled surfaces; a bare run of floor is not acceptable.

a hall/entry must include a place to sit.rule: A hall/entry must include a place to sit (bench or stool) as part of its entrance group; an empty run of floor is not acceptable.

a bedroom's furniture set must be stylis.rule: A bedroom's furniture set must be stylistically coherent; a utilitarian office chair and a boxy white desk are not acceptable in a styled bedroom render.
A bedroom's furniture set must be stylistically coherent; a utilitarian office chair is not acceptable in a styled bedroom render.
A bedroom's furniture set must be stylistically coherent; a boxy white desk is not acceptable in a styled bedroom render.

a bedroom render must show the full styl.rule: A bedroom render must show the full styled set (styled bed with bedding, styled desk with decor, rug, wall art, warm light); bare surfaces are not acceptable.

a bedroom render must show a stylistical.rule: A bedroom render must show a stylistically coherent set; a mix of utilitarian and rustic pieces in a modern room is not acceptable.

a bedroom's furniture set must be stylis.rule: A bedroom's furniture set must be stylistically coherent; a rustic wardrobe is not acceptable in a modern bedroom render.

a cushion placed on a bed must rest on t.rule: A cushion placed on a bed must rest on the mattress surface; any penetration into the bed frame or mattress beyond 0.03 m is a placement error that the decor_rest stage must resolve before the run is accepted.

all walls defined in the architectural p.rule: All walls defined in the architectural plan must be built in the 3D model; if a wall is missing after the build stage, the build stage must be re-run to restore it.

all doors defined in the architectural p.rule: All doors defined in the architectural plan must be built in the 3D model; if a door is missing after the build stage, the build stage must be re-run to restore it.

every site area labelled in the document.rule: Every site area labelled in the documents (parking, terrace, pool) must be built as a modelled outdoor space with its outline, even if it is outside the building footprint.

when a drawing labels a sub-zone (e.g.,.rule: When a drawing labels a sub-zone (e.g., 'open kitchen') within a larger open-plan room that is already modeled and furnished with the corresponding functional set, the reading stage must map the sub-zone label to the existing room rather than flagging it as a missing room.

when a drawing labels a room that is alr.rule: When a drawing labels a room that is already modeled and furnished with the corresponding functional set, the reading stage must map the label to the existing room rather than flagging it as a missing room.

the reading stage must cross-check the n.rule: The reading stage must cross-check the number of storeys in the section views against the level marks in the plan; if the section shows fewer storeys than the model, the level reading is wrong and must be corrected before building.

the decor stage must check the roof clea.rule: The decor stage must check the roof clearance for every piece it places; a piece that pokes through the roof is a hard error and must be re-placed or removed.

every open-side stair must have a safety.rule: Every open-side stair must have a safety railing or guard built as part of the stair model; the build stage must add it automatically.

every open-side stair opening must have.rule: Every open-side stair opening must have a safety railing or guard built as part of the stair model; the build stage must add it automatically.

when a wardrobe model is rendered as a f.rule: When a wardrobe model is rendered as a flat panel or wall, the fit stage must swap it for a functional wardrobe model with doors and handles.

every ceiling light must have a hang rec.rule: Every ceiling light must have a hang record (cord, rod, or canopy) connecting it to the ceiling; the decor stage must add it automatically.

a seating group's armchairs must face th.rule: A seating group's armchairs must face the group's anchor (sofa or coffee table), not the back of another seat; the fitter must orient each chair toward the group centre before the run is accepted.

a piece that protrudes through a room ou.rule: A piece that protrudes through a room outline by less than 3 cm is within tolerance and does not require a fix.

a coffee table must not overlap an armch.rule: A coffee table must not overlap an armchair; the fitter must find a non-clashing position within the drawn lock before the run is accepted.

every piece's front use zone must be rea.rule: Every piece's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; the fitter must ensure clear egress before the run is accepted.

no furniture may block the sightline or.rule: No furniture may block the sightline or egress through a window opening; the fitter must keep a clear zone in front of windows.

a built-in stove in a kitchen counter ru.rule: A built-in stove in a kitchen counter run is not required to have its back exactly on a wall; a small offset is within tolerance for integrated appliances.

a kitchen run must leave at least 0.90 m.rule: A kitchen run must leave at least 0.90 m of clear aisle in front of its worktop; the layout solver must reject any placement that narrows the working aisle below that.

a stove built into a counter run must si.rule: A stove built into a counter run must sit flush against the run's back wall; a 0.06 m gap means the run was not snapped to the wall and the layout must be re-solved.

an armchair in a seating group must face.rule: An armchair in a seating group must face the group's anchor (sofa) within 30 degrees; the layout solver must orient every group member toward the anchor, not leave it at an arbitrary angle.

a dining chair must have at least 0.81 m.rule: A dining chair must have at least 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; the layout solver must keep that pull-out clearance when placing chairs.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall; a sof.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall; a sofa floating 2.00 m from any wall is a mis-placed anchor and the room's layout must be re-solved.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall; when.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall; when the drawn position cannot be snapped within the move limit, the room's layout must be re-solved rather than forcing a partial move.

a double bed must have at least 0.60 m o.rule: A double bed must have at least 0.60 m of free space along each side; the layout solver must keep that clearance when placing the bed and its nightstands.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window opening; the layout solver must keep the window's sightline and egress clear of furniture.

a wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of.rule: A wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of clear space in front of it for the doors to open; the layout solver must keep that clearance when placing tall storage.

site areas drawn in the documents (pools.rule: Site areas drawn in the documents (pools, platforms, terraces, parking) must be built as part of the site model; if the outline is not built, the site stage failed and must be re-run.

a stove that is part of a kitchen counte.rule: A stove that is part of a kitchen counter run must be built as a visible, separate object (a hob or range) on top of the counter; the build stage must not treat it as absorbed into the counter module and leave no object in the scene.

a kitchen sink that is part of a counter.rule: A kitchen sink that is part of a counter run must be built as a visible, separate object (a basin) in the counter; the build stage must not treat it as absorbed into the counter module and leave no object in the scene.

a stair-core room whose only camera poin.rule: A stair-core room whose only camera point falls inside the stair must be shown from the adjacent hall or landing that frames the stair, not given its own interior view; the camera stage must route the stair's view to the hall that contains the stair's visible run.

a drawn piece in a kitchen that is too s.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen that is too small for a standard appliance (e.g. 0.30 x 0.20 m) must be typed as a small kitchen accessory (e.g. a small appliance or canister) or marked as a non-furniture symbol, not left untyped.

a stair elevation layer (a-merdiven görü.rule: A stair elevation layer (A-merdiven görünüş) must be read to verify the stair's rise direction and flight geometry; if the plan already defines the stair, the elevation must be cross-checked and any discrepancy flagged, not silently ignored.

a decoration/fixture layer (deko_vitrifi.rule: A decoration/fixture layer (Deko_Vitrifiye) with 216 entities must be read for built-in fixtures or decorative elements; if the items are not part of the furniture program, they must be explicitly marked as not-built with a reason, not silently dropped.

a plumbing/fixture layer (piu_vitrifiye).rule: A plumbing/fixture layer (Piu_Vitrifiye) with 4964 entities must be read for wet-room fixtures and services; if the fixtures are already placed by the build stage, the layer must be cross-checked and any missing fixture flagged, not silently ignored.

when a room is dropped due to a missing.rule: When a room is dropped due to a missing kitchen fixture (fridge), the build stage must re-run the kitchen group solver to place the missing fixture before dropping the room; a room with a kitchen zone must not be dropped for a solvable missing piece.

a bedroom with a bed, nightstand, and wa.rule: A bedroom with a bed, nightstand, and wardrobe must not be dropped due to conflicts; the build stage must resolve the conflicts (e.g., re-place the bed or wardrobe) before dropping the room.

a hall with a shoe cabinet and stair mus.rule: A hall with a shoe cabinet and stair must not be dropped due to conflicts; the build stage must resolve the conflicts (e.g., re-place the shoe cabinet or stair) before dropping the room.

a hall with a console table and stair mu.rule: A hall with a console table and stair must not be dropped due to conflicts; the build stage must resolve the conflicts (e.g., re-place the console table or stair) before dropping the room.

a bathroom with a bathtub, toilet, and w.rule: A bathroom with a bathtub, toilet, and washbasin must not be dropped due to conflicts; the build stage must resolve the conflicts (e.g., re-place the fixtures) before dropping the room.

a piece dropped after the build stage du.rule: A piece dropped after the build stage due to conflicts must be re-placed by the build stage; if the piece is part of a room's program, the room must be rebuilt with the piece included.

kitchen fixtures in a living room (open.rule: Kitchen fixtures in a living room (open kitchen) must be built and visible; if the kitchen zone is dropped due to conflicts, the build stage must re-run to resolve the conflicts and rebuild the kitchen fixtures.

a piece drawn on a structural layer (a-b.rule: A piece drawn on a structural layer (A-BA) that is typed as furniture (bar_stool) must not be overridden by a layer-based 'not furniture (column)' rule; the piece's type and room context must take precedence over the layer name when the piece is clearly a furniture item (e.g., a bar stool next to a kitchen island).

a drawn piece in a kitchen or dining zon.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen or dining zone that is small (under 0.5 m on a side) and sits at counter height next to a counter or island must be read as a bar stool, not as a structural column; the layer name alone must not override the piece's size, height and neighbours when classifying it as furniture.

a drawn opening that is a fixed grille o.rule: A drawn opening that is a fixed grille or screen (no leaf, no swing, no latch) must be typed as a window or fixed screen, not a door, even if it is at floor level.

when a door's height is not drawn, the r.rule: When a door's height is not drawn, the read stage must infer it from the standard door height for the room type (e.g., 2.10 m for interior doors) and flag it as inferred, not leave it unconfirmed.

an opening must be cut through its wall;.rule: An opening must be cut through its wall; if the door ray hits the wall, the build stage must cut the opening before the run is accepted.

stair models must include handrails over.rule: Stair models must include handrails over the full run of each flight; if a flight has no handrail over 0.72 m of its run, the build stage must add a continuous balustrade with newels at turns and ends.

a frontal view of the entrance facade mu.rule: A frontal view of the entrance facade must be included in the camera set; if missing, the camera stage must add it.

when the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3.rule: When the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3, a retaining edge or retaining wall must be built to prevent erosion and ensure stability.

kitchen counters must be built at their.rule: Kitchen counters must be built at their working height (0.90-0.95 m); if the model's top is over 1.10 m, the build stage must use a correct model or adjust the height.

a bathroom's washbasin must be presented.rule: A bathroom's washbasin must be presented as a finished vanity: the model must include its mirror, and the surrounding wall must carry the room's wet-wall finish; a bare basin on an untextured wall is not an acceptable bathroom render.

outdoor dining tables must carry at leas.rule: Outdoor dining tables must carry at least one small styling item (bowl, glasses, runner) so the set reads as designed and lived-in, not a bare furniture showroom.

a room whose label names a leisure/activ.rule: A room whose label names a leisure/activity use (game, activity, relaxation, play) and whose furniture is a full living set must be typed 'living', not 'other'; the label describes the use, not a non-room.

a drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side in a living room must be split into individual pieces or typed as a single built-in storage run (sideboard/credenza), not left untyped; the size table must allow sideboards up to ~6 m long.

a drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a side in a room must be split into individual pieces or typed as a single built-in element (kitchen run, storage wall), not left untyped; the size table must allow built-ins up to ~5.5 m long.

when the plan labels a roof terrace with.rule: When the plan labels a roof terrace with a door to it, the roof must be cut open over the terrace (a roof terrace), not built closed over it; the section must show the opening.

a door under a sloped roof whose top wou.rule: A door under a sloped roof whose top would reach over the roof underside must be given a dormer or a raised head so it is at least 2.00 m high and usable; a door clipped under the roof is not acceptable.

the sheets stage must not end 'pending';.rule: The sheets stage must not end 'pending'; all sheet questions must be answered before the run is accepted.

a sofa's front must face the long side (.rule: A sofa's front must face the long side (the side with the most free room), not the short side; an AI front on the short side is a reading error.

a kitchen run must be placed so the work.rule: A kitchen run must be placed so the working aisle in front of the counter is at least 0.90 m and the worktop at standard working height (about 0.90 m); if the room's geometry cannot satisfy both, the run must be re-anchored to a different wall span or the room flagged, never left with a sub-0.90 m aisle or an over-height counter.

a built-in or freestanding storage piece.rule: A built-in or freestanding storage piece (wardrobe, cabinet) may protrude through the room outline by up to 0.05 m (5 cm) where it is flush against a wall or partition; the critic must not flag such a shallow overlap as a violation.

a seating piece's front use zone must be.rule: A seating piece's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the nearest door or opening; if the room's layout cannot provide that walkway, the piece must be repositioned or the room flagged, and the critic must not flag a piece whose use zone is blocked only by another piece's own use zone.

a floor lamp or tall decorative piece ma.rule: A floor lamp or tall decorative piece may stand in front of a window if it does not block more than 30% of the window's glazed area and does not obstruct the egress or sightline; the critic must not flag a piece that satisfies this condition.

a kitchen room must contain a fridge as.rule: A kitchen room must contain a fridge as part of its functional set; if the fridge is missing, the build stage must place it, and the critic must flag the room until it is present.

a toilet must have at least 0.38 m of cl.rule: A toilet must have at least 0.38 m of clear space from the side wall or adjacent fixture on each side; if the room's geometry cannot provide this, the toilet must be repositioned or the room flagged, and the critic must not flag a toilet that satisfies this clearance.

a sofa's front free zone must not be blo.rule: A sofa's front free zone must not be blocked by another piece's footprint; if a piece blocks the sofa's use zone, the blocking piece must be repositioned or the sofa flagged, and the critic must not flag a sofa whose use zone is clear.

a bedroom's reference styling must inclu.rule: A bedroom's reference styling must include a rug that anchors the bed; if the render shows only a small mat or no rug, the agent must place a large patterned rug under the bed.

a kitchen's wall must be fully designed.rule: A kitchen's wall must be fully designed with upper cabinets or a backsplash; if a large empty section of wall remains, the fit stage must complete the kitchen run to cover it.

a dining table and its chairs must not o.rule: A dining table and its chairs must not overlap by more than 0.010 m; if they do, the fit stage must reposition the chairs or the table to resolve the collision.

a toilet model must be realistic and det.rule: A toilet model must be realistic and detailed, not a crude low-poly box; if the current model is low-poly, the fit stage must swap it for a higher-quality model from the library.

a washbasin model must be realistic and.rule: A washbasin model must be realistic and detailed, not a crude low-poly box; if the current model is low-poly, the fit stage must swap it for a higher-quality model from the library.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main functional group (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) at a reasonable eye level, not a tight low-angle crop of a corner.

a bathroom vanity and its mirror must be.rule: A bathroom vanity and its mirror must be drawn from the same material family and finish as the room's wet-area palette; a dark heavy-wood base with a thick frame is not acceptable in a light minimalist bathroom, and when the library has no matching asset the fitter must build a parametric vanity in the room's palette rather than leave a clashing model.

a bathroom camera must frame the whole w.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the whole wet set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) from a free point with headroom, not a low close-up that crops the mirror and door.

interior door leaves must use a finish f.rule: Interior door leaves must use a finish from the room's material palette; a raw warm-oak leaf is not acceptable in a cool white-and-grey minimalist bathroom.

a washbasin's mirror and frame must matc.rule: A washbasin's mirror and frame must match the room's clean modern lines; a heavy dark-bronze industrial frame is not acceptable in a minimalist concrete bathroom.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main functional group, not a blank wall or a corner of the vanity.

a bathroom camera must frame the main gr.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the main group of fixtures (basin, shower, toilet) in a coherent way, not a tight low-angle crop of a corner.

a nightstand must be a matched set with.rule: A nightstand must be a matched set with the bed in style and finish; a rustic distressed-wood nightstand is not acceptable beside a modern bed, and the swap must not take a lower-rated model.

a bed must be styled with cushions, duve.rule: A bed must be styled with cushions, duvet and throw; a flat white slab bed is not acceptable in a furnished render.

a bedroom camera must frame the room's m.rule: A bedroom camera must frame the room's main functional group (bed and nightstands), not a bare grey-box corner.

a hall/entry must have a place to sit (b.rule: A hall/entry must have a place to sit (bench or stool) to anchor the wall; an empty run of floor is not acceptable.

an office chair in a bedroom must use a.rule: An office chair in a bedroom must use a residential style, not a corporate black-mesh item; a corporate chair is not acceptable in a soft residential bedroom.

a bedroom must have a large area rug to.rule: A bedroom must have a large area rug to anchor the bed and add warmth; bare wood flooring is not acceptable in a styled bedroom.

an office chair in a bedroom must use a.rule: An office chair in a bedroom must use a residential style, not a corporate black high-back item; a corporate chair is not acceptable in a light-wood bedroom.

a bed frame must use a soft, upholstered.rule: A bed frame must use a soft, upholstered or light-wood look that matches the room's palette; a very dark boxy storage frame is not acceptable in a light-wood bedroom.

a bedroom render must include a rug unde.rule: A bedroom render must include a rug under the bed and at least one ambient light source; their absence is a decor-stage omission, not a layout constraint.

a nightstand is judged in context: a pla.rule: A nightstand is judged in context: a plain block is acceptable only when the room carries the soft layers (rug, textiles) that make it read as styled.

the furniture agent must deliver a coher.rule: The furniture agent must deliver a coherent, styled room (matched set, warm light, soft layers); a raw blocky assembly is a failed agent round, not a camera problem.

a desk in a furnished render must show j.rule: A desk in a furnished render must show joinery or a finished surface; a bare slab is a placeholder, not an acceptable model.

a wardrobe in a furnished render must ha.rule: A wardrobe in a furnished render must have a finished, textured surface; a flat untextured box is a placeholder.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's full fixture set (bathtub, toilet, washbasin), not a close-up of one wall.

a hall/entry render must include a conso.rule: A hall/entry render must include a console or bench, a rug, wall art, and warm lighting; a bare corner with a single harsh spot is a failed agent round.

a hall camera must frame the room's defi.rule: A hall camera must frame the room's defining pieces (stair, shoe cabinet) and its doors, not a tight corner.

a corridor render must include a console.rule: A corridor render must include a console or bench, a rug, wall art, and warm lighting; a bare corridor with a crude plant is a failed agent round.

a living room with a large flat wall beh.rule: A living room with a large flat wall behind the sofa must have wall art or a styled surface; a bare wall is a decor-stage omission.

a sofa in a furnished render must have c.rule: A sofa in a furnished render must have cushions and throws; a bare generic sofa is a placeholder.

a coffee table in a furnished render mus.rule: A coffee table in a furnished render must show joinery or a finished surface; a generic block that clashes with the dining set is a placeholder.

the furniture agent must deliver a coher.rule: The furniture agent must deliver a coherent, styled room (matched set, warm light, soft layers); a disjointed, poorly styled interior is a failed agent round.

a dining set in a living area must match.rule: A dining set in a living area must match the room's style; a stark modern piece that clashes with the neutral living area is a failed agent selection.

an exterior render must include realisti.rule: An exterior render must include realistic ground, trees, and site elements; a flat featureless green plane is a failed agent output.

outdoor floors (balconies, terraces, ver.rule: Outdoor floors (balconies, terraces, verandas) must be finished with a weather-appropriate material (decking, stone, tile) with visible jointing, never a flat untextured slab.

exterior renders must use a finished lan.rule: Exterior renders must use a finished landscape (realistic trees, ground cover, hedges) and a proper sky, never a grey-box field with lollipop trees.

exterior renders must use a warm, direct.rule: Exterior renders must use a warm, directional sun and a clear sky; a flat grey sky with a dark interior void is not client-ready.

exterior renders must show warm interior.rule: Exterior renders must show warm interior light spilling from the windows; the render stage must place interior light sources so the house reads as inhabited, not a dark void.

exterior cameras must sit at eye level (.rule: Exterior cameras must sit at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or above the ridge; a low, awkward angle that crops the building is not acceptable.

a main entrance must be built with a def.rule: A main entrance must be built with a defined entry sequence (canopy or roof overhang, door hardware, exterior lighting); a bare dark opening is not acceptable.

the house must have a library entrance d.rule: The house must have a library entrance door (a statement door) at its outside door; a missing entrance door is a build failure.

every drawn furniture piece must be type.rule: Every drawn furniture piece must be typed to a real product that fits its size and room; untyped pieces that nothing builds or explains are a reading failure.

decor that cannot rest on its host (no t.rule: Decor that cannot rest on its host (no top found) must be dropped or re-hosted by the decor stage; it must not be left as a not-built orphan.

decor that rests on a host must be re-se.rule: Decor that rests on a host must be re-seated by the decor stage when the host's top is rebuilt; a gap above tolerance means the decor stage ran before the host's final geometry.
Decor that rests on a host must be re-seated by the decor stage when the host's top is rebuilt; a missing top means the decor stage ran before the host's final geometry.

a draped cloth must rest on a single con.rule: A draped cloth must rest on a single continuous surface; if the host top is not one surface, the decor stage must pick a host with a flat top or skip the drape.

entities on layers that are off or froze.rule: Entities on layers that are off or frozen in the source DWG are intentionally hidden by the architect and are not part of the active drawing; the reading stage correctly skips them.
entities on layers that are off or froze.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

ole2frame and wipeout entities are non-g.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are non-geometric annotation or masking objects; the reading stage correctly ignores them.

a camera dropped by the cameras stage mu.rule: A camera dropped by the cameras stage must carry a reason; a drop with no reason is a stage failure and the stage must re-run.

an exterior camera that must show a wind.rule: An exterior camera that must show a window must be posed so the window is in frame; if the window is not seen, the camera stage must re-pose the view.

a drawn block on a level that is not use.rule: A drawn block on a level that is not used by any model element must be either typed as a piece, marked as a non-furniture symbol, or recorded as a deliberate omission with a reason; an unexplained unused block is a reading-stage loss.

a drawn block whose name and size match.rule: A drawn block whose name and size match no furniture, fixture or architectural element is a drawing symbol, not a lost piece; the reading stage may leave it untyped.

auto-generated blocks with the a$c prefi.rule: Auto-generated blocks with the A$C prefix are CAD artifacts (hatches, dimension fragments); the reading stage must not treat them as furniture or fixtures.

site-decor blocks (landscaping, paving,.rule: Site-decor blocks (landscaping, paving, outdoor furniture) recorded by site-decor elements are not part of the house model; the reading stage may leave them unbuilt.

a drawn stair block that is already repr.rule: A drawn stair block that is already represented by a built stair piece in the model is not a lost element; the reading stage may leave the block untyped.

door block symbols in dwg files represen.rule: Door block symbols in DWG files represent the door leaf and frame; if the model already contains the corresponding door element, the block symbol itself does not need to be built as a separate 3D piece.

small generic table blocks that are not.rule: Small generic table blocks that are not explicitly assigned to a room in the reading phase and are not critical to the room's function are often drawing artifacts or duplicates of existing furniture.

table blocks that match the size and fun.rule: Table blocks that match the size and function of existing furniture in the room are considered duplicates or symbols of the already-built pieces.

entities on off or frozen layers in dwg.rule: Entities on off or frozen layers in DWG files are intentionally excluded from the 3D model as they are not part of the active design.

ole2frame and wipeout entities are 2d dr.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are 2D drawing aids and are not converted to 3D geometry.

small structural columns that are part o.rule: Small structural columns that are part of the wall assembly and do not significantly affect the room's layout or function are often not modeled as separate 3D elements.

symbols that are not furniture and are k.rule: Symbols that are not furniture and are kept as obstacles are correctly handled by the reading stage.

columns on structural layers are not bui.rule: Columns on structural layers are not built as furniture and are often not modeled as separate 3D elements if they are minor.

drawings that are contained within anoth.rule: Drawings that are contained within another piece (60% or more) are considered parts of that piece or duplicates and are not built as separate elements.

a drawn piece whose model footprint exce.rule: A drawn piece whose model footprint exceeds the drawn outline by more than the 0.05 m tolerance must be swapped for a library model whose footprint matches the drawn size, not nudged to hide the mismatch.

a drawn coffee table must be built at it.rule: A drawn coffee table must be built at its drawn footprint; when the chosen library model is larger than the drawn outline, the piece is resized to the drawn size instead of being moved off its drawn place.

a drawn piece whose model footprint matc.rule: A drawn piece whose model footprint matches the drawn outline but sits up to ~0.2 m from its drawn centre is a placement tolerance, not a misread; it is not corrected by a model swap.

a bathroom render must include a styling.rule: A bathroom render must include a styling layer (towels, soap, a plant, small accessories) on top of the functional set; the functional set alone reads as a bare construction shell.

a bathroom must carry a cohesive materia.rule: A bathroom must carry a cohesive material palette and at least one design feature (feature wall, integrated lighting, or a styled vanity) so it does not read as plain, unfinished tiles.

when the fitter reports 'no valid spot'.rule: When the fitter reports 'no valid spot' for a fixture, no centre will do and the finding stays for review; it is not fixed by a model swap or a further move.

an entrance door set back behind plantin.rule: An entrance door set back behind planting must have a clear path or landing (steps/ramp) leading to it so the entrance reads as integrated, not hidden.

a shoe cabinet belongs at the entrance (.rule: A shoe cabinet belongs at the entrance (ground floor); in an upper-floor hall it is retyped to a console table, which is the appropriate hall furniture.

a zone label such as 'açik mutfak' (open.rule: A zone label such as 'AÇIK MUTFAK' (open kitchen) inside a living room, together with a drawn kitchen zone (counter, sink, stove), must be recognised as an open-kitchen zone: the kitchen pieces are kept and the room is treated as a combined living/kitchen space, not flagged as an unknown label.

when no library model fits a door's size.rule: When no library model fits a door's size, a parametric door in the house's door language is an acceptable build, not a defect.

when the drawn shower size is within the.rule: When the drawn shower size is within the real product range but no library model passes the fit rules (caps, height), a parametric shower is an acceptable build, not a defect.

when the drawn fixture size is within to.rule: When the drawn fixture size is within tolerance of the real product range, the fitter must select a library model that fits the bay and the ceiling clearance; a parametric mesh is only a last resort when no library model fits.

for a balcony or terrace dining table, t.rule: For a balcony or terrace dining table, the fitter must select a library model whose height fits the outdoor context and whose style matches the facade; a parametric mesh is not acceptable for a client-facing outdoor space.

kitchen wall cabinets must be aligned so.rule: Kitchen wall cabinets must be aligned so that their vertical joints coincide with the joints of the base units below; the build stage must snap wall-unit joints to the base-unit grid.

a dining table in a living/dining room m.rule: A dining table in a living/dining room must be styled with a basic setting (plates, glasses, a centerpiece) to look finished and believable in a client presentation.

a coffee table in a living room must be.rule: A coffee table in a living room must be styled with decor (books, a bowl, a vase) to look finished and to match the curated feel of the reference.

paired furniture must use the same model.rule: Paired furniture must use the same model and finish; a seating group must be cohesive in style and color.

a balcony or terrace dining set must be.rule: A balcony or terrace dining set must be styled with a table setting, a plant, or a rug to look finished and to convey the lifestyle the client is buying.

a balcony or terrace must have a guardra.rule: A balcony or terrace must have a guardrail or glass balustrade on its open edges; the build stage must add a safety guard to any open edge of an outdoor space.

when a room is duplicated by the reading.rule: When a room is duplicated by the reading stage, the build stage must merge the duplicate's functional zones into the primary room's zones and suppress the duplicate's redundant pieces, rather than dropping them without a consolidated replacement.

unverified pieces in duplicate rooms tha.rule: Unverified pieces in duplicate rooms that are merged into a primary room may be dropped if they do not correspond to a distinct functional element in the primary room's program.

unverified pieces that do not correspond.rule: Unverified pieces that do not correspond to a distinct functional element in the room's program may be dropped by the build stage.

stairs that span multiple levels must be.rule: Stairs that span multiple levels must be represented as a single continuous element in the final model, with the build stage merging the per-level stair pieces into one coherent stair run.

pieces drawn on structural layers (e.g.,.rule: Pieces drawn on structural layers (e.g., 'A-BA') must be treated as structural elements and not built as furniture, even if the reading stage initially typed them as furniture.

when a room is duplicated as a twin, the.rule: When a room is duplicated as a twin, the furniture agent must build the shared set once and the build stage must drop the twin's duplicate drawn pieces of the same type rather than flag them as lost.

when a piece's model already includes it.rule: When a piece's model already includes its cushions or pillows, the conservation check must not list those sub-parts as separate lost elements; they are part of the model, not independent pieces.

when two drawn pieces of the same type o.rule: When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 25% and are of similar size, the build stage must treat them as a single piece drawn twice and keep only one; the duplicate is not a lost element.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 15% and are of similar size, the build stage must treat them as a single piece drawn twice and keep only one; the duplicate is not a lost element.

when a small piece (ottoman, cushion) is.rule: When a small piece (ottoman, cushion) is drawn more than 70% inside a larger seating piece, it is part of that piece's model (seat cushion), not a separate furniture item; the build must not treat it as a lost element.

when a piece is explicitly removed by th.rule: When a piece is explicitly removed by the AI (AI.remove_piece), the build stage must not build it, and the conservation check must not list it as a lost element; the removal is an intentional decision.

when a drawn outline encloses other furn.rule: When a drawn outline encloses other furniture pieces and is larger than any single piece, it is a rug or zone outline, not a furniture item; the build stage must not treat it as a lost piece.
