when a stair's upper end arrives at a le.rule: When a stair's upper end arrives at a level, it is not a separate piece to be built on that level; it is the continuation of the stair from the lower level. The conservation check must not list it as a lost element.

when a plan labels an open kitchen ('açi.rule: When a plan labels an open kitchen ('AÇIK MUTFAK') inside a larger living room, the reading stage must split the kitchen zone into its own kitchen room (or sub-zone) so the kitchen program and its area are evaluated separately from the living area.

a drawn desk/table symbol whose footprin.rule: A drawn desk/table symbol whose footprint includes its chair is read as the table at its real size plus a separate chair piece; the combined footprint is not a defect and no model swap is required.

kitchen fixtures placed in a living room.rule: Kitchen fixtures placed in a living room as an open kitchen zone are a valid open-plan layout, not a misplacement; the zone is the fixtures plus the 1.0 m in front of them.

a sofa whose front was not inferred must.rule: A sofa whose front was not inferred must be given the direction that looks into the most open floor, towards its partner.

an armchair whose front was not inferred.rule: An armchair whose front was not inferred must be given the direction away from its wall or towards its partner.

when the plan labels a roof terrace (a r.rule: When the plan labels a roof terrace (a room with a door to it on the top floor) and the section draws the roof closed over it, the roof must be cut open over the terrace footprint so the terrace is open to the sky; a closed roof over a labelled terrace is a roof-reading error.

a door on a top floor under a sloped roo.rule: A door on a top floor under a sloped roof whose headroom is below a usable door height (the roof underside is lower than the door top) must be given a dormer or the roof raised over it; a door clipped under a low slope is not usable.

an opening on an exterior wall with no r.rule: An opening on an exterior wall with no room on either side takes the style floor material at its threshold; this is correct, not a defect.

a ceiling light under a sloped ceiling m.rule: A ceiling light under a sloped ceiling must be hung flush under the slope (at the local ceiling height), not at a fixed height that may collide with or float below the slope.

under a sloped ceiling, a ceiling light.rule: Under a sloped ceiling, a ceiling light must be hung flush to the slope at its lowest point over the fixture, not at a fixed height that leaves a gap to the slope.

a site area that is drawn and whose matc.rule: A site area that is drawn and whose matching built geometry (pool, terrace, parking) exists must be registered as built, not left 'NOT built (no outline)'; the outline is taken from the built geometry when the area polygon was not read.

a drawn terrace/sunbathing site area wit.rule: A drawn terrace/sunbathing site area with matching built paving must be registered as built from the built geometry, not left 'NOT built (no outline)'.

a drawn parking site area must be regist.rule: A drawn parking site area must be registered as built from its drawn outline or built paving, not left 'NOT built (no outline)'.

a kitchen counter must be at working hei.rule: A kitchen counter must be at working height (~0.90 m) with a >= 0.90 m aisle in front; a counter over 1.10 m or with a sub-0.90 m aisle is a misfit, not a valid kitchen.

the model's storey count must match the.rule: The model's storey count must match the section; an extra storey not in the section is a misread, not a valid addition.

when reading room labels from plans, the.rule: When reading room labels from plans, the full label including any numeric suffix (e.g., '2', '4') must be parsed and preserved to ensure unique room identities. If two rooms have the same base name but different numbers, they must be treated as distinct rooms with unique IDs and labels in the model.

all labelled site areas (pools, terraces.rule: All labelled site areas (pools, terraces, gardens) must be extracted from the site plan and built into the 3D model. If an outline is missing or ambiguous, the stage must flag it for manual review rather than omitting the element.

a room whose label and furniture read as.rule: A room whose label and furniture read as a living room must be typed living, not other, even when its name is a long Turkish compound.

a circulation room that contains a stair.rule: A circulation room that contains a stair plus storage is a hall, not a stair room; the stair is a piece, not the room type.

site areas drawn in the plan (pool, terr.rule: Site areas drawn in the plan (pool, terrace, parking) must be built as site elements with their drawn outline, not left as 'no outline'.

the number of storeys must match the sec.rule: The number of storeys must match the section; a model with more storeys than the section shows is a misread of the levels.

an interior room camera must frame the r.rule: An interior room camera must frame the room's defining functional group (a kitchen's run and island, a bedroom's bed) so the room reads as its type, not as a generic or secondary zone.

a scene check that reports a detached el.rule: A scene check that reports a detached element must be re-run after the build stage so the element is re-attached to its room before the check is scored.

a scene check that reports a geometry fa.rule: A scene check that reports a geometry failure must be re-run after the build stage so the offending geometry is corrected before the check is scored.

a site area labelled as a built outdoor.rule: A site area labelled as a built outdoor space (veranda, balcony) must be built with its outline and structure, not left as an unrecognised open deck.

a stair piece must be assigned to a hall.rule: A stair piece must be assigned to a hall or dedicated stairwell room, never to a kitchen or other habitable room; the reading stage must re-assign a stair found inside a kitchen to the nearest hall or stairwell.

a furniture piece present in the decor s.rule: A furniture piece present in the decor stage must survive the agent stage; if it is dropped, the agent stage must be re-run to restore it.

a sink_kitchen piece must be built with.rule: A sink_kitchen piece must be built with a valid library model; if the current model is not built, swap to a valid model of the same type.

a door that must be shown in a view must.rule: A door that must be shown in a view must be included in the view's show list so the camera frames it.

drawings on the furniture layer that rep.rule: Drawings on the furniture layer that represent a sofa and chairs around a table must be read as furniture pieces, not lost.

a second label of a room that names a di.rule: A second label of a room that names a distinct space (ANTRE) must be read as a separate room, not as a second label of the existing room.

a dresser named in the documents must be.rule: A dresser named in the documents must be read as a furniture piece in the model.

a bookshelf piece that is not built must.rule: A bookshelf piece that is not built must be swapped to a valid library model of the same type.

an ottoman piece that is not built must.rule: An ottoman piece that is not built must be swapped to a valid library model of the same type.

a drawn nightstand that cannot be placed.rule: A drawn nightstand that cannot be placed because the bed's footprint leaves no room is a layout conflict, not a reason to drop the piece: the furniture stage must re-solve the sleeping group (bed + nightstands) as one unit so the nightstand keeps its drawn place, rather than deleting it.

a labelled outdoor space (veranda, balco.rule: A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) that the documents outline must be built as a structured outdoor space (floor, guard on open edges, and a light roof where the plan shows one), not left as an unmodelled label.

a dressing room whose drawn wardrobe lea.rule: A dressing room whose drawn wardrobe leaves no free span for the dressing group (mirror, bench) must have its wardrobe re-placed or the room re-typed so the defining pieces fit, rather than being left functionally empty.

a kitchen whose drawn counter run leaves.rule: A kitchen whose drawn counter run leaves no free span for the missing fridge (or whose relayout is blocked by the aisle rule) must have the counter run re-solved as one unit with the fridge included, rather than being left functionally empty.

a bathroom fixture listed in the room's.rule: A bathroom fixture listed in the room's pieces but absent from the render must be given a real library model (not a parametric mesh) so it is built and visible.

a bathroom camera that points at a corne.rule: A bathroom camera that points at a corner and misses the primary fixtures (washbasin, toilet) must be re-aimed to show the main function of the space.

a bathroom camera that misses the primar.rule: A bathroom camera that misses the primary fixtures (shower, toilet, basin) must be re-aimed to show the main function of the space.

a dressing room camera that cuts off the.rule: A dressing room camera that cuts off the main furniture (wardrobes) and shows no defining pieces must be re-aimed to show the space's function.

a stair read into a kitchen (or any room.rule: A stair read into a kitchen (or any room where a stair does not belong) must be re-read as the missing kitchen fixture (fridge) if its size and position match, or removed if it is a misread symbol, rather than being left as a stair in the kitchen.

a door read from its lines (no swing arc.rule: A door read from its lines (no swing arc) in an outer wall that is blocked by a drawn piece (no passage) must be re-read as a window at the floor's sill.

a gap in an outer wall that is blocked b.rule: A gap in an outer wall that is blocked by drawn pieces (no passage) must be re-read as a window at the floor's sill.

a door read from its lines (no swing arc.rule: A door read from its lines (no swing arc) in an outer wall that is blocked by drawn pieces (no passage) must be re-read as a window at the floor's sill.

a door read from lines without a swing a.rule: A door read from lines without a swing arc in an outer wall, whose approach is blocked by furniture, is a window at the floor's sill, not a door.

a gap in an outer wall blocked by furnit.rule: A gap in an outer wall blocked by furniture is a window, not a door.

a wall cabinet must not be placed over a.rule: A wall cabinet must not be placed over a window; if no free wall span exists, it must be removed or the window moved.

furniture must not cover a window openin.rule: Furniture must not cover a window opening.

every room must be reachable from the en.rule: Every room must be reachable from the entrance through doors, openings, or stairs.

every floor must be reachable from the e.rule: Every floor must be reachable from the entrance.

a piece that blocks the ray through a wi.rule: A piece that blocks the ray through a window or door opening is a placement error: the fitting stage must keep the clear zone of every opening free of furniture, or move the piece to the nearest free spot.

a washbasin in a bathroom is always acco.rule: A washbasin in a bathroom is always accompanied by a mirror above it; the bathroom_set group must include a mirror as a mandatory member.

a door leaf must be built with its frame.rule: A door leaf must be built with its frame and threshold at the correct floor level; a floating door leaf indicates a missing frame or a level mismatch in the door builder.

a site area marked 'not built (no outlin.rule: A site area marked 'NOT built (no outline)' that is referenced by a door or window in the plan must be built as an outdoor space with a floor slab and guard rails; the site stage must not skip it.

a kitchen must have a continuous run of.rule: A kitchen must have a continuous run of base cabinets, wall cabinets, and appliances; the kitchen_run group must be placed as a single unit.

a door that opens onto an outdoor space.rule: A door that opens onto an outdoor space must have that outdoor space built; the site stage must build the balcony or terrace before the door is placed.

the garden must include planted beds, sh.rule: The garden must include planted beds, shrubs, ground cover, and a path or parking area; the site stage must not leave it as bare flat grass.

a veranda or balcony marked 'not built (.rule: A veranda or balcony marked 'NOT built (no outline)' must be built with a floor slab, guard rails, and a roof if drawn; the site stage must not skip it.

an entrance door must have a proper appr.rule: An entrance door must have a proper approach with steps, a landing, and cheek walls; the site stage must build the entrance solution.

a door that is blocked by furniture and.rule: A door that is blocked by furniture and has no outside passage is a reading error; it should be read as a window at the floor's sill height.

the pipeline must not end in 'pending' w.rule: The pipeline must not end in 'pending' with recognition questions written; it must resolve all recognition questions before completing.

a washing machine's front must face a fr.rule: A washing machine's front must face a free side with at least 0.45 m clearance; the reading stage must verify the front direction against the room geometry.

a scene check failure for a built decor.rule: A scene check failure for a built decor item must be resolved before the level is marked complete; the build stage must verify all decor items against the scene checks.

the big loop must run at least one full.rule: The big loop must run at least one full cycle before stopping; a zero-cycle stop with no gain is a failure to attempt, not a valid convergence.

views marked for review must be resolved.rule: Views marked for review must be resolved by the agent in the next round; a check finding is not a fix.

when a piece blocks a door or window and.rule: When a piece blocks a door or window and cannot be moved due to snap constraints, swap it for a narrower model that fits the available wall span.

when a tv unit cannot snap to a wall due.rule: When a TV unit cannot snap to a wall due to openings, swap for a model with a different depth or width that allows a valid placement.

when a bed model is rated as a 'crude pl.rule: When a bed model is rated as a 'crude placeholder' but higher-rated models are refused due to quality gates, swap for a generated model that offers better visual detail even if its library rating is lower, provided it fits the room.

dressing rooms must include a dressing t.rule: Dressing rooms must include a dressing table or vanity group with accessories (mirror, stool, decor) to satisfy the 'styled surfaces' requirement; a wardrobe alone is insufficient.

bedrooms should have a feature wall (e.g.rule: Bedrooms should have a feature wall (e.g., slatted wood, paneling) behind the bed to add visual interest and match the reference style.

nightstands in master bedrooms must be s.rule: Nightstands in master bedrooms must be styled with accessories (books, vases, art) to avoid looking bare.

living rooms must include a large area r.rule: Living rooms must include a large area rug under the seating group to anchor the space.

bedrooms should have a feature wall (e.g.rule: Bedrooms should have a feature wall (e.g., paneling) behind the bed to add visual interest.

bathroom cameras must show the main fixt.rule: Bathroom cameras must show the main fixtures (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) to demonstrate the room's function and style.

bathtub surrounds should use warm wood t.rule: Bathtub surrounds should use warm wood tones to match the project's aesthetic, not dark untextured panels.

bathroom walls should use large-format p.rule: Bathroom walls should use large-format porcelain tiles or stone to create a cohesive, high-end look, not flat cold white tiles.

bathroom cameras must show the vanity un.rule: Bathroom cameras must show the vanity unit and mirror to capture the room's style.

kitchen cameras must show the kitchen ru.rule: Kitchen cameras must show the kitchen run, island, and appliances, not just the dining nook.

kitchen cameras must focus on the kitche.rule: Kitchen cameras must focus on the kitchen functional group, not the dining table.

a kitchen's program must include a style.rule: A kitchen's program must include a styled-surface layer (small decor on the counter and island: a kettle, a fruit bowl, a cutting board) placed by the furniture agent, not only the functional run; a bare counter is a failed kitchen render.

a bathroom's program must include a mirr.rule: A bathroom's program must include a mirror above the washbasin; a bare wall above the basin is a failed bathroom render.

a bedroom window's program must include.rule: A bedroom window's program must include a full-height two-layer curtain treatment (sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track; a single short sheer panel is a failed bedroom render.
A bedroom window's program must include a full-height two-layer curtain treatment (sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track; a single flat white panel is a failed bedroom render.

an interior camera of a small wet room m.rule: An interior camera of a small wet room must be posed from a free point with headroom that shows the room's main fixtures (shower, basin, toilet), never from a corner framing a wall and a door leaf.

a second interior view of a small room m.rule: A second interior view of a small room must frame the room as a whole, not a close-up of one fixture.

two armchairs placed as a pair in one ro.rule: Two armchairs placed as a pair in one room must share a coherent style and palette; when they do not, swap the one that breaks the set to a model that matches its partner.

a piece listed in a room's program that.rule: A piece listed in a room's program that is 'not built' must be built (or the room re-laid out) before the room is judged; a bare wall where a drawn work set belongs is a missing piece, not a styling gap.

an interior camera of a hall must show t.rule: An interior camera of a hall must show the hall's functional furniture (shoe cabinet, bench, console), not a bare blank wall.

a hall's entrance group is not complete.rule: A hall's entrance group is not complete with only a shoe cabinet; the furniture agent must add the missing styled layer (bench, hooks, mirror) that the reference shows.

an interior camera of a small hall must.rule: An interior camera of a small hall must show the console and the space, not be jammed into the corner between the door and a wall.

a bed's layered bedding (duvet, second b.rule: A bed's layered bedding (duvet, second blanket, euro shams, decorative cushion) is a styling layer the furniture agent must add; a model swap that lowers the rating is not the fix.

windows in a furnished bedroom must carr.rule: Windows in a furnished bedroom must carry layered curtains (sheer plus drape on a track); bare windows are a missing styling layer the furniture agent must add.

nightstands and dressers in a furnished.rule: Nightstands and dressers in a furnished bedroom must carry styled surfaces (vase, books, mirror, leaning art); bare tops are a missing styling layer the furniture agent must add.

an interior camera of a small room must.rule: An interior camera of a small room must show the room's main furniture and layout, not be pressed against a door and a wardrobe edge.

a second interior view of a small room m.rule: A second interior view of a small room must show the room and its furniture, not a close-up of a wall corner and door edge.

when a drawn piece is identified as a de.rule: When a drawn piece is identified as a detail of a larger piece (e.g., a sink bowl or appliance front) but an AI pass names it as a distinct furniture type that fits its size, the reading stage must not discard it as a detail if the AI naming is plausible and the piece is not fully contained within the larger piece's functional zone.

the reading stage must process all entit.rule: The reading stage must process all entity types present in the source DWG file, including ATTDEF entities, to ensure no data is lost during the initial parsing phase.

the reading stage must correctly associa.rule: The reading stage must correctly associate site decor elements with the appropriate level (L0 for ground floor site elements) and ensure that decor read outside the walls of upper levels is not duplicated or lost.

when a room outline holds multiple label.rule: When a room outline holds multiple labels for distinct functional zones (e.g., 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ'), the reading stage must split the room into separate entities if the labels represent distinct spaces with their own areas, rather than treating them as a single room with multiple labels.

layers named after fixtures (e.g. 'deniz.rule: Layers named after fixtures (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' for washbasin) that contain only line entities and no corresponding built fixture in the model should be checked: if the fixture is already built from another layer or source, the layer is redundant and the warning should be suppressed; if the fixture is missing, the layer's geometry should be used to place it.

when an opening is read twice (duplicate.rule: When an opening is read twice (duplicate) and the build stage drops it, the build stage should check if the opening is a duplicate of an already-built opening (same wall, same position within tolerance). If it is a true duplicate, suppress the warning; if it is a distinct opening that was lost, rebuild it.

when decor elements are not built becaus.rule: When decor elements are not built because their host piece is not built, the build stage should either (a) build the host piece, or (b) re-parent the decor elements to the room directly so they are built independently, or (c) explicitly mark them as not built with a clear reason. Silently dropping them is a loss.

living rooms should include a rug under.rule: Living rooms should include a rug under the seating area as part of the default decor set. The rug should be placed under the sofa and coffee table, sized to cover the seating group, and should not block door walkways.

bathrooms with a washbasin should includ.rule: Bathrooms with a washbasin should include a mirror over the washbasin as part of the default bathroom set. The mirror should be placed on the wall above the washbasin, centered, at a standard height.

a parametric opening in the style's fini.rule: A parametric opening in the style's finish is an acceptable build when no library model of the building's window family fits the opening's dimensions; it is not a defect.

when a piece is built with a parametric.rule: When a piece is built with a parametric mesh because no library model fits, the fitting stage must record the piece's room and id so that a later swap_model or retype can target it; otherwise the library gap is unfixable by the agent.

a kitchen counter or island in a furnish.rule: A kitchen counter or island in a furnished render should carry at least one small appliance or decor item to avoid reading as an unfinished worktop.

a shower in a bathroom render should hav.rule: A shower in a bathroom render should have a clear glass screen or proper tiling definition; a flat, untextured surface reads as a placeholder.

nightstands in a bedroom should match th.rule: Nightstands in a bedroom should match the wood tone of the room's feature wall panelling to avoid introducing a clashing third wood tone.

a bedroom in a furnished render should h.rule: A bedroom in a furnished render should have at least two layers of light (e.g., a statement fixture over the bed plus bedside lamps) to match the project's style.

doors in a furnished render should have.rule: Doors in a furnished render should have a wood tone and hardware that match the project's style; plain flat slabs with a single handle read as generic wardrobes.

a hall in a furnished render should have.rule: A hall in a furnished render should have a rug to ground the space and add warmth, especially when the reference shows one.

doors in a furnished render should have.rule: Doors in a furnished render should have a wood tone and hardware that match the project's style; plain flat slabs in a pale wood read as generic placeholders.

a wardrobe model whose doors render as f.rule: A wardrobe model whose doors render as flat, untextured colour blocks is a low-quality asset: swap it for a library model of the same family with real door material, never move the piece to hide the look.

a facade that reads as flat planes with.rule: A facade that reads as flat planes with simple reveals needs a material with real surface breaks (render/plaster with texture, or a cladding) rather than a single flat colour; set the facade slot to a textured exterior look.

when a bedroom's tv unit has no suitable.rule: When a bedroom's TV unit has no suitable opposite wall for a media wall (due to openings, doors, or room shape), the TV unit should be repositioned to a side wall or removed if no valid placement exists, rather than leaving it in a position with no viewing wall.

a cushion placed on a bed must sit on th.rule: A cushion placed on a bed must sit on the mattress surface; its bottom must not penetrate the bed frame or mattress by more than 0.03 m.

every site area labeled in the documents.rule: Every site area labeled in the documents (parking, terrace, pool, etc.) must be built in the model with its outline and appropriate ground treatment.

every room labeled in the documents must.rule: Every room labeled in the documents must be created in the model with its correct label, level, and area.

a wardrobe must have at least 0.50 m of.rule: A wardrobe must have at least 0.50 m of clear space in front of it for its doors to open and be used.

any decorative or furniture piece placed.rule: Any decorative or furniture piece placed on the top floor must be checked against the underside of the roof (including mansard slopes); if its top exceeds the roof line, it must be lowered, resized, or removed so nothing pokes through the roof.

ceiling lights must be hung with a visib.rule: Ceiling lights must be hung with a visible connection (cord, rod, or canopy) to the ceiling; if no hang record exists, the light must be re-placed with a proper hang fixture or removed.

a scene check that fails on a level afte.rule: A scene check that fails on a level after the build stage is a build-stage defect: rerun the build stage so the level's geometry is regenerated and re-checked.

when an armchair faces the back of a sof.rule: When an armchair faces the back of a sofa and both rotate and swap are refused, the furniture agent's next round must re-place the seating group so the armchair faces the coffee table, not the sofa's back.

a wardrobe that crosses the room outline.rule: A wardrobe that crosses the room outline by a few centimetres must be nudged back inside the wall line by the furniture agent, not left protruding.

a coffee table that overlaps an armchair.rule: A coffee table that overlaps an armchair must be re-placed by the furniture agent so the seating group clears; a move that only trades one overlap for another is refused.

an armchair whose front use zone is not.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the furniture agent to open the circulation path.

a sofa whose front use zone is not reach.rule: A sofa whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the furniture agent to open the circulation path.

a floor lamp that stands in front of a w.rule: A floor lamp that stands in front of a window and blocks its light must be moved by the furniture agent to a free spot away from the window.

a stove whose back is not on a wall must.rule: A stove whose back is not on a wall must be snapped back onto the kitchen run by the furniture agent; a stove floating off the counter line is a misplacement.

a kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in.rule: A kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in front of the counter must be opened by the furniture agent re-placing the kitchen run or the island to restore the working aisle.

a stove is a wall fixture: its back must.rule: A stove is a wall fixture: its back must sit on the kitchen run's wall, not float 6 cm off it.

a kitchen run must leave at least 0.90 m.rule: A kitchen run must leave at least 0.90 m of aisle in front of it.

a seating group's chairs must face the g.rule: A seating group's chairs must face the group's centre; when individual rotations and moves keep failing, re-solve the whole room's AI layout.

a dining chair needs at least 0.81 m fro.rule: A dining chair needs at least 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall; a sof.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall; a sofa floating 2 m from any wall is a mis-placed piece.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall..rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall.

a seating group's chairs must face the g.rule: A seating group's chairs must face the group's centre.

a double bed needs at least 0.60 m of fr.rule: A double bed needs at least 0.60 m of free space along each side.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window (sill + 0.05 m).

a wardrobe needs at least 0.80 m of free.rule: A wardrobe needs at least 0.80 m of free space in front of it.

a shower whose drawn footprint is outsid.rule: A shower whose drawn footprint is outside the product range of its assigned model must be swapped to a model whose real size fits the drawn bay, not left at a non-existent size.

when a drawn shower's size is within tol.rule: When a drawn shower's size is within tolerance of the real range but its assigned model does not match, swap to a model whose real size matches the drawn footprint rather than resizing or rotating.

when a bed's side clearance is below the.rule: When a bed's side clearance is below the minimum and moving it individually worsens other findings, re-layout the whole room so the solver can place the bed with adequate clearance on both sides.

when a wardrobe's front clearance is bel.rule: When a wardrobe's front clearance is below the minimum and no free wall span exists within the allowed move distance, re-layout the room to find a placement with adequate clearance.

when a bed's side clearance is below the.rule: When a bed's side clearance is below the minimum, re-layout the room so the solver can place the bed with adequate clearance.

when a wardrobe's front clearance is bel.rule: When a wardrobe's front clearance is below the minimum and moving it does not resolve the finding, re-layout the room.

when a sofa's free zone in front is bloc.rule: When a sofa's free zone in front is blocked by another piece, re-layout the room so the solver can arrange the seating group with clear sight and access lines.

when a coffee table is not in front of t.rule: When a coffee table is not in front of the sofa, re-layout the room so the seating group is arranged correctly.

when an armchair is too far from the cof.rule: When an armchair is too far from the coffee table or at the wrong angle, re-layout the room to fix the seating group geometry.

when a chair's clearance behind is below.rule: When a chair's clearance behind is below the minimum, re-layout the room to fix the dining group spacing.

when a sofa's free zone in front is bloc.rule: When a sofa's free zone in front is blocked by another piece, re-layout the room.

when a coffee table is not in front of t.rule: When a coffee table is not in front of the sofa and individual moves are refused due to drawn-lock constraints, re-layout the room.

when an armchair is too far from the cof.rule: When an armchair is too far from the coffee table or at the wrong angle, re-layout the room.

when a dining table stands in front of a.rule: When a dining table stands in front of a window, re-layout the room to move the dining group away from the window.

when a chair stands in front of a window.rule: When a chair stands in front of a window, re-layout the room to move the dining group away from the window.

inspector findings must name the piece b.rule: Inspector findings must name the piece by its recorded type and room, not by a guessed label; a wall_cabinet in a kitchen is a valid upper cabinet and is not a shoe cabinet.

the furniture agent must not drop a plac.rule: The furniture agent must not drop a placed dining table from a room's set; a dining table is a core member of the dining group and must be re-placed if it is lost between the decor and agent stages.

the furniture agent must not drop a dini.rule: The furniture agent must not drop a dining chair that belongs to a placed dining table; chairs are members of the dining group and must be re-placed if lost.

the furniture agent must not drop a plac.rule: The furniture agent must not drop a placed decorative piece (potted plant) from a room; decor pieces placed in the decor stage must be preserved through the agent stage.
The furniture agent must not drop a placed lighting piece (floor lamp) from a room; lighting pieces placed in the decor stage must be preserved through the agent stage.
The furniture agent must not drop a placed seating accessory (ottoman) from a room; seating accessories placed in the decor stage must be preserved through the agent stage.

the furniture agent must not drop a nigh.rule: The furniture agent must not drop a nightstand that belongs to a placed bed; a nightstand is a member of the sleeping group and must be re-placed if lost.

the furniture agent must not drop a plac.rule: The furniture agent must not drop a placed media unit (tv_unit) from a living room; a tv_unit is a core member of the living set and must be re-placed if lost.
The furniture agent must not drop a placed storage piece (sideboard) from a living room; a sideboard is a member of the living storage set and must be re-placed if lost.

the build stage must place every planned.rule: The build stage must place every planned kitchen fixture (stove, sink, counter) in the scene; a planned stove that has no scene object is a build failure and must be re-run.

a planned piece that the build stage lea.rule: A planned piece that the build stage leaves without a scene object is a build loss, not a reading error: the build stage must place every planned piece or record why it cannot.

a stair core that fills its room has no.rule: A stair core that fills its room has no free interior camera point; the stair must be shown from the adjoining hall, not from inside the stair.

a piece of the final stage that the buil.rule: A piece of the final stage that the build stage drops (named in a conflict) is a build loss: the build stage must keep every final-stage piece or record why it removed it.

when a level is duplicated (two rooms wi.rule: When a level is duplicated (two rooms with identical area and identical piece lists), the duplicate is a build-stage artifact; findings on the duplicate that are satisfied by the original room are not real losses.

in a bathroom smaller than 6 m2, if the.rule: In a bathroom smaller than 6 m2, if the toilet's side clearance is under 0.38 m and no model swap or rotation can fix it, the finding is a room-size constraint, not a fixable placement error; flag it for architect review rather than looping on model swaps.

In a bathroom smaller than 6 m2, if the bathtub's front clearance is under 0.53 m and the drawn size is within 30% of the real range, the shortfall is a room-size constraint; flag for architect review rather than looping on model swaps.

in a bathroom smaller than 5 m2, if the.rule: In a bathroom smaller than 5 m2, if the shower's front clearance is under 0.53 m and the drawn size is within 30% of the real range, the shortfall is a room-size constraint; flag for architect review rather than looping on model swaps.

In a bathroom smaller than 5 m2, if the shower's front clearance is under 0.53 m and both fix_fixture and rotate_piece are refused, the shortfall is a room-size constraint; flag for architect review rather than looping on model swaps.

in a bathroom under a sloped ceiling whe.rule: In a bathroom under a sloped ceiling where the height limit prevents model swaps, if the toilet's side clearance is under 0.38 m, the finding is a room-size and ceiling-height constraint; flag for architect review rather than looping on model swaps.

a drawn bathtub or shower up to 5 cm lon.rule: A drawn bathtub or shower up to 5 cm longer than its bay is a misread size: without center, the code moves it to the nearest valid spot that clears the required front clearance.

a toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m fr.rule: A toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m from a side wall or fixture is a placement problem: fix_fixture without center moves it to the nearest valid spot that clears the side clearance.

a washbasin that fails the fit rules und.rule: A washbasin that fails the fit rules under a sloped ceiling (height cap) must take a lower library model that fits the ceiling.

a room typed 'other' that is furnished a.rule: A room typed 'other' that is furnished as a living room (sofa, armchairs, coffee table, dining table) and whose twin is typed 'living' must be retyped to 'living'.

the number of storeys in the model must.rule: The number of storeys in the model must match the number of storeys shown in the section drawing; if the section shows two storeys, the model must not have more than two levels (excluding basements and terraces).

an opening that is not cut through its w.rule: An opening that is not cut through its wall (the door ray hits the wall) must be fixed by putting the opening back on its wall.

a stair flight must have a handrail over.rule: A stair flight must have a handrail over at least 0.72 m of its run; if it does not, the build stage must add a continuous balustrade with newels at its turns and ends, its handrail over the nosing line, stopped under the slab and beside the floor guard of the level above, and a wall handrail where a flight has none.

a frontal view of the entrance (+y) faca.rule: A frontal view of the entrance (+y) facade must be added if it is missing.

if the terrain slopes up to 1:0.3 (steep.rule: If the terrain slopes up to 1:0.3 (steeper than 1:3), a retaining edge must be built to prevent erosion and ensure stability.

a kitchen counter whose top is over its.rule: A kitchen counter whose top is over its working height (0.97 m) must take a model that fits the working height.

a dining table on an outdoor terrace mus.rule: A dining table on an outdoor terrace must take a lighter, weather-resistant model that is appropriate for outdoor use.

a stair drawn as a slab outline must be.rule: A stair drawn as a slab outline must be built as a full stair (stringers, supports, connection to the floor it lands on); a floating slab with no supports is a build failure, not a drawing feature.

the entrance area must be built as a con.rule: The entrance area must be built as a continuous, connected path (steps, landing, railings) from the ground to the door; floating or disconnected elements are a build failure.

site areas that are drawn in the plan (p.rule: Site areas that are drawn in the plan (pools, terraces) must be registered with their outlines even if the geometry is built separately; 'NOT built (no outline)' for a drawn site area is a loss.

a kitchen counter must be at working hei.rule: A kitchen counter must be at working height (0.85-0.95 m) with at least 0.90 m aisle in front; a counter at 1.18 m with a 0.55 m aisle is not usable.

the storey count in the model must match.rule: The storey count in the model must match the section; a two-storey section must not produce a 3-storey model (L0, L1 plus basement pair).

room names must be unique per level; two.rule: Room names must be unique per level; two rooms both named 'Yatak Odası 2' on L0 is a reading error that suggests the documents label them as distinct bedrooms.

a drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a side in a living room is likely a group of drawn pieces that the reading stage failed to split; it must be decomposed into individual furniture items.

a roof terrace drawn in the plan with a.rule: A roof terrace drawn in the plan with a door to it must have the roof cut over it; the roof stage must recognize terrace rooms and cut the roof accordingly.

a door whose head would rise above the r.rule: A door whose head would rise above the roof underside at its wall is not a usable door: the roof stage must provide a dormer (or the door is re-read as a window) before the build places it; a door clipped under a sloped roof is a defect, not a placement.

a stage that ends 'pending' with written.rule: A stage that ends 'pending' with written questions must be answered in the next agent round before the run is considered complete; pending questions are a defect, not a normal stop.

a sofa's front is its long side; a front.rule: A sofa's front is its long side; a front read on the short side is a recognition error and must be corrected to the long side facing the most open room.

a bench's front is its long side; a fron.rule: A bench's front is its long side; a front read on the short side is a recognition error and must be corrected to the long side, with its back on the wall.

a scene check failure on a built decor i.rule: A scene check failure on a built decor item must be resolved in the next agent round by inspecting the scene check output and correcting the item; a failed scene check is a defect, not a normal stop.

the big loop must run at least one cycle.rule: The big loop must run at least one cycle and raise the house score before the run is considered complete; 0 cycles with no score improvement is a defect.

views marked for review must be inspecte.rule: Views marked for review must be inspected and corrected in the next agent round; a view left in review is a defect, not a normal stop.

the build stage must record a leaf state.rule: The build stage must record a leaf state (open or closed) for every inside door; an inside door stands open by default (UL116), and a door with no recorded leaf state is a defect.

the build stage must open a door when a.rule: The build stage must open a door when a camera view looks through it into a room worth showing (UL126); a view that shows only a closed door where an open door would reveal a room is a defect.

when a tv_unit (or similar long low piec.rule: When a tv_unit (or similar long low piece) cannot be placed on any wall span because doors and windows block all free stretches, the agent must either (a) swap to a shorter model that fits a free span, or (b) the room's wall layout must be re-read; a tv_unit that cannot rest on a wall is a defect that requires a model swap or a geometry correction, not repeated move attempts.

when a nightstand stands in front of a w.rule: When a nightstand stands in front of a window and cannot be moved (overlaps the bed) or swapped (style/fit mismatch), the window's sill must be raised (raise_sill to 0.90 m) or the nightstand must be removed; a nightstand blocking a window is a defect that requires a window adjustment or piece removal, not repeated move/swap attempts.

a seating group (sofa, armchairs, lounge.rule: A seating group (sofa, armchairs, lounge chairs) must be chosen from one style family and a coherent palette; the furniture agent must verify the set before placing, and a single clashing piece is a defect of the whole group.

every visible horizontal surface in a fu.rule: Every visible horizontal surface in a furnished room (coffee table, TV unit, sideboard) must carry styled decor objects; a bare surface is a defect.

a client-facing render must show a coher.rule: A client-facing render must show a coherent, styled room (matching furniture set, rug, layered lighting, styled surfaces); a flat 'grey box' render is a defect.

a large seating group must sit on a rug.rule: A large seating group must sit on a rug that anchors the room; a bare floor under the main seating is a defect.

full-height window walls in a living roo.rule: Full-height window walls in a living room must have layered curtains (sheer and drape); bare glass is a defect.

every visible horizontal surface in a fu.rule: Every visible horizontal surface in a furnished room must carry styled decor objects; a bare surface is a defect.

a seating group (sofa, armchairs, dining.rule: A seating group (sofa, armchairs, dining chairs) must be chosen from one style family and a coherent palette; a single clashing piece is a defect of the whole group.

a client-facing render must show a coher.rule: A client-facing render must show a coherent, styled room (matching furniture set, styled surfaces, proper lighting); a flat 'grey box' render is a defect.

dining chairs at one table must be a mat.rule: Dining chairs at one table must be a matching set in style and colour; a single clashing chair is a defect.

a dining table in a furnished room must.rule: A dining table in a furnished room must carry a table setting (plates, glasses, centerpiece); a bare table is a defect.

a bathroom render must show the main fix.rule: A bathroom render must show the main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) and styled surfaces with warm lighting; a render that omits the bathtub is a defect.

a bathroom must have warm, layered light.rule: A bathroom must have warm, layered lighting that creates an inviting glow and contrast; flat grey lighting is a defect.

a bathroom camera must frame the room as.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room as a whole, showing the main fixtures; a close-up of a corner or a single small object is a defect.
A bathroom camera must frame the room as a whole, showing the main fixtures; a tight close-up that omits the main fixtures is a defect.
A bathroom camera must frame the room as a whole, showing the main fixtures; a camera positioned too close and at an awkward angle is a defect.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's layout and main fixtures; a close-up that fails to show the layout is a defect.

an interior camera must be posed to show.rule: An interior camera must be posed to show the room's doors, windows and openings, not pressed against a bare wall corner.

a hall or living room render must includ.rule: A hall or living room render must include a rug or floor treatment to define the space; a bare flat floor is not client-ready.

furniture in a living room must be a coh.rule: Furniture in a living room must be a coherent, styled set matching the project's modern aesthetic; blocky low-poly placeholders and mismatched traditional pieces are not acceptable.

a sofa model must match the room's moder.rule: A sofa model must match the room's modern/minimal aesthetic; blocky low-poly placeholders with crude piping are not acceptable.

a dining table must match the room's mod.rule: A dining table must match the room's modern/minimal aesthetic; a dark traditional table with turned legs is a mismatch.

a sofa model must match the room's moder.rule: A sofa model must match the room's modern/minimal aesthetic; bare boxy models without styling are not acceptable.

a living room render must include a rug.rule: A living room render must include a rug to anchor the seating area; a bare flat floor is not client-ready.

a living room render must include stylin.rule: A living room render must include styling layers (rug, art, soft furnishings) to be client-ready; a grey-box placeholder is not acceptable.

a large empty wall behind a sofa in a li.rule: A large empty wall behind a sofa in a living room must have art, panels, or texture; a completely bare wall is a significant omission.

furniture in a living room must be a coh.rule: Furniture in a living room must be a coherent, styled set; mismatched blocky models are not client-ready.

the exterior environment in a render mus.rule: The exterior environment in a render must have realistic ground texture, varied vegetation, and a proper sky; a flat untextured green field with low-poly lollipop trees is not client-ready.

the view through a window must show a re.rule: The view through a window must show a realistic landscape with depth, vegetation, and ground detail; a flat untextured green plane is not acceptable.

a potted plant model must look realistic.rule: A potted plant model must look realistic with variation and texture; crude low-poly clumps of blades are not acceptable.

a balcony dining table should have a tab.rule: A balcony dining table should have a table setting to look lived-in; a bare table is not client-ready.

balcony chairs must match the table's st.rule: Balcony chairs must match the table's style; white plastic garden chairs with an industrial metal table look accidental and cheap.

the exterior environment in a render mus.rule: The exterior environment in a render must have realistic ground texture, varied vegetation, and a proper sky; a broken grey-box environment undermines the render.

outdoor terrace furniture must be a cohe.rule: Outdoor terrace furniture must be a coherent set (matching material family) and the ground must carry a real grass texture, not a flat green plane.

the site ground must be given a real gra.rule: The site ground must be given a real grass (or paving) look, never a flat untextured green plane.

exterior presentation renders must show.rule: Exterior presentation renders must show finished facade materials, landscaping and warm lighting, not a grey-box massing.

exterior night/evening renders must incl.rule: Exterior night/evening renders must include warm interior lighting so rooms glow through the glazing.

exterior renders must show a structurall.rule: Exterior renders must show a structurally supported staircase and finished materials, not a floating stair in a void.

an exterior view must be framed at eye l.rule: An exterior view must be framed at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or above the ridge, never pressed against a wall from above the roofline.

exterior presentation renders must show.rule: Exterior presentation renders must show finished materials, landscaping and depth, not a sterile grey-box void.
Exterior presentation renders must show the specified cladding, landscaping and architectural detailing, not a raw massing study.

every drawn furniture symbol must be typ.rule: Every drawn furniture symbol must be typed by a rule or model; if a symbol cannot be matched to a known type, the reading stage must flag it for manual typing rather than leaving it 'unknown' and unbuilt.

decor that cannot find a valid resting s.rule: Decor that cannot find a valid resting surface on its host is correctly left unbuilt rather than floating.

decor that penetrates its host beyond to.rule: Decor that penetrates its host beyond tolerance is correctly left unbuilt rather than showing the host through the cloth.

decor that cannot rest within tolerance.rule: Decor that cannot rest within tolerance of its host is correctly left unbuilt rather than floating.

a small decor item (plant, book, throw).rule: A small decor item (plant, book, throw) assigned to a host whose built top is not a single flat surface (no top found, or the top tears) must be dropped from the scene rather than left as a failed, un-built rest; the decor stage should verify the host exposes a flat top before placing it.

a soft decor (throw) must not be placed.rule: A soft decor (throw) must not be placed on a host whose top is not one continuous surface (tears > 0.25 m) or that pokes through the cloth; the decor stage should drop it.

a decor item whose rest gap to its host.rule: A decor item whose rest gap to its host exceeds 0.01 m must be dropped rather than left un-built.

a small decor item assigned to a host wi.rule: A small decor item assigned to a host with no built top must be dropped from the scene.

every camera dropped by the camera stage.rule: Every camera dropped by the camera stage must carry a recorded reason (e.g. blocked, duplicate, bare wall); a drop with no reason is a defect and the view must be restored.

a drawn block whose name and size match.rule: A drawn block whose name and size match a known fixture (e.g. a small cabinet or appliance) must be mapped to a piece in the model; an unmapped named block is a reading loss.

a drawn block named 'merdiven' (stair) m.rule: A drawn block named 'merdiven' (stair) must be mapped to a stair piece in the model; an unmapped stair block is a reading loss.

a drawn block whose name is not a known.rule: A drawn block whose name is not a known furniture or fixture symbol and whose size does not match any buildable piece is recorded as a drawing mark, not a lost element.

a drawn block that is site decor (landsc.rule: A drawn block that is site decor (landscaping, paving, pool furniture) is recorded as a site symbol, not a lost interior element.

a drawn stair symbol that is already rep.rule: A drawn stair symbol that is already represented by a built stair piece in the model is not a lost element.

blocks under 0.10 m on one side that sit.rule: Blocks under 0.10 m on one side that sit on dimension or annotation layers are marks, not furniture or structure, and are not built.

sheet-frame and title-block blocks are d.rule: Sheet-frame and title-block blocks are drawing furniture, not building elements, and are never built into the model.

small square symbol blocks that are tags.rule: Small square symbol blocks that are tags or markers rather than furniture footprints are not built; only blocks whose size and context match a furniture or fixture type are modelled.

entities on layers that are off or froze.rule: Entities on layers that are off or frozen in the source DWG are not read, because the author has hidden them from the active design.

ole2frame and wipeout entities are non-g.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are non-geometric (embedded objects and masks) and are never read as building elements.

structural columns that stand out of the.rule: Structural columns that stand out of the wall band are not modelled as walls; they are separate structural elements outside the wall-building scope.

a drawn symbol that both reading passes.rule: A drawn symbol that both reading passes classify as not_furniture is kept as an obstacle and not built, unless an architect action reclassifies it.

elements drawn on structural layers (e.g.rule: Elements drawn on structural layers (e.g. 'A-BA') are treated as structure, not furniture, and are not built as furniture pieces.

a small drawn piece (tap, drain, handle).rule: A small drawn piece (tap, drain, handle) that sits 60% or more inside a larger fixture of the same set is a part of that fixture, not a duplicate; the reading merges it and the ledger must not flag the merge as a lost piece.

when two pieces of the same type overlap.rule: When two pieces of the same type overlap and one is drawn inside the other, the larger is the piece and the smaller is its inner symbol (shade, base); the reading keeps the larger and the ledger must not flag the inner symbol as a lost piece.

layers whose name indicates 2d annotatio.rule: Layers whose name indicates 2D annotation (axis bubbles, dimensions, text) are not part of the 3D model; the ledger must not flag their entities as lost.

layers whose name indicates decoration o.rule: Layers whose name indicates decoration or finish (tile patterns, floor texture) are not part of the 3D model; the ledger must not flag their entities as lost.

layers whose name indicates finish or an.rule: Layers whose name indicates finish or annotation (vitrification, coating) are not part of the 3D model; the ledger must not flag their entities as lost.

the agent must not remove a piece that i.rule: The agent must not remove a piece that is the defining fixture of a room's program (e.g. a shoe cabinet in a hall) unless the room's program explicitly excludes it.

when the build stage drops a piece as pa.rule: When the build stage drops a piece as part of a conflict cluster, the ledger must flag it as lost and the build stage must be re-run to restore it.

a bench is not a type allowed in an 'oth.rule: A bench is not a type allowed in an 'other' room; the reading must retype it to a type that fits the room (e.g. console_table) or the room type must be changed.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms (e.g. 'Salon' and 'AÇIK MUTFAK'), the reading must check for a missing wall between them and split the room into two if the labels indicate different room types.

a drawn piece that is off its drawn cent.rule: A drawn piece that is off its drawn centre by more than the 0.05 m tolerance must be moved back to its drawn position (or the nearest free spot within the 0.3 m drawn-lock) before the render check, so the layout stage, not the render stage, owns drawn-piece placement.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the whole wet set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet, tall cabinet) so the render shows a complete, furnished bathroom, not a bare wall with a partially visible fixture.

a site area drawn on the plan (parking,.rule: A site area drawn on the plan (parking, terrace, pool) must be built as a site element (outline, paving, or pool) in the site stage; if the drawing shows it, the site stage must not leave it as 'NOT built (no outline)'.

a zone label that names a kitchen (e.g..rule: A zone label that names a kitchen (e.g. 'AÇIK MUTFAK') inside a room typed living must split the room into a living part and a kitchen part (or retype the room kitchen) so the kitchen is checked and furnished as its own space, not absorbed into the living room.

a ceiling light placed under a sloped ce.rule: A ceiling light placed under a sloped ceiling must be hung flush with the slope (its top at the local ceiling height), not at a fixed height that leaves a gap under the slope.

when the fitting stage falls back to a p.rule: When the fitting stage falls back to a parametric mesh for a piece, the next round must swap it to a library model that matches the project's style chain and passes the fit rules, rather than leaving the parametric placeholder.

when a wall_cabinet run is built, its un.rule: When a wall_cabinet run is built, its unit joints must be aligned to the base units' joints directly beneath it; the kitchen module builder must snap the upper run's divisions to the lower run's divisions so no joint is left unpaired.

a bedroom is not required to have a tv;.rule: A bedroom is not required to have a TV; the room is correctly furnished as a bedroom (bed, nightstand, wardrobe) and the code already refused every TV placement because the view is blocked.

a bathroom's program includes storage; w.rule: A bathroom's program includes storage; when the bathroom set is built without a storage unit, the layout stage must add the missing storage group so the fixtures are not left standing alone.

a living room must be furnished to at le.rule: A living room must be furnished to at least 25% of its floor; when the layout stage leaves wide empty floor, it must re-place the pieces (relayout) to fill the room to the furnished threshold.

a bathroom's program includes a storage.rule: A bathroom's program includes a storage element (tall_cabinet or wall_cabinet); the room_fill stage must place one whenever the room has no storage piece, so its fixtures are never left standing alone.

a bedroom's accent wall must carry a fea.rule: A bedroom's accent wall must carry a feature finish (fluted/panelled) and the wood floor a parquet look; the decor stage's professional dressing and the build's finishes must apply both so the room meets the professional bar.

a bed's bedding set must include a deep.rule: A bed's bedding set must include a deep duvet whose hem overhangs the free foot side (about 0.24 m) and a woven, fringed throw pair; the decor bedding plan and the build's textiles.bedding_set must apply both.

a bed's bedding set must include a woven.rule: A bed's bedding set must include a woven, fringed throw pair laid across the foot; the decor bedding plan and the build's textiles.bedding_set must place it.

a kitchen worktop must carry a few small.rule: A kitchen worktop must carry a few small props (a fruit bowl, a kettle, a cutting board) so the counter reads as inhabited and designed, not empty.

interior door frames must match the room.rule: Interior door frames must match the room's palette; in a light, modern hallway the door and its frame take a light painted finish, not a dark heavy one.

an office chair must match the room's st.rule: An office chair must match the room's style and palette; a generic black dated model is not acceptable in a light-wood modern room, so the fit stage must pick a modern model from the allowed list.

a wardrobe must be built from a textured.rule: A wardrobe must be built from a textured, finished library model, not a flat untextured slab; the build stage must assign a real wardrobe model with visible material.

a living room's main wall behind the sof.rule: A living room's main wall behind the sofa must carry wall art and decor to anchor the space; the decor stage must place it, not leave the wall bare.

a console table and a coffee table must.rule: A console table and a coffee table must carry styled surfaces (books, a vase, a decorative tray) so they read as lived-in, not as an empty showroom.

a balcony's program includes a place to.rule: A balcony's program includes a place to sit (a chair or a small table with seating); the layout stage must place a balcony group so the outdoor space reads as livable, not a construction site.

facade window/door joinery must vary in.rule: Facade window/door joinery must vary in material and size to create rhythm; a monotonous plain repetitive joinery is not acceptable, so the build stage must mix materials (wood, stone, glass) and vary sizes.

a window that reads as a dark slatted gr.rule: A window that reads as a dark slatted grille louver is a placeholder and clashes with clean modern glazing; the build stage must assign a clean modern glazing look, not a louver.

a dining table must carry a table settin.rule: A dining table must carry a table setting (plates, a bowl or a vase) so it reads as set for use, not empty.

a desk with a facing seat must carry a w.rule: A desk with a facing seat must carry a work set (a laptop or computer on it facing the seat) so the seat reads as used, not facing nothing.

when a decor element's host piece is not.rule: When a decor element's host piece is not built, the build stage must either build the host or explicitly record why the host is excluded; silently dropping the host and all its children is a loss.

a drawn symbol that both recognition pas.rule: A drawn symbol that both recognition passes classify as not_furniture is kept as an obstacle and is not built as a piece; this is correct behaviour, not a loss.

a drawn outline that encloses a table an.rule: A drawn outline that encloses a table and its chairs and is mostly empty space is a rug mark, not a furniture piece; it is handled by the decor stage, not built as a piece.

cushions that belong to a piece's family.rule: Cushions that belong to a piece's family cushion set are built as part of that piece's dressing, not as separate pieces; this is correct behaviour.

cushions and pillows that are part of a.rule: Cushions and pillows that are part of a library model are not separate pieces; they are included in the model and not built individually.

when two floor lamps of the same room ar.rule: When two floor lamps of the same room are drawn overlapping (one inside the other), they are one lamp drawn twice; the larger one is kept and the smaller duplicate is not built.

a small ottoman drawn mostly inside an a.rule: A small ottoman drawn mostly inside an armchair is the armchair's seat cushion, not a separate piece; it is not built.

when a plan carries a zone label for a k.rule: When a plan carries a zone label for a kitchen (e.g. 'AÇIK MUTFAK') inside a room that also holds living furniture, the room is an open-plan living/kitchen space: the reading stage must record the kitchen zone as a sub-zone of the room (keeping the room type living) and the build stage must place the kitchen run within that zone, so the kitchen is not lost or mis-typed.

a piece typed by context from its size a.rule: A piece typed by context from its size and neighbours is correct when it fits its room and the drawing; the absence of a codified rule for the inference is not a defect in the built model.

when a table/desk symbol's drawn footpri.rule: When a table/desk symbol's drawn footprint includes its chair, the desk is sized to the table portion and the chair is placed as a separate piece in front; this is correct handling, not a misread.

kitchen fixtures in a living room are va.rule: Kitchen fixtures in a living room are valid when the layout is an open-plan kitchen; the room type remains living and the kitchen zone is a sub-zone.

a sofa's front must face the open floor.rule: A sofa's front must face the open floor and its partner; when the front is inferred, it should be set explicitly to the direction that looks into the most open floor.

an armchair's front must face away from.rule: An armchair's front must face away from its wall or towards its partner; when the front is inferred, it should be set explicitly.

a living room without a tv unit does not.rule: A living room without a TV unit does not require a TV wall; the absence of a suitable wall for a TV is not a defect when no TV is present.

a bedroom without a tv unit does not req.rule: A bedroom without a TV unit does not require a TV wall; the absence of a suitable wall for a TV is not a defect when no TV is present.

a media-wall / tv placement check must b.rule: A media-wall / TV placement check must be skipped for rooms whose program does not include a TV (bedrooms, bathrooms, halls); a missing TV in a non-living room is not a defect.

when a plan labels a room as a terrace/b.rule: When a plan labels a room as a terrace/balcony with a door to it, the roof stage must cut an opening in the roof over that room (a roof terrace), not build the roof closed over it.

when a door on the top floor would reach.rule: When a door on the top floor would reach above the roof underside at its wall, the roof stage must provide a dormer or cut the roof to give the door full headroom (at least 2.0 m clear).

ceiling lights without a host room are g.rule: Ceiling lights without a host room are generic decor; a size cap warning on them is informational and does not require action.

when a door's top is above the roof unde.rule: When a door's top is above the roof underside at its wall, the door height must be clipped to the roof underside minus a clearance, or the roof must be raised/cut to accommodate the door.

ceiling lights under sloped ceilings sho.rule: Ceiling lights under sloped ceilings should be hung flush under the slope; a warning about this is informational and does not require action.

a cushion placed on a bed must rest on t.rule: A cushion placed on a bed must rest on the mattress surface; its bottom face may not penetrate the mattress by more than 0.03 m. The decor stage must verify the resting height of every soft item against the support it sits on and nudge it up to the surface if it intersects.

every site area the documents label (par.rule: Every site area the documents label (parking, terrace, pool, etc.) must be built as an outdoor space with its outline; the site stage must not drop a labelled area without a recorded reason.

every room label the documents place on.rule: Every room label the documents place on a level must be matched to a model room on that level; the reading stage must not leave a labelled room unassigned when a model room of the same size and position exists.

when a bathroom is under a sloped ceilin.rule: When a bathroom is under a sloped ceiling, the fit rules must allow the standard bathroom fixtures (washbasin, toilet, bathtub) to be placed at their working heights even if the ceiling at that point is below the generic 1.60 m cap, provided the fixture's own height is below the local ceiling; the sloped-ceiling cap must be applied per-fixture-height, not as a blanket 1.60 m limit that rejects every washbasin model.

a wardrobe (or any front-opening storage.rule: A wardrobe (or any front-opening storage) is placed only on a wall span that leaves at least its door-swing depth (0.50 m) clear in front; if no such span exists in the room, the piece is not placed rather than parked against a blocked wall.

any decorative or furniture piece whose.rule: Any decorative or furniture piece whose top exceeds the clear ceiling height of its room (ceiling minus the piece's own clearance) is rejected at placement and re-seated lower or removed; a piece is never allowed to poke through the roof or ceiling.

every stair with an open side (no wall o.rule: Every stair with an open side (no wall or balustrade along its full run) is built with a safety railing/guard on that open side as part of the stair assembly; a stair is never placed without a guard on its open edge.

every stair opening (void) in a floor is.rule: Every stair opening (void) in a floor is built with a safety railing/guard around its open edges as part of the floor build; a stair opening is never left unguarded.

a camera view that renders entirely blac.rule: A camera view that renders entirely black or empty (no room, no main group, no architecture at eye height) is a failed render and must be re-run through the layout/room_fill stage before it is accepted.

a wardrobe (or any storage run) is built.rule: A wardrobe (or any storage run) is built from a library model that renders as a functional storage unit with doors or handles, not as a flat wall panel; if the only available model for the run's length renders as a panel, the run is split into shorter modules or a different model is used.

scene check s5 (detached elements) must.rule: Scene check S5 (detached elements) must pass for every level before the build stage is accepted; any element that fails S5 is re-seated or removed in the build stage, not carried forward to the final stage.

every ceiling light is built with a hang.rule: Every ceiling light is built with a hang record (cord, rod, or canopy) connecting it to the ceiling; a ceiling light is never placed without a visible or recorded connection to the ceiling above it.

scene check s1 (geometry) must pass for.rule: Scene check S1 (geometry) must pass for every level before the build stage is accepted; any element that fails S1 is re-seated or removed in the build stage, not carried forward to the final stage.

scene check s2 (geometry) must pass for.rule: Scene check S2 (geometry) must pass for every level before the build stage is accepted; any element that fails S2 is re-seated or removed in the build stage, not carried forward to the final stage.

when an armchair faces the back of anoth.rule: When an armchair faces the back of another seat and rotation is refused because it would face a wall, the furniture agent's next round must re-place the seating group so each seat faces the shared table, not a neighbour's back.

a piece that crosses a room outline by 0.rule: A piece that crosses a room outline by 0.02 m or less is within tolerance and is not a defect.

when a coffee table overlaps a seat and.rule: When a coffee table overlaps a seat and every move is refused (it would still overlap or break a clearance), the furniture agent's next round must re-solve the seating group so the table clears every seat.

when a seat's front use zone is not reac.rule: When a seat's front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room door, the furniture agent's next round must re-place the seating so the approach to each seat is clear.

when a sofa's front use zone is not reac.rule: When a sofa's front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room door, the furniture agent's next round must re-place the seating so the approach to the sofa is clear.

a floor lamp must not stand in front of.rule: A floor lamp must not stand in front of a window: the furniture agent's next round must place it clear of the window's sight and light line.

when a coffee table overlaps a seat and.rule: When a coffee table overlaps a seat and every move is refused (it would still overlap, break a clearance, or exceed the move limit), the furniture agent's next round must re-solve the seating group so the table clears every seat.

a stove or any back-to-wall kitchen fixt.rule: A stove or any back-to-wall kitchen fixture must be placed flush against a wall; a gap greater than 0.03 m is a placement error, not a tolerance.

a kitchen counter run must leave at leas.rule: A kitchen counter run must leave at least 0.90 m of clear aisle in front of it; a tighter aisle is a placement error.

when individual rotate/move edits of a s.rule: When individual rotate/move edits of a seating group keep failing the facing and clearance checks, re-solve the whole room's AI layout so the group is placed coherently.

a dining chair needs at least 0.81 m fro.rule: A dining chair needs at least 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; a tighter gap is a placement error.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall; a sof.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall; a sofa floating 2 m from any wall is a missing-wall placement error.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall; a gap.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall; a gap greater than 0.03 m is a placement error.

a double bed needs at least 0.60 m of fr.rule: A double bed needs at least 0.60 m of free space along each side; a tighter gap is a placement error.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window; it must be placed clear of the window's sill and swing.

a wardrobe needs at least 0.80 m of free.rule: A wardrobe needs at least 0.80 m of free space in front of it for the doors to open; a tighter gap is a placement error.

a piece that blocks a window's clear zon.rule: A piece that blocks a window's clear zone (sill + 0.05 m) is moved to the nearest free place in its room, clear of the opening.

a wardrobe with less than 0.80 m in fron.rule: A wardrobe with less than 0.80 m in front is moved to a free place that gives its full opening clearance.

a drawn shower whose size is outside the.rule: A drawn shower whose size is outside the product range is corrected to a real product size that fits its bay.

a bed with less than 0.60 m along its si.rule: A bed with less than 0.60 m along its side is moved to a free place that gives its full side clearance.

a piece that blocks the free zone in fro.rule: A piece that blocks the free zone in front of a sofa is moved to a free place that clears the sofa's front.

a coffee table not in front of the sofa.rule: A coffee table not in front of the sofa is moved to the free place in front of it.

an armchair that is too far from the cof.rule: An armchair that is too far from the coffee table is moved to a free place within 2.50 m of it.

a chair with less than 0.81 m behind it.rule: A chair with less than 0.81 m behind it is moved to a free place that gives its full clearance.

a chair or any piece whose seat height e.rule: A chair or any piece whose seat height exceeds a window sill plus 0.05 m must not be placed in front of that window; the furniture agent must keep a clear zone in front of every window.

a shoe cabinet must be built from a dedi.rule: A shoe cabinet must be built from a dedicated shoe-cabinet model, never from a generic wall_cabinet/wall_run module; the build stage must match the piece type to a model of the same type.

the furniture agent must not drop decor-.rule: The furniture agent must not drop decor-stage pieces (dining table, chairs, plants, lamps, ottoman, tv_unit, sideboard) when re-placing a room; every decor-stage piece must be carried into the agent stage.
The furniture agent must not drop decor-stage pieces when re-placing a room; every decor-stage piece must be carried into the agent stage.

a planned piece whose model is a module.rule: A planned piece whose model is a module of another piece (a stove or sink inside the kitchen run) must be built as its own object; the build stage must not drop a planned piece because its model is shared with a neighbour.

a stair core room whose only camera poin.rule: A stair core room whose only camera point is inside the stair must be shown from the adjacent hall; the camera stage must place the view in the hall looking at the stair, not inside the stair volume.

a piece named in a conflict resolution m.rule: A piece named in a conflict resolution must survive the build stage; the build stage must not drop a piece that the conflict resolver kept.

a drawn piece in a kitchen that is not a.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen that is not a recognised kitchen fixture and whose retype to a plausible type is refused on overlap must be kept as a parametric piece and built, not left untyped and unbuilt with no warning.

when a level's rooms are dropped by the.rule: When a level's rooms are dropped by the build stage as a conflict cluster, its drawn furniture is not a separate reading loss; restore the level first.

kitchen fixtures in a room dropped by th.rule: Kitchen fixtures in a room dropped by the build stage are not separate reading losses; restore the room first.

stair layers (a-merdiven, a-merdiven gör.rule: Stair layers (A-MERDIVEN, A-merdiven görünüş) must be read and a stair piece placed on every level that has a stair, even when the level's rooms are in a build conflict cluster; the stair is structural and must not be dropped with the rooms.

stair elevation layers (a-merdiven görün.rule: Stair elevation layers (A-merdiven görünüş) must be read to inform the stair piece placement on every level that has a stair, even when the level's rooms are in a build conflict cluster.

decorative layers (deko_*, vitrifiye) ar.rule: Decorative layers (Deko_*, Vitrifiye) are drawing decorations and are not expected to be used by the model; they should not be flagged as lost.

vitrification/finish layers (piu_vitrifi.rule: Vitrification/finish layers (Piu_Vitrifiye, *_Vitrifiye) are drawing finish layers and are not expected to be used by the model; they should not be flagged as lost.

the build stage must not drop an entire.rule: The build stage must not drop an entire room because a single kitchen fixture (e.g. fridge) is missing from the kitchen zone; it should build the room and flag the missing fixture for the furniture agent to add.
The build stage must not drop an entire level's rooms because of a single kitchen fixture issue in one room; each room should be evaluated independently.

the build stage must not drop kitchen fi.rule: The build stage must not drop kitchen fixtures because a single fixture (e.g. fridge) is missing; it should build the kitchen zone with the available fixtures and flag the missing one.

stoves and other wall-mounted kitchen fi.rule: Stoves and other wall-mounted kitchen fixtures should be snapped to their wall; a gap of 0.06 m is a drawing artifact, not a real gap.

a wall-adjacent fixture read from the pl.rule: A wall-adjacent fixture read from the plan must be snapped flush to its wall; a residual gap of more than 0.02 m between the fixture back and the wall is a reading error, not a clearance.
