a kitchen room's program requires a frid.rule: A kitchen room's program requires a fridge; when the drawn kitchen run lacks one, the run is re-solved as a unit to add the missing member rather than leaving the room incomplete.

when a toilet's side clearance is short.rule: When a toilet's side clearance is short by less than 0.05 m and no model swap or rotation can fix it, the fixture is re-centred within its bay to maximise the minimum side clearance; if the bay itself is too narrow, the room's layout is flagged for the architect rather than forcing a non-compliant fit.

a bathtub's front clearance is governed.rule: A bathtub's front clearance is governed by the room's layout, not the model; when the drawn bay leaves less than 0.53 m in front, the room's fixture arrangement is re-solved (or the architect is asked to confirm the tight fit) rather than swapping to a shorter tub that still does not clear.

a shower's front clearance is governed b.rule: A shower's front clearance is governed by the room's layout; when the drawn bay leaves less than 0.53 m in front, the room's fixture arrangement is re-solved or the architect confirms the tight fit, rather than swapping to a model that still does not clear.

a drawn bathtub/shower is placed at its.rule: A drawn bathtub/shower is placed at its drawn centre; when the resulting front clearance is under the minimum, the code must re-seat it to the nearest valid spot (not just flag it).

a toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m fr.rule: A toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m from a side wall/fixture must be re-seated to the nearest valid spot, not just flagged.

an entry hall must carry an entrance gro.rule: An entry hall must carry an entrance group (bench/console/mirror) to anchor the entry; the furniture agent must place it when the hall is otherwise bare.

a room's type must match its fixtures an.rule: A room's type must match its fixtures and furniture; a 40.5 m2 room furnished as a living room (sofa, armchairs, coffee table, dining table) is 'living', not 'other'.

a circulation room that holds a stair pl.rule: A circulation room that holds a stair plus a wardrobe/shoe cabinet is a 'hall' (a hall with a stair), not a 'stair' room; the type 'hall' is correct.

the storey count must be read from the s.rule: The storey count must be read from the section/elevation, not inferred from the number of floor levels in the plan; a two-storey building with a basement and a mezzanine is still two storeys above ground.

an opening must be cut through its wall;.rule: An opening must be cut through its wall; if the door ray hits a wall, the opening is not cut and must be re-cut.

a stair flight must have a handrail over.rule: A stair flight must have a handrail over its full run; if a flight has no handrail over 0.72 m of its run, the build stage must add a wall handrail or a balustrade.

every facade must have a frontal exterio.rule: Every facade must have a frontal exterior camera view; if the +y facade has none, the camera stage must add one.

when the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3.rule: When the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3, a retaining edge (retaining wall or stepped plinth) must be built at the building's perimeter.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.90-0.97 m); if the model's top is higher, the build stage must use a model at the correct height.

a kitchen counter (kitchen_run) must be.rule: A kitchen counter (kitchen_run) must be built with its worktop at the standard working height (0.90-0.95 m); a counter whose top is placed above 1.00 m is a misread and must be corrected to working height before the run is accepted.

every interior room must be lit in the r.rule: Every interior room must be lit in the render (ceiling or wall light, or daylight through its windows); a room rendered with no visible light source is a failed render and must be re-lit.

the outdoor environment (lawn, trees, gr.rule: The outdoor environment (lawn, trees, ground) must be a believable landscape, not a flat untextured plane with low-poly placeholder trees; a placeholder site is a failed render.

entrance steps and railings must clearly.rule: Entrance steps and railings must clearly connect to a path and a door; floating railings or steps that do not link to a circulation path are a build error.

site areas that are drawn and labelled i.rule: Site areas that are drawn and labelled in the documents (pools, terraces, parking) must be registered with their outlines in the model; a site area recorded 'NOT built (no outline)' when the documents show it is a loss.

a kitchen must have a worktop at working.rule: A kitchen must have a worktop at working height (0.90-0.95 m) and a clear aisle of at least 0.90 m in front of it; a kitchen with a counter above working height and an aisle under 0.90 m is not usable and must be corrected.

the storey count of the model must match.rule: The storey count of the model must match the section drawing; if the section shows two storeys, the model must not have three (or vice versa). A basement pair (L-1/L-1b) that the section does not show is a misread.

room names must be unique per level; if.rule: Room names must be unique per level; if the documents label two distinct bedrooms, the model must not give them the same name. Duplicate room names on the same level are a reading error.

a drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a side in a living room is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; it must be split into its constituent pieces and typed individually, not left as an untyped cluster.

a room-type finding must be re-checked a.rule: A room-type finding must be re-checked against the model's current type before being raised: if the model already carries the correct type, the finding is a false alarm and is closed, not re-fixed.

when the plan draws a roof terrace (a ro.rule: When the plan draws a roof terrace (a room labelled terrace on the top level, with a door to it), the roof stage must cut the roof over that room's footprint and add a guard on its open edges, instead of closing the roof over it.

when a top-floor door or window head wou.rule: When a top-floor door or window head would be clipped by a sloped roof underside, the roof stage must provide a dormer (or a flat roof pocket) over that opening so the full door/window height is usable.

a stage that ends 'pending' with open qu.rule: A stage that ends 'pending' with open questions must be rerun (or the questions answered) before the run is considered complete; a pending stage is a failed step, not a finished one.

a sofa (or any long piece) read with its.rule: A sofa (or any long piece) read with its front on a short side is a reading error: the front must be set on the long side facing the most open space, and the build step must be rerun when this is detected.

a console table (or any long, narrow pie.rule: A console table (or any long, narrow piece) read with its front on a short side is a reading error: the front must be set on the long side with the back on the wall, and the build step must be rerun when this is detected.

a scene check failure (s5) for a built d.rule: A scene check failure (S5) for a built decor item must trigger a rerun of the build/scene step for that level so the item is corrected before the run is considered complete.

views marked for review must be re-evalu.rule: Views marked for review must be re-evaluated (rerun the render/check stage) before the run is considered complete; a view left in 'review' is an open item.

inside doors must stand open by default.rule: Inside doors must stand open by default in the build (door_states); a door with no leaf state recorded is a build error and the door_states step must be rerun.

a door that a camera view sees into a ro.rule: A door that a camera view sees into a room worth showing must stand open in that view (door_states.revise_for_cameras); a closed door in such a view is a build error.

a wardrobe whose drawn footprint is deep.rule: A wardrobe whose drawn footprint is deeper than the clearance its room allows must be swapped to a shallower model of the same type (depth <= 0.55 m) rather than moved, so its front clearance meets the minimum without leaving its wall.

a toilet that sits above its floor (a ra.rule: A toilet that sits above its floor (a raised or wall-hung model) must be swapped to a floor-standing model whose base rests on the floor, not moved.

a washbasin whose lowest point is above.rule: A washbasin whose lowest point is above its floor (a wall-hung or raised model) must be swapped to a floor-standing or counter model that rests on the floor, not moved.

a coffee table that overlaps a seating p.rule: A coffee table that overlaps a seating piece and cannot be moved within the drawn-lock limit must be swapped to a smaller model that fits the free zone, not moved.

a drawn piece longer than 4.5 m and no d.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m and no deeper than 0.70 m in a living or dining room is a built-in storage run; the reader must split it into a run of standard-depth (0.40-0.60 m) cabinets rather than leaving it untyped.

a wardrobe that reaches up to 0.020 m th.rule: A wardrobe that reaches up to 0.020 m through the room outline is within tolerance and must not be flagged as F9.

an armchair whose front use zone is not.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from a door is acceptable when the armchair is part of a seating group that is itself reachable.

a floor lamp standing in front of a wind.rule: A floor lamp standing in front of a window is acceptable when the lamp is shorter than the window head and does not block the view.

a kitchen that has a fridge in its drawn.rule: A kitchen that has a fridge in its drawn set is not missing a fridge, even if the fridge is in a different room.

a toilet whose centre is 0.33 m from the.rule: A toilet whose centre is 0.33 m from the side wall is acceptable when the toilet is 0.50 m wide (the gap on the other side is >= 0.38 m).

a sofa whose free zone in front is block.rule: A sofa whose free zone in front is blocked by a coffee table is acceptable when the coffee table is part of the seating group.

a toilet model that is a crude, low-poly.rule: A toilet model that is a crude, low-poly box must be swapped to a realistic toilet model with a proper cistern shape.

a living room's seating group (sofa, arm.rule: A living room's seating group (sofa, armchairs, coffee table) must be a coherent set: same style family and a limited palette (max 2 accent colours), with a rug under the group and styled surfaces (books, vases, throws) on the coffee table and TV unit.

a dining set (table + chairs) must be a.rule: A dining set (table + chairs) must be a coherent group: same style family and material, with a table setting (plates, glasses) on the table.

a bathroom of 5 m2 or more must include.rule: A bathroom of 5 m2 or more must include a bathtub as its anchor fixture, with warm lighting and styled surfaces (towels, plants, decor) to match the reference standard.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main fixtures from a free point with headroom, not a close-up of a corner.

a bedroom render must show layered beddi.rule: A bedroom render must show layered bedding, styled surfaces and a feature wall to meet the project's presentation standard.

a bedroom's surfaces (nightstand, consol.rule: A bedroom's surfaces (nightstand, console) must carry styled objects (mirror, vase, books) to look finished.

a bed must show layered bedding (throw,.rule: A bed must show layered bedding (throw, second blanket, euro shams) to meet the presentation standard.

a bedroom render must show soft furnishi.rule: A bedroom render must show soft furnishings, lighting, and architectural details to meet the project's standard.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's floor and main furniture, not a corner and a door leaf at a low angle.

an office chair in a residential bedroom.rule: An office chair in a residential bedroom must be a softer, upholstered or wood chair that matches the bed and desk, not a corporate black leather piece.

a desk in a modern, minimalist bedroom m.rule: A desk in a modern, minimalist bedroom must be a modern, minimalist piece, not a dated, traditional Shaker-style piece.

a bedroom's wall behind the bed must be.rule: A bedroom's wall behind the bed must be a feature wall (e.g., vertical fluted or slatted wood panelling) to anchor the bed.

a bedroom render must show a rug, layere.rule: A bedroom render must show a rug, layered curtains, warm light, styled surfaces, and layered bedding to meet the project's standard.

a wardrobe in a modern, minimalist bedro.rule: A wardrobe in a modern, minimalist bedroom must have a refined finish that matches the headboard and walls, not a raw, light wood that looks unfinished.

a bedroom render must show a feature wal.rule: A bedroom render must show a feature wall, rug, curtains, layered bedding, and a styled desk to meet the project's standard.

a bed must show layered bedding (throw,.rule: A bed must show layered bedding (throw, second blanket, euro shams) and its base must match the room's palette.

a desk must carry a work set (laptop, bo.rule: A desk must carry a work set (laptop, books, decor) to look believable.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main fixtures from a free point with headroom, not a black, empty frame.

a hall or corridor render must include a.rule: A hall or corridor render must include at least one styling layer (rug, art, or lighting) and the camera must not frame a bare wall; a grey-box corridor is not client-ready.

every hall or corridor must carry a floo.rule: Every hall or corridor must carry a floor styling layer (rug or runner) in the furnished model so renders are not bare.

a corridor camera must look down the cor.rule: A corridor camera must look down the corridor axis and show its doors, not the side of a storage piece; a side-on wardrobe view is a bad pose.

a living/activity room render must use c.rule: A living/activity room render must use coherent, textured furniture in one style and include styling layers (rug, throws, art); blocky grey-box placeholders are not client-ready.

a sofa must use a real product model (no.rule: A sofa must use a real product model (not a generated placeholder with guessed units) when a real product of the type fits within the caps.

a dining table in a modern/minimal room.rule: A dining table in a modern/minimal room must use a model matching the room's style; a dark traditional table with turned legs is a mismatch.

a living/activity room must have a rug u.rule: A living/activity room must have a rug under the seating group to anchor the space; a bare untextured floor is not client-ready.

a living/activity room render must use c.rule: A living/activity room render must use coherent, textured furniture in one style and include styling layers; blocky grey-box placeholders are not client-ready.

a large empty wall behind a sofa or cons.rule: A large empty wall behind a sofa or console must carry art, a feature panel, or texture; a completely bare wall is a significant omission for a client-ready image.

an exterior or terrace render must show.rule: An exterior or terrace render must show a textured, detailed environment (lawn, varied trees, hedges); a flat untextured green plane and identical low-poly trees are not client-ready.

a terrace or balcony floor must use a de.rule: A terrace or balcony floor must use a designed outdoor material (paving, decking, stone); a bare untextured grey slab is not client-ready.

an exterior or terrace render must show.rule: An exterior or terrace render must show a textured, detailed environment; a flat untextured green plane is not client-ready.
An exterior or terrace render must show a textured, detailed environment; a flat untextured lawn and identical low-poly trees are not client-ready.

a terrace dining table must have a table.rule: A terrace dining table must have a table setting (cloth, place settings) to read as a designed outdoor dining surface; a bare table on a bare slab is not client-ready.

a balcony or terrace render must show a.rule: A balcony or terrace render must show a coherent, finished outdoor furniture set on a finished floor (decking or paving) with planters; a mismatched set on a bare slab is not client-ready.

exterior renders must be lit by a warm s.rule: Exterior renders must be lit by a warm sun (not flat grey) and show a finished facade plus a landscaped site (paths, planters, trees); a grey-box massing study is not client-ready.

exterior and facade views must carry a w.rule: Exterior and facade views must carry a warm sun and warm interior light glowing through the windows; a flat overcast grey render is not client-ready.

exterior renders must show a finished fa.rule: Exterior renders must show a finished facade (cladding/texture) and landscape integration (mature planting, defined paths); a sterile massing study is not client-ready.

a balcony or veranda must carry a place.rule: A balcony or veranda must carry a place to sit (a balcony group: seating plus a table); a bare slab with no lounging area is not a finished outdoor space.

exterior views must carry architectural/.rule: Exterior views must carry architectural/garden lighting (warm sun, a defined path, planters) so the facade and approach read as inviting; a completely unlit exterior is not client-ready.

an exterior view must frame the whole bu.rule: An exterior view must frame the whole building from a valid eye-level or aerial position; a close-up that cuts off the building and focuses on a corner is not a valid presentation view.

exterior renders must show a finished, s.rule: Exterior renders must show a finished, styled home (crisp cladding, defined entrance, landscaped garden with places to sit); a grey-box massing study is not client-ready.

exterior renders must show material rich.rule: Exterior renders must show material richness (cladding, stone), landscaping and architectural detailing (canopies, railings); a raw grey-box massing study in a void is not client-ready.

every drawn furniture symbol must be typ.rule: Every drawn furniture symbol must be typed by a rule or model, or explicitly marked as a non-furniture symbol with its recognition crop; a drawn piece left 'unknown' with nothing built and nothing explaining it is a reading loss.

decor that rests on a host must find a v.rule: Decor that rests on a host must find a valid top on the built host; if the host has no restable top, the decor is dropped rather than left floating or unplaced.

a throw or cloth decor must rest on its.rule: A throw or cloth decor must rest on its host with penetration within tolerance (<= 0.007 m); if the host shows through the cloth, the decor is re-seated or dropped.
A throw or cloth decor must rest on its host with penetration within tolerance (<= 0.007 m); if the host pokes through the cloth, the decor is re-seated or dropped.

a bowl or small decor must rest on its h.rule: A bowl or small decor must rest on its host with a gap within tolerance (<= 0.01 m); if the gap is larger, the decor is re-seated or dropped.

the reading stage must read entities on.rule: The reading stage must read entities on off or frozen layers (or explicitly log every skipped layer with its entity count) so the ledger can verify that no load-bearing geometry was hidden; silently skipping invisible layers is not allowed.
the reading stage must read entities on.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

the camera stage must record a reason wh.rule: The camera stage must record a reason whenever it drops a view (or keep the view); a camera may never be removed silently.

the reading stage must map every drawn b.rule: The reading stage must map every drawn block/insert on a plan to a model element (a piece, a fixture, or an explicit 'not furniture' mark); a drawn block that no element uses is a loss and must be accounted for.

a drawn block whose name is not a known.rule: A drawn block whose name is not a known furniture or fixture symbol and whose size does not match any library piece is a drawing mark, not a piece: the reading stage records it and does not build it.

a drawn block that is a site-decor symbo.rule: A drawn block that is a site-decor symbol (landscaping, paving, pool furniture) is recorded as site decor and not built as a house piece.

a drawn stair block is read as the stair.rule: A drawn stair block is read as the stair piece of the room it sits in; when the room already has a built stair, the block is the same stair and is not a lost piece.

two floor-lamp outlines of the same room.rule: Two floor-lamp outlines of the same room where the smaller is drawn inside the larger are one lamp drawn with two outlines; the reading keeps the larger and the ledger must not flag the smaller as a lost piece.

a dwg layer whose name is a generic 2d/a.rule: A DWG layer whose name is a generic 2D/annotation tag (2D, TEXT, DIM, AXIS) holding only circles and lines is reference geometry, not furniture or structure; the model may ignore it without a warning.

a dwg layer whose name denotes a decorat.rule: A DWG layer whose name denotes a decorative finish pattern (Deko, Zemin, Seramik, tile, pattern) holding arcs/ellipses/splines is a 2D finish hatch, not furniture or structure; the model may ignore it without a warning.

A DWG layer whose name denotes a decorative finish (VITR, vitrification, glaze) holding only arcs and lines is a 2D finish hatch, not furniture or structure; the model may ignore it without a warning.

the furniture agent must not remove a dr.rule: The furniture agent must not remove a drawn piece that is the defining storage of a hall/entrance (shoe cabinet); if it does not fit, it is re-typed or moved, never deleted.

when the build stage drops a drawn piece.rule: When the build stage drops a drawn piece as part of a level conflict cluster, the conflict must be resolved (the level's walls/openings rebuilt) rather than silently dropping the piece; a re-run of the build stage after the conflict is cleared must restore every dropped piece.

a bench drawn in a room typed 'other' (a.rule: A bench drawn in a room typed 'other' (a multi-purpose activity room) is read as a console_table (a low seating/leaning piece that fits an activity room) rather than a bench, which is not an allowed type there.

when one room outline carries two labels.rule: When one room outline carries two labels and one of them is an open kitchen (AÇIK MUTFAK) inside a living room, the reading must split the outline into a living room and an open-kitchen zone (or keep the kitchen as a sub-zone of the living room) so the kitchen fixtures are placed in the kitchen zone, not the whole living room.

a drawn piece offset by less than 0.25 m.rule: A drawn piece offset by less than 0.25 m from its drawn centre, where the model swap is refused as no_change and no better model exists, is a minor layout drift, not a misread.

a drawn piece offset by less than 0.10 m.rule: A drawn piece offset by less than 0.10 m from its drawn centre is within tolerance and not a misread, even if a slightly better model exists but is unavailable.

a drawn armchair offset by less than 0.1.rule: A drawn armchair offset by less than 0.15 m where the model swap is not attempted or refused is a minor layout drift, not a misread.

a drawn piece offset by less than 0.15 m.rule: A drawn piece offset by less than 0.15 m where both rotate and swap are refused is a minor layout drift, not a misread.
A drawn piece offset by less than 0.15 m where the swap is refused as asset_unusable is a minor layout drift, not a misread.

a drawn coffee table offset by more than.rule: A drawn coffee table offset by more than 0.5 m where the move is refused due to overlap with a neighbouring piece is a layout constraint, not a misread; the size mismatch is a model limitation.
A drawn coffee table offset by more than 0.5 m where multiple move attempts are refused due to overlap or drawn_lock is a layout constraint, not a misread.

a drawn nightstand offset by less than 0.rule: A drawn nightstand offset by less than 0.20 m is a minor layout drift, not a misread.
A drawn nightstand offset by less than 0.15 m where the swap is refused multiple times is a minor layout drift, not a misread.

a drawn sofa offset by less than 0.35 m.rule: A drawn sofa offset by less than 0.35 m is a minor layout drift, not a misread.

a drawn armchair offset by less than 0.3.rule: A drawn armchair offset by less than 0.35 m where the rotate is refused is a minor layout drift, not a misread.

a bathroom camera that shows only a bare.rule: A bathroom camera that shows only a bare wall or a partially visible fixture should be reframed to show the main fixtures (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) together.

a washbasin that looks like a bare bowl.rule: A washbasin that looks like a bare bowl when all alternative models are audit-removed is a model limitation, not a fixable issue.

a chair on a balcony that looks generic.rule: A chair on a balcony that looks generic when the only better model is refused due to height constraints under a sloped ceiling is a model limitation, not a fixable issue.

a bathroom's program includes a storage.rule: A bathroom's program includes a storage piece (tall_cabinet or wall_cabinet); the room_fill stage must place one whenever the bathroom set lacks it, so no bathroom is left with only bare fixtures.

a living room's furniture coverage must.rule: A living room's furniture coverage must reach the furnished-room bar; the decor/dressing stage must add the missing layers (curtains, bedding, styled surfaces, wall art) and the build must apply feature walls and parquet so the room reads as finished, not a bare showroom.

a bedroom's accent wall must carry a fea.rule: A bedroom's accent wall must carry a feature finish (fluted/panelled wall) in the professional dressing; the decor stage must specify it and the build must apply the feature_walls finish so the room meets the professional bar.

a bed's bedding plan must include a deep.rule: A bed's bedding plan must include a deep duvet that overhangs the free foot side (hem to the floor) and a throw pair; the decor stage must specify the free sides and the build must apply the textiles.bedding_set dressing.

a bed's bedding plan must include a thro.rule: A bed's bedding plan must include a throw across the foot; the decor stage must specify the throw pair's weave and the build must apply the textiles.bedding_set dressing.

a kitchen worktop must carry a few style.rule: A kitchen worktop must carry a few styled props (fruit bowl, kettle, small plant) in the dressing so the counter reads as inhabited, not an empty slab.

a living room's main wall behind the sea.rule: A living room's main wall behind the seating must carry wall art or decor to anchor the space; the decor stage must specify the art layer and the build must place it.

styled surfaces (console and coffee tabl.rule: Styled surfaces (console and coffee tables) must carry books, a vase or a decorative tray in the dressing so they read as lived-in, not a showroom.

a dining table (indoor or terrace) must.rule: A dining table (indoor or terrace) must carry a table setting (plates, glasses, a centrepiece) in the dressing so it reads as styled, not bare.

a stone-clad wall must use a high-qualit.rule: A stone-clad wall must use a high-quality, varied stone look (ledger/ashlar with depth) rather than a flat repetitive texture; the build's material assignment must pick a finished stone look for cladding.

an entrance door must be dressed with ar.rule: An entrance door must be dressed with architectural interest (lighting, a path or steps, surrounding landscaping) so it reads as a proper entrance, not a bare panel.

a desk with a seat must carry a work set.rule: A desk with a seat must carry a work set (laptop or computer facing the seat) in the dressing so the workspace reads as in use.

the agent stage must not drop a placed f.rule: The agent stage must not drop a placed furniture piece (e.g. a shoe_cabinet) that the decor stage built; any re-layout must preserve existing pieces or explicitly re-place them, so nothing is silently lost between stages.

The agent stage must not drop a placed furniture piece (e.g. a nightstand) that the decor stage built; any re-layout must preserve existing pieces or explicitly re-place them, so nothing is silently lost between stages.

sub-parts of a built piece (shelves, cus.rule: Sub-parts of a built piece (shelves, cushions, drawers) that the agent drops are not a conservation loss; only the parent piece's disappearance is.

a tall_cabinet drawn in a bathroom that.rule: A tall_cabinet drawn in a bathroom that the agent drops must be restored in the next agent round; the bathroom set is incomplete without its storage.

a level that belongs to a specific varia.rule: A level that belongs to a specific variant is expected to be absent from the base build; it is built in the variant's own scene.

decor elements whose host piece is not b.rule: Decor elements whose host piece is not built must not be silently dropped; the build stage must either build the host or flag the decor for the agent to re-place.

elements on structural layers (a-ba, a-w.rule: Elements on structural layers (A-BA, A-WALL) are correctly kept as obstacles and not built as furniture.

furniture symbols drawn on the 'a-tefris.rule: Furniture symbols drawn on the 'A-TEFRIS' layer must be built as furniture, not skipped; the layer name indicates furniture (Turkish 'tefrishat' = furnishings).

elements on decor layers (deko_*) are co.rule: Elements on decor layers (Deko_*) are correctly deferred to the decor stage, not the build stage.

elements with 60%+ overlap inside a buil.rule: Elements with 60%+ overlap inside a built fixture are correctly treated as parts of that fixture, not separate pieces.

site areas (parking, terrace, pool) that.rule: Site areas (parking, terrace, pool) that are drawn in the plan must be built as site elements (paving, grass, water) even if they are exterior; 'not built' is not an acceptable outcome for drawn site areas.

details inside a kitchen counter (applia.rule: Details inside a kitchen counter (appliance fronts, drawers) are correctly treated as parts of the counter, not separate pieces.

clusters larger than 4.5 m are correctly.rule: Clusters larger than 4.5 m are correctly identified as groups, not single pieces; the agent stage resolves them.

elements that both recognition passes cl.rule: Elements that both recognition passes classify as not_furniture are correctly kept as obstacles.

rug outlines (drawn around a table and c.rule: Rug outlines (drawn around a table and chairs, with the table and chairs inside) are correctly identified as rug marks, not furniture pieces; the decor stage places them.

cushion sets that are part of a piece's.rule: Cushion sets that are part of a piece's dressing are built with the piece; their colour-variant dec elements are not separate build targets.

cushions and pillows that are integral t.rule: Cushions and pillows that are integral to a furniture model's asset are not separate build targets; they come with the model.

when two pieces of the same type overlap.rule: When two pieces of the same type overlap significantly in the same room, the build keeps the larger/clearer one and drops the duplicate; this is correct deduplication, not a loss.

a small piece drawn mostly inside a larg.rule: A small piece drawn mostly inside a larger seat (armchair, sofa) is its cushion, not a separate ottoman; the build correctly drops it.

pieces explicitly removed by an ai actio.rule: Pieces explicitly removed by an AI action are not built; the build correctly honours the removal.

large flat outlines around groups of fur.rule: Large flat outlines around groups of furniture are rugs or zone markers, not furniture pieces; they are handled by the decor rules, not the furniture build.

a large flat outline (roughly 2x2 m or b.rule: A large flat outline (roughly 2x2 m or bigger) that encloses two or more placed pieces and has no product of its own is a rug or zone outline, not a furniture piece; it is not built as a piece.

a piece removed by an explicit remove de.rule: A piece removed by an explicit remove decision is intentionally not built; its absence is not a loss.

the upper end of a stair that arrives at.rule: The upper end of a stair that arrives at the top level is not rebuilt as a separate piece; the stair is built once between its two floors.

a decor item whose host piece is not bui.rule: A decor item whose host piece is not built is not built either; its absence follows from the host's.

a bed model that already includes its ow.rule: A bed model that already includes its own made bedding is not additionally dressed with a throw; the model's bedding is kept as is.

a zone label naming a kitchen (e.g. 'açi.rule: A zone label naming a kitchen (e.g. 'AÇIK MUTFAK' / open kitchen) inside a living room marks an open-kitchen zone: the reading stage must classify the enclosed counter as a kitchen zone and keep it as part of the living room's open kitchen, not drop it as an unknown label.

an l-shaped outline with 0.5-1.3 m deep.rule: An L-shaped outline with 0.5-1.3 m deep arms in a living room is a corner sofa; the open inner corner is its front.

a single 0.6-0.7 m seat on one side of a.rule: A single 0.6-0.7 m seat on one side of a coffee table, facing it, is an armchair.

a desk symbol whose footprint includes t.rule: A desk symbol whose footprint includes the chair drawn in front of it is read as the desk at its wall depth plus the chair in front; the chair is kept as a separate piece.

a desk symbol whose drawn footprint is d.rule: A desk symbol whose drawn footprint is deeper than a desk (roughly 0.9 m or more) is a desk-plus-chair block: build the desk at its real depth against the wall and place the chair in front of it; do not flag the chair as a separate misread.

when a level has no separate kitchen roo.rule: When a level has no separate kitchen room but the plan draws kitchen fixtures inside a living room, treat it as an open kitchen: keep the fixtures in the living room and do not flag them as misplaced.

a sofa whose front was inferred must be.rule: A sofa whose front was inferred must be given the direction that looks into the open floor towards its seating partner, not left unoriented.

an armchair whose front was inferred mus.rule: An armchair whose front was inferred must be given the direction away from its wall or towards its seating partner, not left unoriented.

when a living room has no drawn tv or me.rule: When a living room has no drawn TV or media wall and no wall 1.5-4 m from the seating axis is clear of windows and doors, do not require a TV place; the room may be a living room without a TV.

when a bedroom has no drawn tv and the w.rule: When a bedroom has no drawn TV and the wall the bed faces is blocked by furniture (wardrobe, bench, etc.) at every candidate TV position, do not require a TV place; a bedroom does not need a TV.

when the plan labels a room as a terrace.rule: When the plan labels a room as a terrace or balcony on the top floor and the section draws the roof closed over it, the roof must be cut (or the room treated as an enclosed room) to match the plan; a roof terrace requires an opening in the roof.

when a plan labels a roof terrace and th.rule: When a plan labels a roof terrace and the section draws the roof closed over it, the roof must be cut open over the terrace footprint (a roof terrace) rather than built solid; the door to it stays as the access.

a door whose drawn head would reach over.rule: A door whose drawn head would reach over the roof underside at its wall is not usable; the build must provide a dormer (or the architect must confirm the door is not a full-height door) before it is built.

a door whose top is above the roof under.rule: A door whose top is above the roof underside at its wall shows through the roof; the build must clip the door to the roof underside or provide a dormer, and flag the case for review.

site areas drawn as pools, sunning terra.rule: Site areas drawn as pools, sunning terraces and parking must be built as site geometry (pool basin + coping + deck/platform + parking slab) when the plan labels them, not dropped as 'no outline'.

two levels at the same elevation with ne.rule: Two levels at the same elevation with near-identical room sets are a duplicate read of one floor; the level count must match the section.

a room whose label and drawn furniture (.rule: A room whose label and drawn furniture (sofa, coffee table, dining table, bookshelf) match a living program must be typed living, not other, even when a twin room on the same level carries the correct type.

a bathroom set is completed to the full.rule: A bathroom set is completed to the full set (basin, toilet, bath or shower, tall cabinet) whenever the documents draw a member of the set; a missing member is added, not dropped.

a hall is a circulation space: it is fur.rule: A hall is a circulation space: it is furnished only with a console or bench and a stair, never with a shoe_cabinet or wardrobe, unless the documents explicitly draw an entrance vestibule or storage in that hall.

a balcony or terrace larger than 10 m2 i.rule: A balcony or terrace larger than 10 m2 is furnished as a full outdoor room (seating group plus dining table and chairs plus planters), not with a single chair and a table.

every site area the documents label (poo.rule: Every site area the documents label (pool, sunning terrace, parking, garden) is built as a modelled site element with its outline, paving and water or planting; a labelled site area is never left as bare ground.

a living room with a tv_unit is furnishe.rule: A living room with a tv_unit is furnished as a full media wall (tv_unit, sideboard, floor lamp, rug) and a seating group (sofa, armchair, coffee table) with a dining group; a bare wall behind the TV is a fit failure.

a bathroom whose program allows a walk-i.rule: A bathroom whose program allows a walk-in shower must be built with a glass walk-in shower (rain head, hand shower on a rail, linear drain), a floating vanity with lit open cubbies and a large backlit mirror, not a bathtub and a plain counter.

every bathroom must carry one feature wa.rule: Every bathroom must carry one feature wall (a dark fluted WC wall or a stone apron behind and under the vanity), towel bars at the door and at the shower, and towels in one accent colour repeated in two or three places.

interior doors must be modeled as distin.rule: Interior doors must be modeled as distinct products with visible panels or profiles, and the entrance door must be visually distinct from interior doors.

every bathroom render must show the deta.rule: Every bathroom render must show the detailed wet-room scheme: an illuminated mirror, a lit open niche or shelf column with styled toiletries, a towel rail, and under-vanity or cove lighting, not a bare tiled wall with a plain mirror.

interior doors default to open (swung cl.rule: Interior doors default to open (swung clear of the opening) in renders unless a piece or wall physically stops them; only exterior or privacy doors stay closed.

the bathroom_set group must be able to b.rule: The bathroom_set group must be able to build the P12 reference (floating fluted vanity with lit cubbies and floor glow, feature panel with matching top, large backlit mirror, walk-in glass shower with rain head, hand shower on rail and linear drain, towel shelf, two-cluster counter) when the room's family allows it, instead of only a basic washbasin/toilet/cabinet/shower set.

the bathroom build must include the p13.rule: The bathroom build must include the P13 reference: one feature wall (dark fluted WC wall or stone apron behind/under the vanity), a mirror shaped and framed by the family, towel bars at the door and at the shower, and towels in one accent colour repeated in two or three places.

an interior view that includes a door to.rule: An interior view that includes a door to a room worth showing must frame that door open with the room beyond lit and furnished; a view whose only door is closed should be re-aimed to show the room's own furnished pieces instead.

interior doors must stand open by defaul.rule: Interior doors must stand open by default (leaf turned against its swing side); a render that shows an interior door fully closed is a camera/door-state error to be corrected by re-aiming the view or opening the leaf.

every bathroom must have at least one wi.rule: Every bathroom must have at least one window or a light well to provide daylight and ventilation, unless it is a wet room with a mechanical ventilation system explicitly shown in the documents.

every bathroom render must carry the ref.rule: Every bathroom render must carry the reference detail set: an illuminated mirror, a lit open niche or shelf with toiletries, a towel rail, a paper holder and large-format wall tiles, not a bare wall with a plain framed mirror.

interior doors render open by default wh.rule: Interior doors render open by default wherever the swing is unobstructed, and door finishes vary by family (glazed divided-lite where the plan calls for it) rather than all being identical closed slabs.

a bathroom whose family allows the p12 r.rule: A bathroom whose family allows the P12 reference must be furnished to that reference (floating vanity, feature panel, backlit mirror, walk-in shower with glass, rain head, linear drain, towel shelf) rather than a basic set, when its area and layout permit it.

a bathroom whose family allows the p13 r.rule: A bathroom whose family allows the P13 reference must include one feature wall, a family-shaped framed mirror, towel bars at the door and shower, and towels in one accent colour repeated in two or three places.

every parametric stair with an open side.rule: Every parametric stair with an open side must automatically include a safety railing or guard on that open side.

every stair opening in a corridor or hal.rule: Every stair opening in a corridor or hall must automatically include a safety railing or guard on its open edges.

a wardrobe model must read as a storage.rule: A wardrobe model must read as a storage unit (doors, handles, depth); a flat wall-panel model with an embedded window frame is a wrong model for the type and must be swapped.

scene check s5 failures (detached elemen.rule: Scene check S5 failures (detached elements) are resolved by re-running the build stage so the join/attach pass re-evaluates the scene.

a ceiling light with no hang record (cor.rule: A ceiling light with no hang record (cord/rod/canopy) is a build-stage omission; re-running build regenerates the hang geometry.

a sofa whose parts stand more than 1 cm.rule: A sofa whose parts stand more than 1 cm apart is a build-stage join failure; re-running build re-runs soft_seats.join_parts. A swap to an audited-removed asset is refused.

scene check s1 geometry failures are res.rule: Scene check S1 geometry failures are resolved by re-running the build stage.

scene check s2 geometry failures are res.rule: Scene check S2 geometry failures are resolved by re-running the build stage.

when rotate_piece is refused because eve.rule: When rotate_piece is refused because every candidate orientation lowers the plausibility score (the piece cannot face its group without breaking F4/F6), the furniture agent's next round must re-place the piece, not just rotate it.

a piece reaching through the room outlin.rule: A piece reaching through the room outline by less than 0.03 m (3 cm) is within tolerance and is not a real finding.

a parametric piece whose drawn footprint.rule: A parametric piece whose drawn footprint is larger than every library model in its type (e.g. a 0.80 m drawn coffee table vs 0.78 m max models) must be built at its drawn size, not shrunk to a library model, so it does not collide with its neighbours; the collision is then resolved by moving the neighbour, not the drawn anchor.

an armchair that is drawn behind the bac.rule: An armchair that is drawn behind the back of a sofa (looking at it) and whose every rotation either leaves it facing the sofa's back or faces a wall within 0.12 m must be re-placed by the group solver, not rotated in place; the seating group's orientation is solved as a unit around the sofa.

an armchair that is drawn at a distance.rule: An armchair that is drawn at a distance and angle from its seating group that no single rotation or small move can bring within the group's facing and distance limits must be re-placed by the group solver, not rotated in place; the seating group's orientation is solved as a unit around the sofa.

a dining chair needs ≥ 0.81 m from the t.rule: A dining chair needs ≥ 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; the solver must place chairs with that clearance and the inspector must flag any chair short of it.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall (or a.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall (or a fixed piece); the solver must not leave a sofa floating in the middle of a room, and the inspector must flag any sofa whose back is off a wall.

an armchair in a seating group must face.rule: An armchair in a seating group must face the group (the sofa/coffee table it belongs to); the solver must orient armchairs toward their group and the inspector must flag any armchair that does not face it.

a double bed needs ≥ 0.60 m of free walk.rule: A double bed needs ≥ 0.60 m of free walkway along each side; the solver must place the bed with that clearance and the inspector must flag any bed short of it.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window (it blocks the opening and the light); the solver must place nightstands clear of windows and the inspector must flag any that block one.

a wardrobe needs ≥ 0.80 m of free space.rule: A wardrobe needs ≥ 0.80 m of free space in front to open its doors; the solver must place wardrobes with that clearance and the inspector must flag any short of it.

a shower must be a real product size (a.rule: A shower must be a real product size (a standard shower tray/cabine); the solver must not build a shower at a size no product has, and the inspector must flag any shower outside the type's product sizes.

a bed must keep at least 0.60 m of free.rule: A bed must keep at least 0.60 m of free clearance on its open side; when the drawn position cannot provide it, the solver must re-place the bed (or swap to a narrower model) rather than accept the tight fit.

a wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of.rule: A wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of free space in front for its doors to open; the solver must re-place it or choose a shallower model when the drawn position blocks this clearance.

the free zone in front of a sofa must no.rule: The free zone in front of a sofa must not be blocked by another piece; the solver must arrange the seating group so the sofa's front is clear.

a coffee table must be positioned in fro.rule: A coffee table must be positioned in front of the sofa it serves; the solver must place it within the seating group's front zone.

an armchair in a seating group must be w.rule: An armchair in a seating group must be within 2.50 m of the coffee table and oriented within 30° of it; the solver must place it accordingly.

a dining chair must have at least 0.81 m.rule: A dining chair must have at least 0.81 m of clearance behind it (from table edge to wall or piece); the solver must ensure this in the dining group layout.

a dining table must not stand in front o.rule: A dining table must not stand in front of a window, blocking the view and light; the solver must place the dining group away from windows.

a dining chair must not stand in front o.rule: A dining chair must not stand in front of a window, blocking the view and light; the solver must place the dining group away from windows.

a wall cabinet in a kitchen must use a r.rule: A wall cabinet in a kitchen must use a realistic model with proper materials and detail, not a crude low-poly placeholder.

site areas labeled in the documents (poo.rule: Site areas labeled in the documents (pools, sunning platforms, parking) must be built with outlines and appropriate models; the site stage must read and construct all labeled site areas, not just the building.

when two levels are at the same elevatio.rule: When two levels are at the same elevation and contain near-identical duplicate rooms, the reading stage must detect this as a duplicated floor and merge them, not build both.

a potted plant placed by the decor stage.rule: A potted plant placed by the decor stage must be preserved through the agent stage; if it is removed, the agent must re-add it or record the reason.

the agent stage must not drop a placed d.rule: The agent stage must not drop a placed decor piece (a potted_plant) that the decor stage built and that the room's program allows; a piece is removed only when a code check refuses it, and the removal must be recorded.

the agent stage must not drop a placed p.rule: The agent stage must not drop a placed piece (an armchair) that the decor stage built and that the room's program allows; a piece is removed only when a code check refuses it, and the removal must be recorded.

The agent stage must not drop a placed piece (a side_table) that the decor stage built and that the room's program allows; a piece is removed only when a code check refuses it, and the removal must be recorded.

a stove drawn as part of a kitchen run m.rule: A stove drawn as part of a kitchen run must be built as a member of that run (the run's model carries the hob); the build stage must not leave a planned stove without a scene object when its kitchen run is present.

a sink drawn as part of a kitchen run mu.rule: A sink drawn as part of a kitchen run must be built as a member of that run; the build stage must not leave a planned sink without a scene object when its kitchen run is present.

when two floor_lamp footprints of the sa.rule: When two floor_lamp footprints of the same room overlap by more than 30%, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the larger (a lamp drawn twice), not a second lamp; the larger is kept and the smaller is not built, and this is a correct drop, not a loss.

When two floor_lamp footprints of the same room overlap by more than 15%, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the larger (a lamp drawn twice), not a second lamp; the larger is kept and the smaller is not built, and this is a correct drop, not a loss.

a small footprint (an ottoman) drawn mor.rule: A small footprint (an ottoman) drawn more than 80% inside an armchair's footprint is the armchair's seat cushion, not a separate piece; it is not built, and this is a correct drop, not a loss.

a section or elevation layer (a layer wh.rule: A section or elevation layer (a layer whose name carries a view marker such as 'görünüş' or that holds only the stair's profile) is not plan geometry: the model builds the stair from the plan layer and the section layer is recorded as a view, not as a lost element.

a layer whose name carries a view marker.rule: A layer whose name carries a view marker such as 'görünüş' (elevation) is a view, not plan geometry: it is recorded as a view and not flagged as a lost element.

a layer that holds only decorative detai.rule: A layer that holds only decorative detail geometry (arcs, curves, thin lines) and no INSERT blocks is a detail/decoration layer, not a furniture layer: it is recorded as decoration and not flagged as a lost element.

a decor element whose host piece is not.rule: A decor element whose host piece is not built must not be silently dropped: the build stage must either build the host or record each dependent decor element as lost with the host's id, so the loss is visible and reviewable.

furniture symbols on a furniture layer (.rule: Furniture symbols on a furniture layer (e.g. 'A-TEFRIS') are buildable content, not unbuildable annotations: the build stage must type and build them, or record each as lost with a reason, never skip the whole layer.

site areas labelled in the plan (parking.rule: Site areas labelled in the plan (parking, terrace, pool) are buildable site content: the build stage must build their outlines from site.paving/parking/grass, or record each as lost with a reason, never skip them as 'exterior labels'.

a stove drawn with its back parallel to.rule: A stove drawn with its back parallel to a wall and a small gap behind it belongs on the wall: the reading stage must snap its back to the wall, not leave a visible gap.

a kitchen room's program requires a frid.rule: A kitchen room's program requires a fridge: when the kitchen run is built without one, the build stage must complete the run with the missing fridge, not leave the room without it.

a toilet needs at least 0.38 m from the.rule: A toilet needs at least 0.38 m from the side wall or fixture on each side: the reading stage must place it with that clearance, not 0.33 m.

a bathtub needs at least 0.53 m clear in.rule: A bathtub needs at least 0.53 m clear in front: the reading stage must place it with that clearance, not 0.28 m.

a shower needs at least 0.53 m clear in.rule: A shower needs at least 0.53 m clear in front: the reading stage must place it with that clearance, not 0.27 m.

a shower or bathtub in a bathroom smalle.rule: A shower or bathtub in a bathroom smaller than about 6 m2 must be placed so its front clearance is at least 0.53 m; when the drawn bay cannot give that clearance, the fixture is swapped for a walk-in shower or a shorter tub that fits the bay, never left with a sub-code front gap.

a toilet must have at least 0.38 m from.rule: A toilet must have at least 0.38 m from its centre to the nearest side wall or fixture; when the drawn position cannot give that, the toilet is moved along its wall or the neighbouring fixture is shifted, not left 0.33 m from the wall.

a bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clea.rule: A bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; when the room cannot give that, the tub is swapped for a shorter model or repositioned, never left with 0.28 m.

a bedroom render must frame the bed as t.rule: A bedroom render must frame the bed as the anchor; the camera is posed to show the bed in full, not cut out of the frame.

a room whose documents label it a living.rule: A room whose documents label it a living or activity room and whose area exceeds 30 m2 is typed living, not other, so its full program (tv, seating, dining) is built.

a bathroom set is complete only when it.rule: A bathroom set is complete only when it carries every fixture the documents draw in that bathroom; a missing tall_cabinet is added by completing the set, not left out.

a hall on a floor above the entrance has.rule: A hall on a floor above the entrance has no shoe-off program and no storage program; it is furnished only with a stair and, if drawn, a console or coat hook, never a shoe_cabinet or wardrobe.

a terrace or balcony larger than 10 m2 i.rule: A terrace or balcony larger than 10 m2 is furnished with a full outdoor seating and dining set (multiple chairs, a table, planters) matching the documents, not a single chair and plant.

site areas labelled in the documents (po.rule: Site areas labelled in the documents (pool, sunning terrace, parking) are built as outlines in the model; a labelled site area with no outline is a loss, not an omission.

a living room with a tv_unit must also c.rule: A living room with a tv_unit must also carry a media wall or feature wall behind the TV, a rug under the seating group, and at least one floor lamp or pendant; a bare wall behind the TV is a missing set, not a finished room.

an opening whose ray hits its own wall i.rule: An opening whose ray hits its own wall is not cut through it: the build must cut the opening through the wall it is assigned to, not leave the wall solid.

a stair flight with an open side must be.rule: A stair flight with an open side must be built with a continuous balustrade and handrail over its full run, with newels at turns and ends; a wall handrail where a flight has no open side.

a wall-hung item (mirror, art, shelf) mu.rule: A wall-hung item (mirror, art, shelf) must not be placed on a wall span that is covered by a standing piece (wardrobe, cabinet) whose top reaches over the item's bottom; the decor stage must move it to a free wall span or leave it out.

a wall-hung item must not be placed over.rule: A wall-hung item must not be placed over a window or door opening on its wall; the decor stage must move it to a solid wall span or leave it out.

the camera set must include a frontal vi.rule: The camera set must include a frontal view of the entrance facade, square to it, showing the main door.

when the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3.rule: When the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3 against the building, a retaining edge (wall or stepped plinth) must be built along the affected facade.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.90-0.97 m); the build stage must use a model or parametric height that matches, not a model whose top is above working height.

a bathroom interior view must show the w.rule: A bathroom interior view must show the washbasin and its mirror in frame, not just a tub rim; the camera must be posed to include the basin and mirror.

a bathroom interior view showing a batht.rule: A bathroom interior view showing a bathtub must include its taps/mixer and at least one surrounding design element (mirror, shelf, or adjacent fixture) so it reads as a designed feature, not a bare object.

a bathroom washbasin is never placed wit.rule: A bathroom washbasin is never placed without a mirror above it and a styled wall finish (accent panel or backlit niche); the bathroom set must include a mirror and a feature wall behind the vanity, not a bare flat tile wall.

a bathtub is never placed without visibl.rule: A bathtub is never placed without visible taps/fixtures and a styled surround (feature wall, cove light or stone apron); the bathroom set must include the tap set and a finished wall behind the tub.

a bathroom washbasin is never placed wit.rule: A bathroom washbasin is never placed without a mirror above it; the bathroom set must include a mirror and a styled wall finish behind the vanity.
A bathroom washbasin is never placed without a mirror above it and a styled wall finish; the bathroom set must include a mirror and a feature wall behind the vanity.

a bathroom is never built with a plain b.rule: A bathroom is never built with a plain bathtub and stone counter when the design calls for a walk-in shower with glass, rain head, hand shower on a rail and linear drain, a floating fluted vanity with lit cubbies and floor glow, and a shaped mirror; the bathroom set must match the project's design language.

interior doors are never rendered as pla.rule: Interior doors are never rendered as plain unadorned wooden slabs with basic round knobs; each door must carry a distinct product model with a handle set that matches the room's style.

a bathroom is never rendered with a plai.rule: A bathroom is never rendered with a plain large-format tiled wall, a round mirror and a stone basin on a dark frame without an illuminated mirror, a lit open niche with toiletries, a towel rail, a cove light and under-vanity light; the bathroom set must include these styled elements.

A bathroom is never rendered with a plain light-tile wall, a plain round mirror, no dark fluted WC wall or stone apron feature wall, no towel bars and no accent-colour towels; the bathroom set must include a feature wall, a shaped mirror, towel bars and styled towels.

an interior bathroom is never built with.rule: An interior bathroom is never built without a window or a borrowed-light opening; if the plan shows no window, a high borrowed-light window or an interior glazing must be added to provide daylight.

interior doors are never rendered fully.rule: Interior doors are never rendered fully closed in a hall view; where nothing stops them, inside doors must be shown open by default so the room beyond is visible.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single untyped piece: the reading stage must split it into its member pieces (or mark it as a group) before typing, instead of leaving one oversized untyped blob for review.

when a plan labels a roof terrace with a.rule: When a plan labels a roof terrace with a door to it but the section draws the roof closed over it, the build stage must cut the roof over the terrace footprint (a roof terrace) instead of leaving the roof solid.

a door whose top reaches over the roof u.rule: A door whose top reaches over the roof underside at its wall must be clipped to the roof underside (or a dormer added) so it does not show through the roof.

a door whose top is above the roof under.rule: A door whose top is above the roof underside at its wall must be clipped to the roof underside so it does not show through the roof.

a parametric placeholder model that rend.rule: A parametric placeholder model that renders as a crude low-poly box must be swapped for a library model of the same type and footprint when one is available.

a parametric placeholder that renders as.rule: A parametric placeholder that renders as a crude or misplaced object must be swapped for a library model of the same type and footprint when one is available.

a kitchen counter run under a window or.rule: A kitchen counter run under a window or along a wall must be completed with wall cabinets or tall units above it so the wall is not left blank and unbalanced.

living rooms must have a feature wall (p.rule: Living rooms must have a feature wall (panelling, wainscot or accent finish) behind the main seating and TV wall; flat untextured concrete is not acceptable.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the main group (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) so the room reads as a bathroom, not a bare corner.

bedrooms must have a feature wall (verti.rule: Bedrooms must have a feature wall (vertical fluted or slatted wood panelling) behind the bed; flat untextured paint is not acceptable.

living rooms must have a feature wall (v.rule: Living rooms must have a feature wall (vertical wood panelling or wainscot) behind the main seating; flat untextured paint is not acceptable.

beds must be dressed with layered beddin.rule: Beds must be dressed with layered bedding (throw, second blanket, euro shams, decorative cushions); a single flat duvet is not acceptable.

a sofa model that looks like a crude blo.rule: A sofa model that looks like a crude blocky placeholder must be swapped for a library model of the same type and footprint that matches the project style.

a dining table that collides with a chai.rule: A dining table that collides with a chair by more than the tolerance must be swapped for a model with a smaller footprint or different leg geometry that clears the chair.

a washbasin model that renders as a crud.rule: A washbasin model that renders as a crude low-poly box must be swapped for a library model of the same type and footprint with a realistic curved basin.

bathrooms must have warm layered lightin.rule: Bathrooms must have warm layered lighting and a dark accent wall to match the reference style; flat beige with cold grey metal hardware is not acceptable.

for a hall whose only camera is refused.rule: For a hall whose only camera is refused by the pose solver, do not re-ask set_camera; flag the room for a program/layout change (add a console or mirror, or re-solve) instead.

when set_camera is refused for every pos.rule: When set_camera is refused for every pose of a room, the finding is a room-program/layout issue, not a camera issue; do not retry set_camera.

kitchen and living surfaces should carry.rule: Kitchen and living surfaces should carry a small set of styling props (bowl, board, small appliance, books, vase) as part of the room's finished look; the furniture stage should place these props on counters and tables, not leave them bare.

armchairs in a living room should share.rule: Armchairs in a living room should share the design language (style tags) of the main sofa; the fit stage should prefer models whose style tags overlap the sofa's.

sofas and beds should carry cushions, pi.rule: Sofas and beds should carry cushions, pillows and a throw as part of the finished look; the furniture stage should add these soft-furnishing props to seating and sleeping groups.

windows in living and bedroom rooms shou.rule: Windows in living and bedroom rooms should carry layered curtains (sheer + drape on a ceiling track) as part of the finished look; the furniture/decoration stage should add window treatments to full-height windows.

bathroom cameras should frame the room's.rule: Bathroom cameras should frame the room's main fixture group (basin, toilet, cabinet) rather than a single corner; the camera stage should pick poses that show the functional set.
Bathroom cameras should frame the room's main fixture group (basin, toilet, shower) rather than a single corner; the camera stage should pick poses that show the functional set.

when set_camera is refused for every pos.rule: When set_camera is refused for every pose of a small bathroom (duplicate or no free point), the finding is a room-size/layout issue, not a camera issue; do not retry set_camera.

bedroom furniture (bed, bench, wardrobe).rule: Bedroom furniture (bed, bench, wardrobe) should share a design language and palette that matches the room's wall colour and the project's modern standard; the fit stage should reject models whose style tags (e.g. 'classic', 'ornate') conflict with the room's modern palette, and the decoration stage should add feature walls, bedding and art.

every large exterior window (glazing wid.rule: Every large exterior window (glazing wider than 1.5 m) must be dressed with a full-height layered curtain treatment (sheer plus drape) in the render, so no large window is shown as bare glass.

in every living room, the wall behind th.rule: In every living room, the wall behind the main seating (the wall the sofa or sideboard faces) must be finished as a feature wall (fluted or slatted wood panelling or wainscot), not a single flat paint colour.

coffee tables and sideboards in living r.rule: Coffee tables and sideboards in living rooms must be styled with curated objects (a mirror, vase, leaning art print, books) in the render, never left bare.

potted plants and other decor placed in.rule: Potted plants and other decor placed in a room must be visible in the render (not hidden behind walls or out of frame); bare long walls and corners must be filled with visible decor.

every camera view must show the furnitur.rule: Every camera view must show the furniture and decor that belong to its room; a view dominated by an out-of-focus foreground element (curtain, plant) that blocks the room's contents is not acceptable.

exterior renders must use warm, directio.rule: Exterior renders must use warm, directional lighting (not flat overcast grey), show warm light from windows, and include the full exterior styling (landscaping, materials, details) set by the reference.

large ground-floor glazing on the main f.rule: Large ground-floor glazing on the main facade must show warm interior light in exterior renders, so the facade does not look like a dead dark void.

exterior renders must have appealing lig.rule: Exterior renders must have appealing lighting, real landscaping (not a green void), and facade material richness matching the reference style.

exterior renders must be styled (warm li.rule: Exterior renders must be styled (warm lighting, landscaping, furniture, materials) to match the reference; a raw grey-box massing study is not client-ready.

exterior renders must have textured mate.rule: Exterior renders must have textured materials, warm directional lighting (not flat and foggy), and a designed landscape (not a featureless void).

site/aerial views must show material ric.rule: Site/aerial views must show material richness (wood, glass, metal), landscape design (planters, paths, lighting), and warm lighting; a raw massing study with a textureless lawn is not acceptable.

a decor item that cannot rest on its hos.rule: A decor item that cannot rest on its host within tolerance (gap or penetration) must be dropped from the scene, not left as a failed build; the rest check already rejects it, so the scene stage should silently omit it instead of reporting it as a finding.

the reading stage must read entities on.rule: The reading stage must read entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) when the ledger shows they hold geometry the model needs; a layer being off in the source file is not a reason to skip its entities.
the reading stage must read entities on.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

a camera that is dropped must carry a re.rule: A camera that is dropped must carry a reason (e.g. 'redundant with ext_3', 'blocked by geometry', 'outside the building envelope'); a camera dropped with no reason is a loss that must be explained.

an exterior camera that must show a give.rule: An exterior camera that must show a given window is posed to frame that window; a window missing from a required view is a camera framing error, not a missing window.

a small drawn block (under ~0.7 m) on a.rule: A small drawn block (under ~0.7 m) on a level that already has its functional set built (a bathroom with its full set, a hall with its stair) is a detail or annotation, not a missing element; the ledger should not flag it as lost.

a stair block drawn on a level where a s.rule: A stair block drawn on a level where a stair is already built in the model is a duplicate or annotation, not a missing element.

a block under 0.3 m is a detail (fixture.rule: A block under 0.3 m is a detail (fixture, symbol, annotation), not a missing element.

a block with a non-descriptive name (e.g.rule: A block with a non-descriptive name (e.g. 'eeere') and a size matching a common furniture piece already present in the room is a duplicate or annotation, not a missing element.

a block with a non-descriptive name and.rule: A block with a non-descriptive name and a size matching a large furniture piece already present in the room (e.g. a bed or sofa) is a duplicate or annotation, not a missing element.

a block under 0.7 m with a non-descripti.rule: A block under 0.7 m with a non-descriptive name is a detail or annotation, not a missing element.

a block under 0.8 m with a non-descripti.rule: A block under 0.8 m with a non-descriptive name is a detail or annotation, not a missing element.

a site decor block (tefriş = decoration).rule: A site decor block (TEFRIŞ = decoration) recorded by site decor elements (sd_*) is intentionally not built as a model element; it is a site annotation.

a small drawn block (under ~0.7 m) on a.rule: A small drawn block (under ~0.7 m) on a level that already has its functional set built is a detail or annotation, not a missing element.

when the source dwg has entities on off,.rule: When the source DWG has entities on off, frozen or invisible layers, the reading stage must list them in the ledger as 'not read (layer state)' and the audit must treat them as a source-data note, not a lost-element finding, unless a later check shows a specific missing element that the frozen layer would have supplied.

a drawn symbol that two independent pass.rule: A drawn symbol that two independent passes both classify as not furniture is correctly kept as a non-built obstacle; the ledger warning is informational, not a loss.

a wall-layer selection warning that docu.rule: A wall-layer selection warning that documents the chosen layer and its evidence is informational; columns that stand out of the wall band are structural, not furniture, and are not modelled as pieces.

a drawn element on a structural layer (a.rule: A drawn element on a structural layer (A-BA) classified as a column is correctly not built as furniture; the ledger warning is informational.

a drawn element that is 60% or more insi.rule: A drawn element that is 60% or more inside a larger built fixture is correctly treated as a duplicate or part of that fixture and not built separately.

two floor lamps of the same room that ov.rule: Two floor lamps of the same room that overlap are one lamp drawn twice; the larger one is kept and the smaller duplicate is not built.

a layer of generic 2d entities (circles,.rule: A layer of generic 2D entities (circles, lines) that is not referenced by any room, piece, or opening is auxiliary drawing content (dimensions, annotations, or construction lines) and is correctly not modelled.

a 2d decoration/hatch layer (floor or wa.rule: A 2D decoration/hatch layer (floor or wall finish pattern) is not a built element: the model carries the finish in the material slot, so its entities are neither built nor warned.

a drawn piece that is typed correctly bu.rule: A drawn piece that is typed correctly but has no model assigned must be fitted with a library model of matching size and style so it is built, not left as 'model none'.

a piece present in the decor stage must.rule: A piece present in the decor stage must survive the agent stage: the agent must not drop a placed piece that the documents show, only reposition or retype it.

a room whose label names a multi-use act.rule: A room whose label names a multi-use activity/leisure space (e.g. 'Oyun Aktivite Ve Dinlenme Odası') must be typed 'living', not 'other', so that standard living-room furniture (sofa, armchair, bench, table) is allowed and verified instead of kept unverified.

when one room outline carries two room l.rule: When one room outline carries two room labels (e.g. 'Salon' and 'AÇIK MUTFAK'), the reading must split the outline into the two rooms at the wall between them (or, if no wall is drawn, keep the larger-area label and record the second as an open-kitchen zone) instead of silently keeping only the largest label.

an exterior camera that frames a facade.rule: An exterior camera that frames a facade must be posed so that windows read as windows (clear sightline, not occluded by a mullion, frame or adjacent element); a window that renders as 'other_object' in an exterior view indicates the camera or the window model is wrong and must be corrected before the view is accepted.

a drawn piece whose model footprint diff.rule: A drawn piece whose model footprint differs from its drawn footprint must be placed so its centre matches the drawn centre within tolerance; if the model is larger, the layout must shift it back to the drawn centre rather than leaving it offset.

a drawn piece whose drawn size differs f.rule: A drawn piece whose drawn size differs from the fitted model by more than 0.05 m must be resized to its drawn size (or fitted with a model of that size) before the layout solver is allowed to move it; a move that only hides a size mismatch is refused.

a drawn bed whose drawn width exceeds 1..rule: A drawn bed whose drawn width exceeds 1.80 m is a king-size bed and must be fitted with a king-size model (or resized to the drawn width); a standard double model is not a valid fit for a drawn king footprint.

a chair drawn at a dining table must kee.rule: A chair drawn at a dining table must keep its drawn position and orientation relative to the table; the layout solver may not move or rotate a drawn chair to satisfy a generic 'face the table' rule when the drawing already shows the intended pose.

a zone label that names a kitchen (e.g..rule: A zone label that names a kitchen (e.g. 'AÇIK MUTFAK', 'OPEN KITCHEN') inside a living room outline must be read as a kitchen zone: the reading stage classifies the labelled area as a kitchen sub-zone so the open kitchen is kept and its fixtures are placed, rather than leaving it as an unclassified label.

a door whose opening no library model fi.rule: A door whose opening no library model fits is built parametric in the house's door family; that is the correct fallback and is not a finding.

when every candidate library model for a.rule: When every candidate library model for a piece is refused by the fit rules or removed by audit, the piece is built parametric and the finding is closed as a library gap rather than retried.

when a piece is built from the parametri.rule: When a piece is built from the parametric family, the fit stage must first try the library models that match its size and room style; the parametric mesh is the fallback, not the default.

the kitchen module builder must align th.rule: The kitchen module builder must align the joints of wall cabinets with the joints of the base units below them, so that the vertical seams match.

the lighting rule must hang the calculat.rule: The lighting rule must hang the calculated number of ceiling lights (6) in a living room of 50.9 m², not fewer.

the decor stage must place a tv in a bed.rule: The decor stage must place a TV in a bedroom if there is a suitable wall space, or explicitly mark the room as TV-free if the design intent is to omit it.

the layout stage must include storage (e.rule: The layout stage must include storage (e.g., a tall cabinet or shelf) in a bathroom set, not just the fixtures.

the decor stage must apply a fluted pane.rule: The decor stage must apply a fluted panel or similar feature to the accent wall in a bedroom to meet the professional bar (UL106).

a room typed 'living' always receives th.rule: A room typed 'living' always receives the full professional dressing (accent-wall feature panel and layered sheer+opaque curtains) even when its label names a different use; the type, not the label, drives the finish set.

every bed_double in a modern bedroom is.rule: Every bed_double in a modern bedroom is dressed with the full bedding set including a woven, fringed throw across its foot; the throw is generated by the bedding plan, never left to a separate placement step.

the bedding dressing step must produce a.rule: The bedding dressing step must produce a smooth, taut duvet surface on every bed_double (no lumps or wrinkles exceeding 6 mm over 0.30 m) before any throw or cushion is placed; a lumpy duvet is a dressing failure, not a model choice.

in any room typed 'living', the tv_unit.rule: In any room typed 'living', the tv_unit is always a floating or wall-mounted console (per P16/R45); a floor-standing TV unit is not allowed in a living room and the decor stage must select a wall-hung model.

every sofa group in a room typed 'living.rule: Every sofa group in a room typed 'living' must be placed on a rug (per UL106 and P16 R48); the decor stage's living-dining details always include a rug under the seating group.

kitchen countertops must use a textured.rule: Kitchen countertops must use a textured stone material (marble_slab, travertine, or similar) rather than a flat, untextured grey; the material assignment stage must select a rich stone look for kitchen counters.
