all chairs in a dining group must use th.rule: All chairs in a dining group must use the same model or a matching set; the decor stage must assign a single chair model to every chair around a dining table to maintain set coherence.

door materials must be consistent with t.rule: Door materials must be consistent with the room's material palette; a door's finish must not clash with the dominant floor and wall materials of the room it serves. The material assignment stage must check door finishes against the room's palette.

terraces and balconies longer than 3 m m.rule: Terraces and balconies longer than 3 m must include decking, planters, or accent elements to break up the paving; the decor stage must add these as part of the terrace dressing.

terrace and balcony views must have a te.rule: Terrace and balcony views must have a textured landscape background (trees, hedge, or garden) rather than a flat, untextured green plane; the site dressing stage must add a textured background to all outdoor views.

all balconies and upper terraces must in.rule: All balconies and upper terraces must include planters or greenery to soften the hard stone and glass; the decor stage must add planter boxes with plants to every balcony.

a desk in a bedroom or study that has a.rule: A desk in a bedroom or study that has a seat facing it must carry a work set (laptop or computer) on its top, oriented to the seat, so the workstation reads as used.

a drawn outline larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn outline larger than 4.5 m on a side that encloses other pieces is a zone or rug mark, not a furniture piece; the build stage must not build it as a piece.

when both recognition passes classify a.rule: When both recognition passes classify a drawn symbol as not_furniture, the build stage correctly keeps it as an obstacle and does not build it as a piece.

a drawn outline that encloses a table an.rule: A drawn outline that encloses a table and chairs and is identified as a rug mark is not a furniture piece; the decor stage handles rug placement.

when two floor lamps of the same room ov.rule: When two floor lamps of the same room overlap by more than 15%, they are one lamp drawn twice; the larger footprint is kept and the smaller duplicate is not built.

a small ottoman drawn more than 50% insi.rule: A small ottoman drawn more than 50% inside an armchair or sofa is its seat cushion or part of that piece, not a separate furniture item; it is not built independently.

a piece removed by an explicit ai.remove.rule: A piece removed by an explicit AI.remove_piece decision is not built; the removal is intentional and the finding is a record of that decision.

a large outline (over 3 m on a side) tha.rule: A large outline (over 3 m on a side) that encloses other pieces is a rug or zone mark, not a furniture piece; the decor stage handles rug placement.

the upper end of a stair that arrives at.rule: The upper end of a stair that arrives at the top level of the building is not built as a separate piece; the stair is already represented by its lower-level instance.

a ceiling light must be hung from the ce.rule: A ceiling light must be hung from the ceiling with a cord or rod and a canopy; a gap greater than 0.02 m between its top and the ceiling is a defect.

a cushion placed on a bed must rest on i.rule: A cushion placed on a bed must rest on its surface; penetration deeper than 0.03 m is a defect.

when one room outline holds the labels o.rule: When one room outline holds the labels of several rooms, the reading must split it into separate rooms at the internal walls; a label with no room of its own is a lost room.

a ledger a1 'no room uses this label' is.rule: A ledger A1 'no room uses this label' is a false alarm when a room of the same level and function already exists at the label's anchor with a larger outline; report it as a size mismatch, not a lost room.

A ledger A1 'no room uses this label' is a false alarm when a room of the same level and function already exists at the label's anchor within 1 m² of the label's area; report it as a size mismatch, not a lost room.

a balcony or terrace room must have its.rule: A balcony or terrace room must have its terrace_lounge group placed; an empty outdoor space is a failed fit, not a taste issue.

any floor opening (stairwell, void, or m.rule: Any floor opening (stairwell, void, or mezzanine edge) that drops to a lower level must have a guard (railing or glass pane) at least 1.10 m high built along its open edge; the build stage must detect floor openings and add guards automatically.

decor elements must be clipped or reposi.rule: Decor elements must be clipped or repositioned so their top does not exceed the roof line (ridge height minus a 0.1 m clearance); the build stage must check decor heights against the roof and refuse or adjust any element that pokes through.

an interior camera must show at least on.rule: An interior camera must show at least one main fixture or piece of the room; a black or empty frame is a failed camera and must be repositioned to show the room's content.

scene check failures (s5) indicate geome.rule: Scene check failures (S5) indicate geometry or placement errors; the build stage must be re-run to resolve them.

sofa and soft-seat models must have thei.rule: Sofa and soft-seat models must have their parts joined within 1 cm; the build stage must re-run soft_seats.join_parts if parts are separated by more than 1 cm.

scene check failures (s1) indicate geome.rule: Scene check failures (S1) indicate geometry errors; the build stage must be re-run to resolve them.

scene check failures (s2) indicate geome.rule: Scene check failures (S2) indicate geometry errors; the build stage must be re-run to resolve them.

a scene check that fails on a level is a.rule: A scene check that fails on a level is a build-stage defect: re-run the build for that level so the geometry is regenerated and re-checked.

when every rotation of a drawn piece is.rule: When every rotation of a drawn piece is refused because it cannot face its group without breaking another rule, the furniture agent's next round must re-solve the whole seating group (sofa, coffee table, armchairs) as one unit rather than rotating a single piece.

a tv_unit whose back is off a wall and w.rule: A tv_unit whose back is off a wall and whose rotation is refused must be re-placed by the furniture agent against the wall it belongs to, as part of the seating group it serves.

a piece that reaches through the room ou.rule: A piece that reaches through the room outline by 0.020 m (2 cm) is within the 0.03 m tolerance and is not a real defect.

when a drawn coffee table overlaps an ar.rule: When a drawn coffee table overlaps an armchair and every move is refused (drawn lock, max tries), the furniture agent must re-solve the seating group so the table and chairs are spaced correctly.

a piece whose front use zone is not reac.rule: A piece whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the furniture agent so the walkway is clear.

a sofa whose front use zone is not reach.rule: A sofa whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the furniture agent so the walkway is clear.

when every rotation of a drawn piece is.rule: When every rotation of a drawn piece is refused because it cannot face its group without breaking another rule, the furniture agent's next round must re-solve the whole seating group as one unit.

when a drawn coffee table overlaps an ar.rule: When a drawn coffee table overlaps an armchair and every move is refused (max tries), the furniture agent must re-solve the seating group so the table and chairs are spaced correctly.

a stove whose back is not on a wall must.rule: A stove whose back is not on a wall must be re-placed by the furniture agent against the kitchen counter run it belongs to.

a kitchen run is placed so the working a.rule: A kitchen run is placed so the working aisle in front of the counter is at least 0.90 m; if the drawn run leaves less, the run is re-solved on the same wall with the aisle met.

a stove is part of the kitchen run and i.rule: A stove is part of the kitchen run and its back sits on the wall; a run re-solve snaps the stove to the wall.

a sofa is placed with its long side as t.rule: A sofa is placed with its long side as the seat (back on a wall); a seating group re-solve orients the sofa correctly.

a sofa's back sits on a wall; a seating.rule: A sofa's back sits on a wall; a seating group re-solve snaps it to the nearest free wall span.

an armchair in a seating group faces the.rule: An armchair in a seating group faces the group's centre; a seating group re-solve orients it.

an armchair's front use zone is kept cle.rule: An armchair's front use zone is kept clear; a seating group re-solve places the chairs so their fronts are not blocked.

a dining chair has at least 0.81 m behin.rule: A dining chair has at least 0.81 m behind it to the wall or piece; a dining group re-solve places the chairs with that clearance.

a double bed has at least 0.60 m free on.rule: A double bed has at least 0.60 m free on each side; a sleeping_double group re-solve places the bed with that clearance.

a wardrobe has at least 0.80 m free in f.rule: A wardrobe has at least 0.80 m free in front for the doors to open; a storage group re-solve places it with that clearance.

a drawn shower whose footprint is not a.rule: A drawn shower whose footprint is not a real product size is a misread bay: fix it to the nearest real shower size that fits the bay, not a parametric stretch.

when a bed's side clearance is under 0.6.rule: When a bed's side clearance is under 0.60 m, swap to a narrower bed model that fits the room instead of moving the bed off its drawn wall.

a wardrobe whose front clearance is unde.rule: A wardrobe whose front clearance is under 0.80 m and whose wall has no free span within 1.2 m of its drawn place is a room-program conflict: the room is too narrow for a full-depth wardrobe on that wall, so the wardrobe must be swapped to a shallower model or the room re-laid out, not nudged.

when a wardrobe's front clearance is und.rule: When a wardrobe's front clearance is under 0.80 m, swap to a shallower wardrobe model that fits the room instead of moving the wardrobe off its drawn wall.

an armchair that stands behind the back.rule: An armchair that stands behind the back of its seating group and cannot be rotated to face the group without facing a wall is a group-layout conflict: the room's seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the single chair rotated.

a sofa whose front free zone is blocked.rule: A sofa whose front free zone is blocked by another sofa (a double-sofa layout) is a group-layout conflict: the two sofas must be re-solved as one seating group, not one sofa moved.

a coffee table that is not in front of t.rule: A coffee table that is not in front of the sofa and cannot be moved more than 0.3 m (drawn lock) is a group-layout conflict: the seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the table nudged.

an armchair that is off-angle and too fa.rule: An armchair that is off-angle and too far from the coffee table and cannot be moved more than 0.3 m (drawn lock) is a group-layout conflict: the seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the chair nudged.

a tv_unit whose back is 1.01 m off a wal.rule: A tv_unit whose back is 1.01 m off a wall and whose walls have no free span (doors, windows) is a room-program conflict: the room's walls are too interrupted for a wall-mounted tv_unit at its drawn place, so the tv_unit must be re-solved with the seating group or the room re-laid out.

an armchair that stands behind the back.rule: An armchair that stands behind the back of the tv_unit and cannot be rotated to face the group without facing a wall is a group-layout conflict: the seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the single chair rotated.

a coffee table that is not between the s.rule: A coffee table that is not between the sofa and its TV is a group-layout conflict: the seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the table nudged.

site areas that the documents label and.rule: Site areas that the documents label and outline (pools, sunning terraces, parking) must be built as site geometry (pool basin with coping/deck, terrace platform, parking slab) at their drawn outline; a labelled site area with no outline in the model is a loss, not an optional omission.

when two levels are read at the same ele.rule: When two levels are read at the same elevation and hold near-identical duplicate rooms, the reading has split one floor into two; merge them into a single level instead of building a duplicated floor.

the agent stage must not drop a drawn pi.rule: The agent stage must not drop a drawn piece of a room's seating set; a dropped piece is a loss, not a detail.

a planned kitchen piece (stove) must be.rule: A planned kitchen piece (stove) must be built; a planned piece with no scene object is a build loss.

a planned kitchen piece (sink) must be b.rule: A planned kitchen piece (sink) must be built; a planned piece with no scene object is a build loss.

a drawn piece that is a duplicate of a l.rule: A drawn piece that is a duplicate of a larger same-type piece (one lamp drawn twice) is a detail, not a loss; the larger piece stays.

a drawn piece that is a seat cushion of.rule: A drawn piece that is a seat cushion of a larger same-type piece (one armchair drawn with its cushion) is a detail, not a loss; the larger piece stays.

a stair core room whose only camera poin.rule: A stair core room whose only camera point is inside the stair is shown from the adjacent hall, not from inside the stair; the hall's camera must include the stair.

a drawn stove block on a level must be b.rule: A drawn stove block on a level must be built; a drawn block with no model element is a loss.

a drawn toilet block on a level must be.rule: A drawn toilet block on a level must be built; a drawn block with no model element is a loss.

a drawn block that duplicates a fixture.rule: A drawn block that duplicates a fixture the room already builds (same type, same room, within 0.5 m of the built one) is a drawing duplicate, not a lost element: the ledger must not flag it as unused.

a drawn piece whose type is correct but.rule: A drawn piece whose type is correct but whose model is 'none' (no library model assigned) must be fitted to a library model of its type in the next furniture round, not left unbuilt.

an interior room camera must be posed to.rule: An interior room camera must be posed to show every door of that room; if a door is not in the frame, the camera is re-aimed to include it.

a drawn piece in a kitchen that is too s.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen that is too small to be a fixture (under 0.40 m on its long side) and sits beside the counter is a small appliance or stool: the reading must type it (e.g. bar_stool or a small appliance) or record why it is not furniture, never leave it 'unknown' with no warning.

a stair layer (a-merdiven) that the mode.rule: A stair layer (A-MERDIVEN) that the model already represents with a built stair element is a drawing source, not a lost element: the ledger must mark it as consumed by the stair and not flag it as unused.

a stair elevation/section layer (a-merdi.rule: A stair elevation/section layer (A-merdiven görünüş) that the model already represents with a built stair element is a drawing source, not a lost element: the ledger must mark it as consumed by the stair and not flag it as unused.

decorative tile layers (deko_vitrifiye,.rule: Decorative tile layers (Deko_Vitrifiye, Piu_Vitrifiye) must be read as finish data: either mapped to a material slot (wet_walls, splashback, floor) or explicitly logged as decorative texture, never silently dropped without a warning.

the agent stage must not drop a drawn ba.rule: The agent stage must not drop a drawn bathroom fixture (tall_cabinet) when the room's program requires it; if placement fails, the piece must be kept in a valid fallback position or the failure must be escalated, not silently removed.

when a host piece is not built, its depe.rule: When a host piece is not built, its dependent decor elements must not be silently dropped; the build stage must either build the host or explicitly log each dependent as lost with a reason.

furniture symbols on the a-tefris layer.rule: Furniture symbols on the A-TEFRIS layer must be read and built as furniture, not treated as unbuildable; the build stage must not skip drawn furniture symbols without a valid reason.

site areas labeled in the plan (parking,.rule: Site areas labeled in the plan (parking, terrace, pool) must be built as site geometry (paving, pool outline, terrace slab) or explicitly logged as not built with a reason; the build stage must not treat them as exterior labels and skip them.

a stove drawn 0.06 m off its wall with i.rule: A stove drawn 0.06 m off its wall with its back parallel is a drawing gap; the reading stage must snap it to the wall.

a toilet with 0.33 m clearance to a side.rule: A toilet with 0.33 m clearance to a side wall (needs 0.38 m) in a 5.0 m2 bathroom is a room-size constraint, not a model problem; the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture layout, and the build stage must not swap models to fix a clearance that is a function of room geometry.

a bathtub with 0.28 m clearance in front.rule: A bathtub with 0.28 m clearance in front (needs 0.53 m) in a 5.0 m2 bathroom is a room-size constraint; the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture layout. The bathtub is drawn fixed equipment and cannot be retyped.

a toilet with 0.33 m clearance to a side.rule: A toilet with 0.33 m clearance to a side wall (needs 0.38 m) in a 5.0 m2 bathroom is a room-size constraint, not a model problem; the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture layout.

a bathtub with 0.28 m clearance in front.rule: A bathtub with 0.28 m clearance in front (needs 0.53 m) in a 5.0 m2 bathroom is a room-size constraint; the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture layout.

a drawn bathtub longer than the free wal.rule: A drawn bathtub longer than the free wall span in front of it is a misread size: the fixture is resized to the real product that fits the bay, leaving the required 0.53 m clearance in front.

a drawn shower tray longer than the free.rule: A drawn shower tray longer than the free wall span in front of it is a misread size: the fixture is resized to the real product that fits the bay, leaving the required 0.53 m clearance in front.

a drawn toilet wider than the free side.rule: A drawn toilet wider than the free side span in its bay is a misread size: the fixture is resized to the real product that fits the bay, leaving the required 0.38 m centre-to-side clearance.

a bedroom render must show the bed as th.rule: A bedroom render must show the bed as the anchor; the interior camera is re-posed to frame the bed.

a kitchen run the room already has is co.rule: A kitchen run the room already has is completed with what it misses; the fridge is a required member of the kitchen run.

a bathroom render must show its primary.rule: A bathroom render must show its primary fixtures; the interior camera is re-posed to frame the washbasin, toilet and bathtub.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's primary fixtures (toilet, basin, tub/shower); a view that omits them is not client-ready.

a bathroom's program set must be complet.rule: A bathroom's program set must be completed to the full set drawn in the documents (tall_cabinet included) even when the room already holds a partial bathroom_set; the set-completion pass must not stop at the members it already has.

a hall's storage program is set by its f.rule: A hall's storage program is set by its function: an entrance hall takes a shoe_cabinet, but a circulation hall on an upper floor (no entrance, no shoe-off) takes no shoe_cabinet and no wardrobe; the fit stage must not place entrance storage in a non-entrance hall.

site areas labelled in the documents (po.rule: Site areas labelled in the documents (pool, sunning terrace, parking) must be built as outlines/geometry on the site; a labelled site area with no outline and no reason is a loss, not a skip.

a living room's seating group must be co.rule: A living room's seating group must be completed with its supporting pieces (media wall behind the tv_unit, a rug under the seating, and lighting) so the room does not read as a bare box; the fit stage must place these with the group, not leave the tv_unit floating on a bare wall.

a stair flight must be built with a cont.rule: A stair flight must be built with a continuous handrail over its full open run (with newels at turns and ends); a flight with no handrail over more than 0.72 m of its run is incomplete and must be built with its guard, not left bare.

a wall-hung item (mirror, art, unit) mus.rule: A wall-hung item (mirror, art, unit) must not be placed over a tall piece of furniture standing in front of its wall; the wall-item pass must raise it over the furniture, move it along the wall to a free stretch, or leave it out.
A wall-hung item (mirror, art, unit) must not be placed over a window or other opening in its wall; the wall-item pass must move it to a free wall stretch or leave it out.

a hung wall item (desk unit, shelf, mirr.rule: A hung wall item (desk unit, shelf, mirror) must never be placed over a window or door opening on its wall: the decor pass must check the opening extents on the wall and, if the item's span overlaps an opening, move it to a free wall span or leave it out.

a living room with more than 4 m of oute.rule: A living room with more than 4 m of outer wall and no window or door on that wall is a blank facade: the reading must flag it and the architect must add a window or door, or the building stage must not leave a blank facade on a habitable room.

every project must have a frontal exteri.rule: Every project must have a frontal exterior view of the entrance facade (+y direction) so the main entrance is visible in the render set.

when the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3.rule: When the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3, a retaining edge (wall, terrace, or stepped foundation) must be built to support the building and prevent erosion.

a glass balustrade on a roof terrace mus.rule: A glass balustrade on a roof terrace must be at least 1.10 m high to provide a safe guard against falling, per building codes.

a retaining wall supporting a raised gar.rule: A retaining wall supporting a raised garden bed must have a material that matches the building's facade (e.g., stone cladding for a stone facade), not bare concrete.

a bathroom set must include a mirror abo.rule: A bathroom set must include a mirror above the washbasin and a towel rail; the bathroom_set group must be defined to include these members.
A bathroom set must include a mirror above the washbasin; the bathroom_set group must be defined to include a mirror as a member.

a bathtub in a bathroom must have visibl.rule: A bathtub in a bathroom must have visible taps and mixer fixtures; the bathroom_set group must include a tap/mixer as a member, or the bathtub model must include fixtures.

the outdoor setting must have textured g.rule: The outdoor setting must have textured ground (grass, paving, etc.) and a designed horizon, not a flat untextured plane with floating sprites.

a side table on a terrace should be a de.rule: A side table on a terrace should be a designed or textured piece that matches the terrace's style, not a plain generic model.

a balcony or terrace program must be fur.rule: A balcony or terrace program must be furnished as a complete outdoor lounge set (seating, table, and greenery) so the space reads as designed, not as a few isolated plants.

every interior camera of a room must be.rule: Every interior camera of a room must be posed to show the room's door so the entry is visible in at least one view.

an exterior camera that must show the en.rule: An exterior camera that must show the entrance facade must be placed in the free stretch of the view line in front of the door at eye height (1.5-1.7 m); if the plot has another building on the line, the camera is placed in the nearest free gap, never inside a building.

a kitchen counter's top must sit at its.rule: A kitchen counter's top must sit at its working height (about 0.90-0.97 m); a model whose top is higher is a wrong model and must be refitted or swapped.

a site or aerial view keeps its role and.rule: A site or aerial view keeps its role and is not re-posed to show an interior window; a window that must be seen is shown by an interior or facade view, not by the aerial site view.

a bathroom camera must frame the full fi.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the full fixture set (bathtub, basin, toilet) with their surroundings so the room reads as designed, not a single isolated object.

a drawn piece's orientation must match t.rule: A drawn piece's orientation must match the drawing within tolerance; a 90-degree turn is a reading error corrected by rotating the piece to its drawn front.

a terrace camera must frame the furnitur.rule: A terrace camera must frame the furniture completely so the pieces read as finished, styled elements, not cut off at the frame edge.

outdoor furniture on a terrace must be a.rule: Outdoor furniture on a terrace must be an outdoor-rated model (weather-resistant, appropriately scaled); an indoor glass-top table is a wrong model for the space.
Outdoor furniture on a terrace must be a curated, outdoor-rated set that matches the project's style; a generic indoor set is a wrong model for the space.

a bathroom's wet fixture must match the.rule: A bathroom's wet fixture must match the project's specified type (e.g. a walk-in shower with glass, rain head, and linear drain); a bathtub in place of the specified shower is a wrong type and must be retyped.

an interior camera that shows a door mus.rule: An interior camera that shows a door must frame the door open or with the room beyond visible and lit, so the view shows a space, not a closed door and a bare wall.

an interior camera that frames an interi.rule: An interior camera that frames an interior door must show the leaf open on its swing side so the room beyond is visible, not a closed slab.

interior doors must be rendered as a cho.rule: Interior doors must be rendered as a chosen product (panelled or styled leaf with a matching handle set), not a plain slab with a generic knob, and the style must be consistent per room family.

a bathroom must be furnished to a detail.rule: A bathroom must be furnished to a detail standard (illuminated mirror, lit open niche with toiletries, towel rail, cove or under-vanity light) rather than a plain tiled wall with a round mirror and stone basin.

bathrooms need a feature wall behind the.rule: Bathrooms need a feature wall behind the vanity/WC (fluted or stone apron), a shaped/framed mirror, towel bars at door and shower, and repeated accent-colour towels, not a plain light-tile wall.

a hall render that looks through an inte.rule: A hall render that looks through an interior door must show the door open and the room beyond lit and furnished, not a closed door.

a drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side in a.rule: A drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side in a living room is a built-in or long low unit (e.g. a media wall or sideboard run) and must be typed as a group of standard pieces, not left untyped.
A drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side in a living room is a built-in or long low unit and must be typed as a group of standard pieces, not left untyped.

a drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side is a.rule: A drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side is a built-in or multi-piece run and must be typed as a group of standard pieces, not left untyped.

a door under a sloped ceiling must have.rule: A door under a sloped ceiling must have at least 1.60 m headroom; where the roof slope leaves less, a dormer or raised roof is required at that wall.

a bathroom drawn with a tub may be upgra.rule: A bathroom drawn with a tub may be upgraded to a walk-in shower with glass, rain head, hand shower on a rail and linear drain per the style, but a drawn fixed tub keeps its type unless the architect re-specifies it.

an interior camera that frames an interi.rule: An interior camera that frames an interior door must show the leaf open so the room beyond is lit and furnished, not a closed door and bare wall.

a bathroom set must include its tall_cab.rule: A bathroom set must include its tall_cabinet; when the mirror room lacks it, the set is incomplete and the missing member must be placed.
A bathroom set must include its tall_cabinet; when the room lacks it, the set is incomplete and the missing member must be placed.

a sofa with no front set must be oriente.rule: A sofa with no front set must be oriented so its front faces the open floor towards its partner, not left unoriented.

a balcony or terrace of 15 m2 or more mu.rule: A balcony or terrace of 15 m2 or more must be furnished with a terrace_lounge group (at least two seats and a table) in addition to any single chair; a single armchair is not an acceptable program for a terrace of that size.

when a door's head is above the roof und.rule: When a door's head is above the roof underside at its wall, the build stage must clip the door to the roof underside (reduce its height) so it does not show through the roof; the door's drawn width and position are kept.

the sheets stage must resolve every ques.rule: The sheets stage must resolve every question it writes to sheets/requests.json before it may end; a run that leaves questions pending must be re-run until the ledger is empty, not accepted as 'pending'.

when a long piece (sofa, bench, console).rule: When a long piece (sofa, bench, console) is drawn with its long side against a wall, the front is the side facing the open floor (the long side), never the short end; an AI front on the short side is a reading error and must be corrected to the long side before the piece is built.

a bench or console drawn with its back o.rule: A bench or console drawn with its back on a wall has its front facing away from that wall (the long side into the room); the front is never the short end, and a piece already facing the correct long side must not be rotated.

a built decor item that fails a scene ch.rule: A built decor item that fails a scene check (S5) must be re-fitted or re-placed before the level is accepted; the scene stage must not pass a level that still holds a failing decor item.

the big loop must keep cycling while the.rule: The big loop must keep cycling while the house score can still rise; a single no-gain cycle is not a stop condition when the score is far from the target.

a stair core room whose stair fills the.rule: A stair core room whose stair fills the room has no interior camera point; its view must be taken from the adjoining hall (the room that shows the stair), not from inside the stair core.

a fitting that chooses a parametric mesh.rule: A fitting that chooses a parametric mesh for a piece that has a real library model of the same type and size is a wrong-model choice; the real model must be used, and a parametric mesh is only a fallback when no real model fits.

a sofa drawn without a front must have i.rule: A sofa drawn without a front must have its front set to the side facing the most open floor towards its seating partner, not left unoriented.

a toilet under a sloped ceiling must be.rule: A toilet under a sloped ceiling must be fitted to the headroom at its own position (the ceiling height above the piece), not to the room's nominal floor-to-floor height; when no library model fits that headroom, the parametric family is the correct build and the 'built below the library level' flag is a false alarm.

a room whose label names a multi-use fun.rule: A room whose label names a multi-use function (play, activity, relaxation) is typed 'living' and its furniture is judged against the living-room program; a bench is a valid piece of a living room, so the 'bench is not a piece of a living room' refusal is a false alarm and the room type 'other' is the misread.

a dining chair's clearance to the wall o.rule: A dining chair's clearance to the wall or piece behind it is measured from the chair's backrest, not its seat edge; when the drawn chair is 0.78 m from the table edge to the wall and the chair depth is 0.55 m, the backrest-to-wall clearance is 0.23 m, which is below the 0.45 m minimum, so the finding is real and the chair must be moved or the table shifted.

a tv_unit's back must be on a wall; when.rule: A tv_unit's back must be on a wall; when the drawn position is 1.01 m off the nearest wall and no free wall span exists (doors, windows block every span), the tv_unit is a misread of a wall-mounted tv or a console that belongs on a different wall, and the general rule is that a tv_unit drawn in the middle of a room with no wall behind it is a misread and must be retyped or moved to the nearest wall span.

a 5.6 m blank outer wall in a 40.5 m2 li.rule: A 5.6 m blank outer wall in a 40.5 m2 living room is a facade defect, not a furniture problem; the general rule is that a blank outer wall longer than 3 m in a habitable room must have a window or door added by the architect, and the furniture agent cannot fix it.

a nightstand in front of a window is acc.rule: A nightstand in front of a window is acceptable when the window sill is at or above the nightstand's top (0.60 m); when the sill is at 0.20 m, the nightstand blocks the window and must be moved to the other side of the bed or the window sill raised; the general rule is that a nightstand in front of a window with a sill below 0.60 m is a conflict that must be resolved by moving the nightstand or raising the sill.

a coffee table overlapping an armchair b.rule: A coffee table overlapping an armchair by 0.12 m2 is a layout conflict; the general rule is that a coffee table must be at least 0.40 m from the front of every seat in the seating group, and when the drawn layout cannot satisfy this, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit, not the coffee table moved alone.

a sofa with no front (front_inferred) in.rule: A sofa with no front (front_inferred) in a room with a clear open floor must have its front set to face the most open floor; the general rule is that a sofa drawn without a front in a room with a clear open floor must have its front set to face that floor, and the agent must use set_front, not move_piece or resize_piece.

a sofa's back must be on a wall; when th.rule: A sofa's back must be on a wall; when the drawn position is 0.59 m off the nearest wall and no free wall span exists within 1.2 m of the drawn position, the sofa is a misread of a freestanding sofa or a sofa that belongs on a different wall, and the general rule is that a sofa drawn in the middle of a room with no wall behind it is a misread and must be moved to the nearest wall span or retyped.

a sofa drawn in a living room is a drawn.rule: A sofa drawn in a living room is a drawn anchor: the seating group is re-solved around it, and the agent may not move it to chase a walkway finding on a neighbour; a walkway that is blocked by the drawn sofa is a layout conflict to report, not a reason to relocate the anchor.

a drawn coffee table is locked to its dr.rule: A drawn coffee table is locked to its drawn position (0.3 m, 1.2 m to a wall); when the drawn position does not sit in front of the sofa, the finding is a drawing/layout conflict to report, not a move the agent may make.

a washbasin that is part of a bath_set m.rule: A washbasin that is part of a bath_set module is pinned to the module's counter: the agent may not swap its model to a freestanding one; a style finding on a module member is a style conflict to report, not a swap.

a toilet whose lowest point is 0.20 m ab.rule: A toilet whose lowest point is 0.20 m above its floor is a parametric height error: the fix is to set its floor/height, not to swap its model; a swap that changes the height is refused by the fit rules.

a drawn bed is a drawn anchor: the agent.rule: A drawn bed is a drawn anchor: the agent may not move it to open a 0.60 m side walkway; a side gap that is too small is a layout conflict to report, not a move of the anchor.

a drawn coffee table that overlaps a dra.rule: A drawn coffee table that overlaps a drawn armchair by 0.12 m2 is a drawing conflict: the drawn_lock (0.3 m) forbids the move that would clear it, so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a move.

a drawn armchair that stands behind the.rule: A drawn armchair that stands behind the back of the drawn sofa is a drawing conflict: rotating it to face the group is refused when it faces a wall or leaves the room, so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a rotation.

a drawn nightstand that stands in front.rule: A drawn nightstand that stands in front of a window is a drawing conflict: the move that clears the window is refused (overlap with the bed, inside_room), so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a move.

a drawn wardrobe whose front clearance i.rule: A drawn wardrobe whose front clearance is 0.17 m (needs 0.80 m) is a drawing conflict: the move that opens the clearance is refused (no free wall span, still short), so the conflict is reported, not fixed by a move.

a washbasin that is part of a bath_set m.rule: A washbasin that is part of a bath_set module and whose lowest point is 0.384 m above its floor is a module height error: the agent may not swap its model; the height must be corrected, which no tool in this run does.

a drawn piece that reaches up to 0.020 m.rule: A drawn piece that reaches up to 0.020 m (0.05 m2) through the room outline is within the drawing tolerance: the architect's rule F5 already says these are fine, so the critic's F9 finding on them is a false alarm and the rule needs no change.

a front use zone that is not reached by.rule: A front use zone that is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from a door is a layout conflict the architect must decide on: the rule C1 must state whether such a zone is acceptable (e.g. when the piece is drawn and the walkway is blocked by another drawn piece) or must be fixed.

a toilet whose centre is 0.33 m from the.rule: A toilet whose centre is 0.33 m from the side wall (needs 0.38 m) is a layout conflict the architect must decide on: the rule S4 must state whether such a clearance is acceptable (e.g. when the toilet is drawn) or must be fixed.

a sofa whose free zone in front is block.rule: A sofa whose free zone in front is blocked by another piece is a layout conflict the architect must decide on: the rule F4 must state whether such a blockage is acceptable (e.g. when both pieces are drawn) or must be fixed.

rule e1 (facade openings) must require t.rule: Rule E1 (facade openings) must require that every outer wall span of a habitable room longer than 3.0 m carries at least one window or door; a blank facade span is a defect to be resolved by adding an opening, not by re-laying out the furniture.

an interior camera of a wet room must fr.rule: An interior camera of a wet room must frame the room's main fixture group (basin, bath/shower, toilet) from a free point with headroom, never a tight crop of a single corner.

a drawn fixed piece whose current librar.rule: A drawn fixed piece whose current library model clashes with the room's palette (cold metal hardware on a warm scheme) must be swapped for a model in the same size class whose finish matches the room's style.

a corridor camera must frame the hall's.rule: A corridor camera must frame the hall's main group (storage and the doors it serves) so the passage reads as a designed hall, not an empty wall.

a shoe cabinet model that reads as a bar.rule: A shoe cabinet model that reads as a bare parametric grid of open cubbies must be swapped for a finished, closed-front model in the same size class.

a kitchen render must carry styled workt.rule: A kitchen render must carry styled worktop props (fruit, board, small appliance) so the counter reads as lived-in, not bare.

a kitchen counter's worktop must carry s.rule: A kitchen counter's worktop must carry styling props (kettle, fruit, board) to read as a complete, lived-in kitchen.

a lounge chair whose wood tone and desig.rule: A lounge chair whose wood tone and design language clash with the room's main seating set must be swapped for a model in the same size class that matches the set's palette.

a sectional that renders as a bare shell.rule: A sectional that renders as a bare shell with no cushions or throws must be swapped for a model that includes styled cushions and shams in the same size class.

coffee and side tables in a living room.rule: Coffee and side tables in a living room must carry styled objects (books, vase, small items) to create a warm, curated feel.

full-height windows in a living room mus.rule: Full-height windows in a living room must carry layered curtains (sheer and drape on a ceiling track) so the room does not read as exposed and unfinished.

a dining chair whose material or tone cl.rule: A dining chair whose material or tone clashes with the rest of the dining set must be swapped for a model in the same size class that matches the set's palette.

an interior camera of a wet room must fr.rule: An interior camera of a wet room must frame the room's main fixture group from a free point with headroom, never a tight crop of a single corner.
An interior camera of a wet room must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet) from a free point, not a corner pressed to the vanity and door.

a corridor runner must be a neutral, pro.rule: A corridor runner must be a neutral, properly proportioned rug that layers the floor, not a clashing accent that reads as a mistake.

a bedroom's nightstand and bed-side area.rule: A bedroom's nightstand and bed-side area must carry styled objects (console, mirror, vase, books) so the space reads as finished, not bare.

a desk in a bedroom work corner must be.rule: A desk in a bedroom work corner must be furnished as a work set (laptop or monitor, lamp, books) so it reads as a used desk, not a bare slab.

a bedroom's desk chair must match the ro.rule: A bedroom's desk chair must match the room's calm styled set; a black mesh office chair is not allowed in a bedroom.

a bedroom's headboard wall must carry a.rule: A bedroom's headboard wall must carry a feature finish (fluted/slatted panelling or wainscot) matching the project style; flat paint alone is not acceptable for the wall behind the bed.

an interior camera must establish the ro.rule: An interior camera must establish the room and its main furniture; it must not be pressed against a foreground object that obscures the space.

two sofas in one living room must not be.rule: Two sofas in one living room must not be identical clashing models; they should read as a designed set, not a showroom of one product.

dining table and chairs must match the s.rule: Dining table and chairs must match the seating style of the room; a lighter style table against heavy bench seating is a mismatched set.

a large living-room window must carry a.rule: A large living-room window must carry a layered curtain treatment (sheer plus drape); bare glass is not acceptable.

a living room's seating wall must carry.rule: A living room's seating wall must carry a feature finish (fluted/slatted panelling or wainscot) matching the project style; flat paint alone is not acceptable.

coffee tables and sideboards in a living.rule: Coffee tables and sideboards in a living room must be styled with curated objects (mirror, vase, art, books), not left bare.

a seating group's armchairs and side tab.rule: A seating group's armchairs and side table must be one coherent style; mixing a solid wood frame, all-rattan, and a third style is a mismatched set.

terrace potted plants must be visible an.rule: Terrace potted plants must be visible and the terrace's bare walls and corners must be dressed so the space reads as finished.

large ground-floor glazing must show war.rule: Large ground-floor glazing must show warm interior light so the facade reads as inhabited, not a dead dark void.

a bathroom camera must show the room as.rule: A bathroom camera must show the room as a whole (washbasin, cabinet, toilet, tub); a close-up of a corner is not acceptable.

a hall camera must show the space with i.rule: A hall camera must show the space with its furniture and decor; a close-up of a corner and door frame is not acceptable.

the view outside a window must show a de.rule: The view outside a window must show a designed landscape (planters, seating, landscaping), not a flat low-poly green field.

a kitchen must be a complete functional.rule: A kitchen must be a complete functional set: fridge, oven, range hood, counter, sink, stove; a missing fridge or hood makes it fundamentally incomplete.

a seating group in one room must be one.rule: A seating group in one room must be one coherent style and colour family; a single piece of a different material or colour family is a wrong model, not a placement problem.

a full-height window wall in a living ro.rule: A full-height window wall in a living room must carry a curtain or drape layer (sheer plus drape) as part of the room's finish; a bare glass wall is an incomplete set, not a wardrobe problem.

a dining table in a furnished living/din.rule: A dining table in a furnished living/dining room must be styled with a table setting (plates, glasses, centrepiece) as part of the dining group; a bare tabletop is an incomplete set.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (bathtub or shower, toilet, washbasin) from a free point with headroom, not a corner or a single small object.

an interior hall/entrance camera must fr.rule: An interior hall/entrance camera must frame the hall as a space (its entry furniture and the door it leads to) from a free point, not a low-angle corner of a single door.

an office chair in a residential bedroom.rule: An office chair in a residential bedroom/desk corner must be a soft, upholstered or wood chair in the room's style, not a corporate black leather task chair.

a desk in a modern minimalist bedroom mu.rule: A desk in a modern minimalist bedroom must be a clean, flat-front modern or scandinavian piece, not a traditional raised-panel Shaker desk.

a wardrobe in a scandinavian/modern bedr.rule: A wardrobe in a scandinavian/modern bedroom must have a refined, finished surface that matches the headboard and walls, not a raw, unfinished light wood.

an interior hall camera must frame the h.rule: An interior hall camera must frame the hall as a styled space (its storage, the stair it serves) from a free point with headroom, not a bare, unstyled corridor.

a large empty wall behind a sofa in a li.rule: A large empty wall behind a sofa in a living room must carry wall art, a feature panel or textured wallpaper as part of the room's finish; a bare wall is an incomplete set.

the site ground around a building must c.rule: The site ground around a building must carry a real ground material (grass, paving, gravel) with texture, not a flat untextured plane.

an outdoor terrace floor must carry a re.rule: An outdoor terrace floor must carry a real outdoor floor material (paving stone, decking, terracotta) with texture, not a bare untextured grey slab.

the garden/outdoor environment must carr.rule: The garden/outdoor environment must carry a real ground material (grass, planting) with texture, not a flat untextured green plane.

an outdoor floor (terrace, balcony, vera.rule: An outdoor floor (terrace, balcony, veranda) is never left as bare untextured concrete; it is given a finished paving or decking look.

the facade is never left as a flat grey.rule: The facade is never left as a flat grey box; it is given a finished cladding or render look with a defined entrance.

a balcony or terrace is furnished with a.rule: A balcony or terrace is furnished with a place to sit (a lounge or seating group), not left as a bare slab.

an exterior view is framed at eye level.rule: An exterior view is framed at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or as a high view above the ridge, never a close-up that cuts off the building.

a bedroom floor is laid in a designed pa.rule: A bedroom floor is laid in a designed pattern (herringbone or chevron), not a flat untextured slab.

a stone-clad wall is given a finished, v.rule: A stone-clad wall is given a finished, varied stone look, not a flat repetitive placeholder texture.

an entrance door is registered in the si.rule: An entrance door is registered in the site entrances list so it can be styled with steps, a path, and lighting.

an interior view shows the room's main g.rule: An interior view shows the room's main group, not a tight crop of a corner.
An interior view shows the room's main group, not a partial view that misses the anchor piece.

a bedroom is furnished with a cohesive,.rule: A bedroom is furnished with a cohesive, styled set (matching bed, nightstands, wardrobe, rug, art, curtains), not a mismatched classic-modern clash.
A bedroom is furnished with a cohesive, styled set (matching bed, nightstands, wardrobe, rug, art, curtains), not a bare grey-box corner.

a decorative accessory (plant, throw, cu.rule: A decorative accessory (plant, throw, cushion) that cannot rest on the built host's top surface is dropped silently; it is not a conservation loss and needs no build.

when a bathroom set is reported complete.rule: When a bathroom set is reported complete but a member (e.g. tall_cabinet) is absent from the built room, the set-completeness check must compare against the built pieces, not the planned set, and the solver must place the missing member.

the dwg reading stage must read entities.rule: The DWG reading stage must read entities on all layers, including those that are off, frozen, or invisible, because the architect may have toggled layer visibility without removing the geometry.
the dwg reading stage must read entities.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

ole2frame and wipeout entities are ole/c.rule: OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entities are OLE/clip objects, not architectural geometry; the reading stage may skip them without a conservation loss.

the camera stage must not drop a planned.rule: The camera stage must not drop a planned exterior view without recording a reason; if a view is redundant or blocked, it must be logged with the cause.

an exterior camera that must show a spec.rule: An exterior camera that must show a specific window must be positioned so the window is in frame; if the current pose misses it, the camera is moved.

every drawn block on a plan that is not.rule: Every drawn block on a plan that is not a dimension, text, or symbol must be mapped to a model piece or explicitly recorded as not built with a reason.

blocks smaller than 0.3 m on a side are.rule: Blocks smaller than 0.3 m on a side are typically symbols, fixtures, or details, not furniture; they may be skipped without a conservation loss.

a drawn insert whose block name is a pla.rule: A drawn INSERT whose block name is a placeholder or anonymous string (e.g. 'eeere', 'bulmak', 'A$C...') and has no label, no matching library model and no room context is a drawing artifact, not a furniture element: the reading stage records it as untyped and the ledger must not flag it as a lost element.

autocad anonymous blocks (names starting.rule: AutoCAD anonymous blocks (names starting with 'A$C') that are smaller than 0.10 m in any dimension are drawing artifacts (hatch boundaries, dimension fragments, annotation pieces), not furniture: the reading stage must not flag them as lost elements.

a drawn insert whose block name is a pla.rule: A drawn INSERT whose block name is a placeholder or anonymous string (e.g. 'eeere', 'bulmak', 'A$C...', 'DFGNHNBG') and has no label, no matching library model and no room context is a drawing artifact, not a furniture element: the reading stage records it as untyped and the ledger must not flag it as a lost element.

A drawn INSERT whose block name is a placeholder or anonymous string (e.g. 'eeere', 'bulmak', 'A$C...', 'TA161') and has no label, no matching library model and no room context is a drawing artifact, not a furniture element: the reading stage records it as untyped and the ledger must not flag it as a lost element.

a drawn insert that is a site decor elem.rule: A drawn INSERT that is a site decor element (e.g. 'TEFRIŞ', 'decoration', 'trim') and is already recorded as site decor (sd_*) is intentionally not built as furniture: the ledger must not flag it as a lost element.

a drawn insert that is a stair block (e..rule: A drawn INSERT that is a stair block (e.g. 'merdiven') and the model already has a stair in the same room or level is a duplicate/annotation block, not a missing element: the ledger must not flag it as a lost element.

autocad anonymous blocks (names starting.rule: AutoCAD anonymous blocks (names starting with 'A$C') that are smaller than 0.30 m in any dimension are drawing artifacts (hatch boundaries, dimension fragments, annotation pieces), not furniture: the reading stage must not flag them as lost elements.

a6 must not flag annotation-scale blocks.rule: A6 must not flag annotation-scale blocks (under ~0.10 m on a side) as lost furniture; they are dimension or text marks, not buildable elements.

a6 must not flag large landscape/site sy.rule: A6 must not flag large landscape/site symbol blocks (over ~1.5 m, on a site or outdoor layer) as lost furniture; they are site graphics, not buildable interior elements.

a6 must not flag a small table symbol th.rule: A6 must not flag a small table symbol that duplicates an already-built table in the same room as a lost element; one built table satisfies the drawn set.

a6 must not flag a table symbol that dup.rule: A6 must not flag a table symbol that duplicates an already-built table in the same room as a lost element.

a7 must not flag entities on off/frozen/.rule: A7 must not flag entities on off/frozen/invisible layers as lost; the reading correctly excludes non-active layers.

a7 must not flag ole2frame and wipeout e.rule: A7 must not flag OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT entity types as lost; they are embedded objects and masks, not buildable elements.

a7 must not flag the wall-layer selectio.rule: A7 must not flag the wall-layer selection rationale or structural columns standing out of wall bands as lost furniture; columns are structure, not buildable pieces.
A7 must not flag the wall-layer selection rationale or structural columns as lost furniture.

a7 must not flag a symbol that both read.rule: A7 must not flag a symbol that both reading passes classify as not_furniture (kept as an obstacle) as a lost element.
A7 must not flag a symbol that both reading passes classify as not_furniture as a lost element.

a7 must not flag a piece on a structural.rule: A7 must not flag a piece on a structural layer (A-BA) classified as a column as lost furniture; it is structure, not a buildable piece.
A7 must not flag a piece on a structural layer (A-BA) classified as a column as lost furniture.

a drawn entity that is 60% or more insid.rule: A drawn entity that is 60% or more inside a larger built fixture of the same room is a part of that fixture (faucet, bowl, tap) and is not a separate piece; it is suppressed, not a loss.
A drawn entity that is 60% or more inside a larger built fixture of the same room is a part of that fixture and is suppressed, not a loss.

two floor lamps never stand inside each.rule: Two floor lamps never stand inside each other; a smaller lamp footprint drawn inside a larger one of the same room is the same lamp drawn twice (base and shade) and the duplicate is suppressed, not a loss.
Two floor lamps never stand inside each other; a smaller lamp footprint drawn inside a larger one of the same room is the same lamp drawn twice and the duplicate is suppressed, not a loss.

a layer named for 2d annotation (axis bu.rule: A layer named for 2D annotation (axis bubbles, dimensions, circles) that contains only CIRCLE/LINE entities is drawing annotation, not buildable content; it is correctly left unused and needs no warning.

a layer whose name denotes a decorative.rule: A layer whose name denotes a decorative floor/finish pattern (Deko, Seramik, tile) holding ARC/ELLIPSE/SPLINE/LINE is a material pattern, not buildable geometry; it is correctly left unused and needs no warning.

a layer named for a finish or decorative.rule: A layer named for a finish or decorative treatment (VITR, vitrified) holding ARC/LINE is a finish pattern, not buildable geometry; it is correctly left unused and needs no warning.

a piece present in the decor stage and n.rule: A piece present in the decor stage and named in a copied_from record must survive the agent stage; the agent must not drop a placed piece without a documented reason.
A piece present in the decor stage and named in a slot record must survive the agent stage; the agent must not drop a placed piece without a documented reason.

a room whose furniture set (sofa, tv_uni.rule: A room whose furniture set (sofa, tv_unit, table_dining, armchair) and area indicate a living/activity space must be typed 'living', not 'other'; a piece allowed in the room's true type must not be flagged as not-allowed because of a mis-typed room.

when one room outline carries two room l.rule: When one room outline carries two room labels (e.g. Salon and AÇIK MUTFAK) because the separating wall was not read, the reading must split the outline into the two labelled rooms (or flag the missing wall) rather than keep only the largest-area label and merge the rooms.

a window seen from an exterior view must.rule: A window seen from an exterior view must render with a recognisable frame and glazing (not a bare opening or a solid panel) so that the render check does not classify it as other_object; the fit stage must verify the window's exterior appearance, not only its geometry.

a drawn piece is placed at its drawn cen.rule: A drawn piece is placed at its drawn centre; a shift beyond the 0.05 m tolerance is a layout error, not a model error.

a drawn piece is locked to its drawn cen.rule: A drawn piece is locked to its drawn centre within the 0.05 m tolerance; a model larger than the drawn footprint must be centred on the drawn centre, and neighbour overlap is resolved by moving the neighbours, not the drawn anchor.

a drawn piece is placed at its drawn cen.rule: A drawn piece is placed at its drawn centre and orientation; a shift or rotation beyond the 0.05 m tolerance is a layout error, not a model error.

an interior camera must frame every piec.rule: An interior camera must frame every piece it lists in show fully inside the frame; a piece cut off at the frame edge is a failed pose, not a stylistic choice.

a zone label naming a kitchen (e.g. 'açi.rule: A zone label naming a kitchen (e.g. 'AÇIK MUTFAK') inside a living room outline marks an open-kitchen zone: the reading stage must classify the enclosed counter/island pieces as a kitchen zone of the room, not drop the label as unknown.

a sofa with no front set must be oriente.rule: A sofa with no front set must be oriented by the code to face the most open floor towards its partner; a missing front is a fit error, not a taste choice.

a media-wall/tv-place check must not fir.rule: A media-wall/TV-place check must not fire for a room whose plan shows no TV; the check should be skipped when the room's drawn program has no TV piece.

a parametric door built in the house's d.rule: A parametric door built in the house's door family is an acceptable substitute when no library model fits the opening; this is not a defect.

when a piece is built below the library.rule: When a piece is built below the library level (parametric mesh), the fitting stage must pick a library model of the same type and size class; a parametric fallback is a library gap to be closed by a swap.

a living or living-dining room's main se.rule: A living or living-dining room's main seating group (sofa + coffee table) must sit on a rug sized to the group; the decor stage's salon details must place it.

a kitchen counter's top and splashback m.rule: A kitchen counter's top and splashback must use a richer, textured stone (marble/travertine) look, not a flat generic grey, to match the project's modern finish.

interior door leaves must share the proj.rule: Interior door leaves must share the project's cohesive palette (painted/neutral) rather than a warm wood that clashes with cool grey tiles and terrazzo.

a terrace/balcony camera must frame the.rule: A terrace/balcony camera must frame the whole space (seating, planters, paving) from a higher, wider pose, not a low close-up where one armchair fills the frame.

a terrace/balcony floor must use a warm.rule: A terrace/balcony floor must use a warm decking or textured paving look (with planters) to break up a long run, not plain grey slabs.

the background/landscape behind a terrac.rule: The background/landscape behind a terrace or exterior view must use a textured grass/ground look, not a flat untextured green plane.

upper balconies/terrace edges must carry.rule: Upper balconies/terrace edges must carry planters or greenery to soften the hard stone and glass; the decor stage must place them.

windows in the reference style must use.rule: Windows in the reference style must use full-height curtains in two layers (a sheer behind a heavier drape); the decor stage must add both.

door and window frames must share one co.rule: Door and window frames must share one consistent frame finish across the project, not mix black and bronze/gold.

an exterior door leaf must be a finished.rule: An exterior door leaf must be a finished, well-detailed product (rich wood or textured finish) that reads clearly against the stone wall, not a flat dark leaf.

side tables must carry styled, textured.rule: Side tables must carry styled, textured decor (vases/candles with real materials), never untextured placeholder cylinders.

terrace potted plants should be larger a.rule: Terrace potted plants should be larger and more varied (taller, fuller models) to add life and style, not small generic ones.

a desk with a work chair must carry a la.rule: A desk with a work chair must carry a laptop/computer on it facing the seat (tabletop work set); the decor stage must place it.

the agent stage must not drop a built de.rule: The agent stage must not drop a built decor piece (a shoe_cabinet in a hall) without a reason; a dropped piece is restored.
The agent stage must not drop a built decor piece (an armchair) without a reason; a dropped piece is restored.

the agent stage must not drop a placed d.rule: The agent stage must not drop a placed decor piece without a recorded reason; a dropped piece named in the decor record is a loss to be re-placed in the next agent round.

a level that belongs to a variant only i.rule: A level that belongs to a variant only is built in that variant's scene, not in the base build; this is correct variant separation, not a loss.

elements drawn on structural layers (a-b.rule: Elements drawn on structural layers (A-BA) are structure, not furniture; they are kept as obstacles, not built. This is a correct reading.

elements drawn on furniture symbol layer.rule: Elements drawn on furniture symbol layers (A-TEFRIS) are furniture symbols, not built pieces; they are not built. This is a correct reading.

elements drawn on decor layers (deko_ahs.rule: Elements drawn on decor layers (Deko_Ahsap01) are decor, not furniture; the decor stage places them, not the build stage. This is a correct reading.

elements drawn inside another piece (60%.rule: Elements drawn inside another piece (60% or more) are the same piece drawn twice, or a part of it; they are not built. This is a correct reading.

details inside a kitchen counter leg (an.rule: Details inside a kitchen counter leg (an appliance front or drawers) are not separate pieces; they are not built. This is a correct reading.

a cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is.rule: A cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of drawn pieces, not a single piece; it is not built. This is a correct reading.

a drawn symbol that both recognition pas.rule: A drawn symbol that both recognition passes call not_furniture is not furniture; it is kept as an obstacle, not built. This is a correct reading.

a rug outline drawn around a table and i.rule: A rug outline drawn around a table and its chairs is a rug mark, not a piece; the decor stage places it. This is a correct reading.

a floor lamp drawn 33% or more inside a.rule: A floor lamp drawn 33% or more inside a larger floor lamp of the same room is one floor lamp drawn twice, not two; the smaller one is not built. This is a correct reading.

when two drawn pieces of the same type o.rule: When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 15% of the smaller footprint, treat them as one piece drawn twice: keep the larger (or the one with a model) and do not build the duplicate.

a small drawn piece (under 0.5 m) that s.rule: A small drawn piece (under 0.5 m) that sits more than 70% inside a larger seat (armchair, sofa, bed) is its cushion or pad, not a separate piece: do not build it.

a piece removed by an explicit remove_pi.rule: A piece removed by an explicit remove_piece decision is not a loss: the build honours the removal and the conservation check should not flag it.

a large drawn outline (over 2 m on a sid.rule: A large drawn outline (over 2 m on a side) that encloses other pieces is a rug or zone outline, not a piece: the decor pass lays the rug, the build does not build it as furniture.

the upper end of a stair that arrives at.rule: The upper end of a stair that arrives at the top level is not built again: the stair is built once at its lower end and the upper end is the arrival, not a second stair.

a decor item whose host piece is removed.rule: A decor item whose host piece is removed is not a loss: it follows its host and is not built when the host is not built.

a drawn cushion or pillow that the libra.rule: A drawn cushion or pillow that the library model of its host piece already includes is not a loss: the model's own cushions are part of the piece, not separate decor.

a room labelled 'salon' with an 'açik mu.rule: A room labelled 'Salon' with an 'AÇIK MUTFAK' label is an open-plan living/kitchen; kitchen fixtures in the living room are correct and not a finding.

a sofa without a drawn front should have.rule: A sofa without a drawn front should have its front set to the side facing the most open floor or its partner piece.

an armchair without a drawn front should.rule: An armchair without a drawn front should have its front set to the side away from its wall or towards its partner.

in an open-plan living room, the media w.rule: In an open-plan living room, the media wall check should consider all walls including partition walls and kitchen walls as valid TV placement surfaces, not only exterior walls.

when all tv placement candidates on the.rule: When all TV placement candidates on the wall a sofa faces are blocked by furniture, the check should consider alternative walls in the room for TV placement, or flag the blocking furniture for relocation.

when the plan labels a room as a terrace.rule: When the plan labels a room as a terrace (Teras) with a door, and the roof section shows the roof closed over it, the roof must be cut or modified to create an open terrace. The roof type should be adjusted to include a flat terrace section or a dormer opening.

when a door under a sloped roof has head.rule: When a door under a sloped roof has headroom below 1.60 m, a dormer or roof modification is required to provide usable headroom. The check should flag this and require a dormer or raised roof section.

When a door under a sloped roof has headroom below 1.60 m and no nearby spot provides more, a dormer or roof modification is required. The check should flag this and require a dormer or raised roof section.

a door whose headroom under a sloped cei.rule: A door whose headroom under a sloped ceiling is under 1.60 m everywhere within 0.5 m along its wall must be flagged as a design conflict requiring a dormer or raised roof, not silently lowered to 1.00 m.

a labelled site pool or terrace area in.rule: A labelled site pool or terrace area in the documents must be built as a site element with its outline; 'NOT built (no outline)' for a drawn, labelled pool is a loss.

a room that appears twice with the same.rule: A room that appears twice with the same area, type and piece list is a duplicate build, not two rooms; the reading stage must deduplicate rooms before building.

a stair piece must connect two existing.rule: A stair piece must connect two existing levels; a stair on the lowest level with no level below it is a misread and must be removed or re-pointed to the level it actually serves.

a dining table belongs in a dining room.rule: A dining table belongs in a dining room or an open kitchen, not a living room; a wardrobe belongs in a bedroom or hall, not a living room. Pieces must match the room type they are placed in.

twin en-suite bathrooms of the same area.rule: Twin en-suite bathrooms of the same area and type should have the same fixture set; a missing tall_cabinet in one twin is an inconsistency.

bathrooms of the same area and type acro.rule: Bathrooms of the same area and type across levels should have a consistent fixture set; a missing tall_cabinet in one is an inconsistency.

a dining table in a living room with no.rule: A dining table in a living room with no dining room is out of place; it should be in a dining room or an open kitchen.

a wardrobe in a living room with no bedr.rule: A wardrobe in a living room with no bedroom is out of place; it should be in a bedroom or hall.

a bathroom's set must be complete: every.rule: A bathroom's set must be complete: every fixture its twin or its program calls for (tall_cabinet, washbasin, toilet, shower/bathtub) must be present, not just the ones that fit the first pass.

a living room's set must be complete: ev.rule: A living room's set must be complete: every fixture its twin or its program calls for (floor_lamp, sofa, table_coffee, tv_unit) must be present, not just the ones that fit the first pass.

a room whose area, furniture set (sofa,.rule: A room whose area, furniture set (sofa, dining table, TV unit) and label match a living room must be typed 'living', not 'other', even if it is a duplicate or secondary instance.

a bathroom set must include a tall_cabin.rule: A bathroom set must include a tall_cabinet (storage) in addition to the bathtub, toilet and washbasin, matching the set on all other floors of the project.

a shoe_cabinet is only appropriate in a.rule: A shoe_cabinet is only appropriate in a ground-floor entrance hall; upper-floor halls should have a console_table or sideboard instead.

a balcony or terrace larger than 10 m2 m.rule: A balcony or terrace larger than 10 m2 must have a terrace_lounge set (seating, table) to be functional, not just a single armchair and plant.

minor furniture differences between dupl.rule: Minor furniture differences between duplicate rooms are acceptable and do not require a fix.

a wardrobe in a large hall (over 10 m2).rule: A wardrobe in a large hall (over 10 m2) is acceptable as built-in storage.

different bathrooms can have different f.rule: Different bathrooms can have different fixtures (bathtub vs shower) without issue.

a potted_plant on a balcony is appropria.rule: A potted_plant on a balcony is appropriate and does not require a fix.

every bathroom set must be dressed to it.rule: Every bathroom set must be dressed to its family's P13 reference: one feature wall (dark fluted WC wall or stone apron behind and under the vanity), a mirror shaped and framed by the family, towel bars at the door and at the shower, and one accent-colour towel repeated in two or three places.

every interior door must be rendered ope.rule: Every interior door must be rendered open by default, its leaf turned open against its swing side (ajar only where a piece or wall stops it), with only the entrance and terrace doors closed.

bathroom p12 reference: a floating flute.rule: Bathroom P12 reference: a floating fluted vanity with lit open cubbies and a floor glow, a feature panel on the vanity wall with a matching top, a large backlit mirror, a walk-in shower with glass, a rain head, a hand shower on a rail and a linear drain, a towel shelf beside the towel rail, and the counter styled in two clusters.

bathroom p13 reference: one feature wall.rule: Bathroom P13 reference: one feature wall (a dark fluted WC wall or a stone apron behind and under the vanity), a mirror shaped and framed by the family, towel bars at the door and at the shower, and towels in one accent colour repeated in two or three places.

in every interior view that sees a door.rule: In every interior view that sees a door to a room worth showing (a dressing room, an en-suite, a hall or living space), that door stands open with the room beyond lit and furnished, while private doors (a WC) stay closed or ajar, so no view shows only closed doors.

every interior door stands open by defau.rule: Every interior door stands open by default (its leaf turned open against its swing side, ajar only where a piece or a wall stops it), with only the entrance and terrace doors closed.

a ceiling light is only placed when its.rule: A ceiling light is only placed when its top is within 0.02 m of the ceiling or a cord/rod and canopy connect it to the ceiling; a light left floating is a placement failure, not a detail.

a soft item placed on a bed must rest on.rule: A soft item placed on a bed must rest on the mattress surface; penetration deeper than 0.03 m is a placement error, not a soft-body tolerance.

every room label the documents name on a.rule: Every room label the documents name on a level must be matched to a model room of that level; a label with no matching room is a lost room, not a duplicate.

a labelled room outline in the plan is a.rule: A labelled room outline in the plan is always built as a room; when a label falls inside an already-read outline, the outline is split at the label's wall, never the label is dropped.

every floor opening wider than 0.5 m on.rule: Every floor opening wider than 0.5 m on a level above ground is built with a guard (railing or glass pane) at its open edges in the same stage that cuts the opening.

every stairwell opening is built with a.rule: Every stairwell opening is built with a guardrail or safety barrier at its open edges in the same stage that builds the stair.

every stair opening in a hall is built w.rule: Every stair opening in a hall is built with a guard or railing at its open edges in the same stage that builds the stair.

no decor piece may extend above the roof.rule: No decor piece may extend above the roof underside; the build stage checks every decor piece's top against the roof and refuses or resizes it.

a soft-seat model whose back or arm is n.rule: A soft-seat model whose back or arm is not flush with its seat (gap over 5 mm) is a build defect: the rest_plan must seat every back, back cushion and arm against the seat and down onto its support before the piece is accepted.

scene geometry checks (s1) must pass for.rule: Scene geometry checks (S1) must pass for every level before the build is accepted; a level with failed S1 checks is not a finished build.

scene geometry checks (s2) must pass for.rule: Scene geometry checks (S2) must pass for every level before the build is accepted; a level with failed S2 checks is not a finished build.

when a single-piece rotation cannot make.rule: When a single-piece rotation cannot make a seat face its group without breaking another check (facing a wall, losing group alignment), the whole seating group must be re-solved as a unit rather than rotating one piece in isolation.

a tv unit must be placed on a wall withi.rule: A TV unit must be placed on a wall within 0.30 m of the sofa axis and facing the seating; when it ends up behind a seat's back, the TV/sofa axis must be re-solved as a unit, not by rotating or nudging the unit alone.

a piece must lie fully inside its room o.rule: A piece must lie fully inside its room outline; a wardrobe (or any piece) that crosses the outline, even by a few centimetres, must be pulled back inside rather than left protruding.

a coffee table must not overlap a seat;.rule: A coffee table must not overlap a seat; when single moves cannot clear the overlap without breaking another check, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit.

every seat's front use zone must be reac.rule: Every seat's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; a seat whose front zone is cut off by the layout must be re-placed, not left unreachable.

a seating group's coffee table must be p.rule: A seating group's coffee table must be placed clear of the armchairs' foot zones; when the solver's best candidate still overlaps a chair, the room's AI pieces are re-solved as a group rather than nudged one piece at a time.

every seat's front use zone must be reac.rule: Every seat's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; a seat that cannot be reached without crossing another seat's zone is a group-placement failure to re-solve, not a single move.

a corner sofa's front use zone must be r.rule: A corner sofa's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; when the sofa is drawn against a wall that blocks the path, the room's AI pieces are re-solved around the drawn anchor.

a stove's back must sit on a wall; a 0.0.rule: A stove's back must sit on a wall; a 0.06 m offset is a placement slip of the kitchen run, corrected by re-solving the run against the wall, not by swapping the stove model.

a kitchen counter needs a >= 0.90 m aisl.rule: A kitchen counter needs a >= 0.90 m aisle in front of it; a 0.55 m aisle means the run is placed too far into the room and must be re-solved against the wall.

a stove's back must sit on a wall; a 0.0.rule: A stove's back must sit on a wall; a 0.06 m offset is a placement slip of the kitchen run, corrected by re-solving the run against the wall.

a sofa's footprint must match its produc.rule: A sofa's footprint must match its product orientation (width along the front, depth along the back); a 0.90 x 2.13 m piece read 90 degrees against its sizes is a misread orientation, corrected by re-solving the seating group so the sofa sits with its back on a wall.

a sofa's back must sit on a wall; when t.rule: A sofa's back must sit on a wall; when the drawn position is 0.59 m off and no free wall span exists within the move limit, the seating group is re-solved so the sofa snaps to a wall.

an armchair must face its seating group;.rule: An armchair must face its seating group; when the group's sofa is misoriented, the armchair's orientation is a symptom, corrected by re-solving the group.

an armchair's front free zone must not b.rule: An armchair's front free zone must not be blocked by another seat; a blocked zone in a mis-solved seating group is fixed by re-solving the group.
