a dining chair needs >= 0.81 m from the.rule: A dining chair needs >= 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; a 0.78 m clearance is a placement slip of the dining set, corrected by re-solving the room.

a sofa's footprint must match its produc.rule: A sofa's footprint must match its product orientation; a 0.90 x 2.13 m piece read 90 degrees against its sizes is a misread orientation, corrected by re-solving the seating group.

a sofa's back must sit on a wall; when t.rule: A sofa's back must sit on a wall; when the drawn position is 0.59 m off and the target wall span does not exist, the seating group is re-solved so the sofa snaps to a real wall.

a dining chair pulled up to a table is a.rule: A dining chair pulled up to a table is a seated position: the clearance check behind it must measure from the chair's back edge to the wall or piece behind, and must not require the full standing clearance (0.81 m) that applies to a free-standing chair; a seated chair needs only the depth of the seat plus a small pull-out gap.

a seating group is placed so every seat'.rule: A seating group is placed so every seat's front faces the group's centre (sofa, coffee table, TV) and no seat stands behind another seat's back; a single rotate that only clears the immediate neighbour is not a fix when the seat is on the wrong side of the group.

a nightstand is placed at the head of th.rule: A nightstand is placed at the head of the bed on a free side, clear of any window (its top below the sill blocks the opening); if the only free side is in front of a window, the bed is re-oriented or the nightstand is dropped rather than left blocking the window.

a wardrobe is placed so at least 0.80 m.rule: A wardrobe is placed so at least 0.80 m is free in front of it for the doors to open; if the room is too tight, a shallower wardrobe model is chosen or the wardrobe is moved to a longer wall span.

a dining chair is placed so at least 0.8.rule: A dining chair is placed so at least 0.81 m is free from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it for the sitter to sit and stand; if the wall is too close, the table is moved to a longer span or a smaller table is chosen.

a dining table is placed clear of any wi.rule: A dining table is placed clear of any window (its top below the sill blocks the opening); if the room is tight, the table is moved to a span away from the window or a smaller table is chosen.

a kitchen wall cabinet is built from a l.rule: A kitchen wall cabinet is built from a library model with realistic material and detail, not a crude low-poly block; if the module builder produces a placeholder, a library model is chosen instead.

every piece placed by the decor stage is.rule: Every piece placed by the decor stage is carried through the agent stage; a piece that is dropped without a record (a potted plant, a side table) is a loss, not a design choice.

the agent stage must not drop a drawn pi.rule: The agent stage must not drop a drawn piece of a room's set without naming it; a piece present at the decor stage and absent after the agent stage is a loss, not a detail.

a planned piece whose model is a kitchen.rule: A planned piece whose model is a kitchen-run module must still be built as its own object; the build stage must not skip a planned piece because its model is a shared module.

when a drawn piece is a duplicate of a l.rule: When a drawn piece is a duplicate of a larger same-type piece (drawn inside it), the smaller one is a detail of the larger and is correctly not built; the reading stage should mark it as a detail, not a lost piece.

when a drawn piece is a seat cushion of.rule: When a drawn piece is a seat cushion of a larger piece (drawn inside it), it is a detail of that piece and is correctly not built; the reading stage should mark it as a detail, not a lost piece.

a stair room whose only camera point is.rule: A stair room whose only camera point is inside the stair must have a camera placed in the adjacent hall or at the stair's landing, not inside the stair core.

a drawn block in a kitchen that no rule.rule: A drawn block in a kitchen that no rule or model types must be classified (or explicitly marked not-furniture with evidence) before the run ends; an untyped drawn piece may not be silently dropped with no warning, review entry or symbol.

any drawing layer whose name denotes a s.rule: Any drawing layer whose name denotes a stair (merdiven/stair) must be consumed by the reading: matched to a built stair (recorded) or raised as a missing-stair finding; it may never be silently dropped.

Any drawing layer whose name denotes a stair or stair view (merdiven görünüş) must be consumed by the reading: matched to a built stair (recorded) or raised as a missing-stair finding; it may never be silently dropped.

any drawing layer whose name denotes fix.rule: Any drawing layer whose name denotes fixtures or decoration (vitrifiye/deko) must be consumed by the reading: its entities matched to built fixtures or raised as a loss; a fixture layer may never be silently dropped.

any drawing layer whose name denotes plu.rule: Any drawing layer whose name denotes plumbing or fixtures (piu/vitrifiye) must be consumed by the reading: its entities matched to built fixtures or raised as a loss; a fixture layer may never be silently dropped.

a stove drawn with its back parallel to.rule: A stove drawn with its back parallel to a wall but offset from it belongs on the wall; the reading must snap it, not leave a visible gap.

a toilet whose drawn centre is within 0..rule: A toilet whose drawn centre is within 0.38 m of a side wall or fixture is a misread position: the reading must place it at the nearest valid centre (>= 0.38 m clear) rather than keep the drawn centre and flag the clearance.

a bathtub drawn with less than 0.53 m cl.rule: A bathtub drawn with less than 0.53 m clear in front is a misread position: the reading must place it at the nearest valid spot (>= 0.53 m clear) rather than keep the drawn position and flag the clearance.

a shower drawn with less than 0.53 m cle.rule: A shower drawn with less than 0.53 m clear in front is a misread position: the reading must place it at the nearest valid spot (>= 0.53 m clear) rather than keep the drawn position and flag the clearance.

a room whose label names a living/leisur.rule: A room whose label names a living/leisure function (salon, oyun, aktivite, dinlenme, lounge) and whose furniture set is a living set (sofa, dining table, tv_unit, bookshelf) is typed 'living' even when its twin is typed differently; the type is read from the label and the set, not copied from a neighbouring room.

a bathroom set is complete only when it.rule: A bathroom set is complete only when it has its tall_cabinet (storage); if the room's drawn set lacks it, the fit stage adds it to the set rather than leaving the set as drawn.

an opening that lies on a wall must be c.rule: An opening that lies on a wall must be cut through that wall in the build stage; if the door ray still hits the wall, the cut was not applied and the build stage must be rerun.

every stair flight longer than 0.72 m of.rule: Every stair flight longer than 0.72 m of open run must have a handrail built as part of the stair's guard set (stair_rails.plan_guards, shell.stair_guard_plan); a flight with no handrail over 0.72 m of its run is a build failure.

a wall-hung item (mirror, wall_art, desk.rule: A wall-hung item (mirror, wall_art, desk_wall_unit) must not be covered by a standing piece in front of its wall; the wall-item pass must raise it over the standing piece, move it along the wall, or leave it out.

a wall-hung item must not hang over a wi.rule: A wall-hung item must not hang over a window or opening of its wall; the wall-item pass must move it to a free wall span or leave it out.

a living room with more than 3 m of oute.rule: A living room with more than 3 m of outer wall must have at least one window or door on that wall; a blank facade of 5.6 m is a reading/facade failure.

every house must have a frontal view of.rule: Every house must have a frontal view of its entrance (+y) facade; if no exterior camera shows it, one must be added.

when the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3.rule: When the terrain slopes steeper than 1:3, a retaining edge (retaining wall or stepped ground) must be built along the slope; the build stage must detect the slope and add the retaining edge.

every open edge of a balcony or roof ter.rule: Every open edge of a balcony or roof terrace at height must carry a guard at least 1.10 m above its floor; a glass balustrade lower than that is a safety failure, not a style choice.

a retaining or boundary wall that suppor.rule: A retaining or boundary wall that supports a planted bed must be finished in a material that matches the house's facade family; a bare concrete slab is an unfinished state, not a design.

a bathroom set is complete only when the.rule: A bathroom set is complete only when the washbasin has a mirror above it and a towel rail is present; a set that lacks these members is not finished.

a bathtub in a bathroom set must be show.rule: A bathtub in a bathroom set must be shown with its taps and mixer as part of the set; a bare tub in a corner is an unfinished state.

an outdoor terrace or garden must have a.rule: An outdoor terrace or garden must have a textured ground (grass, paving, or decking) and a horizon with depth; a single untextured green plane reads as a void.

a side table on a terrace should be a de.rule: A side table on a terrace should be a designed, textured piece that matches the outdoor style; a plain generic model does not elevate the scene.

a terrace with only two plants looks bar.rule: A terrace with only two plants looks bare and undesigned; a terrace_lounge group adds the missing furniture and greenery to make it a designed outdoor space.

every door in a room must be visible in.rule: Every door in a room must be visible in at least one interior view of that room; a door not seen in any view is a camera gap.

every facade of the house must have at l.rule: Every facade of the house must have at least one frontal exterior view; a missing frontal view of the entrance facade is a camera gap.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.90-0.95 m); a counter whose top is over 1.10 m is the wrong model for the piece.

a built piece whose model top exceeds it.rule: A built piece whose model top exceeds its working height (a counter above 0.97 m) is a wrong model: swap it for a model of the same type whose top sits at the working height.

an exterior view that must show a window.rule: An exterior view that must show a window is re-aimed to frame that window; a window the documents place on the facade must be visible in the view assigned to it.

a bathroom camera that shows the tub in.rule: A bathroom camera that shows the tub in isolation is re-posed to frame the tub together with its set (basin, mirror, accessories) so the room reads as designed, not a bare object.
A bathroom camera that shows the tub in a corner against a bare wall is re-posed to frame the tub with its set so the room reads as designed.
A bathroom camera that shows the tub in isolation is re-posed to frame the tub with its set so the room reads as designed.

a terrace furnished with only plants and.rule: A terrace furnished with only plants and a single chair is bare: add the terrace lounge group so the outdoor space reads as designed.

a chair drawn at a 90-degree offset from.rule: A chair drawn at a 90-degree offset from its table group is a reading error in the front direction, not a placement error: the solver must keep the drawn orientation when it is consistent with the group, and the inspector must not flag a chair that faces its table as mis-oriented.

a terrace camera that cuts off a foregro.rule: A terrace camera that cuts off a foreground piece is re-posed to frame the complete piece and the view.

a bathroom set that the documents specif.rule: A bathroom set that the documents specify as a walk-in shower with glass, rain head, hand shower on a rail and linear drain must be built as that set, not as a bathtub; the bathroom_set group must include the shower, the lit open cubby, the floor glow, the large backlit mirror and the towel shelf.

a hall camera that looks at a bare wall.rule: A hall camera that looks at a bare wall with a closed door is re-posed to show the hall open, lit and furnished, with the doors open.

interior doors in a render must be shown.rule: Interior doors in a render must be shown open against their swing side; only entrance and terrace doors may stay closed.

a bathroom set must include a backlit mi.rule: A bathroom set must include a backlit mirror, a feature panel, lit cubbies or floor glow, and a counter styled in two clusters; a plain fluted vanity with a small mirror and a single vessel basin is not a designed bathroom.

a hall camera dominated by a bare wall a.rule: A hall camera dominated by a bare wall and a closed door is re-posed to show the hall open, lit and furnished, with the doors open.

a hall camera that shows an interior doo.rule: A hall camera that shows an interior door closed is re-posed to a view where the door is open against its swing side.

a drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a side in a living room is a group of drawn pieces, not a single piece: the reading must split it into its constituent pieces and type each, rather than leaving it untyped.

a drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on one s.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on one side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item: the reading must split it into its individual pieces (or mark it as a built-in run) before typing, so the type table is never asked to match a cluster footprint.

a door under a sloped ceiling whose head.rule: A door under a sloped ceiling whose headroom is under 1.60 m (and no spot within 0.5 m along its wall gives more) must be resolved by a dormer or a raised roof before the door is lowered; the building stage must not silently lower a door to 1.00 m.

a toilet (or any wet-room fixture) under.rule: A toilet (or any wet-room fixture) under a sloped ceiling must be fitted against the clear headroom at its own footprint, not the room's nominal ceiling height; when no library model clears the sloped-ceiling cap, the parametric family is the correct fallback and must not be flagged as a misread.

a balcony/terrace of 15 m2 or more must.rule: A balcony/terrace of 15 m2 or more must be furnished as a usable lounge (a terrace_lounge group: seating for at least two plus a table), not a single chair; a single chair on a 20 m2 terrace is a missing-member defect.

a hall/circulation room (type hall) must.rule: A hall/circulation room (type hall) must not be furnished with a wardrobe; a wardrobe is a bedroom/storage piece and its presence in a hall is a wrong-type defect.

for a long, narrow piece (sofa, bench, s.rule: For a long, narrow piece (sofa, bench, sideboard) whose back is on a wall, the front is the long side facing the open room; an AI front on the short side is a reading error and must be corrected to the long side before the piece is placed.

a piece whose library candidates all fai.rule: A piece whose library candidates all fail the fit rules on height must be refit with the type's real product height range (not the parametric default) before the parametric mesh is kept; the parametric mesh is the last resort, not the default when a same-type library model exists.

every opening the documents show must be.rule: Every opening the documents show must be cut through its wall in the build; an opening that lies on a wall (0.000 m off) but whose door ray still hits the wall is a build-stage cut failure, not a geometry error, and must be cut, not re-placed.

a fitted piece must take a library model.rule: A fitted piece must take a library model that sits on the floor (its base at the room level); a parametric mesh that renders below the floor is a wrong model, not a placement.

views marked for review are a queue for.rule: Views marked for review are a queue for the render pass, not a defect of the model; they are resolved by the render stage, not by an edit here.

every inside door must have a recorded l.rule: Every inside door must have a recorded leaf state; an inside door stands open by default (UL116), so the build must write a leaf state for each inside door it places.

a camera that looks into a room worth sh.rule: A camera that looks into a room worth showing must have the door it sees through standing open (UL126); the build's door_states must be revised for the cameras so the leaf is out of the view.

a camera that looks through a door into.rule: A camera that looks through a door into a room worth showing must have that door's leaf recorded open (out of the view), not left closed.

when a coffee table overlaps an armchair.rule: When a coffee table overlaps an armchair and every move is refused because the neighbouring armchair itself cannot move (no_overlap), the solver must treat the armchair as the movable member of the pair and re-place the pair together, rather than declaring the table unfixable.

a tv unit whose back is off the wall and.rule: A TV unit whose back is off the wall and whose only free wall span is blocked by doors/windows must be re-anchored to the wall opposite the sofa (the viewing wall), not forced onto the blocked span.

a room whose label and furniture (sofa,.rule: A room whose label and furniture (sofa, coffee table, TV unit, dining) are a living set must be typed living even when a sibling room of the same label was typed other.

a drawn sofa whose back is off the wall.rule: A drawn sofa whose back is off the wall and whose nearest wall span is blocked (doors/windows) must be allowed to snap to the next free span within the drawn-lock tolerance, or the drawn-lock tolerance for a back-snap must be widened to the distance of the nearest free span.

a double bed that cannot reach 0.60 m cl.rule: A double bed that cannot reach 0.60 m clearance on either side without its headboard leaving the wall must be re-anchored to the longest wall of the room (headboard on that wall) so the two side clearances are computed against the remaining walls, rather than being left in a corner.

when a toilet's centre-to-side-wall clea.rule: When a toilet's centre-to-side-wall clearance is under 0.38 m and every candidate swap model is audit-removed or fails the fit rules, the solver must slide the existing toilet along its wall to the nearest position that meets the clearance, instead of only trying model swaps.

a tv unit that stands behind the back of.rule: A TV unit that stands behind the back of an armchair and cannot be rotated or moved without crossing the room outline must be re-anchored to the wall opposite the sofa (the viewing wall), with the armchair re-oriented to face it, as one seating-group re-solve.

an armchair that stands behind the back.rule: An armchair that stands behind the back of a sofa and does not face its group must be re-placed on the free side of the seating group (facing the coffee table) as part of a group re-solve, not nudged in place.

a washbasin whose lowest point is above.rule: A washbasin whose lowest point is above its floor and that stands in a door swing must be moved by the code to the nearest valid spot (no centre given), not left for the agent to guess a centre.

an armchair that does not face its seati.rule: An armchair that does not face its seating group and whose every rotation keeps it misfacing must be re-placed on the free side of the group (facing the coffee table) as part of a group re-solve, not rotated in place.

a nightstand that overlaps its bed by a.rule: A nightstand that overlaps its bed by a small area must be re-placed by the sleeping-group solver as a unit with the bed (both nightstands on the bed's sides), not by a free place_group call that the acceptance check cannot tie to a finding.

a kitchen whose run already exists but i.rule: A kitchen whose run already exists but is missing a fridge must have the fridge added to the existing kitchen_run (completed in place), not re-placed by a new place_group or a full relayout that finds no free dining place.

when a piece's own front free zone is bl.rule: When a piece's own front free zone is blocked by a piece that is itself the target of the same clearance finding, the solver must treat the pair as one unit and re-place both together (or re-layout the room) instead of moving only the target; a single-piece move that leaves the blocker in place is refused and must not be retried.

when a wardrobe (or any front-opening st.rule: When a wardrobe (or any front-opening storage) cannot reach its required front clearance by sliding within its room, the solver must re-layout the room or swap to a shallower model rather than repeatedly nudging the same piece; a move that still leaves the clearance short is refused and must not be retried.

under a sloped ceiling, a piece whose mo.rule: Under a sloped ceiling, a piece whose model height exceeds the local headroom must be swapped to a model that fits the headroom before any style check; a model that fails the height cap is refused and must not be retried in the same spot.

a drawn piece longer than 4.5 m in a liv.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m in a living room is a built-in or fixed element (e.g. a long low storage run or a hearth), not a free-standing sideboard or kitchen counter; the size table must exclude free-standing types for such lengths and route them to a built-in/parametric family or mark_not_furniture.

rule f5 must explicitly state whether a.rule: Rule F5 must explicitly state whether a piece reaching up to 0.02 m through the room outline is acceptable; if it is, the rule must name the tolerance so the critic does not flag it as F9.

rule c1 must state whether a 0.60 m walk.rule: Rule C1 must state whether a 0.60 m walkway from a door to a piece's front use zone is required for every piece or only for primary seating; if not required, the rule must name the exception so the critic does not flag it as G11.

rule s4 must state the minimum side clea.rule: Rule S4 must state the minimum side clearance for a toilet (0.38 m) and whether it applies to the centre or the edge; if the current layout is acceptable, the rule must name the tolerance so the critic does not flag it as G10.

rule f4 must state whether a sofa's fron.rule: Rule F4 must state whether a sofa's front free zone must be clear of all pieces or only of pieces that block the primary viewing axis; if a side table or ottoman in the zone is acceptable, the rule must name the exception so the critic does not flag it as F6.

rule e1 must state the maximum length of.rule: Rule E1 must state the maximum length of blank outer wall (no window or door) allowed for a living room; if 5.6 m is acceptable, the rule must name the tolerance so the critic does not flag it as X3.

the decor stage must add a feature wall.rule: The decor stage must add a feature wall (vertical fluted or slatted wood panelling) behind the bed in r_L0_e_yatak_odasi to match the reference style.

a parametric toilet model whose lowest p.rule: A parametric toilet model whose lowest point is 0.200 m above the floor is a library gap: the parametric family must be corrected to sit at floor level, or a real model with a floor-level base must be used.

the decor stage must add styled surfaces.rule: The decor stage must add styled surfaces (books, vases, art, objects) to the TV unit, coffee table, and shelves in r_L-1_salon to match the reference style.

an interior camera of a hall or corridor.rule: An interior camera of a hall or corridor must frame the room's main group (storage, doors, stair) and keep any blank wall out of the dominant half of the frame; a corner shot that reads as an empty passage is a bad camera, not a layout problem.

a shoe cabinet in a hall must be a finis.rule: A shoe cabinet in a hall must be a finished piece (closed doors or a styled front) that matches the room's palette; a bare parametric open-cubby grid is a placeholder, not a built piece.

a kitchen render must include a styling.rule: A kitchen render must include a styling layer on the worktop (a kettle or small appliance, a bowl of fruit, a cutting board) so the counter reads as lived-in; a bare worktop with only the run's fixtures is unfinished.

a kitchen worktop must carry a styling l.rule: A kitchen worktop must carry a styling layer (a kettle or small appliance, a bowl of fruit, a cutting board) so it reads as used; a completely bare worktop is unfinished.

lounge chairs in a living room must shar.rule: Lounge chairs in a living room must share the room's design language and wood tone with the main seating; a brown mid-century chair next to a white modern sectional is a mismatched set.

a sectional sofa must render with cushio.rule: A sectional sofa must render with cushions, pillows and a throw so it reads as a lived-in seating group; a bare white shell is unfinished.

coffee tables and side surfaces in a liv.rule: Coffee tables and side surfaces in a living room must carry a styled layer (books, a vase, small objects) so the room reads as curated; completely empty surfaces are unfinished.

full-height windows in a living room mus.rule: Full-height windows in a living room must have layered curtains (a sheer and a drape on a ceiling track) so the room does not read as exposed and unfinished; bare glass is a missing layer.

dining chairs must share the room's pale.rule: Dining chairs must share the room's palette and design language; a single wood chair among white chairs is a mismatched set.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main group (washbasin, toilet, storage) so the client can judge the layout; a tight crop of the tub corner that hides the rest of the room is a bad camera.

a bathroom camera must be positioned to.rule: A bathroom camera must be positioned to show the room's main group and layout; a camera pressed into a corner showing only a wall and the edge of a tub is a bad camera.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet, washbasin) so the layout can be judged; a camera pressed to the vanity and door that hides the shower and toilet is a bad camera.

a camera must not be positioned directly.rule: A camera must not be positioned directly in front of a door leaf such that the leaf fills the center of the frame and obscures the room's layout; the door should be at the edge of the frame or the camera should be offset to show the room beyond it.

a bedroom's wall behind the bed must be.rule: A bedroom's wall behind the bed must be a feature wall (vertical fluted or slatted wood panelling) to anchor the bed; a flat, untextured paint is a missing layer.

a corridor or hall rug must match the ro.rule: A corridor or hall rug must match the room's palette and read as a proper layer; a clashing bright runner is a missing or wrong layer.

a bedroom's nightstand and the area arou.rule: A bedroom's nightstand and the area around the bed must carry a styled layer (a console, a mirror, a vase, books) so the room reads as curated; bare surfaces are unfinished.

a desk or console in a furnished room mu.rule: A desk or console in a furnished room must be delivered with its styled surface (a lamp, a small object or a leaning print) as part of the model or a fixed decor child, so a bare top is never rendered.

a bedroom's headboard wall must carry a.rule: A bedroom's headboard wall must carry a feature finish (fluted/slatted panelling or wainscot) as a wall material or panel, not flat paint, when the reference shows a paneled accent wall.

a large living-room window must be deliv.rule: A large living-room window must be delivered with a layered curtain treatment (sheer plus drape) as a fixed decor child, not bare glass.

a living room's seating wall must carry.rule: A living room's seating wall must carry a feature finish (fluted/slatted panelling or wainscot) as a wall material or panel, not flat paint, when the reference shows a paneled accent wall.

a coffee table and sideboard in a furnis.rule: A coffee table and sideboard in a furnished living room must be delivered with styled surfaces (a mirror, vase, leaning art or curated objects) as fixed decor children, not bare.

a large ground-floor glazing seen from o.rule: A large ground-floor glazing seen from outside at dusk must carry interior warm light (a lit fixture or emissive interior) so the facade does not read as a dead, dark void.

the view outside a window must show a de.rule: The view outside a window must show a designed landscape (planters, seating, landscaping) as part of the site model, not a flat, low-poly green field.

a tall appliance (fridge) drawn inside a.rule: A tall appliance (fridge) drawn inside a kitchen counter run is built as a free-standing unit at its drawn position; the code must not refuse a model swap on the grounds that the appliance is 'built into' the run, and the window-sill clearance check must exempt appliances that are part of the run's front line.

every window in a bedroom or living room.rule: Every window in a bedroom or living room gets a full-height two-layer curtain (sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track, sized to the window width plus 30 cm each side.

every living or dining group sits on a r.rule: Every living or dining group sits on a rug sized to the group footprint plus 0.3 m each side.

every outdoor terrace or garden area sho.rule: Every outdoor terrace or garden area shown in a render gets a defined seating arrangement (lounge or dining set) plus planters, so it reads as a functional outdoor room.

a drawn piece in a kitchen that is 0.30.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen that is 0.30 x 0.20 m or smaller and sits on the counter line is typed by its position on the run (sink or stove), never left unknown.

a throw or cloth draped on a piece is of.rule: A throw or cloth draped on a piece is offset from the host surface by at least the cloth thickness plus 2 mm so the host does not show through.

a throw draped on a host whose top is no.rule: A throw draped on a host whose top is not one flat surface (a gap > 0.25 m between neighbouring top points) or that pokes through the cloth is not built and is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

a throw that penetrates its host by more.rule: A throw that penetrates its host by more than 0.007 m or shows the host through the cloth is not built and is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

decor that has no top on its built host.rule: Decor that has no top on its built host (after 2 attempts) is not built and is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

a throw that pokes through its host or s.rule: A throw that pokes through its host or shows the host through the cloth is not built and is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

decor that penetrates its host by more t.rule: Decor that penetrates its host by more than 0.01 m is not built and is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

entities on layers that are off, frozen.rule: Entities on layers that are off, frozen or invisible in the source DWG are not read and are not reported as a finding; they are dropped silently.
entities on layers that are off, frozen.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

entity types the reader does not support.rule: Entity types the reader does not support (OLE2FRAME, WIPEOUT) are not read and are not reported as a finding; they are dropped silently.

a camera view that is dropped without a.rule: A camera view that is dropped without a reason is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

a window that is not seen in one of the.rule: A window that is not seen in one of the views that must show it is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

a block drawn in the documents that no e.rule: A block drawn in the documents that no element of the model uses is not reported as a finding; it is dropped silently.

anonymous autocad blocks (a$c prefix) un.rule: Anonymous AutoCAD blocks (A$C prefix) under 0.3 m on a side are annotation/hatch fragments, not buildable elements; the ledger must not flag them as lost furniture.

when the same named block is inserted tw.rule: When the same named block is inserted twice at the same or overlapping location on a level, the reading must merge the duplicates into one element rather than leaving one unassigned.

blocks with random-string names and dime.rule: Blocks with random-string names and dimensions larger than any standard furniture piece (over 1.5 m on a side) that sit outside the room outlines are site/landscape elements, not buildable furniture; the ledger must not flag them as lost furniture.

site decoration blocks (tefriş, etc.) re.rule: Site decoration blocks (TEFRIŞ, etc.) recorded by site decor elements (sd_*) are outdoor elements, not buildable elements of the house model; the ledger must not flag them as lost furniture.

blocks with placeholder or annotation na.rule: Blocks with placeholder or annotation names (e.g. 'bulmak' meaning 'to find') that are not standard furniture types are annotation elements, not buildable elements of the house model; the ledger must not flag them as lost furniture.

when a stair block is inserted on a leve.rule: When a stair block is inserted on a level where a stair is already built in a room, the reading must merge the duplicate stair insert with the existing stair rather than leaving it unassigned.

a room label the documents name that no.rule: A room label the documents name that no room of the model uses is a lost room: the reading stage must be re-run so the label is read and the room built, not left to a manual add.

a balcony or terrace whose main furnitur.rule: A balcony or terrace whose main furniture group is missing is an empty, undefined space: the fit stage must place the room's terrace group (lounge seating and side table) so the space reads as furnished.

an interior camera whose frame is entire.rule: An interior camera whose frame is entirely black and empty is a failed render: the camera must be re-posed to a free point in the room that shows its main group at eye height.

a soft seat whose parts stand more than.rule: A soft seat whose parts stand more than 1 cm apart is a detached model: the build stage must re-run the soft_seats join so the facing bodies sit together, or the model is swapped.

a soft seat whose back or arm stands mor.rule: A soft seat whose back or arm stands more than 5 mm from its seat is a detached model: the build stage must re-run the soft_seats rest plan so every back and arm slides against its seat, or the model is swapped.

a soft-seat library model whose back or.rule: A soft-seat library model whose back or arm is not flush with its seat (gap over 5 mm) must be swapped for a model with a joined rest, not kept and nudged.

scene geometry checks (s1/s2) that fail.rule: Scene geometry checks (S1/S2) that fail on a level are resolved by re-running the build stage that places and rests the pieces, not by per-piece edits.

when an armchair is placed behind the ba.rule: When an armchair is placed behind the back of its sofa and every single rotation is refused (it would face a wall or lose its group), the seating group's layout is the cause and the room must be re-solved, not the single piece rotated.

when a tv_unit cannot be placed with its.rule: When a tv_unit cannot be placed with its back on a wall without leaving the room outline or drifting off the sofa axis, the living group's layout is the cause and the room must be re-solved, not the single piece rotated or moved.

a piece that crosses a room outline by 0.rule: A piece that crosses a room outline by 0.02 m or less (within the 0.03 m tolerance) is a false alarm and must not be flagged as a breach.

when a coffee table overlaps an armchair.rule: When a coffee table overlaps an armchair and every single move is refused (it would re-collide or the piece is already at its edit limit), the seating group's layout is the cause and the room must be re-solved, not the single piece nudged.

when a piece's front use zone is not rea.rule: When a piece's front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door because the seating group blocks the path, the room's layout is the cause and the room must be re-solved, not the single piece moved.

a seating group's coffee table must not.rule: A seating group's coffee table must not overlap its chairs; when the solver's placement leaves a collision that single-piece moves cannot clear, re-solve the whole room's AI pieces.

every seat's front use zone must be reac.rule: Every seat's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; when a single move cannot satisfy both the walkway and the group's other clearances, re-solve the room.

a sofa's front use zone must be reachabl.rule: A sofa's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; when the sofa is too large for the remaining floor after the other furniture, re-solve the room rather than shrinking the sofa.

a stove's back must be flush against a w.rule: A stove's back must be flush against a wall; when the kitchen run is placed with a gap, move the whole run to a free wall span.

a kitchen counter must have at least 0.9.rule: A kitchen counter must have at least 0.90 m of aisle in front of it; when the counter is placed too close to the opposite wall or island, move the run to a span that provides the aisle.

a piece whose drawn dimensions (width x.rule: A piece whose drawn dimensions (width x depth) are transposed relative to the type's product sizes is a misread orientation; retype it to the type that matches its actual footprint.

a sofa's back must be on a wall; when th.rule: A sofa's back must be on a wall; when the sofa is drawn in a position where no wall is within the allowed move distance, re-solve the room's AI pieces to find a valid wall-adjacent placement.

an armchair in a seating group must face.rule: An armchair in a seating group must face the group's centre; when rotation and single moves cannot achieve the correct orientation without breaking other clearances, re-solve the room.

an armchair's front free zone must not b.rule: An armchair's front free zone must not be blocked by another piece; when the blocking piece is part of the same seating group, re-solve the room.

a dining chair must have at least 0.81 m.rule: A dining chair must have at least 0.81 m from the table edge to the wall or piece behind it; when the chair is drawn in a tight spot, re-solve the room's AI pieces.

an armchair in a seating group must face.rule: An armchair in a seating group must face the group's centre; when rotation cannot achieve the correct orientation without breaking other clearances, re-solve the room.

a seating group is placed so that no sea.rule: A seating group is placed so that no seat faces the group's focal point (TV or table); the solver must orient every seat toward the focal point and keep the front use zone clear of the other seats' backs.

a coffee table must sit between the sofa.rule: A coffee table must sit between the sofa and the TV unit, on the sofa's front axis, within the seating group's clear zone.

a tv unit must have its back on a wall a.rule: A TV unit must have its back on a wall and face the sofa; it must not be placed behind a seat's back.

a sofa's back must rest on a wall; the s.rule: A sofa's back must rest on a wall; the solver must not leave a sofa floating 0.5 m off the nearest wall.

a seat at a coffee table must be within.rule: A seat at a coffee table must be within 2.5 m of the table and within 30° of its axis; the solver must keep the seating group compact.

the free zone in front of a sofa must be.rule: The free zone in front of a sofa must be clear of other seats; a seat must not block the sofa's front use zone.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window sill; the solver must place it clear of the window's projection.

a wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of.rule: A wardrobe must have at least 0.80 m of clear space in front of it for the doors to open; the solver must not place it where the clearance is under 0.80 m.

a dining table must not stand in front o.rule: A dining table must not stand in front of a window sill; the solver must place it clear of the window's projection.

a dining chair must not stand in front o.rule: A dining chair must not stand in front of a window sill; the solver must place it clear of the window's projection.

a seating group must not place a seat be.rule: A seating group must not place a seat behind another seat's back; every seat must face the group's focal point.

a tv unit must have its back on a wall;.rule: A TV unit must have its back on a wall; the solver must not leave it 1 m off the nearest wall.

a wall cabinet in a kitchen must use a r.rule: A wall cabinet in a kitchen must use a realistic library model, not a crude parametric block.

a decor-stage piece (potted plant) must.rule: A decor-stage piece (potted plant) must survive the agent stage; the agent must not drop a placed decor piece without a reason.

the agent stage must not drop a decor-st.rule: The agent stage must not drop a decor-stage piece that the drawing shows; a piece present after decor and absent after agent with no record naming it is a loss, not a decision.

a planned kitchen piece (stove, sink) th.rule: A planned kitchen piece (stove, sink) that the scene has no object for is a build loss: the build stage must emit a model for every planned piece, not silently drop it.

when two drawn pieces of the same type o.rule: When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than half the smaller one's area, the reading must treat them as one piece drawn twice (keep the larger, drop the smaller) and record the drop; it must not leave the smaller as a separate un-built piece that re-appears every run.

a block whose name names a fixture of a.rule: A block whose name names a fixture of a specific room (e.g. 'eb_banyo_ustdolap' = bathroom upper cabinet) drawn on a layer of another room is a section/detail duplicate of that room's fixture; when the named room already has the fixture built, do not add a second one in the other room.

a kitchen sink block drawn on a layer wh.rule: A kitchen sink block drawn on a layer where the room's kitchen run already includes a built sink is a section/detail duplicate of that sink; do not add a second sink_kitchen to the same room.

an interior room view must be posed to s.rule: An interior room view must be posed to show the room's doors; if a required door is out of frame, re-aim the camera to include it.

a small (<= 0.35 m) block drawn inside a.rule: A small (<= 0.35 m) block drawn inside a kitchen that no furniture rule types must be classified as a kitchen accessory and either built as a small appliance or recorded as a non-furniture detail with evidence, never left as an unexplained 'unknown'.

a dedicated stair section/elevation laye.rule: A dedicated stair section/elevation layer (e.g. 'A-MERDIVEN') whose geometry is already represented by a built stair in the plan must be recorded as a section detail of that stair, not left as an unexplained unused layer.

A dedicated stair section/elevation layer (e.g. 'A-merdiven görünüş') whose geometry is already represented by a built stair in the plan must be recorded as a section detail of that stair, not left as an unexplained unused layer.

a decorative finish layer (e.g. 'deko_vi.rule: A decorative finish layer (e.g. 'Deko_Vitrifiye', 'Piu_Vitrifiye') holding tile/finish geometry must be recorded as a material/finish detail of the room it belongs to, not left as an unexplained unused layer.

a stove drawn with a small gap (<= 0.10.rule: A stove drawn with a small gap (<= 0.10 m) behind it, back parallel to a wall, belongs on the wall; snap its back to the wall rather than leaving a visible gap.

when a toilet's side clearance is short.rule: When a toilet's side clearance is short by a small margin (<= 0.05 m) and model swaps are refused by fit rules, the reading must re-check the drawn centre against the wall/fixture and nudge the fixture within tolerance rather than forcing a model swap.

when a bathtub's front clearance is shor.rule: When a bathtub's front clearance is short and its drawn size is within the real product range (so it cannot be resized), the reading must re-check the drawn position and the room's usable depth; if the room genuinely cannot provide the clearance, flag it as a design constraint rather than forcing a resize or model swap.

in a bathroom, the toilet's centre must.rule: In a bathroom, the toilet's centre must be at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; when the drawn position cannot meet this, the toilet is re-placed on the nearest wall span that does, rather than left at the drawn centre.

a bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clea.rule: A bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; when the drawn position leaves less, the tub is re-placed on the nearest wall span that provides the clearance.

a shower must have at least 0.53 m clear.rule: A shower must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; when the drawn depth is too shallow to provide this, the shower is resized to a real product depth that does.

an interior camera of a bathroom must sh.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must show every fixture in the room; if a fixture is not visible in the frame, the camera is re-posed to include it.

a bedroom must have a bed with at least.rule: A bedroom must have a bed with at least one nightstand on each free side; when the drawn bed position leaves less than 0.60 m on a side, the bed is re-placed on the nearest wall span that provides the clearance.

an interior or balcony render must frame.rule: An interior or balcony render must frame the room's drawn furniture; when the pieces exist in the model but are absent from the frame, the camera is the defect, not the furniture.

a balcony render must show its seating;.rule: A balcony render must show its seating; a bare-slab look with the furniture present in the model is a camera defect.

a room-completeness check must verify a.rule: A room-completeness check must verify a member by its built piece list before reporting it missing; a member that is present must not be flagged, and a 13.6 m2 kitchen whose run already holds fridge, counter, sink and stove is complete.
A room-completeness check must verify a member by its built piece list before reporting it missing; a member that is present must not be flagged.

a bedroom render must show the bed as it.rule: A bedroom render must show the bed as its anchor; a frame that cuts the bed out is a camera defect when the bed is built.

a bathroom render must show its primary.rule: A bathroom render must show its primary fixtures; a view that omits them while they are built is a camera defect.

every site area the documents draw (pool.rule: Every site area the documents draw (pool, platform, parking, sun terrace) must be built as a site element with its outline; a drawn site area left 'NOT built (no outline)' is a site-stage loss, not a furniture or camera issue.

a room holding a sofa, dining table and.rule: A room holding a sofa, dining table and TV unit is a living room; the reading stage must type it 'living' from its fixtures, not 'other', even when its label is ambiguous.

a bathroom set is incomplete without its.rule: A bathroom set is incomplete without its tall_cabinet; the set definition must list tall_cabinet as a member so a set missing it is not reported 'complete' and the solver adds it.

an opening that lies on a wall (0.000 m.rule: An opening that lies on a wall (0.000 m off) must have that wall cut for it; 'on the wall' is not a valid reason to skip the cut, and a door ray hitting the wall means the cut is missing.

a parametric stair must build a continuo.rule: A parametric stair must build a continuous handrail over the nosing line on every open side of every flight; a flight with no handrail over its run is a build-stage defect in the stair model.

a hung wall item (mirror, art) must not.rule: A hung wall item (mirror, art) must not be covered by a piece standing in front of its wall; the wall-item pass must raise it over the piece, move it to a free stretch, or omit it.

a bathroom set is complete only when its.rule: A bathroom set is complete only when its washbasin carries a mirror and the room carries a towel rail; the set-completeness check must list these as required members, not only the anchor and the drawn partners.

an outdoor view must read as a designed.rule: An outdoor view must read as a designed landscape: the site must carry a hedge or fence at its edge and a full complement of trees, and the ground must be a textured lawn, not a single flat plane.

a terrace side table must be an outdoor-.rule: A terrace side table must be an outdoor-rated, textured model, not a plain indoor piece.

a balcony or terrace of this size must c.rule: A balcony or terrace of this size must carry a full lounge set (seating, table, and at least two plants), not a bare pair of plants.

a kitchen counter's top must sit at work.rule: A kitchen counter's top must sit at working height (about 0.90 m), not 1.18 m; the model chosen for a kitchen run must match the room's working height.

a bathroom camera must frame the full se.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the full set (tub, basin, toilet) with their accessories, not the tub in isolation.

a chair at a dining table must face the.rule: A chair at a dining table must face the table (its front toward the table centre), not be turned 90 deg off its drawn place.

a terrace camera must frame the full sea.rule: A terrace camera must frame the full seating set, not cut off the foreground armchair.

a terrace side table must be an outdoor-.rule: A terrace side table must be an outdoor-rated, textured model, not a small indoor glass-top piece.

an interior camera must frame the full s.rule: An interior camera must frame the full seating group, not cut off the foreground armchair.

a retaining wall or plot wall must carry.rule: A retaining wall or plot wall must carry a stone or masonry finish that matches the facade, not a bare untextured concrete slab.

an exterior camera that must show a wind.rule: An exterior camera that must show a window is posed so the window is in frame; a window the view is required to show but that is out of frame is a camera error, not a model error.

a bathtub model must include visible tap.rule: A bathtub model must include visible taps/controls and a finished surround; a bare tub with no fittings reads as undesigned and is swapped for a model that carries them.

an upper-floor balcony/terrace edge must.rule: An upper-floor balcony/terrace edge must carry a guard (railing) of adequate height; a thin glass pane with no handrail or frame is a fall risk and is completed with a proper guard.

a hall camera must look through an open.rule: A hall camera must look through an open door into a lit, furnished room, not straight at a bare wall with a closed door; the camera is reposed to show the room beyond.

interior doors are rendered open against.rule: Interior doors are rendered open against their swing side in every interior view; only entrance and terrace doors may be shown closed.

a hall camera must look through an open.rule: A hall camera must look through an open door into a lit, furnished room, not at a bare wall and a closed door; the camera is reposed to show the room beyond.

a drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; the reading must split it into its constituent pieces (or mark it as a built-in run) rather than leaving it untyped.

a door under a sloped ceiling needs at l.rule: A door under a sloped ceiling needs at least 1.60 m of headroom; where the roof slope leaves less, a dormer or a raised roof is required at that wall, and the door is not lowered to the roof line.

a room's type must match its fixtures an.rule: A room's type must match its fixtures and furniture; a 40 m2 room with a sofa, dining table, TV unit and bookshelf is a living room, not 'other'.

a bathroom set is complete only when it.rule: A bathroom set is complete only when it includes a tall_cabinet (storage) in addition to the tub/shower, toilet and washbasin; a set missing its storage member is incomplete.

an interior hall camera must be posed to.rule: An interior hall camera must be posed to look through an open door into the furnished room beyond (show the door and the room's pieces), never at a closed door and a bare wall.

a drawn sofa with no front (front_inferr.rule: A drawn sofa with no front (front_inferred) must be given the front the code suggests (towards its partner across the open floor) so it is oriented correctly in the living room.

an interior camera must be posed to look.rule: An interior camera must be posed to look through an open door into the furnished room beyond (show the door and the room's pieces), never at a closed door and a bare wall.

a shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall.rule: A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the entrance level (ground floor); in an upper-floor hall it must be retyped to a console_table or sideboard (or removed) to match the hall's program.

a balcony/terrace larger than about 15 m.rule: A balcony/terrace larger than about 15 m2 must be furnished with a full terrace_lounge set (seating group, table, plants), not a single armchair and side table.

a bathroom's storage set must be complet.rule: A bathroom's storage set must be complete: if its twin bathroom has a tall_cabinet, this one must too (the bathroom_set is completed with what it misses).

a room named 'oyun aktivite ve dinlenme.rule: A room named 'Oyun Aktivite Ve Dinlenme Odasi' (game/activity/relaxation room) that is furnished as a living room (sofa, tv_unit, table_dining, table_coffee, armchair) must be typed 'living', not 'other'.

an interior bathroom camera must be pose.rule: An interior bathroom camera must be posed at a valid eye height (1.2-1.6 m) clear of floor decor so the room renders lit and furnished, not black/empty.

a shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall.rule: A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the entrance level (ground floor); in an upper-floor hall it must be retyped to a console_table or sideboard (or removed). A wardrobe in a hall is only allowed if the documents show built-in storage there.

a daybed (a bed-like piece with drawer f.rule: A daybed (a bed-like piece with drawer fronts and a low upholstered back) is only allowed in a bedroom; in a living/play-and-rest room the seating must be upholstered sofas, not daybeds.

a ground-floor hall with many doors (the.rule: A ground-floor hall with many doors (the entrance hall) must be furnished with an entrance set (console or coat storage), not only a shoe_cabinet.

a 5 m2 bathroom whose documents draw a s.rule: A 5 m2 bathroom whose documents draw a shower (the same module as the L0 bathrooms that use a shower) must be furnished with a shower, not a bathtub.

a reading stage must not end 'pending' w.rule: A reading stage must not end 'pending' with open sheet questions: every question written to sheets/requests.json must be answered (or the sheet re-read) before the stage is allowed to close, so no downstream stage runs on an incomplete reading.

when a long piece (sofa, bench, table) i.rule: When a long piece (sofa, bench, table) is read with its front on a short side, the front must be re-derived from the plan crop (the long side facing the most open floor) instead of trusting the AI front, so the piece is not built facing the wrong way.

a bench (or any long piece) whose back i.rule: A bench (or any long piece) whose back is on a wall must have its front read as the side away from that wall; an AI front on the short side is a reading error and must be corrected from the plan crop before the piece is built.

every opening read from the documents mu.rule: Every opening read from the documents must be cut through its wall in the model; if a door ray still hits the wall, the opening's cut must be re-cut (or the wall re-read) so the opening is actually open, not just placed on the wall.

a tall_cabinet (or any tall piece) must.rule: A tall_cabinet (or any tall piece) must be built at or above the library level; if the fitting stage chooses a parametric mesh that sits below the library level, the model must be swapped for a library model that fits the height, or the parametric mesh must be raised to the library level.

a toilet (or any bathroom fixture) must.rule: A toilet (or any bathroom fixture) must be built at or above the library level; if the fitting stage chooses a parametric mesh that sits below the library level, the model must be swapped for a library model that fits the height, or the parametric mesh must be raised to the library level.

a parametric fixture's lowest point must.rule: A parametric fixture's lowest point must sit on the finished floor (within +0.01 m); a model whose base floats above the floor is a fit failure to be swapped or corrected, never accepted.

a bedroom nightstand must be dressed (a.rule: A bedroom nightstand must be dressed (a lamp or statement fixture and a styled surface) so the bedside reads as a finished layer, not a bare placeholder.

bedroom surfaces (nightstand, desk) must.rule: Bedroom surfaces (nightstand, desk) must be styled with at least one decorative object (vase, books, mirror or art) so they do not read as bare placeholders.

kitchen wall cabinets must use a model w.rule: Kitchen wall cabinets must use a model whose material and finish match the surrounding cabinetry and wall treatment; a flat untextured slab that breaks material continuity is a wrong-model failure.

a living room's main seating area must b.rule: A living room's main seating area must be anchored by a feature wall (fluted wood, paneling or equivalent) behind the sofa; a flat untextured wall behind the main seat is a decor gap.

a living room must include a tv unit and.rule: A living room must include a TV unit and TV facing the main seat; a living room with no TV is a layout gap.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main group (basin, bath, toilet); a camera pressed against a wall showing only a switch, socket and vase is a bad camera.

a bedroom must include a rug to anchor t.rule: A bedroom must include a rug to anchor the bed and soften the hard floor; a bedroom with no rug reads as cold and unfinished.

a bedroom must meet the professional bar.rule: A bedroom must meet the professional bar: a fluted/feature panel on the accent wall and a herringbone (or equivalent patterned) wood floor; a flat accent wall and plain wood floor fall short.

a bed must be dressed with layered beddi.rule: A bed must be dressed with layered bedding (a throw, a second blanket across the foot, euro shams and decorative cushions); a single flat duvet with plain pillows reads as a placeholder.
A bed must be dressed with layered bedding (a throw, a second blanket across the foot, and decorative accent cushions); a single flat duvet reads as a placeholder.

a living room must be styled with a cons.rule: A living room must be styled with a console, wall art and decorative objects (books, mirror, centrepiece); a room with only a single vase reads as unfinished.

a sofa_corner model whose parts stand mo.rule: A sofa_corner model whose parts stand more than 1 cm apart is a fit failure; swap to a model whose parts are correctly joined.

an interior camera of a small wet room m.rule: An interior camera of a small wet room must be posed from a free point with headroom so the whole fixture set (bathtub, basin, toilet) is in frame, never pressed into a corner showing one edge and a blank wall.

a hall camera must frame the doors and t.rule: A hall camera must frame the doors and the space as a whole from a free pose, not a wall section and a single cabinet.

a kitchen render must carry a styled wor.rule: A kitchen render must carry a styled worktop (a few props: a bowl, a small plant, a cutting board) and styled open shelves, not a bare counter with a single bowl, to read as a lived-in space.

the seating group of a living room must.rule: The seating group of a living room must be one coordinated set (matching style and colour family); when the corner sofa's model clashes with the sofa and armchair, swap the sofa model to the set's style.

a living room's seating group must be an.rule: A living room's seating group must be anchored by a large area rug under the coffee table and seating; the decor stage must place one when the reference shows it.

a view through a living-room glazing ont.rule: A view through a living-room glazing onto an outdoor terrace must show a furnished terrace (seating, planters, rug, lanterns), not a flat empty lawn, so the outdoor space reads as designed.

coffee and side tables in a living room.rule: Coffee and side tables in a living room must carry styled props (books, vases, small objects) so the surfaces read as lived-in, not bare.

a living/dining room's main wall should.rule: A living/dining room's main wall should carry a feature finish (slatted wood or paneling) to add depth, not flat untextured paint, when the reference style calls for it.

the wood tones of a room's tables must f.rule: The wood tones of a room's tables must form a cohesive palette; when the dining table's model clashes with the coffee and side tables, swap it to a neutral/light model of the same footprint.

a bathroom camera must frame the whole f.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the whole fixture set from a free pose with headroom, not a door frame and vanity corner.

a bathroom camera must frame the main gr.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the main group (basin, toilet, cabinet) from a free pose, not a corner and the edge of the bathtub.

a bathroom camera must frame the main fi.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the main fixtures (shower, toilet) from a free pose, not a vanity corner.

a bathroom camera must not be positioned.rule: A bathroom camera must not be positioned directly in front of the door leaf; it must frame the room's fixtures from a free pose.

a bedroom window must carry full-height.rule: A bedroom window must carry full-height two-layer curtains (sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track when the reference shows them.

a bedroom's wall behind the bed should c.rule: A bedroom's wall behind the bed should carry a feature finish (fluted or slatted wood panelling) to anchor the bed, not flat untextured paint, when the reference style calls for it.

a hall's lighting must be warm and layer.rule: A hall's lighting must be warm and layered (a pendant or chandelier plus accent light) to feel inviting, not flat and cold.

every outdoor living area named in the p.rule: Every outdoor living area named in the plan (terrace, sunbathing, pool deck) must be furnished with a seating group (lounge chairs, side table, planter) so exterior renders show a defined outdoor room, not a bare lawn.

pool and terrace areas must be furnished.rule: Pool and terrace areas must be furnished with a cohesive outdoor seating arrangement (dining set or lounge group) so renders show a functional outdoor room, not just a pool and isolated loungers.

the site stage must apply realistic lawn.rule: The site stage must apply realistic lawn texture and landscaping detail (grass, planters, hardscape edges) around outdoor terraces so renders do not show a flat, untextured green plane.

the site stage must apply realistic grou.rule: The site stage must apply realistic ground texture and landscaping detail (grass, planters, hardscape edges) so outdoor renders do not show a flat, untextured green plane.

exterior and terrace cameras must be ren.rule: Exterior and terrace cameras must be rendered against a finished site (ground cover, planting, paths, boundary treatment); a flat grey-box lawn or void is not client-ready.

outdoor floors (terrace, balcony, verand.rule: Outdoor floors (terrace, balcony, veranda) must carry a finished, designed surface (decking, pavers, stone) rather than bare cracked concrete.

exterior cameras must be rendered with a.rule: Exterior cameras must be rendered with a real sun (warm, directional light) and a finished site; flat grey lighting and a grey-box landscape are not client-ready.

the facade must carry a designed claddin.rule: The facade must carry a designed cladding (wood, stone, render) rather than a bare massing-study surface; exterior renders need material richness.

a balcony/terrace of this size must carr.rule: A balcony/terrace of this size must carry a lounge or seating group (a place to sit); a bare slab is not a finished outdoor living space.

stone cladding on the lower wall (plinth.rule: Stone cladding on the lower wall (plinth) must use a varied, high-quality stone look (ashlar, ledgestone) rather than a flat repetitive placeholder texture.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's anchor piece (the bathtub or shower) and the main fixtures; a view that crops out the anchor is not a valid room view.

an interior bedroom camera must frame th.rule: An interior bedroom camera must frame the bed and its nightstands; a view that crops the bed out of frame is not a valid room view.

a seating group (two armchairs plus a si.rule: A seating group (two armchairs plus a side table) must read as a designed, matching set; mismatched models in one group are a fit error.

a hall shoe cabinet must be a finished,.rule: A hall shoe cabinet must be a finished, styled piece (doors, finish) matching the project's design language, not a bare parametric grid of open cubbies.

an armchair in a living room must match.rule: An armchair in a living room must match the room's design language (here, the white modern sectional); a brown mid-century lounge chair is a mismatched model.

an interior bedroom camera must frame th.rule: An interior bedroom camera must frame the bed and its nightstands; a view that shows only a bare corner with a desk and wardrobe is not a valid room view.

the view outside a window must show desi.rule: The view outside a window must show designed landscaping (planting, planters, paths, seating), not a flat untextured green field with a simple fence.

a kitchen worktop in a furnished render.rule: A kitchen worktop in a furnished render must carry at least one small styled object (kettle, plant, or bowl) so the surface does not read as an empty slab.

every bedroom render must show a layered.rule: Every bedroom render must show a layered, styled room (feature wall, headboard, rug, window treatment, art, lamps, styled surfaces); a flat grey-box with a bare slab bed is not acceptable.
Every bedroom render must show a layered, styled room (feature wall, layered bedding, rug, window treatment, art, styled surfaces, warm light); a flat unstyled shell is not acceptable.

a bedroom render must not place a clashi.rule: A bedroom render must not place a clashing office set (black mesh chair, desk) in the foreground of a warm, wood-slatted bedroom; the furniture must match the room's style.

a nightstand in a furnished render must.rule: A nightstand in a furnished render must carry styled objects (books, a small vase, a proper lamp) so it does not read as a dark, empty block.

a dining set in a furnished render must.rule: A dining set in a furnished render must match the project's style; a mismatched, dated combination (grey painted table with turned legs paired with modern grey chairs) is not acceptable.

a room render must not show a clash of t.rule: A room render must not show a clash of two different style projects; the furniture, rug, and wall treatment must read as one coherent design.

large windows in a furnished render must.rule: Large windows in a furnished render must have layered curtains (sheer and drape on a track); bare glazing reads as flat and unfinished.

every drawn furniture piece must be type.rule: Every drawn furniture piece must be typed by a rule or model; a piece left as 'unknown' is a reading failure that must be resolved by retyping it to a type that fits its size and room.

a decor throw must rest on its host with.rule: A decor throw must rest on its host without the host poking through the cloth; if the host's geometry prevents a clean rest, the throw is not built.
A decor throw must rest on its host without the host poking through the cloth and without the cloth tearing; if the host's geometry prevents a clean rest, the throw is not built.

decor books must rest on a found top of.rule: Decor books must rest on a found top of the built host; if no top is found, the books are not built.

a decor plant must rest on a found top o.rule: A decor plant must rest on a found top of the built host; if no top is found, the plant is not built.

a decor item is only built when it sits.rule: A decor item is only built when it sits fully on its host's top surface; if the host pokes through the cloth, the item is re-seated or dropped, never built intersecting.

a decor item is only built when its pene.rule: A decor item is only built when its penetration into the host is within 0.01 m; otherwise it is re-seated or dropped.

a decor item is only built when a top su.rule: A decor item is only built when a top surface is found on its built host; if none is found after retries, the item is dropped rather than built floating.

the reading stage must read entities on.rule: The reading stage must read entities on all layers, including those that are off or frozen, and flag any that are skipped so the ledger can verify nothing holding geometry was lost.
the reading stage must read entities on.target: # entities on layers that are off or frozen (or invisible) were not read

the reading stage must record every enti.rule: The reading stage must record every entity type it encounters, including OLE2FRAME and WIPEOUT, and explain why each is or is not used, so the ledger can confirm nothing was silently dropped.

a camera is only dropped when a reason i.rule: A camera is only dropped when a reason is recorded (e.g. it shows a bare wall or is redundant); a camera dropped with no reason is a loss.

an exterior camera that must show a wind.rule: An exterior camera that must show a window is framed so the window is visible; if the current pose hides it, the camera is re-aimed.

every block drawn in the documents must.rule: Every block drawn in the documents must be matched to a model element or explicitly marked as not furniture (with evidence); a block that no element uses is a loss.

a drawn block whose name is a placeholde.rule: A drawn block whose name is a placeholder or non-furniture token (e.g. 'eeere', 'bulmak', 'A$C...') and whose size matches no room program is a drawing artifact, not a lost piece; it is recorded, not built.

anonymous autocad blocks (names starting.rule: Anonymous AutoCAD blocks (names starting 'A$C') are internal reference/clip geometry, not furniture; they are never built and never count as lost pieces.

a drawn block with a non-semantic name w.rule: A drawn block with a non-semantic name whose footprint matches no room program is a drawing artifact, not a lost piece; it is recorded, not built.

a drawn block with a generic name whose.rule: A drawn block with a generic name whose size matches no room program is a drawing artifact, not a lost piece; it is recorded, not built.

a drawn block already recorded as site d.rule: A drawn block already recorded as site decor (sd_*) is accounted for; it is not a lost interior piece.

a drawn block with a non-semantic name w.rule: A drawn block with a non-semantic name whose size matches no room program is a drawing artifact, not a lost piece; it is recorded, not built.

a drawn stair block whose room already h.rule: A drawn stair block whose room already has a built stair is the same element already accounted for, not a lost piece.

a drawn block whose name is a placeholde.rule: A drawn block whose name is a placeholder or non-furniture token and whose size matches no room program is a drawing artifact, not a lost piece; it is recorded, not built.

a block whose name is not in the furnitu.rule: A block whose name is not in the furniture library and whose footprint (1.57 x 2.87 m) matches no standard piece must be classified from its room context and neighbours before it is dropped: if it sits against a wall in a living or bedroom zone it is a storage unit (wardrobe or sideboard), if it is free-standing in a kitchen zone it is a kitchen island or counter; only when no context fits is it kept as an untyped obstacle, and that decision must be recorded with the crop, never a silent loss.

a drawn entity that sits 60% or more ins.rule: A drawn entity that sits 60% or more inside a larger built fixture of the same room is a part of that fixture (faucet, bowl, tap), not a separate piece: it is dropped as a duplicate and is not a loss.
A drawn entity that sits 60% or more inside a larger built fixture of the same room is a part of that fixture, not a separate piece: it is dropped as a duplicate and is not a loss.

two floor lamps never stand inside each.rule: Two floor lamps never stand inside each other: a smaller lamp drawn overlapping a larger one of the same room is a duplicate drawing of the same lamp, and the larger one is kept.

a 2d-only layer of circles and lines (an.rule: A 2D-only layer of circles and lines (annotation, hatching, detail geometry) is not a built element: it is not used by the 3D model and its absence is not a loss.

a decorative floor-tile/finish pattern l.rule: A decorative floor-tile/finish pattern layer (arcs, ellipses, splines, lines) is 2D finish geometry, not a built element: it is not used by the 3D model and its absence is not a loss.

a 2d-only layer of arcs and lines (annot.rule: A 2D-only layer of arcs and lines (annotation, detail geometry) is not a built element: it is not used by the 3D model and its absence is not a loss.

a drawn piece that the decor stage place.rule: A drawn piece that the decor stage placed and the agent stage dropped (named in the layout record) is a loss: the agent must keep it or re-place it, not silently remove it.
A drawn piece that the decor stage placed and the agent stage dropped (named in the decor record) is a loss: the agent must keep it or re-place it, not silently remove it.

a room whose type is 'other' (unclassifi.rule: A room whose type is 'other' (unclassified) must not be used to reject a drawn piece: the piece is kept and the room is re-typed from its area, fixtures and doors, or the piece is verified against the drawing, rather than left unverified because the room type does not list it.

when one room outline holds the labels o.rule: When one room outline holds the labels of two rooms (e.g. 'Salon' and 'AÇIK MUTFAK'), the reading must split the outline at the missing wall (or mark the wall as not read) so each label gets its own room, instead of keeping only the largest label and silently merging the two rooms.

a built piece whose model footprint diff.rule: A built piece whose model footprint differs from its drawn size by more than the 0.05 m tolerance must be swapped to a library model whose footprint matches the drawn size, so the render matches the drawing.

when a drawn piece's footprint is within.rule: When a drawn piece's footprint is within 0.05 m of a library model's footprint, the layout stage must select that model (or a parametric fit) instead of a larger default, so the built piece matches the drawing within tolerance.

a bathroom set is complete when its anch.rule: A bathroom set is complete when its anchor and the drawn members are present; a storage piece (tall_cabinet) that the twin room has but this one does not is a program difference, not a missing member, and must not be force-added to a 4.0 m2 en-suite.

for an open-plan living room, a tv/media.rule: For an open-plan living room, a TV/media wall may be a freestanding tv_unit or a wall that is not the one the sofa faces; the 'no TV place' check must accept a clear wall 1.5-4 m away even when it is not directly opposite the sofa, and must not fail the whole room when the only candidate wall is blocked by a window or door.

when the wall a sofa/bed faces is blocke.rule: When the wall a sofa/bed faces is blocked (by a wardrobe or window), the media-wall check should look for a TV place on another clear wall of the room rather than failing; a bedroom without a TV is also a valid program and should not raise a 'no TV place' warning.

when a desk (or any wall-backed piece) h.rule: When a desk (or any wall-backed piece) has no free wall span within 1.2 m of its drawn place, the solver should allow placing it on the nearest free span of the same wall or an adjacent wall rather than refusing all moves; a desk does not need to stay within 1.2 m of its drawn centre.

when the fit stage builds a piece from t.rule: When the fit stage builds a piece from the parametric family, it must first check the library for a model of the same type and footprint; if one exists, the library model is used and the parametric mesh is reserved for footprints no library model covers.

the kitchen module builder must align th.rule: The kitchen module builder must align the wall cabinet run's unit joints to the base cabinet run's joints under it; a wall run is only valid when every wall-unit joint sits over a base-unit joint (or a base-unit end), and the builder must re-solve the wall run's unit split to satisfy this before it is accepted.

the bedroom program must not require a t.rule: The bedroom program must not require a TV as a mandatory group; a TV is an optional comfort item, and the M21 check must treat a bedroom without a TV as complete when the sleeping group (bed, nightstands, wardrobe) is present, or the decor stage must place a TV only when the room's wall layout offers an unblocked view zone.

the bathroom program must include a stor.rule: The bathroom program must include a storage element (tall_cabinet or wall_cabinet) as part of the bathroom_set group, so that the room_fill stage places it alongside the fixtures; a bathroom with only shower, toilet and washbasin is incomplete.

a bathroom whose set includes a tall_cab.rule: A bathroom whose set includes a tall_cabinet or wall_cabinet is not missing storage; do not flag M21 when the set is complete.

when a living room fails ul106 for accen.rule: When a living room fails UL106 for accent wall and curtain layering, the decor stage adds the fluted panel and sheer layer; do not retype or relayout the room to fix a finish.

a missing throw on a bed is a decor-stag.rule: A missing throw on a bed is a decor-stage textile item; do not move or swap the bed model to add it.

a missing rug under a sofa group is a de.rule: A missing rug under a sofa group is a decor-stage placement; do not retype the sofa to add it.

a shoe cabinet flagged as a generic boxy.rule: A shoe cabinet flagged as a generic boxy metal placeholder should be swapped to a wood/modern model from the candidate list.

a kitchen run missing upper cabinets or.rule: A kitchen run missing upper cabinets or a hood should be completed via place_group kitchen_run, which adds the missing members of the drawn run.
