a concrete-look kitchen backsplash that.rule: A concrete-look kitchen backsplash that clashes with a warm wood aesthetic should be set to a wood look on the kitchen_walls slot.

a floor lamp that appears off or not con.rule: A floor lamp that appears off or not contributing warmth should be swapped to a model with a visible warm glow in the render.

dark, heavy door frames that clash with.rule: Dark, heavy door frames that clash with a light wood aesthetic should be set to a light wood look on the door slot.

a room with flat, even lighting should h.rule: A room with flat, even lighting should have a statement fixture or warm lamp glow added by the decor stage.

a flat concrete terrace floor should be.rule: A flat concrete terrace floor should be set to a decking or textured look on the paving slot to feel finished.

a plain, flat entrance door should be se.rule: A plain, flat entrance door should be set to a richer wood look on the door slot to add detail and design flair.

an exterior render devoid of lighting fi.rule: An exterior render devoid of lighting fixtures should have outdoor lanterns or path lights added by the decor stage.

a patio that is a single unbroken slab s.rule: A patio that is a single unbroken slab should have an outdoor rug added by the decor stage to define zones.

a kitchen counter devoid of organic elem.rule: A kitchen counter devoid of organic elements should have a small potted plant added by the decor stage.

a plain, flat interior door should be se.rule: A plain, flat interior door should be set to a natural wood look on the door slot to match a high-end style.

a living room of 40 m2 or more gets at l.rule: A living room of 40 m2 or more gets at least two potted plants of different heights so the greenery reads as a layer, not a single accent.

wall art and styling objects are not bui.rule: Wall art and styling objects are not buildable pieces; a bare wall is a taste note, not a defect, unless the brief names the art.

outdoor areas (terrace, pool, entrance p.rule: Outdoor areas (terrace, pool, entrance path) get at least one lighting fixture (lantern or bollard) per 10 m2 of outdoor space, placed at the edge of the paved area.

cushions, throws and other soft furnishi.rule: Cushions, throws and other soft furnishings are sub-parts of their host piece, not separate buildable pieces; their removal from the piece list is expected.

a side_table that is part of a seating g.rule: A side_table that is part of a seating group and is absorbed into the group's layout is not a loss; the group's solver owns it.

cushions, throws and other soft furnishi.rule: Cushions, throws and other soft furnishings are sub-parts of their host piece, not separate buildable pieces.

a piece named in 'layout.copied_from' wa.rule: A piece named in 'layout.copied_from' was copied into the final layout, not lost; the conservation check should not flag it.

a bookshelf that is part of a seating gr.rule: A bookshelf that is part of a seating group and is absorbed into the group's layout is not a loss.

an armchair that stands behind the back.rule: An armchair that stands behind the back of a sofa and cannot be rotated or moved to face the group must be re-placed by the agent in the next round, not dropped.

a shoe_cabinet in a living room is a mis.rule: A shoe_cabinet in a living room is a misread; the agent should retype it to a type that fits the room (console_table, sideboard) or remove it, not drop it silently.

a piece named in 'handed_over.from' was.rule: A piece named in 'handed_over.from' was moved to another room, not lost; the conservation check should not flag it.

a tv_unit that is not on a wall and off.rule: A tv_unit that is not on a wall and off the sofa axis must be re-placed by the agent in the next round, not dropped.

a tall_cabinet that is part of a storage.rule: A tall_cabinet that is part of a storage group and is absorbed into the group's layout is not a loss.

a level that belongs to a variant is not.rule: A level that belongs to a variant is not part of the base build; the conservation check should not flag it as lost.

drawn elements on a structure layer (a-b.rule: Drawn elements on a structure layer (A-BA) that are not furniture are kept as obstacles, not built; the conservation check should not flag them as lost.

site furniture symbols (sd_*) drawn on t.rule: Site furniture symbols (sd_*) drawn on the site layer are outdoor items handled by the site/decor stage, not interior furniture; the build stage must not flag them as lost.

pieces drawn on a decor layer (deko_*) a.rule: Pieces drawn on a decor layer (Deko_*) are decor, not furniture; the build stage must not flag them as lost because the decor stage places them.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside an already-built fixture of the same kind is a duplicate or a part of that fixture, not a separate piece; the build stage must not flag it as lost.

a drawn detail that is a part of a large.rule: A drawn detail that is a part of a larger built piece (an appliance front or drawer inside a counter leg) is not a separate piece; the build stage must not flag it as lost.

a cluster of drawn pieces larger than 4..rule: A cluster of drawn pieces larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group, not individual pieces; the build stage must not flag its members as lost when the group is handled as a unit.

a drawn symbol that both recognition pas.rule: A drawn symbol that both recognition passes classify as not_furniture is kept as an obstacle, not built as furniture; the build stage must not flag it as lost.

a drawn outline that is a rug mark (a ta.rule: A drawn outline that is a rug mark (a table and chairs inside it) is decor, not a furniture piece; the build stage must not flag it as lost because the decor stage places it.

cushions or pillows that are part of a b.rule: Cushions or pillows that are part of a built model's own geometry are not separate pieces; the build stage must not flag them as lost.

a floor lamp drawn 30% or more inside a.rule: A floor lamp drawn 30% or more inside a larger floor lamp of the same room is the same lamp drawn twice, not two lamps; the build stage must not flag the smaller duplicate as lost.

a floor lamp drawn 15% or more inside a.rule: A floor lamp drawn 15% or more inside a larger floor lamp of the same room is the same lamp drawn twice, not two lamps; the build stage must not flag the smaller duplicate as lost.

a small ottoman drawn 80% or more inside.rule: A small ottoman drawn 80% or more inside an armchair is the armchair's seat cushion, not a separate piece; the build stage must not flag it as lost.

a drawn outline that is >= 70% inside an.rule: A drawn outline that is >= 70% inside another piece's footprint and is smaller than that piece is a detail of that piece (cushion, seat), not a separate furniture item; the build should drop it as a detail, not as a lost piece.

a piece removed by an explicit ai.remove.rule: A piece removed by an explicit AI.remove_piece decision is not a conservation loss; the build should not flag it as 'not built'.

a large flat outline (>= 2 m in both dim.rule: A large flat outline (>= 2 m in both dimensions) that encloses other pieces and has no height is a rug or zone boundary, not a furniture item; the build should classify it as decor, not as a lost piece.

when a build step resolves a window or f.rule: When a build step resolves a window or fixture conflict, it must not silently drop unrelated furniture pieces in the same room; each piece's build status should be tracked independently.

a stair's upper landing on the top floor.rule: A stair's upper landing on the top floor is not a separate stair piece; it is the terminus of the stair built on the lower floor. The build should not flag the upper landing as a lost stair.

when a furniture model already includes.rule: When a furniture model already includes cushions or pillows as part of its geometry, separate cushion decor items for that piece should not be built; the build should suppress them, not flag them as lost.

a decor item whose host piece was intent.rule: A decor item whose host piece was intentionally removed is not a conservation loss; it should be dropped with its host, not flagged as lost.

an exterior site area (parking, terrace,.rule: An exterior site area (parking, terrace, pool) whose surface is already built as a paving or platform element is not a conservation loss; the site label is satisfied by the built surface.

a drawn piece whose front the reading co.rule: A drawn piece whose front the reading could not infer (front_inferred) must be given its front from the plan (the side that looks into the open floor or towards its seating partner) before the room is checked, so the facing and media-wall checks run on a real front.

A drawn piece whose front the reading could not infer (front_inferred) must be given its front from the plan (the side away from its wall or towards its seating partner) before the room is checked, so the facing and media-wall checks run on a real front.

a living room whose seating faces a wall.rule: A living room whose seating faces a wall with no clear 1.5-4 m TV wall (a window or door breaks every candidate) must be given a TV unit on the nearest clear wall span, or the seating re-oriented to a wall that has one, so the media wall is not left without a place.

a bedroom whose tv wall is blocked by a.rule: A bedroom whose TV wall is blocked by a wardrobe or other tall piece in the sight line must have the blocking piece moved or the TV placed on a clear wall span, so the media wall is not left without a place.

when the plan labels a roof terrace (a r.rule: When the plan labels a roof terrace (a room with a door to it on the top floor) but the section draws the roof closed over it, the roof must be cut open over the terrace footprint (a roof terrace opening) so the terrace is usable and not buried under the roof.

a door on the top floor under a sloped r.rule: A door on the top floor under a sloped roof whose headroom is under 1.60 m (and whose 2.10 m top would cross the roof underside) must be given a dormer or a raised roof at that wall, or the door removed, so it is a usable door.

a ceiling light whose drawn size exceeds.rule: A ceiling light whose drawn size exceeds the library's maximum (0.6 m) is capped at the maximum; this is a normal size correction, not a defect.

a site area whose label names a pool (ha.rule: A site area whose label names a pool (havuz), terrace (güneşlenme alani) or parking (otopark) must be built as the corresponding site element (pool basin, terrace slab, parking slab) at its drawn outline; a labelled site area may not be left as 'NOT built (no outline)'.

a site area whose label names a terrace.rule: A site area whose label names a terrace or sunning area (güneşlenme alani) must be built as a terrace slab at its drawn outline; it may not be left as 'NOT built (no outline)'.

a site area whose label names parking (o.rule: A site area whose label names parking (otopark) must be built as a parking slab at its drawn outline; it may not be left as 'NOT built (no outline)'.

a bathroom's set (shower/bathtub, toilet.rule: A bathroom's set (shower/bathtub, toilet, washbasin, tall cabinet) must be complete; a bathroom missing a member of its set is incomplete.

a hall/entrance room should carry an ent.rule: A hall/entrance room should carry an entrance group (shoe cabinet, console, coat storage); a hall holding only a single shoe cabinet is under-furnished.

a double bed's sleeping set should inclu.rule: A double bed's sleeping set should include a nightstand on each side; a bedroom with a single nightstand is incomplete.

an interior camera that renders a fully.rule: An interior camera that renders a fully black frame has no valid line of sight into the room; it must be re-posed to a free point that shows the room's main fixtures.

a room whose area, furniture set, and la.rule: A room whose area, furniture set, and label match a known program type must be typed to that type, not 'other'.

a site area that is drawn in the documen.rule: A site area that is drawn in the documents and visible in the 3D model must have its outline recorded and built; 'NOT built (no outline)' is a loss when the geometry is present in the model.

a shoe cabinet belongs at the entrance l.rule: A shoe cabinet belongs at the entrance level (L-1 or L0), not in an upper-floor hall; upper-floor halls take a console table or sideboard.

every site area the documents name (pool.rule: Every site area the documents name (pool, sunning terrace, parking) must be built as a real surface with a path from the house; a named site area left as 'no outline' is a loss, not a choice.

every level difference on the site must.rule: Every level difference on the site must be resolved as a landscape section: banks graded no steeper than 1:3 (1:2 max), one terrace level per side, solid-tread flights with cheek walls and a landing, and paths level or stepped only where steeper than 1:12.

every garden step must sit on its riser.rule: Every garden step must sit on its riser and the ground (no loose tread in the grass), and every retaining wall must be finished in stone or render with a coping, never bare concrete.

each outdoor floor must carry the materi.rule: Each outdoor floor must carry the material of its use (terrace/pool deck, steps, garden path, drive) in one language with the house's base material, never one slab everywhere.

every drawn parking area must be built w.rule: Every drawn parking area must be built with its outline and hold well-made, realistic car models; no stray blocks or step pieces on level paving.

every outdoor stair must meet its landin.rule: Every outdoor stair must meet its landings, walls and planters cleanly, with no block or wall cutting into a step and each flight ending on a landing or the ground.

a paved walkway strip at the foot of a g.rule: A paved walkway strip at the foot of a glazed facade must run the full length of that facade from one end to the other; it must never stop halfway and leave grass or lawn up against the glazing.

the pale paved strip at the foot of a gl.rule: The pale paved strip at the foot of a glazed facade must run flat along the whole facade from one terrace or pool deck to the next, with no raised or sunken walled box in front of the glass.

every drive must be road only (no steps.rule: Every drive must be road only (no steps or stone blocks standing in it) and must lead somewhere: on to the plot's edge and a street outside, never ending at the lawn.

every entrance canopy must be a real fra.rule: Every entrance canopy must be a real framed canopy with its fascia, soffit and tie rods or brackets, at one height along its wall, never a bare white slab stuck out of the wall.

the project must sit among fenced neighb.rule: The project must sit among fenced neighbouring plots with roads that come to it from outside, never alone on an empty lawn with its drive leading nowhere.

a tall wet-room fixture (shower, tub) un.rule: A tall wet-room fixture (shower, tub) under a sloped ceiling must be capped or swapped to a model whose height fits the slope at its position; nothing inside may cross the roof (UL128).

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms (e.g. SALON + AÇIK MUTFAK), the reading must split the outline into the separate rooms each label names, instead of keeping one merged room and dropping the other labels.

every room label the documents name on a.rule: Every room label the documents name on a level must map to a distinct room in the model; a label whose area and anchor do not match any built room is a lost room, not a duplicate.

a balcony/terrace must carry its lounge.rule: A balcony/terrace must carry its lounge group (seating + side table); a terrace whose main furniture group is missing is an empty, undefined space.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height; an all-black frame is a failed render, not a view.

a sectional sofa's parts must be joined.rule: A sectional sofa's parts must be joined (within 1 cm); parts standing apart are a build defect, fixed by re-joining, not by swapping the model.

an armchair's back and arms must rest ag.rule: An armchair's back and arms must rest against its seat (within 5 mm); a gap is a build defect, fixed by re-planning the rests, not by swapping the model.

a soft-seat model whose back or arm is n.rule: A soft-seat model whose back or arm is not flush with its seat (gap over 5 mm) must be rebuilt by the rest plan or swapped for a model that is flush; a 5 cm gap between the rest and the seat is a build defect, not a placement one.

scene geometry checks (s1) that fail on.rule: Scene geometry checks (S1) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.

scene geometry checks (s2) that fail on.rule: Scene geometry checks (S2) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.

scene geometry checks (s4) that fail on.rule: Scene geometry checks (S4) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.

scene geometry checks (s6) that fail on.rule: Scene geometry checks (S6) that fail on a level indicate the build stage produced geometry that does not satisfy the scene constraints; rerun the build stage to regenerate the level geometry.

when an armchair is placed behind the ba.rule: When an armchair is placed behind the back of a sofa and faces it, the fit stage must re-orient or re-place it so it faces its seating group; a rotate that lowers plausibility is refused, so the agent must choose a different orientation or position.

when a tv_unit is placed behind the back.rule: When a tv_unit is placed behind the back of a piece and faces it, the fit stage must re-orient or re-place it so it faces its seating group; a rotate that pushes it through the room outline is refused, so the agent must choose a different orientation or position.

a wardrobe that reaches through the room.rule: A wardrobe that reaches through the room outline, even by a small depth, must be re-placed or resized so it stays within the room; the fit stage must keep all pieces inside the room outline.

when a table_coffee overlaps an armchair.rule: When a table_coffee overlaps an armchair, the fit stage must re-place one of them so they do not overlap; if move_piece is refused because the overlap persists or max_tries is reached, the agent must try a different position or swap a model.

an armchair whose front use zone is not.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed so the walkway is clear; the fit stage must ensure every piece's front use zone is reachable.

a sofa_corner whose front use zone is no.rule: A sofa_corner whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed so the walkway is clear; if swap_model is refused because the asset is unusable, the agent must try a different model or re-place the piece.

a seating group whose members cannot all.rule: A seating group whose members cannot all face each other and keep a 0.60 m walkway from the door is re-solved as one unit (relayout) rather than rotated piece by piece, which only trades one orientation error for another.

a piece that crosses a room outline by 0.rule: A piece that crosses a room outline by 0.02 m or less is within tolerance and is not a finding.

when a coffee table overlaps a chair and.rule: When a coffee table overlaps a chair and every single-piece move is refused (max_tries), the seating group is re-solved as a unit so the table and chairs are placed together with clearances.

a piece whose front use zone is not reac.rule: A piece whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is fixed by re-solving the room's seating group, not by moving the single piece, which would break the group it belongs to.

a corner sofa whose front use zone is no.rule: A corner sofa whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is fixed by re-solving the seating group; swapping to a smaller model is refused when the asset is unusable.

a stove whose back is not on a wall is f.rule: A stove whose back is not on a wall is fixed by re-solving the kitchen run as a unit so the counter, stove and sink are placed together against the wall with the required aisle.

a kitchen counter whose front aisle is u.rule: A kitchen counter whose front aisle is under 0.90 m is fixed by re-solving the kitchen run so the counter is placed against the wall with a full aisle.

a sofa whose drawn footprint is 0.90 m w.rule: A sofa whose drawn footprint is 0.90 m wide by 2.13 m deep is a misread orientation: the piece is re-typed or re-placed so its long side is the seat depth, not the width.

a sofa whose back is 0.59 m off a wall a.rule: A sofa whose back is 0.59 m off a wall and cannot be moved to a free wall span within the drawn-lock limit is fixed by re-solving the seating group so the sofa is placed against a wall.

an armchair that does not face its group.rule: An armchair that does not face its group is fixed by re-solving the seating group so all members face each other.

an armchair whose front zone is blocked.rule: An armchair whose front zone is blocked by another armchair is fixed by re-solving the seating group so the two armchairs are placed with clear front zones.

a dining chair with under 0.81 m behind.rule: A dining chair with under 0.81 m behind it is fixed by re-solving the dining group so the chairs have the required clearance to the wall or piece behind.

a seating group whose members are drawn.rule: A seating group whose members are drawn overlapping or with blocked front zones must be re-solved as a unit, not rotated piece by piece.

a dining chair with less than 0.81 m beh.rule: A dining chair with less than 0.81 m behind it must be re-solved with its table, not nudged alone.

a bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a.rule: A bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a side in a room under 17 m2 must take a narrower model, not be shifted.
A bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a side must take a narrower model when the room cannot give the clearance.

a wardrobe with less than 0.80 m in fron.rule: A wardrobe with less than 0.80 m in front must take a shallower model when the room cannot give the opening clearance.

a shower whose drawn size is outside the.rule: A shower whose drawn size is outside the product range must take a real product model that fits the bay.

a bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a.rule: A bed that leaves less than 0.60 m on a side must take a model that fits the room's side clearance.

an armchair that stands behind the back.rule: An armchair that stands behind the back of its group must be re-solved with the group, not rotated alone.

a sofa whose front zone is blocked by an.rule: A sofa whose front zone is blocked by another piece must be re-solved with the group.

a coffee table not in front of the sofa.rule: A coffee table not in front of the sofa must be re-solved with the seating group.

a dining chair with less than 0.81 m beh.rule: A dining chair with less than 0.81 m behind it must be re-solved with its table.

a tv_unit 1 m off a wall must be re-solv.rule: A tv_unit 1 m off a wall must be re-solved with the room's media group.

a seating group is solved as one unit: t.rule: A seating group is solved as one unit: the armchairs are placed facing the group centre (sofa/TV axis), never with their back to a group member; a rotation that only swaps one F4 for another (wall or group) is refused and the whole group is re-solved.

A seating group is solved as one unit: the armchairs are placed facing the group centre (sofa/TV axis), never with their back to a group member; a rotation that only swaps one F4 for another is refused and the whole group is re-solved.

a coffee table is placed between the sof.rule: A coffee table is placed between the sofa and its TV as part of the seating group; a drawn table that is not on that axis is re-solved with the group rather than moved by hand.

a tv unit is placed with its back on a w.rule: A TV unit is placed with its back on a wall and its front facing the seating group; a rotation that trades its off-wall fault for a facing fault is refused and the group is re-solved.

a sofa is placed with its back on a wall.rule: A sofa is placed with its back on a wall; when no free wall span exists within the drawn-lock, the room's AI pieces are re-solved so the sofa lands on a wall span.

an armchair is placed within 2.50 m of a.rule: An armchair is placed within 2.50 m of and facing the coffee table of its group; a drawn armchair that is out of range is re-solved with the group rather than moved by hand.

the free zone in front of a sofa is kept.rule: The free zone in front of a sofa is kept clear of other group members; a blocking piece is re-solved with the group.

a nightstand is placed beside the bed he.rule: A nightstand is placed beside the bed head, clear of the window; when the drawn spot blocks the window and the swap/move options are refused, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.

a wardrobe is placed with ≥ 0.80 m clear.rule: A wardrobe is placed with ≥ 0.80 m clear in front; when the drawn spot leaves only 0.66 m and the swap/move options are refused, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.

a nightstand is placed beside the bed he.rule: A nightstand is placed beside the bed head, clear of the window; when the drawn spot blocks the window and the move/remove/swap options are refused, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.

a dining table is placed clear of the wi.rule: A dining table is placed clear of the window (sill + 0.05 m); when the drawn spot blocks the window, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.

a dining chair is placed clear of the wi.rule: A dining chair is placed clear of the window (sill + 0.05 m); when the drawn spot blocks the window, the room's AI pieces are re-solved.

a room's type is set from its furniture.rule: A room's type is set from its furniture set; when the set mixes living and dining pieces, the room is typed living and the dining group is placed as a sub-group, not by retyping the room.

a tv unit is placed with its back on a w.rule: A TV unit is placed with its back on a wall; when the drawn spot is 1.01 m off the wall and the relayout candidates keep the fault, the room's AI pieces are re-solved with a different candidate.

the inspector's render-quality finding m.rule: The inspector's render-quality finding must name the piece's actual type and module; a parametric kitchen cabinet (kitchen_run) is not a 'shoe cabinet' and its flat parametric look is expected, not a wrong_model defect.

the agent stage must not drop decor piec.rule: The agent stage must not drop decor pieces (potted_plant, armchair, side_table) that the decor stage placed; every decor-stage piece must survive into the agent stage or be explicitly removed with a reason.

a planned kitchen piece (stove, sink_kit.rule: A planned kitchen piece (stove, sink_kitchen) that is part of a kitchen_run must be built as a distinct object in the scene; the build stage must not silently drop run members that have a planned model.

when two drawn pieces of the same type o.rule: When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 30% and the smaller is fully inside the larger, the reading stage must treat them as one piece (the larger) and mark the smaller as a duplicate, not as a separate piece to be built.

a drawn piece in a kitchen that no rule.rule: A drawn piece in a kitchen that no rule or model can type must be assigned a type from its size, room and neighbours (or explicitly marked not furniture) at the reading stage, so it is either built or explained; it must never be left as 'unknown' with no warning, review entry or symbol.

every source layer that holds entities t.rule: Every source layer that holds entities the model does not use must be named in a warning or review entry with the reason it was not used, so a lost stair or other element is visible to the auditor.
Every source layer that holds entities the model does not use must be named in a warning or review entry with the reason it was not used, so a lost element is visible to the auditor.

a toilet in a bathroom must be placed so.rule: A toilet in a bathroom must be placed so its centre is at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; when the drawn position cannot meet this and no library model fits, the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture set rather than leaving the clearance unmet.

a bathtub or shower in a bathroom must h.rule: A bathtub or shower in a bathroom must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; when the drawn position cannot meet this and no library model fits, the reading stage must flag the room as too small for the drawn fixture set rather than leaving the clearance unmet.

a drawn bathtub longer than its bay is a.rule: A drawn bathtub longer than its bay is a misread size: resize it to the bay and the code re-centres it for its front clearance.

a drawn shower longer than its bay is a.rule: A drawn shower longer than its bay is a misread size: resize it to the bay and the code re-centres it for its front clearance.

a toilet whose side clearance fails is a.rule: A toilet whose side clearance fails is a misread size: resize it to a real product width and the code re-centres it for the 0.38 m side clearance.

an interior view of a wet room must show.rule: An interior view of a wet room must show every fixture of the room's set, not just the anchor.

an interior view of a bedroom must show.rule: An interior view of a bedroom must show the bed and its nightstands, the room's anchor set.

an interior view of a balcony must show.rule: An interior view of a balcony must show its furniture, not a bare slab.
An interior view of a balcony must show its seating area, not a bare slab.

a kitchen run is completed with its miss.rule: A kitchen run is completed with its missing members (fridge, sink, stove) around its drawn anchor.

an interior render of a room must frame.rule: An interior render of a room must frame the room's anchor piece (the bed in a bedroom, the fixtures in a bathroom) so the main element is visible, not cut out of the frame.

a bathroom render must show its primary.rule: A bathroom render must show its primary fixtures (basin, toilet, bath/shower); a view that omits them is not a valid view of the room.
A bathroom render must show its primary fixtures; a view that omits the toilet is not client-ready.

a bathroom view must show the basin; omi.rule: A bathroom view must show the basin; omitting it makes the room look unfinished.

a bathroom render must show its main fix.rule: A bathroom render must show its main fixtures; a view that omits the basin, bath and toilet reads as a room without its fixtures.

a bedroom must be furnished with its bed.rule: A bedroom must be furnished with its bed as the anchor, headboard against a wall; a room furnished as a home office instead of a bedroom is a misread of the room's program.

a bathroom render must show its main fix.rule: A bathroom render must show its main fixtures (toilet, shower); a view that omits them is not functional.

a balcony render must show its main furn.rule: A balcony render must show its main furniture group; a view that shows only plants reads as an empty slab.

an opening in the documents must be cut.rule: An opening in the documents must be cut through its wall; an opening that is not cut is a geometry error.

the decor stage's wall-item pass must no.rule: The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (mirror, art, shelf) over a wall fixture (washbasin, mirror) that occupies the same wall extent; it must raise the item over the fixture, move it along the wall, or leave it out.

The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item over a wall fixture (washbasin) that occupies the same wall extent; it must raise the item over the fixture, move it along the wall, or leave it out.
The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (desk wall unit, art) over a window; it must move the item to a free wall span or leave it out.
The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (wall art) over a window; it must move the item to a free wall span or leave it out.
The decor stage's wall-item pass must not place a hung item (desk wall unit) over a window; it must move the item to a free wall span or leave it out.

a wall-hung item (art, shelf, mirror) mu.rule: A wall-hung item (art, shelf, mirror) must not be placed over an opening (window, door) on the same wall; the placement pass must check the opening's horizontal extent and the item's vertical extent and move the item to a free span or omit it.

a wall-mounted item must not overlap an.rule: A wall-mounted item must not overlap an existing wall fixture (washbasin, mirror, towel rail) on the same wall; the placement pass must check for overlaps and move the item to a free span or omit it.

a room with a large outer wall span (e.g.rule: A room with a large outer wall span (e.g., > 3 m) must have at least one window or door on that span to avoid a blank facade; the layout stage must check for blank facade spans and add a window or door if the room's program allows it.

the camera set must include a frontal vi.rule: The camera set must include a frontal view of the entrance facade (+y) to show the main entrance and facade design.

when the terrain slopes up to 1:0.3 (ste.rule: When the terrain slopes up to 1:0.3 (steeper than 1:3), a retaining edge must be built to support the slope; the site stage must check for steep slopes and add a retaining edge if needed.

a stair flight with a run of > 0.72 m mu.rule: A stair flight with a run of > 0.72 m must have a handrail over the entire run; the build stage must check for handrails on stair flights and add them if missing.

a bathroom set must include all function.rule: A bathroom set must include all functional elements (taps, towel rail, etc.) to make it a usable and stylish space; the fit stage must check for missing elements in bathroom sets and add them if needed.
A bathroom set must include all functional elements (mirror, taps, etc.) to make it a usable and stylish space; the fit stage must check for missing elements in bathroom sets and add them if needed.

an interior camera view must show all do.rule: An interior camera view must show all doors in the room to ensure the door is visible and accessible.

a retaining wall supporting a raised gar.rule: A retaining wall supporting a raised garden bed must have a material that matches the surrounding facade to avoid looking unfinished and out of place.

a bathroom's program set (washbasin, mir.rule: A bathroom's program set (washbasin, mirror, towel rail) is incomplete when the washbasin has no mirror above it; the set must be completed, not just re-camered.

a bathroom whose washbasin is not in fra.rule: A bathroom whose washbasin is not in frame and has no mirror over it is an incomplete set; complete the set rather than re-camering a bare wall.

a bathroom render that shows no mirror o.rule: A bathroom render that shows no mirror over the basin and bare flat tile is an incomplete set; the furniture agent must add the missing members (mirror, styled surfaces) before the camera is judged.

a terrace furnished with only two plants.rule: A terrace furnished with only two plants is bare; the terrace program's lounge group must be placed so the outdoor space reads as designed.

a kitchen counter's top must be built at.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be built at its working height (0.90-0.95 m); a model whose top sits above 0.97 m is a wrong model and must be swapped for one at working height.

an interior bathroom camera must show th.rule: An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub with taps, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single isolated object in a bare corner.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single object in a bare corner.
An interior bathroom camera must show the full fixture set (bathtub with taps, washbasin, mirror) rather than a single isolated object.

a drawn piece turned 90 deg from its dra.rule: A drawn piece turned 90 deg from its drawn orientation is a reading error; rotate it back to its drawn front.

an interior/terrace camera must not cut.rule: An interior/terrace camera must not cut off a foreground piece; frame the complete piece and the view.

a side table on a terrace/balcony must b.rule: A side table on a terrace/balcony must be an outdoor-rated model (weather-resistant, scaled for the space); an indoor glass-top table is a wrong model for the zone.

an interior camera must not cut off a fo.rule: An interior camera must not cut off a foreground piece; frame the complete piece and the view.

a retaining or terrace wall that support.rule: A retaining or terrace wall that supports a raised bed or deck must be given a finished cladding (stone, render or timber) that matches the house's facade family, never left as bare concrete.

every door must open into a finished, fu.rule: Every door must open into a finished, furnished room with a floor material consistent with the room it serves; a door that opens onto a bare void with a mismatched floor is a build error to be corrected before render.

every site area drawn in the documents (.rule: Every site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built as a modelled outline with its own material and content; a drawn pool with no built outline is a site-build failure.

every labelled site area (sunning terrac.rule: Every labelled site area (sunning terrace, deck) must be built as a modelled outline with paving; a labelled terrace with no built outline is a site-build failure.

a drawn parking area must be built with.rule: A drawn parking area must be built with its outline and at least one car model per bay; a parking area with no outline and no cars is a site-build failure.

a paved strip along a glazed facade must.rule: A paved strip along a glazed facade must run the full length of the facade; a half-run that stops short and lets grass reach the glass is a site-build error.

in front of a glazed ground-floor facade.rule: In front of a glazed ground-floor facade the site must be a flat paved strip, not a raised walled box; a raised terrace wall where a flat paving is required is a site-build error.

a site plan must connect the house to th.rule: A site plan must connect the house to the outside: the drive or path must run to the plot boundary or a street, and the plot must show its boundary (fence or hedge) and at least one neighbouring plot or road, so the house is not left standing on an open lawn with a drive that leads nowhere.

an entrance canopy must be a finished el.rule: An entrance canopy must be a finished element: it needs a fascia, a soffit and visible support (tie rods or brackets); a bare slab projecting from the wall is not a canopy.

a site plan must show the plot boundary.rule: A site plan must show the plot boundary (fence or hedge) and at least one neighbouring plot or a road reaching the house; a house standing alone on an empty lawn with a drive that leads nowhere is not a finished site.

a drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; the reading must split it into its members (e.g. a long run of cabinets or a dining set) and type each, instead of leaving it as one untyped cluster.
A drawn piece longer than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; the reading must split it into its members and type each, instead of leaving it as one untyped cluster.

a door under a sloped ceiling must have.rule: A door under a sloped ceiling must have at least 1.60 m of headroom at its wall; where the roof slope leaves less, the build must add a dormer or raise the roof at that spot, not lower the door to the roof line.

a shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall.rule: A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the ground/entrance level; in an upper-floor hall the same footprint (a low 0.60 x 0.25 m piece) must be typed as a console_table or sideboard, not a shoe_cabinet.

a balcony/terrace of 15 m2 or more must.rule: A balcony/terrace of 15 m2 or more must be furnished with a full terrace_lounge set (seating group, table, plant), not a single armchair and side_table.

a room whose label names a game/activity.rule: A room whose label names a game/activity/relaxation function (Oyun Aktivite Ve Dinlenme Odasi) and whose furniture is a living set must be typed 'living', not 'other'; 'other' is reserved for rooms with no recognisable program.

a shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall.rule: A shoe_cabinet is only allowed in a hall on the ground/entrance level; in an upper-floor hall the same footprint must be typed as a console_table or sideboard, not a shoe_cabinet.

a daybed/bed-like piece is only acceptab.rule: A daybed/bed-like piece is only acceptable in a bedroom or a room explicitly typed for sleeping; in a living/activity room a bed-like footprint must be typed as a sofa or chaise, not a daybed.

a site area drawn in the documents (pool.rule: A site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built with its outline and tracked in the site-area record even when its geometry is generated by the model; 'NOT built (no outline)' is only valid when the documents do not draw the area.

a bench (or any piece) whose drawn front.rule: A bench (or any piece) whose drawn front is read on its short side is a reading error: the front is the long side; when the long side faces a wall, the piece is placed with its back to that wall and the front faces the room, and the orientation solver must not be asked to rotate it to the short side.

a sofa whose drawn front is read on its.rule: A sofa whose drawn front is read on its short side is a reading error: the front is the long side; when the long side faces the most open floor, the piece is placed with its back to the opposite wall and the front faces the room, and the orientation solver must not be asked to rotate it to the short side.

an interior camera of a wet room must fr.rule: An interior camera of a wet room must frame the room's main fixtures (basin, toilet, shower/bath) from a free standing point with headroom, never a corner or a single fixture's edge.

a corridor camera must show the doors an.rule: A corridor camera must show the doors and the space as a whole from a free point, not a wall section and a single cabinet.

a kitchen's styled surfaces must include.rule: A kitchen's styled surfaces must include small worktop items and the upper cabinets/hood in frame; a bare worktop with only a fruit bowl is not a finished kitchen.

a kitchen run is not complete without it.rule: A kitchen run is not complete without its upper cabinets/hood and a styled worktop; the upper wall must not be left as an empty void.

a room's seating group (sofa, armchairs).rule: A room's seating group (sofa, armchairs) must be one coordinated set in style and colour, not three mismatched lines.

a living seating group must be anchored.rule: A living seating group must be anchored by a large area rug under it; a bare floor under the sofa and coffee table is not a finished living room.

the view through a living room's glazing.rule: The view through a living room's glazing onto an outdoor terrace must show a furnished, designed terrace, not a flat empty lawn.

coffee and side tables in a living room.rule: Coffee and side tables in a living room must carry styled objects (books, vases, small decor) so the surfaces read as lived-in, not bare.

a living/dining room needs a feature wal.rule: A living/dining room needs a feature wall (slatted wood or paneling) to add depth; flat untextured concrete/paint is too raw for a stylish look.

a room's furniture must share a cohesive.rule: A room's furniture must share a cohesive wood-tone palette; a dark walnut table clashing with light oak and mid-tone pieces is a mismatched set.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (bathtub, toilet, basin) from a free point, not a door frame and vanity corner.

a bathroom camera must show the room's m.rule: A bathroom camera must show the room's main group (basin, toilet, cabinet) from a free point, not a corner and the edge of the bathtub.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet, basin) from a free point, not a vanity corner.

an interior camera must not be positione.rule: An interior camera must not be positioned directly in front of a door leaf that fills the frame and obscures the room.

a bedroom window must have full-height t.rule: A bedroom window must have full-height two-layer curtains (sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track; a bare window is not a finished bedroom.

a bedroom needs a feature wall (fluted o.rule: A bedroom needs a feature wall (fluted or slatted wood panelling) behind the bed to anchor it; flat untextured paint is not a finished bedroom.

every entrance hall and corridor must in.rule: Every entrance hall and corridor must include a warm accent light (pendant or sconce) in its lighting set, not only the general ceiling light, so renders show layered warm light.

a wardrobe model whose mirrored door ref.rule: A wardrobe model whose mirrored door reflects a furnished room that does not exist in the scene must not be used; wardrobe models must have plain or non-reflective doors (or a reflection that matches the room).

every exterior window in a living or bed.rule: Every exterior window in a living or bedroom space must carry a curtain or sheer on a track in the render set, so daylight and the view are framed and the wall does not read as flat paint.

every living or dining group must sit on.rule: Every living or dining group must sit on a rug sized to anchor the seating/dining cluster, so the floor does not read as bare and unfinished.

a drawn outdoor living area (sun terrace.rule: A drawn outdoor living area (sun terrace, pool deck) is built as a furnished outdoor room (seating, planters, paving) from its outline; a site render must show the outdoor space as designed, not a bare yard.

the main entrance door is rendered as a.rule: The main entrance door is rendered as a distinct, styled entrance (leaf, frame, canopy or accent) so the facade's entrance point is clearly readable in an exterior render.

a drawn pool and its deck are built as a.rule: A drawn pool and its deck are built as a cohesive outdoor room (seating, dining or fire pit, planters), not a pool with random loungers.

a bedroom floor specified as herringbone.rule: A bedroom floor specified as herringbone in the reference is rendered with a herringbone wood look, not a plain plank.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixture group (washbasin, toilet, cabinet) so the room reads as a designed space, not a tight crop of one corner.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet) so the layout and design are visible, not a close-up of the vanity and door.

a feature wall behind seating in a livin.rule: A feature wall behind seating in a living room is rendered with a paneled or slatted finish, not a single flat paint colour.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixture group so the room reads as a whole, not a close-up of a corner.

an interior hall camera must frame the h.rule: An interior hall camera must frame the hall's furniture and depth so the space reads as a designed entry, not a close-up of a corner and door frame.

seating pieces in a living room group mu.rule: Seating pieces in a living room group must share a coherent style and colour family; a brown leather armchair is swapped for a minimal/modern armchair that matches the white sofa and black lounge chair.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixture group (bathtub, toilet, cabinet) so the room reads as a whole, not a close-up of a blank wall and toilet roll.
An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (shower, toilet) so the layout is visible, not a close-up that fails to show the room.

an interior hall camera must frame the h.rule: An interior hall camera must frame the hall's furniture and depth so the space reads as a styled entry, not a tight, low-angle shot of a corner and door.
An interior hall camera must frame the hall's furniture and depth so the space reads as a styled corridor, not a bare, unfinished corridor.

the site environment (lawn, planting, pa.rule: The site environment (lawn, planting, paving) is rendered as a designed landscape with texture and planting, not a bare, untextured surface.

a terrace floor is rendered with a desig.rule: A terrace floor is rendered with a designed outdoor floor material (paving stone, decking, or similar), not a bare, untextured grey slab.

the site stage must build the drawn land.rule: The site stage must build the drawn landscape (pools, platforms, trees, parking and sunning areas) with textured ground, planting and hardscape, not a flat untextured plane, so exterior and terrace renders read as a finished environment.

a seating group (armchairs plus side tab.rule: A seating group (armchairs plus side table) must use models from the same design family so the set reads as designed, not as mismatched pieces.

a shoe cabinet in a hall must be a close.rule: A shoe cabinet in a hall must be a closed, finished cabinet (doors, styling) that matches a designed hall, not a bare open-cubby parametric placeholder.

a living room seating group must use mod.rule: A living room seating group must use models from the same design family (matching wood tones and style) so the room does not mix three different design languages.

a kitchen render must show a believable.rule: A kitchen render must show a believable appliance (handles, panels) and styled surfaces; a featureless box or empty counter fails the client test.

a fridge model must have visible handles.rule: A fridge model must have visible handles and panels to read as a real appliance, not a featureless box.

a kitchen render must not show broken or.rule: A kitchen render must not show broken or misplaced appliances; the fridge must be on the floor, not the counter.

a living room render must have a cohesiv.rule: A living room render must have a cohesive color palette; a single clashing accent (like a neon rug) fails the client test.

a dining set must mix bench and upholste.rule: A dining set must mix bench and upholstered/wood chairs, not repeated identical plastic chairs.

a living room render must have a cohesiv.rule: A living room render must have a cohesive color palette; a single clashing accent (like a hot-pink rug) fails the client test.

a bedroom render must have layered styli.rule: A bedroom render must have layered styling (rug, curtains, art, lamps) and a neutral wall color; a loud green wall and bare surfaces fail the client test.

a shoe cabinet must be a believable piec.rule: A shoe cabinet must be a believable piece of furniture, not a crude low-poly metal frame.

a window in a styled room must have laye.rule: A window in a styled room must have layered curtains (sheer + drape), not a single flat drape.

a bedroom render must show the bed and n.rule: A bedroom render must show the bed and nightstand as anchors; a room without them reads as an office.

a nightstand must be styled with lamps,.rule: A nightstand must be styled with lamps, books, or decorative objects to make the room feel lived-in.

an armchair in a neutral palette must no.rule: An armchair in a neutral palette must not be a loud accent (like orange) that clashes with the rest of the set.

a window view must show a believable out.rule: A window view must show a believable outdoor scene, not a flat grey void with lollipop trees.

two armchairs in a seating group must be.rule: Two armchairs in a seating group must be the same model and cushion color to read as a designed set.

a side table must be a believable piece.rule: A side table must be a believable piece of furniture, not a toy-like disc with random pegs.

a flush ceiling light must be at least 2.rule: A flush ceiling light must be at least 2.5 m from a pendant light to avoid reading as two lights together.

a fixture under a sloped ceiling is capp.rule: A fixture under a sloped ceiling is capped at the slope height at its footprint; the cap is independent of the drawn size check, so a size refusal must not block the height fix.

when one room outline carries the labels.rule: When one room outline carries the labels of two or more rooms, the reading must split it at the missing wall before room assignment; a label with no matching room outline is a lost-room signal, not a duplicate.

a balcony or terrace with drawn furnitur.rule: A balcony or terrace with drawn furniture must have that furniture built and visible; an empty outdoor room is a fit failure, not a camera failure.

a stair opening in a hall or landing tha.rule: A stair opening in a hall or landing that drops to a lower level must be built with a guardrail or barrier along its open edge; the guard is part of the stair's set, not an optional detail.

a fixture under a sloped ceiling must be.rule: A fixture under a sloped ceiling must be a model whose height fits the headroom at its position; the shower's height is checked against the roof, not just its drawn footprint.

an interior camera must be posed at a fr.rule: An interior camera must be posed at a free point with headroom that shows the room's main group; a black frame means the pose is inside geometry and must be re-picked.

a soft seat's facing bodies must be join.rule: A soft seat's facing bodies must be joined so no part stands more than 1 cm apart; the build stage's join step is responsible for this.

a soft seat's back, back cushion and arm.rule: A soft seat's back, back cushion and arms must rest against its seat with no gap over 5 mm; the build stage's rest plan is responsible for this.

scene geometry checks (s1) must pass for.rule: Scene geometry checks (S1) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.

scene geometry checks (s2) must pass for.rule: Scene geometry checks (S2) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.

scene geometry checks (s4) must pass for.rule: Scene geometry checks (S4) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.

scene geometry checks (s6) must pass for.rule: Scene geometry checks (S6) must pass for every level; a failure count means the build left geometry inconsistent and must be rerun.

a scene check that fails on a level must.rule: A scene check that fails on a level must be re-run after the level's pieces are corrected; the build stage owns the scene assembly.

when an armchair's orientation is refuse.rule: When an armchair's orientation is refused because rotating it breaks its group facing, the whole seating group must be re-solved so the armchair faces the group and the coffee table.

a tv_unit that stands behind the back of.rule: A tv_unit that stands behind the back of a seat and cannot be rotated without leaving the room outline must be re-placed by the room solver so its back is on a wall and it faces the seating.

a wardrobe that pokes through the room o.rule: A wardrobe that pokes through the room outline by a few centimetres should be swapped for a model whose depth fits the wall bay.

when a coffee table overlaps an armchair.rule: When a coffee table overlaps an armchair and every single move is refused, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit so the table clears the chairs.

an armchair whose front use zone is not.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the room solver so the walkway is clear.

a sofa_corner whose front use zone is no.rule: A sofa_corner whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door must be re-placed by the room solver so the walkway is clear.

when an armchair's orientation is refuse.rule: When an armchair's orientation is refused because rotating it breaks its group facing or faces a wall, the whole seating group must be re-solved.

a tv_unit that stands behind the back of.rule: A tv_unit that stands behind the back of a seat and cannot be rotated (back off wall) or swapped (fit rules) must be re-placed by the room solver against a wall facing the seating.

when a coffee table overlaps an armchair.rule: When a coffee table overlaps an armchair and every single move is refused, the seating group must be re-solved as a unit.

a stove whose back is a few centimetres.rule: A stove whose back is a few centimetres off the wall is a misread centre; the code should snap it to the nearest valid wall spot.

a kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in.rule: A kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in front of the counter must be re-solved by the room solver so the run is placed to give the required aisle.

a wardrobe (or any storage with a door o.rule: A wardrobe (or any storage with a door or drawer front) placed against a wall must keep at least 0.80 m of clear floor in front of its opening face; the solver must reject any wall span shorter than the piece plus that clearance and, when no span fits, flag the room for a smaller or different storage piece rather than placing it with a blocked front.

a seating group's front clearance must b.rule: A seating group's front clearance must be kept free of other pieces; the solver must not place a piece inside the front use zone of a sofa or armchair.

a nightstand must not stand in front of.rule: A nightstand must not stand in front of a window sill; it belongs at the head of the bed on the free side.

a dining table must not stand in front o.rule: A dining table must not stand in front of a window sill; it belongs away from the glazing.

a chair must not stand in front of a win.rule: A chair must not stand in front of a window sill; it belongs at the table, away from the glazing.

an armchair must face the seating group,.rule: An armchair must face the seating group, not stand behind the back of another piece.

a tv_unit must have its back on a wall;.rule: A tv_unit must have its back on a wall; it must not float in the middle of the room.

a sofa's long side is its front; it must.rule: A sofa's long side is its front; it must not be turned 90° against its product size.

an armchair's front clearance must be ke.rule: An armchair's front clearance must be kept free of other pieces.

a piece placed by the decor stage must s.rule: A piece placed by the decor stage must survive the agent stage; if the agent drops it, it must be re-added.

the agent stage must not drop a placed d.rule: The agent stage must not drop a placed decor piece without recording it; a piece present after the decor stage and absent after the agent stage is a loss to be restored, not silently removed.

a stove that is a member of a kitchen ru.rule: A stove that is a member of a kitchen run (module:kitchen_counter:kitchen_run) must be built as part of that run's model, not as a standalone object; the build stage must emit the run's full model (counter, sink, stove) so every planned member has a scene object.

a sink_kitchen that is a member of a kit.rule: A sink_kitchen that is a member of a kitchen run (module:kitchen_counter:kitchen_run) must be built as part of that run's model, not as a standalone object; the build stage must emit the run's full model (counter, sink, stove) so every planned member has a scene object.

when two drawn pieces of the same type o.rule: When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 30% and one is clearly inside the other, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the same object, not a second piece; the larger is kept and the smaller is dropped as a detail.

When two drawn pieces of the same type overlap by more than 15% and one is clearly inside the other, the smaller is a duplicate drawing of the same object, not a second piece; the larger is kept and the smaller is dropped as a detail.

a small piece drawn 80% or more inside a.rule: A small piece drawn 80% or more inside a larger seating piece (armchair, sofa) is its seat cushion or built-in element, not a separate piece; it is dropped as a detail of the larger piece.

a room whose program is a stair core (st.rule: A room whose program is a stair core (stair fills the room, no free floor point) is not given an interior camera; it is shown by the adjacent hall's view instead, and the camera stage must skip it rather than report it as a lost view.

a drawn block in a kitchen whose size ma.rule: A drawn block in a kitchen whose size matches a small appliance (roughly 0.2-0.6 m) that the furniture vocabulary does not type must be recorded with an explicit 'appliance, not modelled' note (or a dedicated appliance type) so it is neither silently dropped nor left unexplained.

a layer whose name is a stair section or.rule: A layer whose name is a stair section or elevation view (A-MERDIVEN, A-merdiven görünüş) is a detail view, not plan furniture: the reading classifies it as a detail view and feeds it to the stair reader, and the ledger does not flag it as lost when the stair it documents is built.

a layer whose name is a decorative or sa.rule: A layer whose name is a decorative or sanitary fixture detail view (Deko_Vitrifiye, Piu_Vitrifiye) is a detail view, not plan furniture: the reading classifies it as a detail view and the ledger does not flag it as lost.

a stove drawn with a small gap behind it.rule: A stove drawn with a small gap behind it (its back parallel to the wall) belongs on the wall: the reading snaps its back onto the wall instead of leaving a visible gap.

a shower drawn with a small gap behind i.rule: A shower drawn with a small gap behind it (its back parallel to the wall) belongs on the wall: the reading snaps its back onto the wall instead of leaving a visible gap.

a toilet whose centre is closer than 0.3.rule: A toilet whose centre is closer than 0.38 m to a side wall or fixture is misread: the reading moves it to the nearest valid spot that gives the required side clearance.

a shower with less than 0.53 m clear in.rule: A shower with less than 0.53 m clear in front is misread: the reading moves it to the nearest valid spot that gives the required front clearance.

a toilet is placed so its centre is at l.rule: A toilet is placed so its centre is at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; if the drawn position cannot meet this, the fixture is moved to the nearest valid spot rather than swapped for a model that still fails the clearance.

a bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clea.rule: A bathtub must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; if the drawn position cannot meet this, the fixture is moved to the nearest valid spot.

a shower must have at least 0.53 m clear.rule: A shower must have at least 0.53 m clear in front; if the drawn position cannot meet this, the fixture is moved to the nearest valid spot.

an interior camera of a bathroom must sh.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, shower/bathtub) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.

a bedroom must show its bed as the ancho.rule: A bedroom must show its bed as the anchor; if the bed cannot be placed with the required clearances (0.60 m along the sides, headboard on a wall), the room is re-laid out so the bed fits.

an interior camera of a bathroom must sh.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (toilet, shower) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.

an interior camera of a balcony/terrace.rule: An interior camera of a balcony/terrace must show the room's main furniture (seating, side table) so the render reads as a designed outdoor living space.

an interior camera of a bathroom must sh.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (toilet, washbasin, shower) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.

an interior camera of a bedroom must sho.rule: An interior camera of a bedroom must show the bed as the anchor so the render reads as a bedroom.

an interior camera of a bathroom must sh.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must show the room's main fixtures (toilet, bathtub, washbasin) so the render reads as a functional bathroom.

an interior camera of a wet room must fr.rule: An interior camera of a wet room must frame its fixtures (basin, toilet, shower/bath); a view that omits the basin makes the room read as unfinished.

a kitchen's run must be completed with i.rule: A kitchen's run must be completed with its missing members (fridge, sink, stove, counter); a run without a fridge is not a kitchen.

a bedroom must be furnished as a bedroom.rule: A bedroom must be furnished as a bedroom (bed, nightstands, wardrobe); a desk-and-chair layout without a visible bed is a misread of the room's program.

an exterior render must show a real grou.rule: An exterior render must show a real ground plane and site context (trees, hedge, court); a flat grey gradient reads as a placeholder.

every opening must be cut through its wa.rule: Every opening must be cut through its wall; an opening whose ray hits the wall is not built.

a wall-mounted decor item must not overl.rule: A wall-mounted decor item must not overlap a wall fixture (basin, mirror, cabinet) on the same wall; the wall-item pass must raise it, move it along the wall, or drop it.

a wall-mounted decor item must not hang.rule: A wall-mounted decor item must not hang over a window opening; the wall-item pass must move it to a free wall span or drop it.

a hung decor item must never be placed o.rule: A hung decor item must never be placed on the wall span occupied by a washbasin or its mirror; the resolve pass must skip that span and use the next free wall, or omit the item if no free span exists.

any outer wall span of a habitable room.rule: Any outer wall span of a habitable room longer than 3 m must contain at least one window or door; the layout stage must add an opening if the drawing does not provide one.

every project must include at least one.rule: Every project must include at least one frontal exterior camera view of the main entrance facade.

if the terrain slope is steeper than 1:3.rule: If the terrain slope is steeper than 1:3, the build stage must include a retaining edge or stepped foundation to support the structure.

outdoor terrace furniture must use model.rule: Outdoor terrace furniture must use models rated for outdoor use (weather-resistant materials).

indoor lighting fixtures (floor lamps) m.rule: Indoor lighting fixtures (floor lamps) must not be placed on outdoor terraces; use outdoor-rated lighting instead.

indoor storage furniture (bookshelves) m.rule: Indoor storage furniture (bookshelves) must not be placed on outdoor terraces.

the inspector must read the room id of t.rule: The inspector must read the room id of the target piece from the facts before judging its placement; a piece in an indoor living room is not on the terrace.

every exterior door must be rendered wit.rule: Every exterior door must be rendered with a modelled leaf and frame that match the window frames' material, and the space beyond an exterior door must be lit and textured (not a dark void) in the render.

every door leaf and frame must be assign.rule: Every door leaf and frame must be assigned a material that matches the project's window frame material (e.g. light wood) so that doors do not read as placeholder slabs.

a bathroom shower or bathtub model must.rule: A bathroom shower or bathtub model must include visible taps, a drain, and at least one accessory (towel rail or shelf) in its render; if the library model lacks these, the building stage must add them as separate fixtures or choose a model that includes them.

every washbasin in a bathroom must be re.rule: Every washbasin in a bathroom must be rendered with a mirror above it; if the library model does not include a mirror, the building stage must place a mirror as a separate fixture above the basin.

every interior camera view of a room mus.rule: Every interior camera view of a room must show at least one door or window of that room, so the viewer can orient themselves.

every exterior camera view must be posit.rule: Every exterior camera view must be positioned outside the building envelope, at a distance of at least 1.5 m from the nearest facade, at eye height (1.6 m) or an aerial height, and must not be under the roof overhang.

every exterior wall, including retaining.rule: Every exterior wall, including retaining walls, must be assigned a material that matches the building's facade material so that no bare concrete slabs are visible.

every bathroom must have a complete bath.rule: Every bathroom must have a complete bathroom_set including a mirror above the washbasin and a towel rail; if the set is incomplete, the building stage must add the missing members.

the inspector must verify that the bathr.rule: The inspector must verify that the bathroom_set members are actually missing before flagging a missing_member finding; if the set is complete, the finding is a false alarm.

every interior camera view of a bathroom.rule: Every interior camera view of a bathroom must show the main fixtures (washbasin, toilet, shower/bathtub) so the room reads as designed.

every bathroom must have a mirror above.rule: Every bathroom must have a mirror above the washbasin and at least one styled surface (accent wall, shelf, or accessory); if the library models do not include these, the building stage must add them as separate fixtures.

every outdoor scene must include texture.rule: Every outdoor scene must include textured ground (grass, paving, or gravel), at least 3 trees or shrubs with visible foliage, and a horizon that is not a hard line; the render stage must use high-quality ground and vegetation assets.

every outdoor furniture piece must use a.rule: Every outdoor furniture piece must use a model that matches the project's style (e.g. scandinavian, modern) and has visible texture or design detail; plain generic models are not acceptable for outdoor scenes.

every terrace or balcony must have a com.rule: Every terrace or balcony must have a complete terrace_lounge group (at least 2 seating pieces, 1 table, and 2 plants) so it reads as a designed outdoor space.

a kitchen counter (kitchen_counter) is b.rule: A kitchen counter (kitchen_counter) is built at its standard working height (top at 0.90-0.95 m) regardless of the drawn footprint's height; a drawn counter taller than its working height is a misread of a tall unit or a wall cabinet, not a counter, and must be retyped or resized, never built as a counter at the drawn height.

a site area labelled as a pool (havuz) i.rule: A site area labelled as a pool (havuz) in the documents must be built as a pool outline in the model; if the site holds multiple pools, each documented pool area is built with its own outline and water surface, not left as an unbuilt label.

a site area labelled as a sunning terrac.rule: A site area labelled as a sunning terrace (guneslenme alani) in the documents must be built as a paved terrace outline in the model, not left as an unbuilt label.

a site area labelled as a parking area (.rule: A site area labelled as a parking area (otopark) in the documents must be built as a paved parking outline in the model, and at least one car model must be placed on it to show it is a parking area, not left as an unbuilt label with no cars.

every interior door leaf is rendered ope.rule: Every interior door leaf is rendered open against its swing side by default; only entrance and terrace doors are closed.

a bathroom render must frame the vanity,.rule: A bathroom render must frame the vanity, mirror, shower and towel storage, not a bare wall above the tub.

a hall render must show the furnished ro.rule: A hall render must show the furnished room beyond, not be dominated by closed door slabs.

a living room must carry its full seatin.rule: A living room must carry its full seating group (sculptural armchairs, round coffee table, lit TV console), not a plain sofa set.

a paved strip at the foot of a long glaz.rule: A paved strip at the foot of a long glazed facade must run the full length of the facade, not stop short at one end.

the facade scheme is white render over a.rule: The facade scheme is white render over a stone base, not stone from base to eaves.

in front of a glazed ground-floor facade.rule: In front of a glazed ground-floor facade the site must be a flat pale paved strip, not a raised walled terrace box.

a paved drive or stair path must lead on.rule: A paved drive or stair path must lead on to the plot edge or a street, not end at the lawn.

an entrance canopy must carry a fascia,.rule: An entrance canopy must carry a fascia, soffit and tie rods or brackets, not be a bare slab stuck out of the wall.

a house on a plot must show fenced neigh.rule: A house on a plot must show fenced neighbouring plots and a road coming to it; the drive must lead somewhere.

a drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side is a.rule: A drawn piece over 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single furniture item; it must be split into its members and typed individually, not left untyped.

a door under a sloped ceiling needs at l.rule: A door under a sloped ceiling needs at least 1.60 m of headroom; where the roof slope leaves less, a dormer or raised roof must be added at that spot.

a door under a sloped ceiling whose head.rule: A door under a sloped ceiling whose headroom is under 1.60 m at its wall and within 0.5 m along it must be flagged for a dormer or raised roof; the building stage must not lower the door to the roof line and leave it unusable.

when a bedroom's drawn bed leaves less t.rule: When a bedroom's drawn bed leaves less than the nightstand depth (0.60 m) on one side, the sleeping set is complete with a single nightstand on the free side; do not flag the missing second nightstand as a defect.

a large living room (>= 40 m2) may carry.rule: A large living room (>= 40 m2) may carry a wardrobe as living_storage; do not flag a wardrobe in a living room of that size as a wrong-type placement.

a wet fixture is typed from the drawn fi.rule: A wet fixture is typed from the drawn fixture in its own room, not from the size table of a piece in another room; when the plan shows a shower, the wet fixture is a shower even if a size match elsewhere suggests a tub.

an interior bathroom camera must frame t.rule: An interior bathroom camera must frame the room's full fixture set (WC, basin, storage, bath/shower) from a corner with headroom, never a single fixture in isolation.

a bathroom whose documents draw a tub bl.rule: A bathroom whose documents draw a tub block (parent-bath set) must be built with a bathtub, not a shower, even when the room is small.

a shoe_cabinet belongs at an entrance ha.rule: A shoe_cabinet belongs at an entrance hall, not at a top-floor landing; a landing hall takes a console or storage instead.

a balcony/terrace larger than about 12 m.rule: A balcony/terrace larger than about 12 m2 must be furnished as a seating set (at least two seats plus a table), never a single chair.

a wc flush plate must render as a slim r.rule: A WC flush plate must render as a slim rounded dual-flush plate with a small and a large button, never as a frame holding two flat panes.

an accent wall finish (e.g. vertical sla.rule: An accent wall finish (e.g. vertical slats) is applied to at most one wall of a room, never to all walls of a room or to every room.

an interior camera must frame at least o.rule: An interior camera must frame at least one fixture or piece of value, never a bare wall, corner or switch.

a facade scheme with a stone base and a.rule: A facade scheme with a stone base and a render body must keep the stone to the base/plinth and apply the render (e.g. white) to the upper walls, never stone from base to eaves.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's built fixtures; a black/empty view is a camera failure, not a missing room.

a site area drawn in the documents (pool.rule: A site area drawn in the documents (pool, terrace, parking) must be built with an outline and tracked as a site area, even when its geometry is already present in the model.

the sheets stage must resolve every shee.rule: The sheets stage must resolve every sheet question before ending; a run that ends 'pending' with open questions has not finished its reading.

a sofa's front is its long side facing t.rule: A sofa's front is its long side facing the most open room; a front read on its short side (an AI front) is a reading error and must be corrected to the long side.

a drawn piece whose size and wall positi.rule: A drawn piece whose size and wall position match a console table (long, narrow, back on a wall) must be typed console_table, not bench, so its front faces the room and its back rests on the wall.

the big loop must run additional cycles.rule: The big loop must run additional cycles when the first cycle yields no gain, to allow the agent to resolve remaining orientation and placement conflicts.

a sofa drawn with its long side against.rule: A sofa drawn with its long side against a wall must have its front facing into the room (away from the wall), not along the long side.

a sofa without a front must have its fro.rule: A sofa without a front must have its front set to face the most open floor, towards its partner.

an armchair without a front must have it.rule: An armchair without a front must have its front set to face away from its wall or towards its partner.

an interior camera must be placed at a f.rule: An interior camera must be placed at a free point clear of walls and tall proxies, showing the required elements.

a table_coffee built below the library l.rule: A table_coffee built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.

a tv_unit built below the library level.rule: A tv_unit built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.

a tall_cabinet built below the library l.rule: A tall_cabinet built below the library level must be swapped to a library model that fits the piece's dimensions and room.

when no library model passes the fit rul.rule: When no library model passes the fit rules for a piece, the fitter must not silently keep the parametric mesh as if it were a library pick; it must either relax the height/cap tolerance to accept the nearest library model or flag the piece as unbuildable, never report a library-level build from a parametric fallback.
