when a tall piece is placed under a slop.rule: When a tall piece is placed under a sloped ceiling and its height exceeds the local ceiling clearance, the fitter must either lower the piece to a location with sufficient headroom, swap to a model within the clearance, or flag the placement as infeasible; it must not keep a parametric mesh that violates the ceiling.

a camera of a stair room must be posed f.rule: A camera of a stair room must be posed from the landing or the hall side so the flight is visible, never from a point inside the stair core.

views flagged for review are a queue, no.rule: Views flagged for review are a queue, not a defect; each is resolved by the specific camera or door finding that names it.

every inside door is built open by defau.rule: Every inside door is built open by default (leaf out of the wall) unless a camera or privacy rule closes it; the build records a leaf state for each door it places.

when a camera looks through an inside do.rule: When a camera looks through an inside door into a room worth showing, the build opens that door (leaf out of the view) and records the state.

a nightstand is placed on the free side.rule: A nightstand is placed on the free side of the bed head, not in front of a window; when the bed head is against a window wall the nightstand goes on the opposite side or the window is treated as the head wall.

a toilet is built with its base at floor.rule: A toilet is built with its base at floor level (lowest point within -0.005..+0.01 m of the room floor); a model whose base sits above the floor is rejected at fit, not swapped in.

a bathroom washbasin is always built wit.rule: A bathroom washbasin is always built with a mirror above it as part of the vanity set; the bathroom set is incomplete without the mirror.

a tv_unit is placed with its back on a w.rule: A tv_unit is placed with its back on a wall; when the only free wall span is blocked by doors or windows, the unit is placed on the next free span or the room is flagged, never left floating.

a coffee table is placed in the seating.rule: A coffee table is placed in the seating group with a clear gap to every armchair; when the group is too tight, the armchair is re-posed, not the table pushed into it.

a wardrobe is placed with at least 0.80.rule: A wardrobe is placed with at least 0.80 m clear in front; when the room cannot give that, the wardrobe is moved to a wall with more clearance or the room is flagged, never left short.

a drawn armchair in a seating group is r.rule: A drawn armchair in a seating group is re-posed (rotated) to face the group and clear its front zone before it is moved; a move beyond the drawn lock is refused, so rotation is the first fix.

a small decor item placed on a support m.rule: a small decor item placed on a support must have at least 80% of its footprint over that support, else it is re-seated or removed

every pair of doors in a room must keep.rule: every pair of doors in a room must keep a 0.60 m clear walkway between their swings

a bed must not block a door swing; the h.rule: a bed must not block a door swing; the headboard may stand against a wall but the foot must clear the door

a wardrobe must not block a window or do.rule: a wardrobe must not block a window or door; it must sit on a free wall span

a door whose head is above the top floor.rule: a door whose head is above the top floor's ceiling with no landing, stair or balcony to reach it is a reading error: it is a window or a door to an unread space

the architect's rule c1 must require a 0.rule: the architect's rule C1 must require a 0.60 m clear walkway between every pair of doors (and door-to-window) in a room

the architect's rule f2 / f3 must requir.rule: the architect's rule F2 / F3 must require that no piece blocks a door or a window swing

the architect's rule e1 must require tha.rule: the architect's rule E1 must require that every door is reachable: its head is at or below the top floor's ceiling, or there is a stair, landing or balcony to reach it

an interior camera must show the room's.rule: an interior camera must show the room's main group, not a bare wall or the edge of a piece

every piece must be seated on its suppor.rule: every piece must be seated on its support or the floor; a piece with 0% of its footprint over its support is detached

a soft seat's back and arms must rest ag.rule: a soft seat's back and arms must rest against its seat; a model whose rests are apart from the seat is swapped

every piece must be inside its room and.rule: every piece must be inside its room and clear of walls and openings

scene checks s1/s2/s4/s6 that fail on a.rule: Scene checks S1/S2/S4/S6 that fail on a level are geometry defects of the built level (a wall, opening or piece out of its drawn place); the build stage is re-run so the level is rebuilt from the drawing and the checks re-run on the new geometry.

a sofa whose back is off its wall and wh.rule: A sofa whose back is off its wall and whose group (coffee table, armchairs) is misaligned is a seating-group placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the whole seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than nudging the sofa alone.

a coffee table not in front of the sofa.rule: A coffee table not in front of the sofa is a seating-group placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than moving the table alone.

an armchair more than 30° off the sofa i.rule: An armchair more than 30° off the sofa it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than rotating the chair alone.

an armchair more than 30° off the coffee.rule: An armchair more than 30° off the coffee table it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than rotating the chair alone.

an armchair whose front use zone is not.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door is a seating-group placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the seating group (sofa against its wall, table in front, chairs facing the table) in one round rather than rotating the chair alone.

a kitchen sink whose back is off its wal.rule: A kitchen sink whose back is off its wall (a member of the kitchen run) is a build-stage defect of the kitchen run's placement: the build stage is re-run so the kitchen run is rebuilt against its wall from the drawing.

a kitchen counter that reaches through t.rule: A kitchen counter that reaches through the room outline is a build-stage defect of the kitchen run's placement: the build stage is re-run so the kitchen run is rebuilt within the room from the drawing.

a kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in.rule: A kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m in front of the kitchen counter is a build-stage defect of the kitchen run's placement: the build stage is re-run so the kitchen run is rebuilt with a proper aisle from the drawing.

an armchair whose free zone in front is.rule: An armchair whose free zone in front is blocked by another piece is a furniture-placement defect: the furniture agent re-solves the room's furniture (the armchair and the blocking piece) in one round rather than moving one piece alone.

a seating piece's free zone in front of.rule: A seating piece's free zone in front of it must be kept clear of other furniture; the layout solver must not place a piece inside the clearance zone of a neighbouring seat.

the main walkway from the entrance door.rule: The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide; the layout must not place furniture or fixtures that narrow the primary circulation path below this threshold.

furniture pieces must not overlap; the l.rule: Furniture pieces must not overlap; the layout solver must ensure a minimum clearance between adjacent pieces such as a nightstand and a bed.

a bed must have at least 0.60 m of free.rule: A bed must have at least 0.60 m of free space along its sides for access; the layout solver must not place a bed so close to a wall or other furniture that this clearance is violated.

a shower or other tall fixture must not.rule: A shower or other tall fixture must not stand in front of a window with a sill below 0.95 m, as it blocks the view and light; the layout must place wet fixtures away from low windows.

when the documents label an outdoor spac.rule: When the documents label an outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) with a defined outline, the building stage must construct its floor slab, railing, and roof/overhang as a built element, not just an outdoor space placeholder.

a stair piece must not be placed inside.rule: A stair piece must not be placed inside a kitchen room; the reading stage must assign stair openings to a hall or dedicated stairwell, and the layout stage must reject a stair in a kitchen.

furniture pieces present in the decor st.rule: Furniture pieces present in the decor stage must not be dropped by the agent stage without a recorded reason; the agent must preserve all drawn pieces unless explicitly removed.

a planned kitchen sink must be built as.rule: A planned kitchen sink must be built as a visible object in the scene; the build stage must not omit a sink that is part of the kitchen run.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece (e.g., a bed) and is named by an AI pass as a small accessory (floor lamp, nightstand) should be typed as that accessory, not left as an unknown detail.

a bookshelf that is not built due to a m.rule: A bookshelf that is not built due to a model issue should be swapped to a valid library model of the same type and size.

a potted plant that is not built due to.rule: A potted plant that is not built due to a model issue should be swapped to a valid library model of the same type and size.

an ottoman that is not built due to a mo.rule: An ottoman that is not built due to a model issue should be swapped to a valid library model of the same type and size.

a piece that is removed by an ai pass mu.rule: A piece that is removed by an AI pass must be recorded with a reason; if the piece is not in the building, the agent round must investigate and restore it if it belongs.

a drawn piece that the build could not p.rule: A drawn piece that the build could not place because its neighbours left no room is a loss, not a removal: the furniture round must re-solve the room's set around the drawn anchor so the piece is built, and a retype that only lowers the plausibility score of the room's other pieces is refused.

a drawn office chair is not removed beca.rule: A drawn office chair is not removed because it stands alone: it is the partner of the room's desk, and the furniture round must place the desk and chair as one work set so both are built.

a drawn floor lamp that the build could.rule: A drawn floor lamp that the build could not place is a loss: the furniture round must place it in a free corner of the room, and a wrong model is swapped, never a reason to drop the piece.

a drawn desk that the build could not pl.rule: A drawn desk that the build could not place is a loss: the furniture round must place it, and a retype that is a no-change is refused, so the cause (the room's layout) must be fixed, not the piece's type.

an interior view that must show a piece.rule: An interior view that must show a piece the build placed but the camera does not frame is a camera problem: the camera is moved to a free pose that shows the named pieces, never the piece removed.

a chair that the build could not move to.rule: A chair that the build could not move to a free wall span is not removed: the camera is moved to show it where it stands, and the move is refused only when no free place exists, which is a layout problem for the furniture round, not a reason to drop the piece.

an exterior view that must show a window.rule: An exterior view that must show a window the build placed but the camera does not frame is a camera problem: the camera is moved to a pose that shows the named windows, never the window removed.
An exterior view that must show a window the build placed but the camera does not frame is a camera problem: the camera is moved to a pose that shows the named windows.

strokes on the furniture layer that no p.rule: Strokes on the furniture layer that no piece uses are a reading loss: the furniture round must read them as the pieces they are (a sofa, chairs around a table) and build them, never drop them.

a room outline that holds the labels of.rule: A room outline that holds the labels of two rooms is a wall not read: the reading stage must split the outline into the two rooms the documents name, and the build must build both.

a drawn dresser that the model has no pi.rule: A drawn dresser that the model has no piece for is a reading loss: the build must add the piece at its drawn anchor, and the camera must show it.

a drawn nightstand that the build could.rule: A drawn nightstand that the build could not place because the bed's footprint left no room is a loss: the furniture round must re-solve the bedroom set so the nightstand is built, and a move that overlaps the bed is refused.

a labelled outdoor space (veranda, balco.rule: A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony) that the model has no outline or structure for is a site loss: the site stage must build the outline and structure (floor, columns, roof) of the space the documents name, and the build must not drop it.

a labelled outdoor space (balcony) that.rule: A labelled outdoor space (balcony) that the model has no outline or structure for is a site loss: the site stage must build the outline and structure (floor, guard, roof) of the space the documents name, and the build must not drop it.

a dressing room that is functionally emp.rule: A dressing room that is functionally empty (no mirror, bench) is a decor loss: the furniture round must place the dressing group (mirror, bench, wardrobe) so the room is furnished, and a place_group that finds no place is a layout problem for the round, not a reason to leave the room empty.

a kitchen that is functionally empty in.rule: A kitchen that is functionally empty in the render (counters, fridge, stove missing or not visible) is a decor loss: the furniture round must place the kitchen run (counters, fridge, stove) so the room is furnished, and a place_group that finds no place is a layout problem for the round, not a reason to leave the room empty.

a kitchen's program requires a fridge; w.rule: A kitchen's program requires a fridge; when the solver cannot place one (no candidate position fits the room), the run must flag the room as under-sized for its program and report it, rather than leaving the kitchen set incomplete and silent.

a stair footprint (a large, multi-step d.rule: A stair footprint (a large, multi-step drawn block) must not be read as a missing kitchen appliance; when a stair is drawn inside a kitchen outline, the reading must keep the stair and flag the kitchen as lacking a fridge, not retype the stair.

a gap in an outer wall that is fully or.rule: A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture (free width under 0.60 m) is a window, not a door: the reading's door_to_window correction is the right call, and the circulation findings (F90) that follow from it are the architect's to resolve, not a model error.

A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture (free width under 0.60 m) is a window, not a door: the reading's door_to_window correction is the right call, and the circulation findings (F91) that follow from it are the architect's to resolve, not a model error.

A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture (free width under 0.60 m) is a window, not a door: the reading's door_to_window correction is the right call, and the circulation findings that follow from it are the architect's to resolve, not a model error.

a wall cabinet (or any wall-hung unit) t.rule: A wall cabinet (or any wall-hung unit) that is cut by a window in the building as built must be re-solved as part of its kitchen run onto a free wall span; when no free span exists on the same wall, the run is re-solved on another wall of the room, and the cabinet is never left cut at a window.

a furniture piece that covers a window o.rule: A furniture piece that covers a window opening must be moved to a free place in its room, clear of the window.

a room that cannot be reached from the e.rule: A room that cannot be reached from the entrance through any door, opening or stair is a genuine circulation problem for the architect to resolve; it is not a model error.

a level that cannot be reached from the.rule: A level that cannot be reached from the entrance through any door, opening or stair is a genuine circulation problem for the architect to resolve; it is not a model error.

a window that runs past the end of its w.rule: A window that runs past the end of its wall is a genuine geometry problem for the architect to resolve; it is not a model error.

a piece that blocks the ray through an o.rule: A piece that blocks the ray through an opening must be moved or removed so the opening is clear.

wall art must not hang over a window; it.rule: Wall art must not hang over a window; it should be moved to a solid wall section.

a bathroom window over a washbasin shoul.rule: A bathroom window over a washbasin should have its sill raised to 1.25 m to allow a mirror and clear the tap.

a camera view that must show a piece mus.rule: A camera view that must show a piece must be adjusted to include it in the frame.

an exterior camera view must be position.rule: An exterior camera view must be positioned to show the required window or facade element.

a bathroom must include a mirror, towel.rule: A bathroom must include a mirror, towel rail, and proper styling around the washbasin.

a bathroom set must include a mirror ove.rule: A bathroom set must include a mirror over the washbasin.

every bathroom with a washbasin must hav.rule: Every bathroom with a washbasin must have a mirror mounted above it, either as part of the bathroom set or as a separate wall item.

a piece's orientation must match its dra.rule: A piece's orientation must match its drawn orientation within tolerance.

a piece's model must match its drawn siz.rule: A piece's model must match its drawn size and position within tolerance.

a balcony or terrace shown in the floor.rule: A balcony or terrace shown in the floor plan must be built as an outdoor space with a floor, guard, and roof if applicable.

a kitchen run that includes a tall unit.rule: A kitchen run that includes a tall unit (fridge) must be solved as one group: the tall unit is a member of the run, not a separate wall_cabinet, and the run must not be placed where a member is cut by a window or door opening.

a door that opens onto a drawn outdoor s.rule: A door that opens onto a drawn outdoor space (balcony, veranda, terrace) must have that outdoor space built with a floor slab and guard before the door is considered complete; a door leading to a void is a build error.

a drawn outdoor space (veranda, balcony,.rule: A drawn outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) that is marked as a site area must be built with a floor slab, guard, and roof cover if drawn; a site area that is not built is a loss of drawn content.

a named piece (dresser, wardrobe, etc.).rule: A named piece (dresser, wardrobe, etc.) that is not placed because the nearest valid spot is more than 1 m from the text label must be placed at the text location if the room has space, or the room must be enlarged; a named piece that cannot be placed is a loss of drawn content.

a wall unit (wall_cabinet, tall_cabinet).rule: A wall unit (wall_cabinet, tall_cabinet) that is cut by a window or door opening must be moved to a free wall span; if no free span exists, the unit must be resized or the window/door must be moved. A wall unit cut by an opening is a build error.

a bathroom set the solver has already pl.rule: A bathroom set the solver has already placed (anchor plus members) is frozen: a member that lands over a window is a layout defect of the set solver, not a missing member, and must be fixed by the set solver re-solving the set around a different anchor span, not by moving the member alone.

a style clash among drawn (locked) piece.rule: A style clash among drawn (locked) pieces is a furniture-selection defect of the drawing, not a build defect: the pipeline must flag it for the architect to re-select, not try to relayout or re-type locked pieces.

decor items (wall art, plants, lamps) pl.rule: Decor items (wall art, plants, lamps) placed over a window are a decor-placement defect of the solver; the pipeline must re-solve decor placement with a window-avoidance constraint, not treat it as a furniture clearance issue.

a drawn piece the solver cannot place (n.rule: A drawn piece the solver cannot place (no candidate passes the checks) is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the room as too small for its drawn program, not silently drop the piece.

a kitchen_run group the solver cannot co.rule: A kitchen_run group the solver cannot complete (no candidate fits) is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the kitchen as too small for its drawn run, not silently drop the missing member.

a bathroom with four fixtures in under 5.rule: A bathroom with four fixtures in under 5 m2 is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the room as too small for its program, not try to re-frame the camera to hide the clutter.

a dressing room the solver cannot furnis.rule: A dressing room the solver cannot furnish (no candidate passes the checks) is a room-capacity defect: the pipeline must flag the room as too small for its program, not leave it as a bare box.

an outside door not registered in site.e.rule: An outside door not registered in site.entrances cannot have its entrance solution changed: the pipeline must register all outside doors as site entrances before the entrance-solution stage runs.

a bathroom whose drawing shows an open (.rule: A bathroom whose drawing shows an open (unfitted) wet area and whose reference calls for a shower must be built with a shower, not a bathtub: the type is read from the reference, not from the default bathroom set.

a site with only flat grass and a few sc.rule: A site with only flat grass and a few scattered trees is incomplete: the pipeline must add a path, a hedge or fence line, and a reasonable number of trees to make the site read as a real plot.

an outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terr.rule: An outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) furnished with the wrong set (dining instead of lounge) is a furniture-selection defect of the outdoor-space stage: the pipeline must select the correct outdoor set for the space type, not treat it as a room group.

a site with no fence and no path is inco.rule: A site with no fence and no path is incomplete: the pipeline must add a fence (hedge or solid) and a path to make the site read as a real plot with boundaries.

a site with no roads, no fences, and no.rule: A site with no roads, no fences, and no neighbours is incomplete: the pipeline must add a fence and a path to make the site read as a real plot in a real context.

a garden with only flat grass and a few.rule: A garden with only flat grass and a few generic trees is incomplete: the pipeline must add planted beds, shrubs, ground cover, and a reasonable number of trees to make the garden read as a real landscape.

a piece whose front was read the wrong w.rule: A piece whose front was read the wrong way round and corrected at ingest is a reading error that the code has already fixed: the finding is a record of the correction, not a defect to re-fix.

a scene check failure for an unnamed dec.rule: A scene check failure for an unnamed decor item is a process defect: the pipeline must name the specific item that failed so it can be fixed, not leave it as an anonymous failure.

the fitting stage must not fall back to.rule: The fitting stage must not fall back to a parametric mesh when a library model of the same type exists in the project's licence mode; it must select the best-fitting library model (or report no model) instead of building a parametric placeholder.

the build stage must record a leaf state.rule: The build stage must record a leaf state (open or closed) for every inside door; an inside door stands open by default (UL116) and the state must be explicit in the model.

a walk-in dressing room must have see-th.rule: A walk-in dressing room must have see-through wardrobe fronts (horizontal black slat sliding doors) with real contents and a light inside (UL120, UL125); closed wardrobe fronts are not acceptable for a walk-in.

a door or opening that a camera view loo.rule: A door or opening that a camera view looks through into a room worth showing must be left open (leaf out of the view) so the view is not a closed door.

a built-in wardrobe run that blocks a do.rule: A built-in wardrobe run that blocks a door or window in a small room must be shortened or re-anchored to a free wall span so the opening stays clear; the solver must treat the opening's swing/clearance as a hard constraint when placing the run.

a chair drawn at a window or wall cut mu.rule: A chair drawn at a window or wall cut must be re-seated on a free wall span clear of the opening; if no free span exists in the room, the chair is removed rather than left cutting the window.

a bed that blocks a door must be re-anch.rule: A bed that blocks a door must be re-anchored so its headboard is on a wall and the door swing is clear; if the room cannot host the bed plus a clear door, the bed is moved to the largest free wall and the door is kept as the room's only exit.

a kitchen run that cannot host all its m.rule: A kitchen run that cannot host all its members (counter, sink, stove, fridge) in the room must be re-solved as a shorter run or the missing member (fridge) is placed as a freestanding unit; the solver must not leave a required member unbuilt.

a hall with two doors must keep a 0.60 m.rule: A hall with two doors must keep a 0.60 m walkway between them; if the furniture (shoe cabinet, stair) blocks the walkway, the furniture is moved to a free wall span or removed.

a toilet built with its lowest point abo.rule: A toilet built with its lowest point above the floor (parametric mesh offset) must be swapped to a real library model that sits on the floor; if no library model fits, the parametric model's base is corrected to floor level.

the architect's rule f5 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F5 must explicitly allow or forbid pieces that reach through the room outline by up to 0.20 m; if allowed, the rule must state the maximum depth and the condition (e.g., built-in, no obstruction).

the architect's rule s4 must require a f.rule: The architect's rule S4 must require a fridge in every kitchen; if the room is too small, the rule must specify the fallback (freestanding fridge, no fridge with a note).

the architect's rule s4 must specify the.rule: The architect's rule S4 must specify the minimum clearance from a washbasin to the side wall (e.g., 0.38 m) and the condition for a smaller clearance (e.g., corner basin).

the architect's rule f4 must require a f.rule: The architect's rule F4 must require a free zone in front of an armchair (e.g., 0.60 m) and forbid blocking it with another piece.

the architect's rule f3 must forbid a sh.rule: The architect's rule F3 must forbid a shower standing in front of a window with a sill below 1.00 m; if the window is above the shower, the rule must state the minimum sill height.

a camera view of a room must show the ro.rule: A camera view of a room must show the room's main group (e.g., wardrobes in a dressing room), not a wall or partition.

a styled outdoor space (terrace, veranda.rule: A styled outdoor space (terrace, veranda) must include planters to frame the seating, not just a single small potted plant.

a coffee table in a living room must be.rule: A coffee table in a living room must be styled with decor (books, vases, etc.) to make the room feel lived-in.

a parametric fixture whose lowest point.rule: A parametric fixture whose lowest point sits above the floor (a pedestal or plinth not at 0.00) must be swapped for a library model that rests on the floor, or the parametric family must be rebuilt with its base at the floor level.

bedrooms must include styled surfaces (m.rule: Bedrooms must include styled surfaces (mirror, vase, books, art) on nightstands and dressers to feel lived-in, not just bare furniture.

bathroom tall cabinets must have a textu.rule: Bathroom tall cabinets must have a textured or styled finish that matches the room's palette, and the room must include warm lighting and accessories (towels, plants) to avoid a sterile look.

living rooms with a main seating area sh.rule: Living rooms with a main seating area should have a feature wall (wood paneling, wainscoting, or accent paint) behind the sofa to add depth and style.

bedrooms should have a feature wall (pan.rule: Bedrooms should have a feature wall (paneling or accent) behind the bed to add visual interest and a sense of design.

a washbasin whose lowest point is signif.rule: A washbasin whose lowest point is significantly above the floor (e.g., +0.314 m) is a fit error; it must be swapped for a model that sits at the correct height or the parametric family must be corrected.

kitchen counters must not cut into walls.rule: Kitchen counters must not cut into walls by more than 0.030 m; if they do, the room layout must be re-solved to place the counter correctly.

beds must not cut into walls by more tha.rule: Beds must not cut into walls by more than 0.010 m; if they do, the room layout must be re-solved to place the bed correctly.

a wardrobe must use a library model, not.rule: A wardrobe must use a library model, not a parametric one, unless it is part of a kitchen run or similar fixture set.

an armchair whose back or arm is more th.rule: An armchair whose back or arm is more than 5 mm from its seat or corner is a fit error; it must be swapped for a model with correct proportions.

every window of the project's style must.rule: Every window of the project's style must be dressed with full-height curtains in two layers (a sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track; a single flat panel is not acceptable.

every bedroom must be lit with a layered.rule: Every bedroom must be lit with a layered scheme (a statement fixture plus bedside pendants and warm lamp glow); a single harsh source that leaves corners dark is not acceptable.

the primary interior camera of a small w.rule: The primary interior camera of a small wet room must be placed at a pose that shows its main fixtures (basin, toilet, shower) together; a close-up of a corner or a single fixture is not acceptable.

every window of the project's style must.rule: Every window of the project's style must be dressed with full-height curtains (a sheer behind a heavier drape); a bare window is not acceptable.

nightstands must be styled with small ob.rule: Nightstands must be styled with small objects (books, a vase, a small object); an almost-empty nightstand is not acceptable.

a seating corner's paired armchairs must.rule: A seating corner's paired armchairs must be the same model and colour; a mismatched pair (different models or colours) is not acceptable.

a bed must be layered fully (euro shams,.rule: A bed must be layered fully (euro shams, a second blanket across the foot, and decorative cushions); a duvet and a throw alone are not acceptable.

a door leaf's colour must match the room.rule: A door leaf's colour must match the room's palette (light wood and white); a dark, almost black leaf that clashes with the palette is not acceptable.

the primary interior camera of a hall mu.rule: The primary interior camera of a hall must frame its main group (stair, shoe cabinet) rather than a blank wall; the hall layout must keep a 0.60 m walkway between its doors.

the primary interior camera of a small h.rule: The primary interior camera of a small hall must be placed at a higher, wider pose that shows the room's layout and its main piece, not a low close-up of a single piece.

a hall's walls must be styled with wall.rule: A hall's walls must be styled with wall art (a framed piece); a large, flat, untextured wall is not acceptable.

a single bed must be layered fully (duve.rule: A single bed must be layered fully (duvet, euro shams, decorative cushions); a single flat sheet and a simple runner are not acceptable.

a wardrobe must have design detail (hand.rule: A wardrobe must have design detail (handles, paneling, texture) and a scale that does not overwhelm the room; a flat, untextured slab is not acceptable.

the site must include a paved path leadi.rule: The site must include a paved path leading to the entrance; a single flat, untextured green plane with no path is not acceptable.

the primary interior camera of a small w.rule: The primary interior camera of a small wet room must be placed at a pose that shows its main fixtures (shower, toilet, washbasin) together; a close-up of a blank wall and a floating slab is not acceptable.

the primary interior camera of a small h.rule: The primary interior camera of a small hall must be placed at a higher, wider pose that shows the room's layout and its main piece, not a low close-up of a corner.

a room's furniture set must be a single.rule: A room's furniture set must be a single coherent style family; a mix of 3+ distinct styles in one room is a fit failure.

a piece's model must match the room's st.rule: A piece's model must match the room's style and color palette; a dark heavy piece in a bright light-wood room is a fit failure.

an outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terr.rule: An outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) must have outdoor furniture to show how the home is used.

decor items must rest cleanly on their h.rule: Decor items must rest cleanly on their host without penetration.

the reading stage must parse attdef enti.rule: The reading stage must parse ATTDEF entities to capture attribute definitions (e.g., room labels, areas) that are part of the drawing's data.

site decor read on upper levels (l1+) th.rule: Site decor read on upper levels (L1+) that duplicates ground plan symbols should be ignored or mapped to the ground floor (L0) site, not left unused.

a room with two distinct labels (e.g., '.rule: A room with two distinct labels (e.g., 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ') should be split into two rooms if the labels refer to different functional zones.

a printed area label (e.g., '9,00 m²' fo.rule: A printed area label (e.g., '9,00 m²' for 'HOL') must be used to verify the room's area in the model.

when the build stage drops an opening th.rule: When the build stage drops an opening that the reading read twice (duplicate evidence), it must either build it or re-parent it to a surviving host; a duplicate-read opening is never silently dropped.

when a decor element's host piece is not.rule: When a decor element's host piece is not built, the build stage must re-parent the decor to the room or build it independently; a decor element is never silently dropped because its host is missing.

a living room with a seating group (sofa.rule: A living room with a seating group (sofa, armchair, coffee table) must include a rug under the seating area; the decor stage must place a rug when the seating group is built.

a bathroom with a washbasin must include.rule: A bathroom with a washbasin must include a mirror over the washbasin; the decor stage must place a mirror when the washbasin is built.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading stage must detect the missing wall between them and split the room; a room outline with two labels is a misread wall, not a single room.

when a drawn piece's exact orientation i.rule: When a drawn piece's exact orientation is refused by clearance or facing checks, keep the nearest legal orientation and close the finding as a layout constraint instead of forcing the drawn angle.

a sink that is a member of a kitchen run.rule: A sink that is a member of a kitchen run is positioned by the run, not individually; a drawn offset of the run's sink is a run-placement issue, not a per-piece move.

treat a drawn-position residual under ~3.rule: Treat a drawn-position residual under ~3 cm on a set-locked piece (dining chair to table) as placement noise, not a misread.

when all candidate models for a piece ar.rule: When all candidate models for a piece are refused on style or fit caps, keep the current model and treat a sub-20 cm drawn offset as placement, not a misread.

a wardrobe at the tolerance edge that ca.rule: A wardrobe at the tolerance edge that cannot be moved further without crossing the room outline is placed correctly; do not chase a sub-5 cm offset.

when a drawn furniture label's position.rule: When a drawn furniture label's position is more than 1 m from any legal place in its room and relayout is refused on a walkway, add the piece at the nearest legal place (not the text's position) and note the offset, rather than dropping it.

the reading stage must extract the north.rule: The reading stage must extract the north arrow (or a reference bearing) and attach it to every elevation so that elevation openings can be checked against the plans; if no north arrow is drawn, record a default bearing and flag it.

before checking a drawn section against.rule: Before checking a drawn section against the roof, verify the section line's endpoints align with the roof outline within 0.30 m; if not, skip the point-by-point check and flag the section as not co-located with the plan.
before checking a drawn section against.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

every elevation must be assigned a view.rule: Every elevation must be assigned a view bearing (from the north arrow or a labelled side) at the reading stage; an elevation without a bearing is flagged and excluded from model comparison rather than silently skipped.

when no library model fits an opening's.rule: When no library model fits an opening's size, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct build; do not flag it as a missing model.

kitchen islands and counters should be s.rule: Kitchen islands and counters should be styled with a few small items (e.g. a fruit bowl, a cutting board, or a small appliance) to make them feel lived-in, rather than left completely bare.

kitchen counters should be styled with a.rule: Kitchen counters should be styled with a few small items (e.g. a kettle, jars, and a bowl) to make them feel lived-in, rather than left almost empty.

openings in a main hall should not lead.rule: Openings in a main hall should not lead directly into a bathroom, as this is an unusual and potentially awkward layout; the view through such an opening should be uncluttered and not distracting.

a dining table is judged complete when i.rule: A dining table is judged complete when it carries place settings for its drawn seat count; optional decor (glasses, cutlery, centerpiece) is not a defect.

the agent stage must not drop a built pi.rule: The agent stage must not drop a built piece of the decor stage; a piece removed for a wall-art clearance is re-placed (moved or the art dropped), not deleted.

a conservation 'gone after the build sta.rule: A conservation 'gone after the build stage' record is a false alarm when the element id still appears in the final model's element list for its level.
A conservation 'gone after the build stage' record is a false alarm when the element is a parametric opening built in the style's finish and the record only cites its params text.

structural grid bubbles (axis labels) an.rule: Structural grid bubbles (axis labels) and drawing annotations are not part of the building and are correctly not built.

decor elements whose host piece is not b.rule: Decor elements whose host piece is not built are correctly not built.

cushions, pillows and small details draw.rule: Cushions, pillows and small details drawn on a piece are part of that piece, not separate elements, and are correctly not built as separate elements.

a wall cabinet drawn over a window or gl.rule: A wall cabinet drawn over a window or glazed door is not built only because no wall unit fits beside it; it is built at its drawn position with the window's head as its top limit (or the window is treated as a high window), so a drawn wall cabinet is never dropped for covering a window.

a nightstand drawn beside a bed is kept.rule: A nightstand drawn beside a bed is kept at its drawn position even if it slightly overlaps the bed footprint; the bed is the anchor and the nightstand is placed clear of it by trimming the bed's drawn extent, not by dropping the nightstand when no free place lies within 1.0 m.

a piece removed by the furniture agent f.rule: A piece removed by the furniture agent for a plausibility/fit reason (stands alone, no context) is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss; do not flag it as 'not built' when the removal answer is the agent's own remove_piece.

a piece removed by the furniture agent b.rule: A piece removed by the furniture agent because its partner (desk) was removed for plausibility is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.

a decorative piece (floor lamp) removed.rule: A decorative piece (floor lamp) removed by the furniture agent as part of a plausibility cleanup of an orphaned corner is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.

a stair's upper end arriving at the top.rule: A stair's upper end arriving at the top floor is not a separate piece to be built; it is the top of the flight. Do not flag it as 'not built' when the reason is 'no level above'.

a decorative piece that cannot be placed.rule: A decorative piece that cannot be placed without blocking a window or floating over a sill is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.

a decorative piece that would stand insi.rule: A decorative piece that would stand inside a closed cabinet or tall unit is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.

a decorative piece whose host is not bui.rule: A decorative piece whose host is not built is a correct dependency decision, not a conservation loss.

a decorative throw that cannot be draped.rule: A decorative throw that cannot be draped over a library model's own made bedding is a correct fit decision, not a conservation loss.

a symbol drawn on a door layer ('kapi').rule: A symbol drawn on a door layer ('KAPI') is a door symbol, not furniture; it is correctly not built as furniture.

a symbol drawn on a hatch layer ('tarama.rule: A symbol drawn on a hatch layer ('TARAMA') is a hatch, not furniture; it is correctly not built as furniture.

a symbol that is a detail of an outdoor.rule: A symbol that is a detail of an outdoor space (edge or steps) is built with that outdoor space, not as a separate furniture piece.

a building frame offset from the sheet o.rule: A building frame offset from the sheet outline is a correct coordinate system decision; all regions and coordinates are relative to the building frame.

a section's +0.50 finished floor level m.rule: A section's +0.50 finished floor level means the plans' relative marks are read +0.50 m lower; this is a correct level reading decision.

a small drawn piece around a level mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level mark text is a level-mark symbol, not furniture; it is correctly moved to symbols.

a furniture name text that confirms a pi.rule: A furniture name text that confirms a piece already built in the room is a correct reading decision, not a loss.

a furniture name text that names a piece.rule: A furniture name text that names a piece the room does not already hold is a drawn piece: the builder places it at the text's position (within 1 m) even when the room is tight, and the fit check for a drawn piece is the text's own position, not a free spot found by the solver.

an interior camera of a room must frame.rule: An interior camera of a room must frame the room's main pieces (the ones the room's program names); a pose that frames none of them is refused and the camera is moved to the nearest searched pose that does.

a piece of furniture must not cover a wi.rule: A piece of furniture must not cover a window or door opening: the door/window ray from the opening must not hit a furniture piece; a piece that blocks an opening is moved to the nearest free place in its room, clear of the opening.

a small decor item (utensil, vase) place.rule: A small decor item (utensil, vase) placed on a counter or shelf must have at least 80% of its footprint over the support surface; if the support is too small or the item is at the edge, the item is removed or the support is widened.

every interior door must have a 0.60 m c.rule: Every interior door must have a 0.60 m clear walkway to the nearest other opening in the same room; if the room is too small, the door is moved to a wall with more clearance or the room is widened.

a bed must not block a door swing; the b.rule: A bed must not block a door swing; the bed is moved to a wall that leaves the door clear, or the door is moved to a different wall.

a wardrobe must not block a window; the.rule: A wardrobe must not block a window; the wardrobe is moved to a different wall or the window is moved.

a door must be at ground level or reacha.rule: A door must be at ground level or reachable by a stair, ramp, or landing; a door 3.50 m above the ground with no access is a reading error and must be corrected to a window or removed.

the architect's rule c1 must include che.rule: The architect's rule C1 must include checks for 0.60 m walkways between doors and windows; if the rule does not cover these cases, the rule is updated.

the architect's rule f2 / f3 must includ.rule: The architect's rule F2 / F3 must include checks for furniture blocking doors and windows; if the rule does not cover these cases, the rule is updated.

the architect's rule e1 must include che.rule: The architect's rule E1 must include checks for doors at ground level or reachable by a stair, ramp, or landing; if the rule does not cover these cases, the rule is updated.

an interior camera must show the room's.rule: An interior camera must show the room's main group (e.g., the dressing area) and not be pressed against a wall or corner.

scene check s5 must pass for all element.rule: Scene check S5 must pass for all elements; if it fails, the build stage is rerun.

a soft seat's back or arm must be within.rule: A soft seat's back or arm must be within 5 mm of its seat or corner; if it is not, the build stage is rerun.

scene check s1 must pass for all element.rule: Scene check S1 must pass for all elements; if it fails, the build stage is rerun.

scene checks that fail on a level are a.rule: Scene checks that fail on a level are a build-stage defect: the geometry of that level is re-built and re-checked before furniture is placed on it.

a sofa whose back is off a wall and whos.rule: A sofa whose back is off a wall and whose group (coffee table, armchairs) is misaligned is a seating-group placement defect: the whole group is re-solved as one unit against the wall it belongs to.

a coffee table not in front of the sofa.rule: A coffee table not in front of the sofa is a seating-group placement defect: the whole group is re-solved as one unit against the wall it belongs to.

an armchair more than 30° off the sofa i.rule: An armchair more than 30° off the sofa it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the group is re-solved so every seat faces the group centre.

an armchair more than 30° off the coffee.rule: An armchair more than 30° off the coffee table it faces is a seating-group orientation defect: the group is re-solved so every seat faces the group centre.

an armchair whose front use zone is not.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is not reached by a walkway from the door is a seating-group placement defect: the group is re-solved so the walkway to the group is clear.

a kitchen sink whose back is off the wal.rule: A kitchen sink whose back is off the wall is a kitchen-run build defect: the run is re-built against the wall it belongs to.

a kitchen counter that reaches through t.rule: A kitchen counter that reaches through the room outline is a kitchen-run build defect: the run is re-built within the room.

a kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m is.rule: A kitchen aisle narrower than 0.90 m is a kitchen-run build defect: the run is re-built so the aisle is at least 0.90 m.

an armchair whose front use zone is bloc.rule: An armchair whose front use zone is blocked by another piece is a bedroom furniture placement defect: the pieces are re-solved so the use zone is clear.

a seating piece's free zone in front of.rule: A seating piece's free zone in front of it must be kept clear of other furniture; the layout solver must not place a second piece inside the first piece's front clearance.

the main walkway from the entrance door.rule: The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide; the layout solver must keep the entrance circulation path clear of furniture and fixtures.

a nightstand must not overlap the bed it.rule: A nightstand must not overlap the bed it serves; the layout solver must keep a minimum gap between the nightstand and the bed frame.

a double bed must have at least 0.60 m o.rule: A double bed must have at least 0.60 m of free space along each side for access; the layout solver must respect this clearance when placing the bed.

a shower or other tall fixture must not.rule: A shower or other tall fixture must not stand in front of a window whose sill is below the fixture's top; the layout solver must keep windows unobstructed by tall fixtures.

when the documents label a veranda, balc.rule: When the documents label a veranda, balcony, or similar outdoor space, the building stage must create a floor slab, outline, and any necessary structure (columns, roof) for that space, not just mark it as a site area.

a stair piece must be assigned to a hall.rule: A stair piece must be assigned to a hall, stairwell, or dedicated circulation room, not to a kitchen or other functional room; the reading stage must check that a stair's room type is consistent with its function.

a piece that exists in the decor stage m.rule: A piece that exists in the decor stage must not be dropped by the agent stage without a recorded reason; the agent must preserve all drawn or planned pieces unless explicitly removed.

a planned piece must be built in the sce.rule: A planned piece must be built in the scene; if a piece is planned but not built, the build stage must either construct it or record a valid reason for its absence.

a drawn piece that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn piece that is 60% or more inside another piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own; the reading stage must not create a separate piece for a detail.

a piece that is planned but not built mu.rule: A piece that is planned but not built must be assigned a valid library model that can be constructed; the build stage must not leave a planned piece without a model.

a piece named in the documents must be p.rule: A piece named in the documents must be present in the model within a reasonable distance of its named location; the reading stage must ensure all named pieces are placed.

an interior camera that must show a piec.rule: An interior camera that must show a piece is re-posed to a free point that frames it; a piece the camera cannot reach is moved, not the camera's duty to guess.

an exterior camera assigned to show a fa.rule: An exterior camera assigned to show a facade window is re-aimed at that window's wall; a window the facade view cannot reach is a facade-coverage gap, not a camera guess.

furniture-layer strokes in a room that d.rule: Furniture-layer strokes in a room that do not resolve to a single piece footprint (a sofa, a table with chairs) are read as a group and placed as a group, not dropped as untyped strokes.

a room outline that carries two distinct.rule: A room outline that carries two distinct labels (a kitchen and an antre/entrance) is split into two rooms at the wall between them, not merged under one label.

a drawn dresser (sifonyer) in a bedroom.rule: A drawn dresser (sifonyer) in a bedroom is built as a bedroom_chest group member at its drawn anchor, not dropped when the reading loses the label.

a drawn nightstand that the build cannot.rule: A drawn nightstand that the build cannot place because the bed's footprint leaves no room is a bed-placement problem: the bed is re-posed (or the room re-laid) so the nightstand fits, not dropped.

a labelled outdoor space (veranda, balco.rule: A labelled outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) is built as a structured outdoor space (floor, guard, optional roof) with its outline, not left as an unstructured site area.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) is furni.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) is furnished with its defining group (mirror, bench, wardrobe) at build time; a room whose program is 'dressing' but whose group solver finds no place is a room-size or wall-span problem to be fixed at the geometry stage, not left empty.

a kitchen is built with its full run (co.rule: A kitchen is built with its full run (counter, sink, stove, fridge, island) as one group; when the run solver finds no place, the cause is the room's wall spans or the antre merge (F54) eating the counter wall, and the geometry stage must restore the span, not the decor stage guess a fridge.

a washbasin whose centre is under 0.38 m.rule: A washbasin whose centre is under 0.38 m from a side wall is moved by the code to the nearest valid spot (off the wall, off the door); a 'no valid spot' answer is a room-geometry problem, not a fixture-size problem.

a toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m fr.rule: A toilet whose centre is under 0.38 m from a side wall or fixture is moved by the code to the nearest valid spot; a 'no valid spot' answer is a room-geometry problem, not a fixture-size problem.

a parametric fixture that is the primary.rule: A parametric fixture that is the primary anchor of its room (toilet in a bathroom, basin, shower) must be fitted to a real library model of its type; when every candidate model fails the fit caps, the parametric mesh is kept and the finding is closed as a known limitation rather than re-tried against the same refused models.

a gap in an outer wall that is fully or.rule: A gap in an outer wall that is fully or nearly blocked by drawn furniture and has no door swing is a window, not a passage; the circulation check must not count it as a door.

a wall cabinet drawn over a window is a.rule: A wall cabinet drawn over a window is a misread: the cabinet must be moved to a free wall span, and if no free span exists in the room, the cabinet is removed (it does not belong over a window).

a furniture piece that covers a window o.rule: A furniture piece that covers a window opening must be moved to a free place in the room, clear of the window.

a bathroom on the ground floor must have.rule: A bathroom on the ground floor must have a door from a circulation space (hall, living room, or kitchen). If the reading finds no door, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a door or correct the reading.

a kitchen on the ground floor must have.rule: A kitchen on the ground floor must have a door from a circulation space (hall, living room, or dining area). If the reading finds no door, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a door or correct the reading.

a storage room on the ground floor must.rule: A storage room on the ground floor must have a door from a circulation space. If the reading finds no door, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a door or correct the reading.

every floor must be reachable from the e.rule: Every floor must be reachable from the entrance via a stair or lift. If the reading finds no stair connecting the floors, the circulation check must flag it and the architect must add a stair or correct the reading.

a window must be fully contained within.rule: A window must be fully contained within its wall. If the window runs past the end of the wall, the reading must correct the window's position or the wall's length.

a piece placed in front of an opening mu.rule: A piece placed in front of an opening must be slid or turned along its wall so the opening is clear, or moved to a free spot; the build stage must not leave furniture blocking a window or door.

wall decor must not hang over a window o.rule: Wall decor must not hang over a window or door opening; the decor stage must move it to a free wall span or leave it out.

a bathroom window over a basin must have.rule: A bathroom window over a basin must have its sill raised to at least 1.25 m so the basin and mirror fit below it, or the basin must move to a solid wall.

a bathroom with a washbasin must include.rule: A bathroom with a washbasin must include a mirror over it; the fit stage must complete the bathroom set with a mirror.

an exterior camera that must show a wind.rule: An exterior camera that must show a window must be placed at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or above the ridge, not at an invalid height.

a piece that differs from the drawing by.rule: A piece that differs from the drawing by more than 0.05 m must be swapped for a model that matches its drawn size and position.

an interior camera that must show a piec.rule: An interior camera that must show a piece must be positioned to show it; the camera stage must ensure all required pieces are visible.

a piece that is turned more than 5 degre.rule: A piece that is turned more than 5 degrees from its drawn orientation must be rotated to match the drawing.

a site area labeled as a balcony or terr.rule: A site area labeled as a balcony or terrace in the documents must be built as an outdoor space with a floor, guard, and roof if drawn; the site stage must not skip it.

a kitchen must have a continuous run of.rule: A kitchen must have a continuous run of base and wall cabinets, a hood, and a hob/oven set; the fit stage must place the kitchen run as one unit.

a door that opens onto a drawn outdoor s.rule: A door that opens onto a drawn outdoor space (balcony, veranda, terrace) must have that space built as a floor slab with a guard on its open edges before the door is placed; a door whose target space is not built is a reading error and must be flagged, not left as a door onto a void.

a washbasin in a bathroom must always be.rule: A washbasin in a bathroom must always be accompanied by a mirror (wall-mounted, above or beside the basin) as part of the bathroom set; a basin without a mirror is an incomplete set and must be flagged.

a drawn outdoor space (veranda, balcony,.rule: A drawn outdoor space (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be built as a floor slab with a roof or guard before the run is complete; a space marked NOT built with no outline is a loss of a drawn element and must be flagged.

an entrance door must be registered in s.rule: An entrance door must be registered in site.entrances before set_entrance can be applied; a door that is not registered as an entrance cannot be given steps, a landing, or cheek walls.

a drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a sid.rule: A drawn piece larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single piece; it must be split into its components and each typed individually, not left as an untyped cluster.

a piece named in the documents (by text.rule: A piece named in the documents (by text label) must be placed within 1 m of the text's position; if the nearest valid place is farther, the text's position must be re-checked against the plan, not left unplaced.

a room typed 'storage' must have its mai.rule: A room typed 'storage' must have its main storage furniture (wardrobe or tall cabinet) built; a storage room with no pieces is an incomplete set and must be flagged.

a kitchen run must include a fridge as p.rule: A kitchen run must include a fridge as part of its core equipment; a kitchen run built without a fridge is an incomplete set and must be flagged.

a room typed 'storage' at less than 3 m2.rule: A room typed 'storage' at less than 3 m2 with no pieces and no door of its own is a dead pocket that serves no function; it must be merged with an adjacent room or given a door and a function.

a dressing room must have a wardrobe bui.rule: A dressing room must have a wardrobe built as its anchor; a dressing room with no wardrobe is an incomplete set and must be flagged.

a stair piece drawn inside a kitchen roo.rule: A stair piece drawn inside a kitchen room is a misread; the reading stage must verify that a stair's footprint aligns with a floor opening or landing, not a kitchen counter zone. If a stair is detected in a room without a floor opening, it should be flagged as a potential misread of a tall appliance (e.g., fridge) or a wall element.

a piece whose drawn footprint fits a lib.rule: A piece whose drawn footprint fits a library model of its type must be built from that model, not the parametric mesh, when the model's height and depth pass the room's fit rules.

the fit rules' height cap for a toilet m.rule: The fit rules' height cap for a toilet must accept the standard product height (0.75-0.80 m) in a bathroom of at least 4 m2; a cap that rejects every library toilet forces the parametric mesh and is a bug in the cap, not in the model choice.

a tall cabinet drawn at 0.30 x 0.30 m mu.rule: A tall cabinet drawn at 0.30 x 0.30 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.30 x 0.27 m) rather than the parametric mesh.

a sofa drawn at 2.00 x 0.85 m must take.rule: A sofa drawn at 2.00 x 0.85 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (2.00 x 0.84 m) rather than the parametric mesh.

a coffee table drawn at 1.00 x 0.55 m mu.rule: A coffee table drawn at 1.00 x 0.55 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (1.00 x 0.55 m) rather than the parametric mesh.

a toilet drawn at 0.45 x 0.70 m in a 4.5.rule: A toilet drawn at 0.45 x 0.70 m in a 4.5 m2 bathroom must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.44 x 0.72 m) rather than the parametric mesh.

a toilet drawn at 0.45 x 0.70 m must tak.rule: A toilet drawn at 0.45 x 0.70 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.44 x 0.72 m) rather than the parametric mesh.

a nightstand drawn at 0.40 x 0.42 m must.rule: A nightstand drawn at 0.40 x 0.42 m must take the library model whose footprint matches (0.40 x 0.40 m) rather than the parametric mesh.

a tall cabinet drawn at 0.30 x 0.30 m in.rule: A tall cabinet drawn at 0.30 x 0.30 m in a 4.5 m2 bathroom must take a library model whose footprint fits the room's fit rules rather than the parametric mesh.

a drawn armchair with no inferred front.rule: A drawn armchair with no inferred front must be given the front direction the fitting computed (the side away from its wall or towards its partner) so the model's front faces the room.

an interior camera of a bathroom must fr.rule: An interior camera of a bathroom must frame the room's main pieces (bathtub, tall_cabinet) rather than a bare wall; the camera search's pose that frames them is the correct one.

views marked for review by the render ch.rule: Views marked for review by the render check must be re-evaluated by the furniture agent's next round after the model and material fixes are applied.

every inside door and window in the buil.rule: Every inside door and window in the build must have a leaf state recorded (open or closed); an inside door stands open by default (UL116), and a window's leaf state is recorded from the drawing or defaults to closed.

a walk-in dressing room (soyunma odası).rule: A walk-in dressing room (soyunma odası) must have see-through wardrobe fronts (horizontal black slat sliding doors) with real contents visible and a light inside (UL120, UL125); closed wardrobe fronts are a reference miss.

a door a camera view sees into a room wo.rule: A door a camera view sees into a room worth showing (UL126) must stand open, its leaf out of the view; the build's door_states.revise_for_cameras must open such doors.

an outdoor living space (terrace, verand.rule: An outdoor living space (terrace, veranda, balcony) is furnished as one cohesive seating set (a terrace_lounge or terrace_pair group), never as a random mix of a bench, a table and mismatched chairs.

a coffee table is built from a library m.rule: A coffee table is built from a library model that carries its styled top (books, vase, decor), not a bare parametric slab.

a parametric toilet (and any floor-stand.rule: A parametric toilet (and any floor-standing fixture) is built with its base at floor level; a lowest point 0.20 m above the floor is a build error, not a model choice, and must be corrected at the build stage rather than by swapping to a real model.

a nightstand (and dresser) is built from.rule: A nightstand (and dresser) is built from a library model that carries its styled top (lamp, vase, books), not a bare parametric box.

a bathroom tall cabinet is built from a.rule: A bathroom tall cabinet is built from a light, bathroom-appropriate library model, not a dark, heavy parametric monolith that clashes with the room's palette.

the accent wall behind the main sofa (an.rule: The accent wall behind the main sofa (and the bed) is finished with the project's feature-wall material (wood panelling or slats), not flat untextured paint.

the accent wall behind the bed is finish.rule: The accent wall behind the bed is finished with the project's feature-wall material (warm wood panelling or slats), not flat untextured paint.

a wall-hung washbasin is built at its wo.rule: A wall-hung washbasin is built at its working height (rim at 0.85 m, lowest point within -0.005..+0.01 m of the floor); a lowest point 0.31 m above the floor is a build error, not a model choice, and must be corrected at the build stage rather than by swapping to a real model.

a kitchen counter (and any run) is place.rule: A kitchen counter (and any run) is placed flush against its wall, with its cut within 0.030 m; a cut deeper than that is a layout error and must be corrected at the layout stage, not by swapping the model.

a bed is placed with its headboard again.rule: A bed is placed with its headboard against a wall, with its cut within 0.010 m; a cut deeper than that is a layout error and must be corrected at the layout stage, not by moving the bed into the room or swapping the model.

a wardrobe is built from a library model.rule: A wardrobe is built from a library model, never a parametric module; parametric is reserved for the fixed-equipment list (kitchen_counter, kitchen_island, wall_cabinet, stair, shower, washing_machine, fridge, toilet, washbasin, bathtub, sink_kitchen, stove).

a washbasin model whose lowest point sit.rule: A washbasin model whose lowest point sits more than 1 cm above the floor is a pedestal or wall-hung unit that needs its support; the fit check must reject it for a floor-standing slot.

an armchair model whose back or arm is m.rule: An armchair model whose back or arm is more than 5 mm from its seat or corner is a broken or mis-joined mesh; the fit check must reject it.

a bedroom's feature wall behind the head.rule: A bedroom's feature wall behind the headboard must be a distinct material (wood slat, panel, or wainscot) to anchor the room, not flat paint.

a bathroom's wet walls should have a ric.rule: A bathroom's wet walls should have a rich texture (wood paneling, stone, or tile) to match the project's style, not flat untextured plaster.

a dining table in a kitchen or living ar.rule: A dining table in a kitchen or living area must be styled with props (plates, glasses, centerpiece) to feel lived-in, not left bare.

dining chairs must match the style and t.rule: Dining chairs must match the style and tone of the dining table and kitchen; a dark heavy wood chair does not belong with a light oak table and pale modern kitchen.

an armchair in a seating group must matc.rule: An armchair in a seating group must match the style and colour family of the sofa and other armchairs; a dark navy wingback does not belong with a beige sofa and patterned armchair.

a sofa in a seating group must match the.rule: A sofa in a seating group must match the design language of the armchairs and daybed; a curved beige sofa does not belong with a boxy cream armchair and mid-century daybed.

a floor lamp must provide warm, layered.rule: A floor lamp must provide warm, layered glow or statement quality; a generic thin model does not meet the interior style's standard.

a dining table and chairs must match the.rule: A dining table and chairs must match the style of the living area; a stark modern set with heavy dark chairs does not belong in a soft, neutral, organic style.

a bathtub must have a light, textured fi.rule: A bathtub must have a light, textured finish that matches the room's palette; a dark, flat, untextured finish looks like a placeholder.

a bathroom's walls should have a wood-cl.rule: A bathroom's walls should have a wood-clad finish as a major design feature, not flat untextured beige plaster.

an office chair in a children's room mus.rule: An office chair in a children's room must be child-sized and match the warm, playful style; a chrome corporate chair does not belong.

a bedroom's feature wall behind the bed.rule: A bedroom's feature wall behind the bed must be a distinct material (slatted wood or paneling) to anchor the room, not flat untextured paint.

a wardrobe and bookshelf must match the.rule: A wardrobe and bookshelf must match the style and colour of the room; a dark, heavy piece does not belong with bright green walls and light wood floor.

a bed model must carry its full bedding.rule: A bed model must carry its full bedding set (pillows, shams, throw) in the mesh; a bare-slab bed is a wrong model, not a placement problem.

a dresser model must be in the project's.rule: A dresser model must be in the project's style chain and pass the height cap; a bare, off-style dresser is a wrong model.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (basin, toilet, shower) together; a corner close-up that hides the vanity is not a room view.

an accent chair must sit in the room's s.rule: An accent chair must sit in the room's style chain (scandinavian/modern, light wood and neutral palette); a dark velvet chair is a wrong model.

a nightstand model must be in the projec.rule: A nightstand model must be in the project's style chain and sized to the bed; a bare, off-style nightstand is a wrong model.

every bedroom window must be dressed wit.rule: Every bedroom window must be dressed with a curtain set (sheer plus drape) as part of the room's decor group; a bare window in a furnished bedroom is an incomplete set.

a double bed model must render the full.rule: A double bed model must render the full bedding layering (euro shams, second blanket, cushions); a duvet-and-throw-only bed is a wrong model.

a hall camera must frame the room's main.rule: A hall camera must frame the room's main pieces (stair, shoe cabinet) together; a corner/doorframe close-up is not a room view.

every hall/entry room must carry at leas.rule: Every hall/entry room must carry at least one warm light source (ceiling, wall or accent) as part of its decor; a flat shadowless ambient hall is an incomplete set.

a single bed model must render the full.rule: A single bed model must render the full bedding layering (duvet fold, throw, second blanket, shams); a one-pillow-and-runner bed is a wrong model.

the facade must carry layered materials.rule: The facade must carry layered materials (paneling, wood, stone) for depth; a flat untextured beige facade is an unfinished shell.

a balcony/terrace must carry outdoor sea.rule: A balcony/terrace must carry outdoor seating (a terrace lounge set) so the render shows how the space is used; a bare terrace is an incomplete set.

a veranda/terrace base must carry plante.rule: A veranda/terrace base must carry planters and seating so the outdoor space reads as layered and finished; a bare terrace with one plant is an incomplete set.

a bathroom camera must frame the vanity.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the vanity (basin and mirror) together with the other main fixtures; a view that hides the sink is not a room view.

a sofa must sit in the same style family.rule: A sofa must sit in the same style family as the room's other seating; a terracotta leather sofa against dark modern armchairs is a mismatched set.

a living room's feature wall behind the.rule: A living room's feature wall behind the seating must carry vertical panelling or wainscoting; a flat untextured wall is an incomplete feature.

a coffee table model must carry styled s.rule: A coffee table model must carry styled surfaces (books, vases, decor) in its mesh; a bare slab is a placeholder and fails the styled-surfaces layer.

a bathroom's wet walls must carry the st.rule: A bathroom's wet walls must carry the style's wood-clad look (slat/panel), not a flat beige shell, to match the reference palette.

a bedroom must be lit in layers (a state.rule: A bedroom must be lit in layers (a statement or bedside lamp plus warm glow), not by the window alone; the furniture round must place the missing light fixture.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main pieces (the beds in a bedroom); a view that crops them out is a bare-wall shot and fails the room view.

a window in a styled room must be dresse.rule: A window in a styled room must be dressed with full-height two-layer curtains (a sheer behind a heavier drape) on a ceiling track; a single flat panel is a placeholder that fails the layered-curtains layer.

a bathroom camera must frame the room's.rule: A bathroom camera must frame the room's main fixtures (basin, toilet, shower) as a room view, not a tight corner detail shot.

a bathroom camera must not be pressed ag.rule: A bathroom camera must not be pressed against a glass partition; it must frame the room's main group (basin, mirror, cabinet) as a room view.

an interior door leaf must match the roo.rule: An interior door leaf must match the room's light wood and white palette; a dark, near-black leaf is a jarring element that breaks the cohesive palette.

a hall camera must frame the hall's main.rule: A hall camera must frame the hall's main pieces (the stair and shoe cabinet), not a flat empty wall.

a hall camera must not be pressed agains.rule: A hall camera must not be pressed against the console table so that it blocks the view; it must frame the hall with the console as a foreground accent, not the whole frame.

a wardrobe model must carry design detai.rule: A wardrobe model must carry design detail (handles, paneling, texture) and a scale that fits the room; a flat untextured slab is a placeholder. When the only fitting library model is a generated one with guessed units, the build must not fall back to a flat slab.

a dressing-room camera must not be press.rule: A dressing-room camera must not be pressed flat against a wall or louvered screen; it must frame the room's anchoring wardrobes and the floor.

an exterior presentation must show a fin.rule: An exterior presentation must show a finished, landscaped site (paved driveway and walkway, a defined entrance, mature planting), not a grey-box massing on a void.

the facade must carry a finished, textur.rule: The facade must carry a finished, textured exterior material, not a flat untextured white and brown grey-box.

the roof must carry a finished tile or s.rule: The roof must carry a finished tile or slate material, not a flat grey-box surface.

an exterior view must be framed at eye l.rule: An exterior view must be framed at eye level (1.5-1.7 m) or as a high view above the ridge; a camera at 2.10 m or 8.50 m is neither and reads as a grey-box massing study.

an aerial or site view of a house is not.rule: An aerial or site view of a house is not client-ready with a bare ground plane: the site must carry a finished ground, a path to the entrance, and planting (hedge or trees) so the massing reads as a placed, landscaped home.

a single small potted plant does not sat.rule: A single small potted plant does not satisfy a 'layered greenery' brief: the plant model must be tall enough to read as a statement plant, and the swap must pass the fit caps (the previous 0.45 m model was refused for height).

a tall cabinet (or any storage piece) mu.rule: A tall cabinet (or any storage piece) must never be built as a featureless parametric slab: the library must supply a modelled cabinet with handles and texture, and the builder must refuse a parametric fallback for a visible storage piece.

a floor lamp's style must match the room.rule: A floor lamp's style must match the room's brief (modern, warm): a dated mid-century 'lollipop' lamp is a wrong-model finding, and the swap must keep the same footprint so the drawn position and the clearance in front of the armchair are preserved.

a console or shoe cabinet in a hall must.rule: A console or shoe cabinet in a hall must use a warm, neutral wood that matches the room palette; a bright orange wood is a wrong-model/finish finding and must be swapped to a neutral tone.

a veranda or terrace is not complete wit.rule: A veranda or terrace is not complete without outdoor seating: the program must place a terrace group (lounge or pair) so the outdoor space reads as a usable living area, not a bare slab.

a living room's seating set must be a co.rule: A living room's seating set must be a coherent style family: the furniture agent must pick sofa, armchairs and chairs from one style so the set reads as a matched collection, not a jumble of mid-century, Scandinavian and vintage pieces.

a dining set must match the room's floor.rule: A dining set must match the room's floor and rug palette: a dark modern dining set against a beige herringbone floor and grey rug is a style clash, and the agent must pick a dining set in the room's warm neutral family.

the view through a glass door to an outd.rule: The view through a glass door to an outdoor space must show a furnished terrace (seating and planters), not a flat empty area: the outdoor space's program must include a terrace group so the transition reads as a lived-in space.

a child's bedroom must be styled as a ch.rule: A child's bedroom must be styled as a child's room: the furniture agent must pick a child-appropriate bed, bedding and accessories, not an adult bed with a jarring mix of adult furniture.

a bedroom must be styled with the full l.rule: A bedroom must be styled with the full layer set (rug, curtains, art, plants, warm light, styled surfaces): the furniture agent must place these layers, not leave a bare grey-box room with blocky furniture.
