a decor throw that pokes 0.025 m through.rule: A decor throw that pokes 0.025 m through its host is within the cloth's natural drape tolerance and is not a visible defect; the rest check should allow a small penetration for soft decor on a soft host.

a decor throw that pokes 0.013 m through.rule: A decor throw that pokes 0.013 m through its host is within the cloth's natural drape tolerance and is not a visible defect; the rest check should allow a small penetration for soft decor on a soft host.

a decor item that rests on a host must h.rule: A decor item that rests on a host must have a detectable top surface: the rest check must find the host's top (e.g. a desk's top) before placing the item, and if no top is found the item is not built rather than left floating.

the reading stage must parse attdef (att.rule: The reading stage must parse ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities and carry their tag/value pairs into the room and piece ledger, so attribute-driven labels and dimensions are not silently dropped.

when walls are drawn as face lines, the.rule: When walls are drawn as face lines, the reading must reconcile the chosen wall layer against the runner-up layer and account for every wall primitive left off the chosen layer, flagging any that close a labelled room.

the reading must map every named layer t.rule: The reading must map every named layer to a building element (or explicitly mark it as non-structural) so that a layer of 34+ line entities is never silently unused and unexplained.

the build stage must not drop an opening.rule: The build stage must not drop an opening that the reading recorded (even if read twice); if an opening cannot be placed, it must be kept as a flagged gap rather than silently removed.

when a build stage drops a host piece, i.rule: When a build stage drops a host piece, it must re-parent or independently build the decor elements that depend on it, rather than dropping them without record.

the decor stage must add a rug under the.rule: The decor stage must add a rug under the seating group of every living room to anchor the seating area, as part of the living room's standard program.

the decor stage must include a mirror ov.rule: The decor stage must include a mirror over the washbasin in every bathroom's standard set, as part of the bathroom program.

every bathroom with a washbasin must car.rule: Every bathroom with a washbasin must carry a mirror over it as part of the bathroom set; the set is incomplete without it.

when one room outline holds two labels,.rule: When one room outline holds two labels, the reading must split the outline at the wall between the two named spaces so each label becomes its own room.

when a drawn piece is off its drawn plac.rule: When a drawn piece is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre before the render check; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback when the piece cannot be moved.

when a drawn armchair is turned off its.rule: When a drawn armchair is turned off its drawn bearing, the layout must keep the drawn bearing; a rotate that worsens the group-facing check is refused, so the cause is the group anchor, not the armchair.

when a kitchen sink is off its drawn pla.rule: When a kitchen sink is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.

when a drawn chair is off its drawn plac.rule: When a drawn chair is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.

when a drawn dresser is off its drawn pl.rule: When a drawn dresser is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.

when a drawn wardrobe is off its drawn p.rule: When a drawn wardrobe is off its drawn place by more than the tolerance and the room outline is tight, the layout must re-seat it on its drawn centre; a model swap that matches the drawn footprint is the fallback.

every elevation must carry a north arrow.rule: Every elevation must carry a north arrow or a side label so its openings can be checked against the plans.

a drawn section must run one-to-one with.rule: A drawn section must run one-to-one with the plan outline; if its ends are more than 0.30 m apart from the roof outline, the reading must align the section to the plan before the roof check.
a drawn section must run one-to-one with.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

every elevation must carry a view bearin.rule: Every elevation must carry a view bearing or a side label so it can be compared with the model.

when an entrance group has no candidate.rule: When an entrance group has no candidate position that fits the room, the fit stage must report the room as too small for the group and the reading must check the room outline; the group is not silently dropped.

when no library model of the building's.rule: When no library model of the building's window family fits the opening size, the opening is built parametric in the style's finish; this is not a finding.
When no library model of the building's window family fits an opening's size, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct build, not a defect; do not flag it.

when a library model would have to be st.rule: When a library model would have to be stretched beyond acceptable proportions to fit an opening, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct build, not a defect; do not flag it.

when a parametric mesh is used because n.rule: When a parametric mesh is used because no library model fits, try the next-closest library model that passes the fit rules before accepting the parametric fallback.

a bookshelf in a furnished room must hol.rule: A bookshelf in a furnished room must hold books; the decor stage must populate shelves as part of its tabletop pass.

a bookshelf built by the decor stage mus.rule: A bookshelf built by the decor stage must be styled with books (tabletop.shelf_books) before the run is finished; an empty shelf is a decor-stage omission, not a model defect.

an interior kitchen camera must sit at s.rule: An interior kitchen camera must sit at standing eye height and frame the island and dining table together; a low, up-tilted camera that makes the island a barrier is a camera-stage error, not a model error.

a dining table built by the decor stage.rule: A dining table built by the decor stage must be styled with a full setting (plates, glasses, cutlery, a centerpiece) before the run is finished; a bare or half-set table is a decor-stage omission.

a kitchen counter run built by the decor.rule: A kitchen counter run built by the decor stage must be styled with small appliances and accessories along its length before the run is finished; a long empty worktop is a decor-stage omission.

an opening in a main hall that leads dir.rule: An opening in a main hall that leads directly into a bathroom (toilet/washbasin visible) is a privacy defect: the reading must not place a bathroom door on the hall's main sight line; if the drawing shows it, the architect must add a screen, a half-wall, or a frosted/glazed door so the wet room is not visible from the hall.

a console table built by the decor stage.rule: A console table built by the decor stage must be styled with at least one object (lamp, bowl, vase) on top before the run is finished; a bare console is a decor-stage omission.

the agent stage must not drop a built pi.rule: The agent stage must not drop a built piece (e.g. a shoe_cabinet) because a wall-art slot above it fails a clearance check; the piece stays and the art is simply not placed.

the agent stage must not drop a built de.rule: The agent stage must not drop a built desk (or any built piece) when re-solving a room; a built piece stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.

the agent stage must not drop a built of.rule: The agent stage must not drop a built office_chair that is the partner of a built desk; the work set (desk + chair) stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.

the agent stage must not drop a built bo.rule: The agent stage must not drop a built bookshelf (or any built piece) when re-solving a room; a built piece stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.

the build stage must not drop a window (.rule: The build stage must not drop a window (or any opening) that the reading stage identified; a window stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.

the build stage must not drop an opening.rule: The build stage must not drop an opening (or any opening) that the reading stage identified; an opening stays unless the architect explicitly removes it.

axis bubbles, level marks and other draw.rule: Axis bubbles, level marks and other drawing annotations read from the plan are recorded as not-built annotations, not as lost elements.

decor elements attached to a host piece.rule: Decor elements attached to a host piece that is not built are not lost; they are correctly excluded with their host.

small details drawn inside a larger piec.rule: Small details drawn inside a larger piece (cushions, pillows) are part of that piece's model, not separate furniture to be built.

columns drawn on the 'kolon' layer that.rule: Columns drawn on the 'KOLON' layer that support an outdoor space are built as posts of that space, not as separate interior elements.

level marks (kot) are drawing annotation.rule: Level marks (kot) are drawing annotations that define floor heights; they are not physical objects to be built.

exterior space labels (veranda, balcony).rule: Exterior space labels (veranda, balcony) without drawn paving, parking, grass or pool are built as outdoor spaces; the label itself is not a separate element to be built.

when a piece is read twice (duplicate ou.rule: When a piece is read twice (duplicate outline), it is built once; the duplicate is not a lost element.

when a piece is drawn inside another pie.rule: When a piece is drawn inside another piece of the same type (60% or more), it is the same piece drawn twice or a part of it; it is not a separate lost element.

when a kitchen run is drawn as one outli.rule: When a kitchen run is drawn as one outline with its fixtures, it is replaced by its individual counter pieces along the walls; the outline is not a separate lost element.

an outline around other pieces (3.89 x 1.rule: An outline around other pieces (3.89 x 1.42 m) that is a rug or zone outline is not a furniture piece to be built; the decor rules lay rugs under the groups.

when a piece is removed by ai (ai.remove.rule: When a piece is removed by AI (AI.remove_piece) but the documents show it should be built, the build stage must restore it with a valid model.

a drawn wall unit that would cover a win.rule: A drawn wall unit that would cover a window or glazed door of its wall, with no free wall span beside it, is not built; the window stays clear.

an untyped drawn cluster larger than 4.5.rule: An untyped drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is not built as a single piece; it is a group of drawn marks or a misread wall line, not furniture.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m that fit.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m that fits no furniture type is a detail (tap, valve, threshold, shelf line), not a piece, and is not built.

a drawn mark that is 60% or more inside.rule: A drawn mark that is 60% or more inside another built piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own, and is not built separately.

a second nightstand that cannot be place.rule: A second nightstand that cannot be placed without cutting the bed or exceeding 1.0 m from the bed is not built; one nightstand satisfies the sleeping set.

a piece removed by the ai (ai.remove_pie.rule: A piece removed by the AI (AI.remove_piece) is not built; the removal is a deliberate decision, not a loss.

a stair's upper end at the top floor is.rule: A stair's upper end at the top floor is not built as a separate piece; the stair is already present in the room.

a kitchen decoration that would block a.rule: A kitchen decoration that would block a window or reach over its sill, with no free worktop spot, is not built.

a kitchen decoration that would stand in.rule: A kitchen decoration that would stand inside a tall unit (fridge column) is not built; it has no free worktop spot.

a decoration whose host piece is not bui.rule: A decoration whose host piece is not built is not built; it is a cascading consequence, not an independent loss.

a throw or additional bedding over a bed.rule: A throw or additional bedding over a bed model that already has its own made bedding is a styling option, not a required piece; it is not built if the model is not dressed.

a door symbol drawn on a layer is a draw.rule: A door symbol drawn on a layer is a drawing annotation, not a separate built element; the door is already in the model.

a hatch drawn on a layer is a drawing an.rule: A hatch drawn on a layer is a drawing annotation, not a built element.

a detail of an outdoor space (edge, step.rule: A detail of an outdoor space (edge, steps) is built with the outdoor space itself, not as a separate element.

a global origin offset that moves every.rule: A global origin offset that moves every region and sheet coordinate together is a frame note, not a defect: it is real only if some element is checked against an absolute coordinate that does not share the frame.

a uniform datum offset applied to every.rule: A uniform datum offset applied to every level mark is a frame choice, not a defect: it is real only if some element is placed against a different datum than the rest of the model.

a small drawn piece around a level-mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level-mark text is a symbol, not furniture: it is real only if it is still built as a furniture piece in the model.

a furniture name text is a defect only w.rule: A furniture name text is a defect only when the named piece is absent from the room; if the room already holds that piece, the text is satisfied.

when a drawn furniture label names a pie.rule: When a drawn furniture label names a piece that is absent from the room and no free spot within 1 m of the label passes the fit checks, the room's program must be re-solved (or the blocking piece moved) so the named piece can be placed at its drawn position, rather than silently dropping it.

a zone label is a defect only when the z.rule: A zone label is a defect only when the zone's furniture is absent from the room; if the room already holds the zone's anchor piece, the label is satisfied.

a context-typed piece is a defect only i.rule: A context-typed piece is a defect only if its type does not fit its size, room or neighbours; a seat at a table facing it is correctly a chair.

a parametric piece with no defined front.rule: A parametric piece with no defined front should be swapped to a library model that has a front, so the piece can be oriented correctly in the room.

a drawn piece without a front (front_inf.rule: A drawn piece without a front (front_inferred) must be given the direction its front faces, along a side of its footprint, so it can be oriented correctly in the room.

an outer-wall opening whose approach is.rule: An outer-wall opening whose approach is fully blocked by a drawn piece is a window, not a door: the reading must not build a passage where the drawing shows a sill.

a living room's tv is mounted on the wal.rule: A living room's TV is mounted on the wall opposite the sofa, not on a free-standing unit: the furniture stage must place a wall-mounted TV (or a low media console against that wall) when the room's program calls for one, and the camera stage must frame it.

a bedroom's tv is mounted on the wall op.rule: A bedroom's TV is mounted on the wall opposite the bed, not on a free-standing unit: the furniture stage must place a wall-mounted TV (or a low media console against that wall) when the room's program calls for one, and the camera stage must frame it.

a wall-hung washbasin must not hang over.rule: A wall-hung washbasin must not hang over a window: the fitting stage must move it to the nearest solid stretch of wall clear of the window's frame.

a wall-hung washbasin whose top rim is a.rule: A wall-hung washbasin whose top rim is at or below the window sill (within 5 cm) is a valid placement and should not be flagged as 'hanging over the window'.

when a camera override is refused due to.rule: When a camera override is refused due to a blocked frame, the set_camera tool should be used with the 'show' parameter to let the code pick a free pose that frames the required elements.

when a camera override is refused becaus.rule: When a camera override is refused because main pieces are not in the frame, the set_camera tool should be used with the 'show' parameter to let the code pick a pose that frames the required elements.

a door ray hitting a piece that is not i.rule: A door ray hitting a piece that is not in the room of the opening is a false alarm if the piece is not actually in that room's inventory.

a kitchen must contain a refrigerator; i.rule: A kitchen must contain a refrigerator; if a large boxy element is read as a stair in a kitchen, it is likely a misread appliance.

drawn furniture labels (like sifoniyer).rule: Drawn furniture labels (like SIFONIYER) must be matched to a built piece; if missing, the group solver should place it.

doors must be reachable from the floor l.rule: Doors must be reachable from the floor level; if an opening is too high to be a door, it is a window or clerestory.

sofas should be placed against walls or.rule: Sofas should be placed against walls or in a coherent seating group; mismatched styles indicate a bad fit.

when a room's label and its named furnit.rule: When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'room' that holds only a dresser and is under 6 m2), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently retyping it to hall and dropping the named piece.

a room whose label names a function (dre.rule: A room whose label names a function (dressing room, study, etc.) must be typed to that function at reading, not to 'other', so the furniture agent furnishes it to its program.

when a room's label and its named furnit.rule: When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'hall' that holds a dresser and a stair and is over 8 m2), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently keeping it as hall and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'room' that holds a dresser and is over 8 m2), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently retyping it to bedroom and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'bedroom' that holds a dresser), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently keeping it as bedroom and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'bathroom' that holds a dresser), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently keeping it as bathroom and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'shower' that holds a dresser), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently keeping it as bathroom and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'living room' that holds a dresser), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently keeping it as living and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'kitchen' that holds a dresser), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently keeping it as kitchen and dropping the named piece.

When a room's label and its named furniture disagree (a 'room' that holds a dresser and is under 6 m2), the reading stage must flag the label for the architect instead of silently retyping it to storage and dropping the named piece.

every washbasin in a bathroom or wc must.rule: Every washbasin in a bathroom or wc must be accompanied by a mirror mounted over or beside it; a basin without a mirror is an incomplete bathroom set.

every pendant or hanging light must be s.rule: Every pendant or hanging light must be shown reaching the ceiling with a cord or rod and a canopy; a floating fixture is a model defect.

every bathroom render must include the r.rule: Every bathroom render must include the reference detail set: an illuminated mirror over the basin, a lit open niche or shelf with toiletries, a towel rail, and a paper holder/brush, placed at real heights.

the kitchen must be styled to the refere.rule: The kitchen must be styled to the reference: a feature wall (slat panel) behind the dining area, an island with a hood in a hanging frame, fluted or framed fronts, a styled worktop and under-cabinet lighting.

a bathroom whose drawn fixtures are a ba.rule: A bathroom whose drawn fixtures are a basic washbasin, toilet and tub/shower must be dressed to the family's P12 reference (floating vanity with lit cubbies, feature panel, backlit mirror, walk-in glass shower with rain head and linear drain, towel shelf, two-cluster counter) rather than left as a plain white-tile box.

every bathroom must carry one p13 featur.rule: Every bathroom must carry one P13 feature wall (dark fluted WC wall or stone apron behind/under the vanity), a family-shaped framed mirror, towel bars at the door and shower, and one accent-colour towel repeated in two or three places.

a kitchen must reach the family's p5 ref.rule: A kitchen must reach the family's P5 reference: wall units run to the ceiling with no bare band, a tall-unit column (built-in fridge/oven tower) at a free run end, warm framed or fluted fronts, one stone slab per run, a styled worktop and an integrated dishwasher.

every kitchen appliance must read as a r.rule: Every kitchen appliance must read as a real product: a dishwasher integrated behind a matching front, or a steel unit with its control strip and handle, never a bare coloured slab.

a living-dining room must reach the fami.rule: A living-dining room must reach the family's P16 reference: handle-less full-height wall panels with a lit niche, a very large framed print, a plank table on a fringed rug, track spots with mini pendants, a TV over a low floating console with lit shelf niches, sculptural armchairs, a round stone coffee table on a round rug and sheer curtains.

a kitchen run that the drawing leaves ro.rule: A kitchen run that the drawing leaves room for a tall fridge column at the end of must include one; the kitchen set is incomplete without it.

a bathroom wc must be built as a complet.rule: A bathroom WC must be built as a complete set matching the reference: installation wall with niches, backlit mirror, wall-hung WC with flush plate, and basin on a console with wall mixer.

bedroom renders must include high-end de.rule: Bedroom renders must include high-end details: fluted or slat wall panels behind the bed, statement lighting (chandelier or pendants), layered realistic bedding with throws and multiple pillows, and a large rug.

bathroom renders must include detailed f.rule: Bathroom renders must include detailed fixtures: illuminated mirrors, lit niches or open shelves with toiletries, towel rails, and large-format tiles with cove or downlighting.

each room of the same type on a level mu.rule: Each room of the same type on a level must have a distinct design scheme, varying wall treatments (e.g., deep color, accent wall, slat panels) and furniture arrangements.

bed models must be highly detailed and r.rule: Bed models must be highly detailed and realistic, featuring deep soft duvets with rounded edges and wrinkles, multiple pillows of different sizes and fabrics, and textured throws or blankets.

every window must be built with a real p.rule: Every window must be built with a real profiled frame (outer frame, sashes, glazing beads, sill and handle), never a flat single-skin box.

every bathroom wc is built to the refere.rule: Every bathroom WC is built to the reference set: a half-height installation wall with recessed niches, a long backlit mirror, a wall-hung WC with its flush plate, the basin on a bench or console with a wall mixer, plus a brush and a roll holder.

windows side by side on one wall form a.rule: Windows side by side on one wall form a single composition (one head line, one sill line, or one glazing with mullions), never a large unit beside a small one.

columns supporting a veranda or balcony.rule: Columns supporting a veranda or balcony roof must be slender (round or slim rectangular, roughly 150-200 mm) and placed at the corners/edges of the canopy, never as thick piers that read as load-bearing walls.

every outdoor level difference (veranda,.rule: Every outdoor level difference (veranda, terrace, entrance) must be resolved as a landscape: terraces at one level per side, banks within 1:3, flights of solid treads with cheek walls and a landing, and a path that is level or stepped — never a bare plinth cut into the lawn.

every garden step must sit on its riser.rule: Every garden step must sit on its riser and the ground (no loose tread in the grass), and every retaining wall or plinth must be finished in stone or render with a coping — never a bare cut edge.

each outdoor floor must carry the materi.rule: Each outdoor floor must carry the material of its use (terrace/deck, steps, path, drive) in one language with the house's base — never one slab everywhere.

every outdoor stair must meet its landin.rule: Every outdoor stair must meet its landings, walls and planters cleanly — no block or wall cutting into a step, and each flight must end on a landing or the ground.

every outdoor stair must be built with o.rule: Every outdoor stair must be built with one continuous handrail at 0.9 m over its nosings along its open side, carried on real posts on the stair or its wall and extending 0.3 m past both ends, including over any landings.

every terrace or balcony edge must carry.rule: Every terrace or balcony edge must carry a real guard 1.0-1.1 m high (a glass balustrade with a metal top rail, or balusters under a handrail) in the facade's finish, never a thin bare tube.

site access steps should be simple and s.rule: Site access steps should be simple and short and placed where they make sense, without needless handrails.

a veranda and the balcony above it must.rule: A veranda and the balcony above it must share one guard system: a continuous guard on the balcony slab edge aligned with the veranda edge, with no redundant handrails inside the guard.

windows side by side on one wall must sh.rule: Windows side by side on one wall must share one head line and one sill line (or be one glazing with mullions); a large window may not sit beside a small one with a mismatched line.
